text:
It makes me sad to discover that this classic bar is now a daiquiri shop. The great thing about stopping at this old school narrow bar was that the drinks were well made, the clientele was reasonable and you were able to use the hotel's nice bathroom.  

Now it's just a sad, sad, sad bastion of machines and neon and no access to the hotel that houses it. Blah.

So, of course, it's John's fault that I went here. I haven't stepped foot in this bar since High School and really another 20+ years will just be fine.

Same people just different bodies.  I've never understood the appeal of these cavernous spaces with bad acoustics and questionable liquor.

Thanks for reminding me that I'd rather drink at home then spend even $2 on a holla.

Also, there are all sorts of sketchy rules (mostly to comply with the neighborhood association who would love to shut them down): everyone had to have their IDs scanned, even though most of us ...are a bit older than 21, we all had to wear "drinking bracelets" and you weren't allowed to leave with your nasty drink.

Copeland's used to be OK.  But now...
Huge plates of inferior food.  I also find some of their choices of sides or sauces sort of random.  Like let's just throw everything at the plate and see what sticks, random.  I used to like this original location (and one of my brothers worked in the kitchen in the 80s~maybe), but now I just think it's past its prime.

Why are people reviewing this location which is currently an empty lot? This location has not been open since the federal flood in 2005.

But seriously Martin's Wine Seller people...what's the hold up with the new building? There has been a concrete base poured for a couple of years and nothing but blowing sand. I would be very unhappy with you as my neighbor at the moment. 

At least the Google street view was when you were actually working on it, I think.  Annoying.

And, yes, I will mark it closed.

How anyone has given them more than one star I don't know.  (Sorry Allison)
Seriously, they are one confused agency.  I so wish the efforts to privatize them had worked a couple of years ago.  Not that I'm normally for privatization of public entities but anything would be better.

My favorite example of their insanity is that their was a leak (pre-K) at Napoleon & Loyola for a good 3 months.  The water was bubbling up into the street.  When did the crew show up to repair the leak?  On July 4th. Can you say triple overtime?

I stopped in for what I thought would be a quick visit on Friday night. Wow. I should have stuck to my regular store. This was only my 2nd visit to this location.

The aisles are tight. Be prepared to say excuse me to other shoppers every few minutes. The aisles that aren't tight? Piled high with stock in the middle of the space so that you still have to run an obstacle course. 

I found what I needed and then proceeded to check out and every line was LONG. Ok so there was an after-work rush. I attempted to use a Rouses GC that I received as a gift. Nope. The machine wouldn't take it. And my sweet cashier tried. Rather than tie up the already long line. I was directed to customer service. Where I stood and stood and stood. There were 2 people staffing the desk, but they mostly spoke to each other and then started taking people who wandered up rather than those of us in line... who couldn't maneuver because of random stock displays in the middle of the floor. I was told that it was my fault for waiting in line. OK. 

I gave up. And I'll figure out the GC thing at my regular Rouse's.

Oh dear lord. I ordered a dozen plus cupcakes for my parents' 55th wedding anniversary. And while the cupcakes were fine, the service...

First I verified online what flavors they offer on Friday. Then I called this store...and it went to voicemail. I left a message. 2 hours later, I called again. The guy who answered the phone seemed surprised to hear they had voicemail that he was maybe supposed to check. 

I ordered the cupcakes and was told that I had to pay in advance. OK. Telling him my credit card number was another bit of ridiculousness since he couldn't remember the numbers long enough to write them down.

Fast forward to pickup. My dozen cupcakes are ready but the couple extra are nowhere. There is a box on top of mine, but it is empty. They are, of course, sold out of the flavor of the extra cupcakes...wedding cake because y'know anniversary party. The girl just stares at me and says she doesn't know what to do. After a couple of beats, I just ask for my money back. She brightens and says sure she can do that.

Next time I'll use a store that actually has employees who care. OTH, they clearly don't need my business because their display case was nearly empty at 5:15 on a Friday.

Lovely little boutique with higher end lines . The layout is open and airy and the clothes are well displayed. The selection skews a bit young for me, but that's not an issue since I'm often buying gifts for the plethora of nieces. 

What is the problem is the staff. Everytime I've been in, I've been ignored. On this last visit my modelesque niece tried asking a question about a sale item and got a deep sigh in response. Really...

Then I had the audacity to ask about an item on a counter display. Same deep sigh and the salesperson grudgingly acknowledged my question and answered me like I was an idiot. 

Whatever. Because that's the attitude of the staff.

Sketchy gas station at the corner of Milan & Claiborne. It used to be a BP and then it was something else...and now it's a Fuel Express...and maybe sells fried chicken inside. But I haven't had that.

There are only 4 pumps at the space is small. Although it is conveniently located, I only go here during the day.  The gas is cheap though.

I ended up here after the Krewe of Halloween because my niece and her friends wanted to catch the World Series game.  I was not too impressed.  I would blame any service bobbles (1 plate out of 6 came 20 minutes late) on the crowds, but then the waiter charged one of the nieces' friends for the entire meal on her card after also receiving cash. Sketchy. He did apologize when called out.  I thought the garlic fries were bitter. And the crabmeat on my seafood cobb salad did not taste fresh.

I guess I should mention that I ate in the bar so maybe that makes a difference.

So I was taking a visiting friend out to dinner and we settled on this spot. Honestly it really was meh. 

The hardest part was that my friend is vegetarian and even the vegetable dishes here aren't. The beans are cooked with meat. And our server could not be bothered to assist us. 

The tacos that I had (spinach & mushroom and fried shrimp) just didn't have much flavor. 

The table and floor where we were seated were slightly grungy and really needed a good cleaning. 

I'm sort of stunned at all the 5 star ratings. Maybe the drinks are really good?

So maybe it was the hour, but the evening started to decline. Physically this was the smallest bar space so getting to it to order a drink was tough. Another bar more karaoke (Saturday night only), which definitely had some regulars singing their favorites.

The welcome from the staff and patrons was...odd since it made you feel like strangers never walk into the bar. Or maybe I was just getting paranoid.

Our final stop on the Party Bus wank tour and really it's pretty sketchy. Loved the sign that said "don't hustle the paying customers." Did not love the drink I received. I have no idea what I ended up with but decided that it was a sign that I shouldn't drink.

A friend who lives nearby says the parking lot is packed between 5 and 8 am so that maybe the most interesting time to go.

This isn't my favorite store; mostly the problem is with the other patrons. I've been hassled in the parking lot by panhandlers, cursed out by old people at the pharmacy counter for perceived slights, and harassed in the aisles by random dudes looking for a "date." So I only stop in when absolutely necessary.

The store alternates between acceptable and dirty; they did a big refurbishment right before the CVS opened across the street but it's already back to being slightly ratty. 

The staff is OK in my opinion. But the store definitely needs better security

I hadn't stopped into Wise Buys in years...like maybe over a decade.  And the sales associates (2 in a tiny store) couldn't be bothered to say hello to me.  I always greet folks in small stores; it's only polite.

Prices were meh.  And I didn't see anything that really blew me away stockwise.  I guess it'll be another decade before I wander back in.

The Pontchartrain Center is on the other end of the earth to me, right off the lake on Williams Blvd.  It is Kenner's answer to the convention center.  It can be rearranged into a variety of configurations.  None have been to great.  The staff was surly, the bathrooms weren't very clean, the parking was nightmare AND I there were men in inappropriately short shorts b/c Back to the Beach was happening just across the levee and the casino.

Thank goodness my niece is quitting dancing school, so I won't have to go to another dance recital here next year.  I hope it will be another decade before I return.

I called Jefferson Appliance in September to look at 3 appliances at my old double (which I'm currently renting out).  Of course, on one appliance the problem wouldn't duplicate while the repair person was there.  Figures.  Another problem turned out to be a loud motor and as the dishwasher was out of warranty, it would cost more for a new motor than to just replace the whole machine.  Satisfactory answers on both and the price of the new motor was related via a follow up call.

The final appliance was a front loader washing machine.  We were told it wasn't working because my tenant was using too much soap and they left.  But it turns out that it only worked once or twice after they tried the approved cleaning method.  So I called Jefferson Appliance back...and left a couple of messages.  No one has ever returned my phone call.

Perhaps they've gone out of business?  Or maybe they just don't want mine.

Since I last went to Ninja, they've changed the menu entirely, and not for the better in my opinion. It makes me really sad to say that the fish tasted slightly off. And the emphasis is on rolls with *lots* of sauce to hide the flavors. I ordered takeout and sat at the bar.

I really wanted the okra tempura which is no longer on the menu, but they did offer to make my veggie tempura all okra, if they could. And they did and it was yummy...although a bit greasy.  The blue crab sushi which was another former favorite ended up in the trash since it tasted awful.  My other items were just blah. Nothing special about them.

I remember eating at their Jeannette location about a million years ago and being amazed by the taste and the presentation. I'm not sure what's going on now.

It had been a few since I last came to this theater. So yesterday I payed $11.50 for a movie and tried to find a seat in the theater that was intact. I was in theater 10 and most of the seats were cracked and broken, some were missing backs. The last time I remembered being horrified by the condition of the ladies room....multiple broken/out of order toilets, broken tile, just felt dirty, so I waited until I got home rather than brave those again. 

The staff was pleasant and as usual I didn't hit the snack bar. But I did notice the upgrade of the fancy coke machines and multiple flavors of icee. There is still a bar in the lobby as well.

The whole place from parking lot to lobby to theaters just seems shabby. Definitely time for a makeover.

So this place wasn't my favorite. While cigarette smoke isn't my favorite, I usually can ignore it. Maybe not so much in a place that says "Smoking Welcome." So there's that.

But really I think the vibe just wasn't doing it for me. Can we pick somewhere else next time?

I know I've said it before...I used to love Nirvana but it's just so uneven these days.  After a long day of home improvements, we just wanted a simple meal and to crash.  We ordered a pakora and chat papri and both were fine.  But the saag paneer we ordered to share was borderline inedible.  And, of course, it made both us sick, so no sleep for us.

It will be a while before I give Nirvana another try.

hmmm...where to start?  I grew up drinking fruit wines that were made in various rural areas of south Louisiana. My grandparents' had friends that served orange wine in their restaurant, somewhere down on the bayou.  And I've had strawberry wine many times.  Both of these were more sherry like than the wines @ Tropical Winery.

The wines here (and I tasted maybe 4 or 5) are all really sweet, like I need it cut with seltzer, sweet.  I didn't taste anything that inspired me to buy an entire drink.  I guess it's just not my thing.

Sometimes you just need the cheapest gas. And this was my go to spot for most of the 80s when it was Tenneco and my parents had given me a gas card. Yep dating myself with all the old-timey references.

It's a pretty sketchy location and mostly the guys hanging outside are just interested in drinking and don't cause any trouble...it is JP afterall. 

Gas is cheap. It is not well lit and I only stop during daylight hours.

So maybe this just isn't my sort of place...although with the cheap prices for premium liquor, you would think it would be.  And it was good for people watching.  But with the booming sound system (my throat was hoarse the next day from yelling over it), the pervasive cigarette smoke (Yuck), and the subzero a/c (brrrr), I was not too comfortable.  

Maybe if friends wanted to go back on a less crowded/smoky/noisy night, I would try again. Or maybe I'll just convince friends to try someplace else.

The space is beautiful and the staff seemed friendly, but we were just picking up takeout for a quick weekday lunch.

But oh dear. I really wanted to like this place...and maybe I might try their breakfast/brunch.  With the quality of food we received for lunch, I don't think I'll be trying their higher priced dinner options.

*the bad*
If you say "lump crabmeat" on your menu, any good New Orleanian is going to expect blue crab. I'm not sure what was on my panini (which wasn't pressed so I'm not sure  what that was about) and I'm going to say maybe it was a different variety of crab (and not krab) that wasn't as tasty as the blues in the gulf.  If I had been dining in for lunch, I would have sent the sandwich back. 

*the good*
My coworker who got the curry chicken sandwich really liked her dish and she said the steak fries were yummy. Only error here, was that the menu says served on a croissant, but she got toast.  Also the side of corn was tasty.  The one person who got a juice (the ginger ale) from the bar really liked it.

*the meh*
Other coworker's turkey club was dry and had no condiments at all included and that her potato salad side was a bit mayonnaise-y.  Also, my side salad was undressed so left me scrounging in the work fridge for dressing.

I usually go to Superior because other people want to...like my brother and his kids.  It's a good place to bring children because it's so loud you don't have to worry about your noisy ones disturbing other folks' meals.  The cocktails are free flowing and the food's OK.

I had an our to kill before meeting some friends so I stopped in for a cup of tea and a snack. Unfortunately, they were out of the tea I wanted so I settled for another type. And the spinach-feta pastry that I had was yummy; I wish it could have been toasted rather than heated in the microwave.

The staff was nice and apologetic about the missing tea. The space indoors is cozy, but the tables are pretty well spaced. The front patio area is spacious...if sitting near Veterans Hwy is your sort of thing.

So let's discuss why this shop gets 3 not 4 stars. The parking lot SUCKS. Because the space has a drive through, parking spaces are almost non-existent. And all the nearby businesses have threatening signs about parking in their lots with dire consequences promised.

Made it to Luke's for dinner and the crabmeat ravioli is AMAZING.  However I'm knocking off a star because the place was a zoo.  

The next table was a 50th birthday party of 9 adults; one of the women was literally yelling at the top of her voice.  With tile/hardwood floors and tin ceilings, the volume in the restaurant almost ruined our meal.  It was exceedingly difficult to carry on a conversation at our table of 5 in between the shrieks next to us.  

Other dishes at our table were the redfish (w/ the crabmeat), the vanilla duck, shrimp & grits, and the shrimp farci.  Everyone thought their food was lovely...if only the atmosphere had been as nice.

Yeah it's a chain but it's very special diet friendly. If you're a veggie or a vegan or gluten free, they have something for you.

The food is pretty good quality for a chain and I like being able to customize to my exact taste...although I'm sure the servers want to throw something at me. "I'd like 1 tablespoon of this and a smidge of that..." OK I'm really not that bad.

I like being able to refill my own beverage too.

Hmm...I ended up here after a show at HoB since my friends really wanted to hang out with the band and they had given us passes. I'm not really a velvet rope kind of girl so that part kind of annoyed me. It's a bar that charges huge prices for drink and you have to be invited in (or you have to a member or something). 

The decor is cool and there was a DJ with accompanying horn player spinning an eclectic selection of music. There's a couple of different spaces (including a VIP area) to escape the music and dancers.

Then there was the crowd. It was bizarre. There was a definite sugar daddy/much younger woman thing happening. Maybe it is the velvet rope thing...people seemed really stoked to be in the space. I don't know. I like weird spaces. But the crowd just didn't do it for me. My friend who got us in acted like she was in hell...until the band showed up and she got to geek out. Then all was right with the world.

The DIS location that I had been using near Touro closed. So I wasn't thinking when I made my appointment and had to drive out to the Metrys. 

The location is fine and efficient. The front office was crowded but they were hustling people through. Technician was quick and professional. Test results were communicated quickly.

My biggest problem is the parking lot. I don't know who designed this strip mall but the parking is a pain. Thank goodness my appointment was after lunch because finding a spot during prime meal times is impossible.

I'm very torn about this restaurant. First it's BEAUTIFUL. Really the views from the window are stunning and the grounds are really lovely.

BUT my food was just OK and after making a point about saying no meat (especially in Catholic Louisiana on Good Friday), they served me dirty rice with my stuffed crab. The stuffed crab was OK; the dirty rice, I gave away and then there was a side vegetable, sweet cooked carrots which were again OK. But not enough food for the price. The garlic bread was yummy. 

Our server was nice. I felt bad for the hostess who kept having to check the men's room for occupancy since the ladies' room was out of order. The inside of the restaurant is pleasant. I just wish the food had been as good as the views.

After reading all my friends' 5 star reviews, I was expecting to be wowed, but the drinks I tasted (during Tales so maybe they were overworked?) were all way too sour. We had the classic Mai Tai, a Hurricane and ...something smokey tasting. The hurricane was actually the best of the drinks. The mai tai was so sour that it tasted more like a margarita, definitely not what I was expecting. 

As for the atmosphere, it's very warehouse-y with a bunch of decorations slapped around. And while there was table service, they were a bit overwhelmed while I was there. The prices are good for the size of the drinks.

Maybe I just need to go back when it's not Tales.

A solid choice for ice cream or sherbet (if you're at this end of Magazine), but there isn't a huge selection...but maybe that's good for the indecisive? I had blueberry something and it was really tasty.  The staff seemed...friendly but indifferent.  

Since I've seen a bunch of businesses come and go on this block, I admire how the current folks have dressed up this location.  The design aesthetic is clean and welcoming.  I'll have to try the shave ice to compare it to a snowball.  

I'll leave y'all to the bubble teas; tapioca freaks me out.

Ultimately, I decided the Skin Studio wasn't for me. I think Christine does great work, but since my issue wasn't acne (which is her main focus), I ultimately wasn't sure where we were going.

I'm not one to get chemical peels or any injectable and so ultimately,  I think this spot was too medically oriented for me.  Maybe I do need the crunchy granola touch instead.

I realized that I never updated my review of this place. I never did go back for another cut.  The cut I was given was expensive and didn't really work with my hair texture.  

So your mileage may be different, I was just underwhelmed and have moved on.

TMI review...I'm not a big waxer. I've had allergic reactions to wax and I also have a big old scar on my leg that's pretty sensitive. But every now and then I break down and decide to bite the bullet.

The good: 
I called and made an appointment about 30 minutes out. 
They're open on Mondays.
Space is nice and inviting.
Yelp deal with check in 10% off.

The meh:
Though the price was still high for lower leg only. 
Wax wasn't fully cleaned up on one leg.

Good news is that I didn't break out into a rash and she worked quickly enough that my scar wasn't too irritated.

I've had fine meals at Katie's and I've had mediocre meals here too.  It is a fun neighborhood spot and the menu is diverse...and maybe too big. How can you make all those various items well?  However the variety is part of the selling point, in that if you're with a group then there is something for everyone.

I would probably give this 4 stars but on my last visit both entrees came with items that were not mentioned on the menu and we both would have opted to NOT have had we known.

There drinks are good.  The A/C can be spotty...like lots of old buildings.

While I normally choose a local shop, I was in the neighborhood & hadn't been to a Baskin Robbins in a while. 

The sales clerk was a little done...but we were there near closing and I was insisting on tasting the weird colored ice cream (like acid green and bright purple). Those flavors mostly tasted like really artificial candy.  So I went with Mississippi Mud.

It's a little less expensive then CC but the product is definitely inferior. Still not a bad choice if you're in the neighborhood.

I want to be comfortable in this space and it is gorgeous and the happy hours that I've been here, it's been hit or miss with the bartenders, like everywhere. But I just can't. 

I am frustrated that this beautiful space was a bit of a political boondoggle and that it was renovated with money that was intended for New Orleans Public Libraries. This is not the fault of the current management or staff but it leaves a bad taste. 

I wish them well.

As I was traveling from point A to point B, I realized that I was starving so I decided to take a chance on this strip mall sushi joint. 

The space is small and very basic. The staff was really nice and accommodating.  I ordered my rolls to go and so didn't really use table service....

The rolls were fine if basic. Everything tasted good...but I did my usual and declined the sauces on top. I hate gooey sauces on top of rolls. I think this makes me an unAmerican sushi eater.

I had a couple of rolls...and they were good so there's that. Next time I might try the sushi.

I do like that they have online ordering...not that I tried it since y'know, driving. But it doesn't seem to be the whole menu.

This place actually delivers to my work so that's a plus. And the pizza has a decent crust and the toppings were generous. Since they sell by the slice, it's nice that the slices are huge. 

Now for the meh. The margeurita pizza had no basil on it and the cheese was definitely not a high quality. When a pizza only has sauce, tomatoes, basil and cheese, missing one is kind of a big deal.

The delivery person arrived on time and while one of our salads was missing; the location corrected that and delivered it within 15 minutes.

This is one of those weird spots that tries to be something for everyone. So I'm usually wary... But this is where friends wanted to go so....

We didn't have cocktails so I can't comment on that. But we ordered a variety of items. One friend got mostly items that I would associate with a Chinese restaurant and two others got mostly sushi and rolls. I got noodle soup because that's what I was craving. But you could also order a steak or pasta or chargrilled oysters. OK. Everything was fine. But the restaurant was pretty empty. I think they do beacoup take out business though.

Oh, Rocky's, how I once loved you.  Your delicious pizzas, your yummy salads, your interesting music choices.  But then you got sloppy; I would get a pizza with someone else's ingredients slopped over on one edge.  The service got...odd.

Then that whole Katrina thing happened, and you abbreviated your menu.  OK we all had to adjust but you never returned to your pre-K menu and you eliminated all my faves.  

Yes it is decent pizza but I go to Theo's or Reginelli's instead now.

The cafeteria is looking pretty good after the renovation a couple of years ago AND new management came in as of January this year.  There are usually a few choices for lunch and a basic breakfast selection (eggs, variety of meats, oatmeal, grits, and biscuits). 

My big gripes are that it really depends on who you get as a server/cashier as to how much food you'll get or how much you'll pay. And nickle & diming over some crackers, margarine is just irritating. 

It is convenient but it's just kind of blah. If I have a choice, I'll go find a food truck on the street instead.

Yay a new ice cream shop...which has only been open a couple of weeks. The space is small but I like the sparkly booth seats.

 The ice cream selection is small but there is definitely something for everyone. I had the peach vanilla and it was fresh and tasty. My only small point was that the peaches bits were large so they got a bit icy to the tooth. But that's probably me just being a weirdo. My friend loved her toasted coconut and it was yummy. 

The business is cash only and supposedly also has snowballs but I didn't see anyone get those while I was there.

Oh my, when we said we were going to Franklin my friend's younger daughter asked us to stop by this candy shop for her favorite...  And they had some super tasty stuff. Loved the self serve jars. They had cute displays for Easter when I was there.

And I was able to buy bulk Spree (which I am NEVER allowed to do again) and some old school satellites (like communion wafers filled with candy) and some fancy chocolates.

Really cute addition to the area.

Since I was just chatting about this new bakery over on twitter, I guess I'll finish my review...

The space is small and they do have dine in tables (but no liquor license if you're here for brunch...but they do have mixers I'm told if you bring your own).  The staff was courteous and prompt. 

But on to the important stuff. The $1 croissant bites are genius. They melt in your mouth with buttery deliciousness but still have a bit of a crunch on the edges. I hate a mushy croissant. I also tried the mixed berry and apple turnovers. They were perfectly sized and the mixed berry was clearly the winner being tart and not too sweet. The apple was good to but the berry was amazing.  As I'm not a coffee person I got a perfectly tasty iced tea and was out the door.

The one thing that is lacking is their signage. Maybe it's building rules or maybe they just haven't gotten there yet. But blink and you'l miss them. They are riverside on Magazine between General Pershing and Milan...so dangerously close to home.

I'll be back soon...

Y'know how you have that impossible person on your gift list and you really have no idea what to buy them. BUT lucky for you, they are obsessed with their pet.  This is the place to buy them a gift.  Yes, it is mostly doggie stuff but I have found items for the cat lovers in my life.  

Plus you can bathe your own dog here in their self-service bathtub which is up on a platform which really could save your back.

Maple Street is not on my usual weekend path, but I've stopped by this bakery the last few times I've been over that way.  Delicious apple turnover, almond croissants, and cheese danish/turnover/thingy.  I even bought my Mom a Thanksgiving cupcake with plastic turkey on top - old school.  

My only criticism is I wish they had a true vegetarian sandwich on their lunch menu.

Cute selection of upscale shoes (and even in my baby feet size!) and handbags. The sales person was helpful without being pushy and actually seemed occupied by store tasks rather than her cellphone!  

The costume jewelry and other accessories were fun too.  Also, this one of the locations where you can check out Dominque Giordano's creations in person since her shop across the street is shut down.

Yelp's own Andrea B wanted to have a UYE (unofficial yelp event) and this is where we ended up and we were treated (yes, treated, I say!) to our girl BELTING out Welcome to the Jungle.  Please do see the pic I posted, but really it doesn't do justice.  

Best of all, there was a random drag queen bake sale going on & I scored an excellent apple pie.  

No I wasn't brave enough to sing myself...maybe next time.

Being a native, St. Claude was the last place I expected to find such a great club, but it's an avenue that's turning around.  Seriously, a dragon (a real one not a costume) could walk into Kajun's and take turn on the stage and no one would bat an eye.

Minus 1 star for the billowing cigarette smoke.

I was on a mission of mercy and picked up dog food (not in my neighborhood) for a friend.  The staff was really nice and repeatedly offered to carry the bag of food to the car. The prices seemed compatible with big box chains, but this is a locally owned store.  (The original is in my childhood neighborhood). PLUS you get the convenience of down the street, well y'know if you're my friend.

Nice selection of doggie items, collars, treats, food, etc. I didn't look at cat stuff.

Looking for a treasure? Or a questionable collectible? Or maybe an Infant of Prague statue? Or even a vintage Mr. Bingle? This might be the store for you. 

Yes, it's super cluttered and it's set up in individual booths and getting someone with the right key to the right case can be a bit challenging. But if you find the exact pitcher you used to use in your grandmother's kitchen for about $20, then it's worth it.

I hate that you have to check your bags...but browsers aren't always honest so I get it.  Although I would say this is not the place to go if you have major dust allergies, but you already knew that.

Santa Fe on Frenchmen has moved to Esplanade Ave. The cocktails were lovely as was the outdoor seating.  We only had appetizers but both were well plated an delicious.  

Plus we were serenaded my fellow diners who were inspired by the 80s soundtrack playing on the sound system.  I think they may have had one too many of the margaritas.

And the veggie pho is delicious...in case you were wondering, as is the spicy tofu appetizer.  

I've also tried their grilled shrimp items and YUMMY.  Love that the place is so low key and that you are greeted like you've just arrived at your favorite aunt's house.

Hmmm...to write a review of lucky dogs or to not. Full disclosure, I last ate a lucky dog in high school so maybe a couple of decades ago. But I am a big fan of the carts and love that they exist.  If you're a hot dog lover, you should definitely have one. Rumor has it that the stand closest to Jackson Square is always the cleanest. And if you are leaving NOLA without having indulged, there's a cart on at least one of the concourses.

If you haven't read Managing Ignatius by Jerry Strahan, add it to your New Orleans book list. It's a memoir not fiction, because who could make some of this stuff up.  I will warn you that if you read it, and you're from here, it'll make you really miss orange julius.

OMG! I just discovered their online shop. Lucky Dog gifts for everyone! http://www.luckydogs.us/shop/index.cfm

I'm so glad this is a restaurant space again. Pre-K I went to Christian's often and it was nice to back inside this churchy location.  

The food was wonderful. I started with a lovely mixed green salad with a pungent & delicious blue cheese. And then had the stuffed baked shrimp withe hominy cakes. Seriously tasty. My dining companion had a very lemony/anchovy-y caesar salad (and I mean that in a good way) and then stuffed salmon with gnocchi and asparagus. Since I sampled her food too, I thought the gnocchi were a bit heavy, but still delicious.  Then for dessert? AMAZING dark chocolate creme brulee. Seriously y'all, I love fancy chocolate pudding and this was the fanciest (and tastiest).

Only off note was that our server was struggling. The restaurant was busy because of superbowl weekend, but we never did get to hear the specials and had to ask for more bread.  Not that big of a deal really, especially when you view it in light of AMAZING dark chocolate creme brulee.

This is a solid neighborhood bar that is spacious and has MLB season pass (if that's important to you). I would hang out here alot except y'know the smoking. 

The liquor is well priced, the bartenders are on point, the clientele is diverse and welcoming. But dang do they smoke.

I've heard their trivia night is outstanding. And just as a note about the women's restrooms, they are spacious (not palatial) but you don't feel trapped and feature my all time dive bar favorite...plywood stalls. Love some industrious carpentry. PLUS they have old high school prom pictures to make you laugh. 

OK I just changed my review rating from 3 (because of the smoke) to 4 (because of the prom pictures).

Sometimes it's the little things...

Love the curry fried rice. Seriously why isn't this a standard on every menu?  And my friend had the mango shrimp salad special; it was fresh and delicious.

And the lack of a liquor license has been confirmed.  I think the liquor behind the bar is just there to tease you.

Plus I have been corrected; the 2 Singhas are the same owners. So, yay, for expansion!

Wow! The new sports areas are amazing! Went out last night to catch my niece's soccer game and I couldn't believe how that end of the park was transformed.  A great addition to an already good space.

Now if we just could do something about the extreme leash laws...my 13 yr old dog isn't wandering away or going to do anything besides collapse.

Ha! Christy L beat me on this review.  

I take my Mom to shop here at least once a year, just so she can walk around and be astonished at the prices people pay for stuff she still has.  But really you could tell me you bought just about anything from this place and I would believe you.  My fave gift from here is an Infant of Prague religious statue.  My fave purchase was a decade old Mr. Bingle.

I finally got to try this food truck outside NOMA one evening with my Mom. We had the Bootz and the Rachel. The Rachel was the definite winner of the two; it had pesto, truffle aioli, provolone, smoked gouda and tomato. The Bootz was good too (colby, swiss & cheddar on sourdough) but it was just pale in comparison to the Rachel. Two sandwiches were the best of both worlds though so we could each have a half. 

Price point was good and the sandwiches came up quickly. Will definitely hit them up again for cheesie goodness.

I stopped in for lunch here while shopping with my Mom on Magazine Street. And the staff was lovely and attentive. The space is really open and attractive.

The food was good and the prices were inexpensive compared to other Vietnamese places. And the food is more traditional than some of the other spots uptown/garden district. 

I had veggie avocado spring rolls and they were perfect. My Mom had a small pho (which was huge for her) and she really enjoyed it. I also had the bun with tofu and it was OK. 

There were definitely regulars who must be in all the time since they were greeted and asked if they wanted their usual dishes, which I would appreciate if I were a regular. The porch seating seemed to be dog friendly too.

The steps were a bit steep and my Mom did struggle with them a little but she had been walking all over the place for a few hours.

A friend randomly chose this restaurant since none of us had ever been before. The decor is...charming but odd. The faux french quarter balcony feels weird when you're just a few miles up river from the real deal, but it's well done and the starry sky is lovely.

We started with cocktails and the oysters rockefeller and the crab cakes meuniere. The oysters were amazing; the addition of brie is genius. The crab cakes were fine but I wasn't as blown away by them as my friends were.

I had a trout special, one friend had the trout long beach and the other steak with sauteed mushrooms. What isn't clear from the online menu, is that when you order an entree, you get a starter and a side. I had a salad which was ok and gratin potatoes. My fish was amazing and the best thing about my night. The salad and gratin potatoes were OK but nothing special. My friends loved both of their meals.

We got a couple of desserts (Yelp checkin deal!). I got what was advertised as a doberge cake...which it wasn't but was a delicious, rich, dense, delicious chocolate cake. And also bread pudding which was served beautifully but differently in slices, rather than in a square or a ramekin. 

Service was good but no obtrusive. There was a preseason Saints game on so we knew when a big play was made, since you can hear Monkey Hill next door...if they're loud enough. Sadly, we only heard that once or twice on that evening. (Geaux Saints anyway...le sigh).

Say you decide that you need a new door...and you only have $35.  Where do you go?  the Green Project. 

Or you have a bunch of left over building supplies, random bits of lumber, some roofing materials, maybe even some paint?  Where can you bring it so it doesn't end up in a landfill?  Again, the Green Project.

The other big french bread bakery in the city.  They don't get the press or the market share of Leidenheimer's but are still really good.

Again, this is the bakery, but they may have a retail store where you can actually purchase items...at least they did once upon a time.  Look for Binder's at your local grocery.

I'm still a big fan of Il Posto (and the currrent duchess, thank you very much), but thought I would update my review based on my observations last night.

Tuesday & Wednesday nights from 5-8 and around 7 last night (a Tuesday) a small herd of cute 20-something gals all came strolling in. They weren't one big group either. So as my public service to single men of the appropriate age, go check it out.

Just bought a great box of fresh, organic produce: blood oranges, strawberries, frisee, lettuce, mushrooms, etc.

I love that they are trying to buy local and it's great service.  Wonderful use of the old Guilliot's nursery.  Check them out! 

Open every Saturday from 10-2.

Oh look it's been 3 years since I last reviewed Fairy...

You know a shop is great when you become friends with the owner. Elizabeth has many years of retail/clothing experience and it shows in the great eye she has for the styles and lines she carries. Not everything is to my taste (we will never agree about pre-ripped jeans), but there are always quite a few things to tempt me. The sale rack in the back is typically full of bargains. She carries GREAT and affordable accessories and I love the sunglasses she carries, so much so that I currently am rotating 3 pairs. 

Love that she supports other small business owners via trunks shows for various local jewelry, hat, purse makers. And, of course, Toulouse is a great shop ambassador. 

Hey Yelp - can I give Fairy 17million stars?

I used my Living Social deal to go visit Christine at Skin Studio yesterday.  Wow.

Her approach is much more clinical and scientific (rather than crunchy granola) compared to previous facials.  We discussed my skin issues, my care regime (such as it is), and my goals.  She gave me multiple options based on my stated goals from very basic to more advanced.  

Basically, if I want my skin to be different than it is, I have to stop being lazy. HMMMM something to consider.

I can really see the difference in my skin today.

Time for a re-review of this spot. While it still has all juice snoballs (current favorite is pineapple mint), they've expanded into smoothies and fancy juice mixes. As well as paninis (although I've never ordered one at the shop).

There is usually just one person working inside but they'll tell you if they are running any specials...like satsuma juice. The prices are affordable considering the quality.

My only annoyance is that I really can't tell if they are open from the street and they used to be less than consistent with their hours but that seems to be getting better.

I had not been on the Natchez for a cruise since grade school and guess what? It's as fun as I remember (even without the getting out of class/field trip aspect).  

I didn't sign up for the YSB cruise since my oldest/dearest BFF was coming into town for a convention the next week for a conference. I had helped him decide on some of the social events, including one on the Natchez.  So I got to cruise the river at night with a bunch of engineers...and explain the food to some of them.

While there were many bars set up all over the boat for this event, the main bar had the best selection of liquor in case you're a brand snob AND for this event, the conference had booked Sunpie Barnes and the Louisiana Sunspots, so much fun!

The food was yummy! My BFF even compared their gumbo to his grandfather's! High praise. I enjoyed the caprese salad on a stick, the passed spanokopitas and the shrimp creole,  The mini-muffalatas and the bananas foster were big hits too!

So on the river, I loved watching the city glide by and the engineers were pretty impressed with boat turning around since the captain let the river handle part of it rather than using fuel to do so.

MUST DO! Stand at the very back and get splashed by the paddle wheel! Makes me feel like a kid again when we were allowed to file past (making sure none of us fell) to feel the water on my skin.

Love this little bridge that crosses Bayou St. John which is pedestrian only... But I have seen people bike across. It's the perfect spot to stop and contemplate the sky and the water or chat with a friend.

There have been various threats to tear it down but the community always rallies to stop the demolition. And it has been proven to be structurally sound for people.

Take a moment and walk around Bayou St. John and then stop on the bridge, perhaps with your favorite beverage and just be. You won't regret it.

mmmm...a choc-work orange, so good.  Flavors to please everyone in the family from the gourmand to the 6 year old.  

This ice cream parlor does traditional bar service in the location of the original McKenzie's Bakery location (and they've left the old neon sign earning eternal love from many New Orleanians).

I'm a big fan of Lafayette Square these days. It's actually being kept clean and is a welcome respite of green in the midst of a lot of concrete.  Plus it's the location of a number of events from the Wednesdays at the Square music series to the Seafood festival to the Blues & BBQ Fest.

Still a great value and a GREAT place to donate used or unnecessary building supplies. Since my last review, I've dropped off paint, paint and more paint, light fixtures, ceiling fans, a bathtub, sinks, the entire contents of my parents' condemned garage.

The staff has always been great, helping us unload and asking questions about our donations. They were very impressed with my Dad's castoff collection of homemade tool boxes.  

Watch for paint drop off locations at alternate locations too. I've dropped off paint and both Hollygrove Market and Whole Food Uptown.

I just love the new space, so much larger and airier than the tee-niny shop they had on Maple.  Love the expanded collection of vintage clothing and coats. And all the purses, oh my.

They are really good about buying vintage items from collectors (a friend has sold them jewelry, furs, purses and clothes). The owner does have a great eye and she's very easy to work with.

The staff member that was in the store when I stopped in a couple of weekends ago was lovely and the space is very conducive to browsing.

Great addition to Magazine Street.

Well I guess I'll go ahead and write their last review. Only open a few years, but they're closing up shop at this location. 

My facialist Nikki just landed here in the last few months and I know she enjoyed the space. I booked an appointment here a few weeks ago and when I arrived I was told it was their last week of services. Final day is tomorrow February 24. 

The space is lovely and very relaxing. Nikki is always great. I'm sorry to see that they are closing.

So a car ran a stop sign... wait, no, she said she stopped at the stop sign and I wasn't there so she zoomed out and ran into me... who knew my car had the power to materialize out of thin air? And while it was minor accident... no injuries, my airbag didn't deploy, her child was in car seat, thank goodness. My poor car had a jacked bumper, hood, quarter panel & light kit. So I limped home and called my insurance and this location was one of the recommended State Farm body shops. OK. I saw that Harry was a fan and one of my car-guy coworkers likes them too. Sold. 

Communication was excellent. I dropped my car over the weekend so called them Monday morning. They explained the insurance estimate process to me. And everything went smoothly. Seriously, I emailed them with questions and they answered promptly... I can't even get that sort of response time from other offices, much less a mechanic.

The car was ready when they told me and they washed and vacuumed it so it looks great!

This is a favorite of my friends in Nashville from the teen daughter to the professional father. And I can see why. Clothing, art, jewelry, toys, musical instruments! Wow I wish this store was in NOLA.

From the street it doesn't look that large, but it just keeps going and going. There is a small parking lot behind the shop with maybe a 2 or 3 spots. And the shop has both a back parking lot door and a front door on the street. 

The staff was great, even getting a giant ladder so I could have just the flying cat that I wanted. I found several great Christmas gifts here and I only wish I had the $ to actually buy myself a bunch of clothes. Next time!

After moving a few times last year, I think this Gallery has settled in at the 600 block of Royal. It's a great space with lots of exposed brick and high ceilings...the better to showcase and hang art!

Beth helped me with my newest Barkus poster, as well as another from a couple of years ago that I skipped. She was great to work with and was very patient with my indecision. 

The gallery still features a variety of artists who find their inspiration from our companion animals. They sell everything from original paintings to notecards so there is a price point for everyone. 

Love the fanciful spirit of the art.

First time over the new expanded bridge today! Wow! It's so nice. Gone are the memories of the super narrow scary bridge where a breakdown (or even slow truck) could ruin a whole trip. 

I do still need to get accustomed to the on and off ramps since I was so familiar with the old ways but small price to pay to sail across.

This shop was actually not part of my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom because she was not interested in hitting clothing stores. BUT I had stopped in the day before Thanksgiving with friends and got distracted and somehow left the store with the wrong dress.  

I ran in while my Mom was in a different shop (that I had also been to 2 days before) and we switched out super easy and very gracious since the shop technically wasn't open yet.  I was even invited back for champagne in an hour. Alas, we had moved further along.

Bonus Toulouse (the bulldog) was not at the shop on Wednesday but on Friday he glued his nose to my pants to get a full whiff of my girl at home.  He made me feel extra welcome.

This is one of these events that I can believe I haven't reviewed.  

I am NOT a bar professional but do love a good drink, especially when it's free! The tasting rooms are amazing and introduce you to a world of liquor or liqueur that I never knew existed.  I've taken vacation days the last two years to attend the weekday events.  

There are also book signings, a gift shop, lectures, and a whole lotta schmoozing.

I still think my all time favorite tasting room was the Old New Orleans Rum mojito bar at 10 one morning.  There was fruit so that counts as breakfast, right?

Many can go wrong with technology that sum the restaurant problem. 

Like - I like restaurant has opening look. Good wall art. Nice party look of the bar area. Seem like everyone have a good time. 

Bad - Service less restaurant. The order is made at the counter. An electronic buzzer is issued to let you know your food is ready. Then you pick up the food your self. Yes it save a lot of money to hire service people. Is you food cheaper? No. 

I have order to go and issue a buzzer. When I pick up the food, there is brown bag of your food is ready. I ask is this buzzer 18. The service people in the kitchen said yes. I took it home and they are not my order. Do I drive back round trip 18 miles for exchange. Probably not. I eat what is in the bag. And it is bean with ground beef burrito. The bean and ground beef below average. It is bad that I not even want to post the picture of the food. With food order wrong, now they have two not happy customers. Customer that have the wrong order and customer did not have the food. 

Below can be improved. Put some service waitress. 1. Do not have the customers to pick up the food themselves at the counter. I cannot tell how many other customers has touch my food. This is not professional. Please hand the right order to the right person. 2. Put identification on the brown bag since each order look alike. Identify the right order staple with order ticket. 3. Train the kitchen people with proper order is make.  

Too confusing. Burrito is below average

I was going to try their wing after workout. I came in the restaurant with my sweat shirt and sock with sandals. I was greeted by one of the employees and he will be get back with me. I saw the menu and decided a to go order. A few minutes later one waiter pass me by and said some one will help me. There were three waiter  and waitress pass by me and none of them can help on the take out order. I was there for 8 minutes seem like my money is not good to order. I really hungry and want to go home. Seem like they are not willing to take order I am not willing too. So turn around walk out the door without order. This will be my third one star review out of my over 800 reviews. If you charge your customers $1.50 per wing, the service should be measure up. I end up at wing express with $0.80 a wing and I am happy with it and walk out with the wings I want at 8 minutes.

The wait for the shuttle getting longer since I have use them for past 8 years. One thing that they have been doing is taking the nearby hotel passenger from airport and prolong the the drop off time to the parking lot since they have drop them off first. I am disappointed with their current business model.

I have make a comment to their employee. And they not willing to admit the customer is right for the delay pick up and drop off. They are getting the shouting match with you. Their attitude from my last parking has turn me away. I am recommending other parking area.

If the pickup include the nearby hotel guest fill up the van, you have to wait for second van. Longer the wait time where they did not tell you.

It has been a while I actually give 1 star on the review. This is my first time here and we don't have good impression but bad experience. 

We have coupon that allow us to buy one master Peanutty Swirl and get one free. We like to experience the 1960 roller skate window serving like the movie. The experience turn out not worthy for the food.

We arrive at Sonic and park on the station of order. The button has been push to call for order but no one has response. I have my engine on and they only have one car on drive thought and one car on station. I can see a lot of the sonic people in the building but none has come out to take order. We turn off the engine and waited for a while. Florida summer is hot even with the window down. We decided use the drive through. The drive through is responded faster than the station parking. We put our order with buy one gets one free. The total come to $8.98 and the discount is $3.59. We told them the incorrect total and ask why the discount is not half. The coupon clearly state BOGO buy one get one free but they only give you 40% discount. The swirl was given to us but spoon was not given to us while we were disagreed with the final total. 

Manager came out and said this is the price. I told my wife it is not worth to argue since the gas spend on waiting for the price correction is already paid for it. Spoon was finally given to us and we drove away. 

If you look at the food they are like ordinary fast food. Mc Donald has enclosed AC space and why I have to wait in hot weather and eat in my car or spent the gas money to be cool and eat in the car. Doesn't make sense. The concept may be work on 60's but not with AC generation. 

Overall coupon is not fully honor, not an AC dining, server stay in building cool themselves and ask the customer to wait, food is not the best or healthy in fast food, bad attitude server, wrong accounting, poor management. I am sadly given the one star.

Super 8 motel now carry the name of Wyndham chain. I would recommend to avoid this hotel. I have not many one star review. This hotel definitely deserves one. 

1. The hotel has long over due renovation. The item they have is old. Furniture is old, carpet is old, edging and corner of the room has many hole. 

2. The room floor and hallway are not clean. You see diet everywhere. I wonder how this house keeping do their job. 

3. Bug can be found in the room. One of the bug crawl to the iPad we are reading and suddenly appear in front of the screen. My leg has bed bug bite. 

4. The ice machine is old. Not sure it clean probably. 

5. The room do not carry a hair dryer. Even call at the front desk and they simply said they don't provide it. This is the most serious of all. If you have lady partner travel with you in the winter time. The hair is not dry with catch serious cold next day. 

6. Breakfast is very lack off and very little. Not sure how the run the hotel. 

With that said. I would said extremely highly not recommend this hotel. The owner need to seriously consider how the manage and maintain this hotel.

This restaurant is evaluating for their food not their local brew beer. The two star was given due to after food experience. After dine their food I have to go to restroom several time. It take me a day to clear my stomach pain. Some of the food is not up to the quality. 

The restaurant do have a lot of customers. Seem like a good joint. Especially the private local brew beer. It has the brewery just next to it with tour. I did not try it. I am straight to the restaurant. 

I got the blackened rock shrimp and the Belgium Blonde. I like the Belgium blonde beer. The rock shrimp dish include the spinach fettuccine, mushroom, andouille sausage, yellow bell pepper. The sauce is creamy. The rock shrimp is firm. Not sure which item did not measured up cause stomach diarrhea. May be the sauce. Anyhow my experience is not good with the food.

I walk in this place try to compare with the one in Brandon. Surprisingly they were not busy at Friday night. I remember the Brandon location take about 4 months to slow down from crazy line to normal busy line. This place is not very busy at all as they told me on the phone when I call to check. The dog house is still there if you want to have the picture. 

We have coupon for a free fried. I have order the half slab baby back a la carts and fried halibut. The baby back is below average. The temperature is warm and is not right. It is dinner standard compare to many wood grilled place. The halibut is definitely disappointed. The fast food fish sandwich place can do better on the crispy coating than this place. The accompanying lettuce is soggy. All food temperature is not good other the fried is right.  The food delivery is way behind schedule. Too slow at a slow day. 

Am I going to return. No, done from my check list. Not even the coupon can bring me back.

We excited for new kid in the block due to our past experience with fresh kitchen on other location. Finally there is one just close to the mall. It make the location easy before I go to the movie to fill my energy. Parking in the front is limited but there are plenty of parking space at the back. 

I like the theme with pink color. Pink color stand for sweet, nice, playful, cute, romantic, charming, feminine, and tenderness. This may be why they found their food. I got the six. Which mean 2 protein, 2 bases, 2 veggies. That is the biggest bowl you can get. After that just add addition. I have Ahi tuna poke, Herb grilled steak, green bean, roasted mushrooms, coconut ginger rice, sweet potatoes noodle. I have add on as pesto tomato. You think by now you have big bowl. That was not. It was not even full to the top. 

After two hours, I have to run to restroom several time. The food didn't seat well. It is just not fresh. Because this incident,  I think it will be 2 stars. In compare to other Fresh Kitchen, this location need some work.

This time of year supposedly very nice out. However, this year weather is cook up in the high temperatures side. This is a special event to welcome the new year ahead of us. The name is midnight in the garden, it is funny we are actually at the top of parking garage. Nice name to attract. We can said finally see the beautiful people of Tampa who dress up. I would said it is the top 80% beautiful people who attend this party. You know who is included :) 

It does have the stunning skyline for the Tampa. A good view to fireworks. You can see two fireworks in the horizon. I would said the fireworks is at least half mile from the city river walk fireworks and 1.5 mile from channelside. The night include all you can drink bar and party live music. The music selection is upbeat and current. This is the positive. My friend warn me about the bathroom and drink line. This year they improve it. 

However, the party is a bit over price for the face value. The reasons follow. 1. The drink is not the your typical mix drink place with great mixologist. 2. The drink do not have a good choice. Even for beer and wine. 3. The fire work is actually still far away. 4. No food!!!! 5. Security is lack off. No check on the purse. 

I do have the good times with some of the yelper.

I was exiting to try a Puertorican Bistro. This place is small and not much of parking space. But there is a empty lot behind the building that you can park there. The plaza parking on the side of building is limited. 

The restaurant has vibrant music. The music are nice and Latin flavor. I am not sure how it work so I walk to counter order and wait for my food. I have order the roasted penil. A Puerto Rico roast pork shoulder. I waited for my food for some time and the people who order the food after me already got their food. At least three tables. Finally some come to table ask me what I have ordered. They when back to the kitchen and comeback to me said they sold all the penil and they can offer me the beef stew combination. I got that. 

Seem like the beef stew is over cook and when you press the meat it shatters to powder. They not the same as fresh cook beef cube. 

Four mistakes on this restaurant. First mistake did not have a hostess and call themselves Bistro. Second inform the customers late about run out of food. Three, no make up or complimentary item for their mistakes. Fourth is offer a dish that is not popular. Seem like the item cannot sale on the night. This is done and done restaurant.

Tree house is very hip. But it do not have my vote. There are several reasons that they are two stars in my book. First, service is too slow. We have to wait for long time to be serve, get a drink and pay out. Second, the hostess has table but have us wait for 20 minutes for seat. They seat people who come later a lot faster after we are seated. Third, food is not rememberable or not at it best. 

We order the chicken waffle and fried chicken. This two item is not impressed. Seem the food is warm which mean it has been seat on the counter sometimes. The waffle is just ok. The fried chicken just average. I am guessing they do well is many young people like it. Seem like Sunday brunch is good goR them. But for me this is been there done that deal.

We have a very off night from this place. We have a group of four went to this place for the ramen. We hope to try some of the new and hot place in town. However, we do not have the good experience tonight. 

We came to this place after the museum night at downtown. We arrive at 7:20 and one of friend family just finish and they let us have the table. Thanks to him that we have no waiting on the table. We put our order in for the food and we order the sake. The sake is a good deal. We have finished our sake and the appetizer has not arrived. It took them 1.25 hour to bring out the appetizer. Before the app is out, I told my friend we should walk out if the food did not come in one hour. However, we are eager to try this restaurant food and we stay and wait for the excitement of the food. 

We waited close to 1.5 hour before our ramen came. We were wonder why it take so long. The food came and I immediately disappointed what we have longing for. The ramen is sticking together and the noodle is not separated. The meat may be cook extreme long time and the meat is easily broken into powder pieces. The soup is considering average on the miso base. I have better ramen in Tampa compare to this place. I not even need to compare to the standard in Japan that I have experience. 

I had ramen in clear broth base, miso base, spicy base, and dry base before. The meat of other place is moist and good for the pork. The good ramen place has marinated egg in half broil. When you break the egg yolk, the yolk will spill into the broth and create another sensation. This place the yolk is complete cooked. 

The output of this restaurant needs to be rethinking. In Japan, I have seen 50 bowls of ramen in 30 minutes but not in this place. I know this is art but also need to consider the wait of the customer. Lack of efficiency, technique, material. I am award 2 stars. Many rooms need improvement.

This location is not comparable with the largo location. Every time I call, they don't have the blue crab. Somehow they need to remove from the menu. Although they don't have blue crab, I decided to paid them a visit to try other items in the menu. 

I order a 15 fried shrimp and scallops special. The 15 shrimp is about $10 and the scallops is $5. The wait is the main problem for this store. I was informed about 15 minutes to 20 minutes wait. It end up the wait is 35 minutes. The size of the shrimp is tiny. 

The taste is not nearly good. It is about same as frozen quality from supermarket. $16 total is in the high side for take out standard. A lot of improvement can be made for this store.

I don't know I come to wrong time or the clerk do not take the order seriously. The coffee we got on the 16 OZ cup with half coffee fill and the rest is whip cream. That tell you what is missing out. This is about 2.5 stars coffee joint. 

This store basically is below of the apartment. Many USF students live here. The store front is visible from 42nd street. But there is no parking spot. Basically this is Neighborhood store only for the people who live there. The people who is there have their own drinks. This tell me something wrong for the customers mind set. 

There many things wrong here. To correct it is difficult. Now with not attractive coffee quantity and expensive cup of joe. I would said very hard to compete at all.

I went to the movie with a group of yelp friend to see the girl scream movie. Our arriving was on time. It did not give us more time to look at the popcorn or drink. Only enough time for rest room before the show. The restroom is clean and nice.

The theater facility is just average. The most important thing for the movie goers is the chair.  The chair that we got cannot recline or push forward. This is very uncomfortable for two hours movie. Furthermore, the chair seat cushion cannot be up right to allow people stand up and let the other people pass in front of you. Basically either you have to squeeze between the knees of the person who are seated and pass them through the other side or take a long walk down to the front row to get to other side. The design is not great. The sound system is not the great. My home theater surround sound system is better than this. People come to theater instead of home is to enjoy the sound system, comfortable seat and thirdly the junk food.  

The theater have enough dim light for safety,  light walk way light, overhead dim light, clear mark exit light. It is save. However I prefer more exit such as exit near the screen. Our auditorium does not have that. With the above reason, I have experience better.

The update review is due to the recent visit. This time I bring a friend with me. Due my good experience on the last visit, I like to repeat it again. This time we ordered the appetizer. The food come out quick. 

We got the Lemon Chili Tuna Tar Tar. I like the decorations and presentation. This dish included the tuna tartare with 4 additional accompanying to share. It has kimchi cucumber, papaya relish, toast coconut, radish. It come with 4 strip of crackers. Before I start, I can smell very fishy on the tuna. We didn't suspect anything. It was a mistake that we eat it without question. We all have food poisoning that day. 

I think they need to check the quality and freshness of the ingredients. It was a bad experience.

This review is getting below their service and and miscommunication to any club play. We were show up and surprised to inform us the badminton court can be kick out if the rain come to outside pickle ball tournaments. We have to make room for their competition if it rain. This decision make because it may rain and the badminton club will be sacrificed to make room. 

They could have informed us not to come. Poor management on the center not to inform us ahead. Some of us travel 45 minutes to get here. Which is a waste. I don't like the ideal they can kick us out anytime. I rather inform us the center is use that day and cancel us instead of give us the unreasonable explanation.

This may be the low end H&M I have been to. I have been to so many of them but this one do not stand out. One positive note is they have cute baby section. The man and women section just simply not there. 

This store occupies good amount area in the mall. It does carry men, women and children. The best is the children. There were number of discounts you can find start from $3, $5, $10, and $15. The store is clean and in order.

This fast food chain is as it advertise star rating. Below average. I believe they don't know how to improve themselves. 

Below are the suggest improvement. 

1. Improve the response time to order at the drive through. The wait is too long for the drive through. 

2. Improve the drive in condition. Be ready to come out to make the order. 

3. The boneless wing is chicken breast. Don't like too much batter.

4. Improve staff training. If the customer pull to the window to paid, be ready to accept. 

I not sure they will be able to improve since this issue has been long time base on past review from other yelper who comments on this store.

The facilities of the gym offer multi phase of exercise. You can work out yourself in the gym with the equipment, team sport, aerobic class, personal trainer. They also have swimming pool, sauna, locker room. 

Not long ago they bought the life style gym and shut down the smaller life style gym. The member of the smaller gym now crowed to this location. Many of the good aerobic teacher left life style and the LA fitness organization, and only the mediocre teacher left. May be LA Fitness do not pay as well to the good gym teacher and they go to other gym. The crowed situation present a shortage of equipment. The class with 7.5 pound dun bar is run out the in the exercise class. Some of the member have to bring their own. I wonder why we paid so much and we have to bring our own exercise equipment. The swimming pool also get crowed. We have an experience that after they sale you the three year membership, they are changing their way of doing business to the bad side. 

The morning class become too crowed which don't have not enough room to reach out your hand during the aerobic class. The big gym sometime has the AC shut off to save the facilities electric bill and cause the member suffer without air while exercising. The management need to listen to the client suggestion to improve the situation. What ever the sale group promise you doesn't work since their operation side decide how the gym run. You have to know their operation group is different than the sales group. You can complaint to the sale group but the operation group won't change the way of business operated. And their answer is corporate policy. This two group within the LA fitness need to be clean up how they really want to run the business.

I am disappointed to their current operation after 4.5 year with them. As a result a two star is awarded.

Drop two star. Simply just not up to the game. This time just not measured up from many front. The waitress who serve us take 7 minutes still did not pass the bowl for us to fill up the food. Not even come to our table to get order. We have to tell the secondary server to get us a bowl to start. We are veterans not required explanation. Not need to wait to pass us a bowl. 

When we get to the food cart to fill the bowl to be cook, some ingredients are empty. The ingredients is just not as good as before. The squid must be in the freezer for long time. It is dry after cook. They use to have the bay scallops and it was removed from the ingredients. 

The sauce table is just too massy. The sauce just drip all over the place. No one come to check or clean. During or dinner there, never see a floor manager come to check. Many hang out at the bar area and left the waitress to handle 5 tables in one time. 

After dinner, the food did not sit well in stomach. What can I said. A lot let down in many front.

Today the YBOR City have the 3rd annual snow parrade. We decided for dinner before the parade. 

This restaurant is kind of away from the center attraction of the YBOR. It located at the 5th Ave and 17th Street. Two Avenue from central YBOR. 

This is Argentina restaurant. They must have done their churrasco correctly. I have order a  baby churrasco and my wife have Mar Y Tierra (surf and turf). While we waiting for the food, we can see across building with the kitchen that pounding the steak. 

Mar Y Tierra came with three grill shrimp, grill skirt steak low grade with a lot of tender. It also  has side rice and side salad. The shrimp is marinated and grill with perfection. The skirt steak also marinate and grill. This dish is yummy for the shrimp and the steak is tasty. No complain for the price of this dish $18. 

The baby churrasco is 8 oz compare to the full churrasco 22oz. The price different is $10. Since I just want to taste the strip cut of the churrasco, I order a baby. When the steak came out, it is a whole piece like my wife dish not like the strip size cut. This is incorrect. It have a lot tendon. I did not say anything because I think this may be the way they have prepare it. So I have finish it. Then my neighbor table order the full portion and I can see there is different of the meat - strip size churrasco not like the flat piece. The correct churrasco should a strip cut no tendon. They should not use the word "churrasco" if they not serve you the Falda cut in Spanish. I am agree the seasoning for the taste is there but the meat material quality is not there. Argentine should know their meat. 

The other thing is the waiter did not ask me how is my steak to be prepared and they came out well done. It was too late to change. The waiter also not attentive. My glass of the water was empty for long time and not come to refill. This restaurant waiter need to be trained. 

With the above experience, I have to give them 2 star.

We have big group of 12 for the office outing lunch. I would said for the number of people we have, the service is not the best but good enough. Only one of our members get the food late. The close out may need to work on it. Tip was added since we have large group which may my bill easy. 

I have order the lamb kebab (Shish Kebab) plate. It come with two choices of side. I got the rice and the babaghanoush. The rice was well cook and nice aroma. The babaghanoush was well prepared and great with extra olive oil. The presentation of the dish is pleasant. However, the meat did not measured up. It was too dry and the marinated is not over the top. They need to improve on this area. 

I have been here several time. My previous experience is better. During the month of Ramadan, they serve the buffet that are plenty of choices and attractive. I would said try them during this time. The buffet of Ramadan usually start at 8:30. Go early because is a lot of customers.

My wife's pick this place since we have a coupon to use. Like RJP said "blame it to the wife". Love to do it when you can get away reasonable doubt by saying wife pick the place. A lot eye candy in the restaurant with my wife. Strange.  

My wife was at the restaurant first and she order ahead. I follow to the restaurant in 10 minutes. She order the lunch special with Chinese stir fry. Chinese food in winghouse? May be not. Her food came out like frozen section ready to cook meal from the Publix. I would not go for their Monday special. 

They have two selection of fish sandwich in the menu. Grouper cousin or Mahi Mahi. Grouper cousin is one type of white fish. I definitely go for the real name fish- the Mahi Mahi. It can be grilled, blackened or deep fried. I have it grilled. The blacken Mahi Mahi is not the spicy type I like but it do have a good taste. This sandwich is better than their daily special. 

The service is average. However, I think they need to be faster for lunch. Most people only have one hour.

This is my second time here. They are open at the Christmas Day night. Not too busy compared to many other restaurant open at that day. The interior of this place is beautifully set up. I like their decorations. 

We were sit immediately on second small room. Including us is about three tables of customers. We have ordered Black pepper basil crispy duck and Spicy noodle with squid. Food delivery is on time. The black pepper basil squid is average. The spicy noodle seem like not cook in high heat because I cannot taste the burn oil. Both dish is actually made for American Thai flavor. The local may like it but I am looking for good Thai which is average. 

The service is not measured up. We were not able to get attention of our waitress. But the other two tables was able grab her attention. Some how we got ignored. The three stars for the food and the service we have experience.

Fancy fast food chain. A lot of choice for the sandwiches. Today I have the shave prime rib basket with upgrade to onion ring ($1 more) and my wife have the Atlantic cod basket with upgrade to shake ($2 more).

They give you a number and the food was brought to the table. This is plus that you don,t need to wait for your order at the counter. The food came in 5 minutes. 

The shave prime rib is a bit salty. The onion ring and the cod came with a thick fried beard coating at the cover. To do the coating for deep fried have two method. The wet flour with material then fried or dry flour with material then fried. This restaurant chose the wet coating. As a result there is oil in the coating if you don't sit the food for a while and serve. 

The service is good. However, I am not a fan for the wet coating. I believe the restaurant can improve on this front.  I not against the fry food but against the oily food due oil residue can be tasted at the onion ring coating.

The Seminole Hard Rock Casino of Tampa has a lot activity. It has the biggest hotel in the Bay Area. I am not much of the gambler but I come here often for their restaurant. 

The casino is not smoke free place. As a result, it is stink to walk at the casino floor. Your cloth also will be stink due to the trap cigarette smoke. Ventilation has to be improved to improve the quality of the air. 

If you feel lucky at night. Put some bating on slot or table games. Or you can test your skill of card games, poker or pi gau the Chinese domino. 

The bars is every where. Drink never be a problem in this place. There is live performance on the casino floor or restaurant. But compare to Vegas, they need to have big auditorium for show. I think this is the area they have lack off.

Extreme Taco bring the taste to the Water Ave Sulphur Springs area. I saw many good comments from my Yelp friend. And my wife brought back a taco for me to try at home. I decided to try at the store. 

Parking at this area is challenging. Very limited or you can park at K-mart at walk across. There is a lot people even it is 4 pm of the day. The owner is very personalized and provides good service. 

I have order the steak, pastor and grouper tacos. I like my Taco naked to see the true taste. When you order extreme, it cover by other ingredients. The grouper and the steak is average for my experience. But the pastor is tasty and well seasoning. 

Overall their price is at the high side. Naked taco is about $2.79 each. The extreme taco is $3.79. For this price I usually treat them at restaurants level. Which they are not. Overall they are good.

Desi located at telecom park. Which they can get a lot Hindu customers who work on IT at this commercial park. They located at the end unit of the plaza which allows them to have some outdoor seating. During the weekday, they serve Tali plate. Weekend they serve buffet for lunch. 

The buffet have a lot meat selection. I like the mutton curry. Among the meat curry, I also like their chili chicken and the chicken curry. Tandoori chicken is also good there.
