It was a nice size Cod Fillet, batter dipped in a light English style coating, and fried enough to slightly harden the batter into a shell that left the fish soft and tender.  No oily taste nor texture.  The French Fries were not house made, but still crispy and fresh tasting. It came with Tartar Sauce or Cocktail Sauce.  I did not ask for Malt Vinegar, but I suspect it was back in the kitchen.  A tin of Old Bay was also placed on the table for the fries. A side of Cole Slaw came along for the ride. It was mayo based, but also fresh and enjoyable.  All the while Tracy was refilling my coffee mug, and telling me more about the restaurant. The only thing missing was having the Fish and Chips served in a newspaper cone as done in England. 

I don't normally do dessert, but Tracy asked if I wanted to hear what was available.  Ok. I was game to listen. She said a few options, and then got to the Fried Oreos and Fried Twinkies. What?!  I went for it. 

A few minutes later out came a large white shallow bowl with four halves of Twinkies, apparently wrapped in a crepe-like blanket, covered in powdered sugar, and drizzled with raspberry sauce.  The Twinkie Cream was slightly oozing out and mixing with the white and red.  

How did it taste?  Well, imagine the first time you ate a Twinkie as a kid; that soft, sweet, creamy surprise...Now, imagine it hot, with extra sugar, and a hint of raspberry stirring your palate... Taste it? 

It was a fun dessert.  

Kriscroix Restaurant. Highly Recommended for fish and fun.

Slate Bleu (Blue Slate) Restaurant is part of a very attractive adaptive reuse of an old brick 19th Century building in Doylestown.  For that alone, the structure is worth a close look. The architect gets 5 Stars for adaptation and execution. 

The restaurant is Au Provence French style look and feel.  Dark wood tones, center floor bar, and a quiet sensibility with white tablecloths, benches along the walls, and simple chairs.  The bartender (owner?) serves as hostess and maître d., serving drinks to the tables after she makes them. A nice touch.  Our waitress was friendly, knowledgeable and unobtrusive. 

The dinner menu is not extensive, but covers all the food groups.  The chef is creative and makes the effort to bring his best to his work.  We had the Green Salad, Bronzino with a Fruit Salsa Sauce, and for dessert shared a Pistachio Souffle.

 The salad was basically a fresh spring mix, but with a dressing that tasted weak in combination with the greens.  The Bronzino (Mediterranean Sea Bass) was very well presented, light tasting with a tasty Mexican-esque fruit salsa combination piled high on the fillet. It was very enjoyable. It was a daily special @ $28 per. Finally, the Souffle was made from scratch and came with a gravy boat full of hot chocolate for pouring into its center.  While very light, fluffy and yummy, the $15. plus price was a chill to the digestion. (I knew in advance and decided to bite the silver bullet in favor of making my companion happy. You know how that is.) 

So, although Slate Bleu is an attractively appointed French/Country space, and the cuisine is very good for the most part, there is a sticker shock that accompanies the experience.  While I would return, it will only be when I have a very special occasion. When a dinner for two comes in over the century mark without drinks, reservations about reservations are appropriate.

This is an excellent and honest auto repair shop. 
Too bad Yelp thinks it is in Clifton Heights, when it is in fact in Newtown, Bucks County.
Check the website to get the right information.
Once you do, you will find a place you can absolutely trust with your car. 
Five stars is not far off.

"I saw a werewolf with a Chinese menu in his hand,
Walking through the streets of SoHo in the rain.
He was looking for a place called Lee How Fook's. 
Gonna get a big dish of beef chow mein.

Aaooooooo
Werewolves of London. 
Aaooooooo.

Aaooooooo.
Werewolves of London.
Aaooooooo."

The historic truth is that the werewolf wasn't from SoHo, London, but Chinatown, Philadelphia.  Poetic license for a largely underappreciated songwriter and rock performer, Warren Zevon. He spent a lot of time in the city, especially in the early 1980s, when he was living with, and ultimately married to a well know radio DJ here. They lived on Rittenhouse Square for several years, before divorce drove him back to California.  If you were very fortunate, you saw his concert at the TLA on South Street, and had your musical life changed.

 He really visited the small Cantonese restaurant on the corner of 11th and Spring Streets and used it for inspiration for the song, "Werewolves of London." Even the kitchen door in an alley off Spring Street, found its way into the lyrics, as the door you must not open unless you sought the fate of the, "Little old lady, got mutilated late last night..." It remains a scary place even today with decades of thick, black grease caked to the walls and pavement. Who knows what evil lurks in those sewer drains?! 

So, I was there the other day after a haircut across the street. I had been singing his songs as I drove to Philly, and wanted to pay homage to the man and have some good Cantonese food. 

The dining room was small, with no more than eight tables. It was well preserved in dark mahogany stained panels.  It was fairly clean and tidy for a joint in C.Town. We were the only customers on arrival, and took liberties to walk around a bit and take a few photos. Amazingly, not a thing memorializing Zevon. Maybe this third generation Asian kitchen doesn't know from American rock and roll. Warren would no doubt get a laugh out of that. 

We ordered Salt Baked Squid, Orange Beef and Fish Hot Pot; more than enough for two of us, but plenty to bring home for the sons. They were all very good, if not best of breed. The squid was tender and mildly salty as expected.  The beef was plentiful with a good dark red amber sauce and sliced onion and green pepper. The fish arrived in a covered casserole still bubbling from the fire in the kitchen. Soft, moist and delicious. Each dish was $11.95. Credit cards accepted. 

This was one of the better Cantonese meals eaten in C.Town, made more desirable by the ability to think about Warren Zevon sitting at the table in back, chowing down and noodling about a song that we are still singing long after his death. 

Aaoooooooo!

It would seem that this supermarket is now part of the 1st Oriental Supermarket group that has a huge facility down at 6th and Washington in South Philly. Looks and feels the same. I think I also recognized some of the clerks and cashiers. 

Anywho, this store carries almost everything you needed for a well stocked Asian kitchen. From butcher to fishmonger, soy sauce and vinegar, noodles from around the world, and even those secret ingredients needed for great dumplings, are right at hand. Vietnam, Thailand, Korea, Cambodia and China are all well represented. The green grocer department has fruit and veggies that often can only be found where they are grown in Asia. They even had a box of super fat green frogs for exotic eating or taking home as pets. 

It was a pleasure to grab a grocery cart after a good dim sum brunch right next door and walk it off up and down the aisles.  The free parking replicates what they have down the city, but it sure makes life easier not to have to hunt and pay for a space for wheels.

Papillon Cafe in Goodnoe Corner, Newtown, PA, was a first for me. A French Kosher Organic Cafe in the heart of this 325 year old ville. It is a sign of the growing diversity in my home town, and it may actually make it, with something tasty for everyone. Even plenty for gluten frees.

This Sunday afternoon, only the owner was running the show. He had a perfect friendly personality, making me feel immediately welcome. His middle eastern accent with French lilt suggested the nature of the house. The shelf full of great looking pastries was one direction, the long list of crepes, another; and Paninis and onion soup, yet other possibilities. The weather frigid, I went for a hot tuna melt panini and coffee washdown. 

The plate was served by the Le Monsieur, sporting the split sandwich on crisp and crumbly pressed baguette, and a pile of thin sliced pan fried potatoes with a garlicky white sauce drip. They were fine, if not inspired. Certainly, a solid contribution for lunch. The pomme frite were interesting - served cold. Rather than being the expected French fries, it became a very good cool potato salad side dish. Like it, even if unintended.

The java was also surprising. Although equipped for expresso drinks, all I wanted was something hot and strongly caffeinated. What I received was a corrugated paper cup that required no heat shielding cuff (clever). For the milk stir-in, I was handed the large stainless frothing pitcher full of cow juice, heated with the steam wand. I poured and stirred like a rookie barista. Great touch, and the Groundwork beans showed their strong roasted roots. Impressive.

I really liked Papillon, but it could use a little TLC. With only one person doing the entire operation, the details  got away from him. Someone bussing tables and sweeping up would eliminate crumbs on tables and floor and make the experience an unqualified pleasure.

3.5 STARS

Our very personable waitperson described Jones as serving, "American Comfort Food."  Even before seeing the menu my mind was wandering about what that would mean to my Chinese friends experiencing local cuisine for just about the first time.  For me, a brownie and a glass of milk is comfort food, but for anyone lacking a database of experience, they might have some fairly wild ideas.  

Turns out, they didn't have a clue and relied on me to order for them.  Okay. I was up for the challenge.  How about a good burger for the 19 year old, and a turkey club for his mother?  Handled.  I've been curious about the chicken & waffles craze, so when I saw it on the menu, I stopped reading.  

We were all satisfied with our lunches.  The burger was a big hit with the young guy.  He believes burgers are the height of American culture.  He could be right.  Turkey is not well known in China, but the combination with bacon, lettuce, spicy mayo and tomato seemed to captivate my friend.  I moved quickly to remove the long wooden picks used to hold each quarter together, as she was unaccustomed to this shiv and nearly poked her eye out.  

The fried chicken arrived as a breast/thigh combo with golden brown crispy coat.  It was good, but perhaps a little too salty.  The waffle was the better companion, done well on an iron and still steamy soft within with a hint of sweetness to counterbalance the NaCl on the bird.  As a lover of Southern Fried Chicken, I did not truly appreciate the passionate embrace of these two carb loads on one plate.  Call me old fashioned, but I will stick with waffles for breakfast and fried chicken for other meals; although I might be convinced to change my mind if someone poured pure maple syrup over both and allowed me this sticky indulgence. 

Jones is a very nice facility with high ceilings, which make the brown sandstone columns around the house quite attractive and draw eyes upward, giving the sense of a mountain lodge in Red Rock, Sedona.  

Made the saying of "Grace" seem totally appropriate.

Shing Kee is one of the few Chinese houses on Washington Avenue.  It serves of Hong Kong/ Cantonese style dishes that are fairly authentic, very tasty, and at good prices.  It came highly recommended by my friends who work in the area, and rightly so.

Service was above average in that promptness and smiles were part of the interaction with the servers.  My only nit was that there were two large HDTVs on the walls that were both tuned to the same channel that no one was watching, although the Eagles preseason game was available.  They just couldn't manage to change over to the game despite saying they would.  I just decided to finish quickly, and catch the game on the car radio.  

The dinner was good aside from that annoyance. Scallion Pancakes were two deep and as wide as a large dinner plate.  Not too greasy, and enough green onion flavor.  The Pork Cutlets were large, well fried and very tasty is a good Garlic Sauce.  There was some bone left, but it was easy to pick them up and work the meat off.  I appreciated that they were a large size and non-oily.  The ubiquitous Broccoli Florets were ho-hum. 

Shing Kee is a definite keeper, especially in light of the absence of many legit alternatives in the area.  It also is a good driving destination as they are in a shopping center with a decent parking lot.  While there, there are a couple of markets for grabbing your Asian ingredients for your adventures in Asian cooking.

This stretch of Bustleton Avenue in Northeast Philadelphia is lined with one strip mall after another, and it is hard to tell them apart. Each has a few restaurants in them, but unless you know what you are looking for you are likely to become numb from their sameness and just keep driving. Taj India could unfortunately suffer than ignominious fate, but luckily is located right next door to the new Georgian Breads, and a street before the new Super Wawa.  It is worth finding. 

This is a vegetarian house.  Their menu consists of six pages of mostly Kerala delights, with a little other North and South India thrown in to keep it interesting and popular. It was a perfect place to settle down after excellent foot massage right up the road at Lavendar Spa.  

We shared these dishes: Sweet Corn Soup, Chili Pakoda, Kaju Curry, Vegetable Jalfrezi and Garlic Naan.  All were good to near excellent, except for the Masala Tea which was tasteless and disappointing. I love most forms of corn soup, and this was fairly standard. Sweet kernels with a light dusting of curry. Not sure if it came from a fresh ear of corn or a can, but it was still good.  The Chili Pakora was a nice surprise - Jalapeno peppers stuffed with mashed potato and spices, dipped in a heavy pakora breading and deep fried.  Very spicy and a strong nod to Indo-Mex cuisine.  The Kaju (cashew) Curry was a cool play on nuttiness in a mild, almost sweet pale orange curry.  Terrific. Perfect for sopping up with the Garlic Naan, which was more lightly tandoored than most I have eaten.  The texture was not heavy with oil nor garlic, despite its strong taste.  Very well done. Finally, the Veggie Jalfrezi provided a mix of mostly standard local green is a pleasant moderately heated curry.  We went with Level 5 on all dishes, except the Chili, and found it adequate for our tastes.  Regardless, some were hotter than others, but quite satisfactory across the board.  

Service was friendly and efficient, and prices on the pleasant side of reasonable. $44 for all the above four dishes, naan and tea.

There are several decent Indian kitchens in this area, and Taj should be on your list when in the neighborhood and in the mood for quality vegetarian meals.

Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch. 
It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.  

This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.  

If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing. 

Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.

My office neighbor and I went to lunch at La Vecchia Osteria this afternoon, after postponing our plans a few times due to busy schedules.  So glad we finally made it!

We were greeted warmly by the owner, Pasquale, and served by his beautiful daughter. The side room was bright with the winter sun streaming in the windows and making the golden amber room glow.  The corner table offered a little privacy, but it was not crowded today.  Small Antipasto with a mix of prosciutto, salami, hard cheeses, buffalo mozz.,  black and green olives to begin.  Fresh, crusty bread with olio and herb dip.  Grilled
Branzino filleted after cooking, and just before bringing to the table.  Pure white tender with light extra virgin and lemon.  Perfect!  My friend had Chicken
Breast in olive oil and capers, with a side of Vodka Rigatoni.  We stopped our chat while we savored our repast.  

Conversation resumed with a slightly gazed countenance of satisfaction as we finished with coffee and sharing a homemade Cannoli that was so smooth, sweet, and creamy that we had to close our eyes to fully absorb the experience.  

Oh well, another dinnerless night.  But, it was so worth it!

If you are like me, and enjoy a small business success story served with whipped cream and strong coffee, the Old Croydon Café is just about as good as it gets.  

I stopped in for the first time this week and took a stool at the counter.  From my vantage point I could look into the kitchen service window and see the heads of the cooks making magic out of eggs and pancake mix.  The old joint is on the north end of State Road, which I soon discovered could be used as a detour from Rt. 95, all the way to Center City.  Good to know!

The place is small, with 7 or 8 stools and an equal number of booths and tables.  I sat next to a house painter, lawn mower repair man, and a roofer.  The conversation was cordial and full of gallant repartee.  The owners worked front and back and kept the dishes coming along with the warm banter.  I really liked OCC even before my French Toast Deluxe arrived.  This was as downhome as this part of Pennsylvania gets. 

When my breakfast arrived I beheld an oval plate framing a still life watercolor.  The 3 slices of well grilled and caramelized French Toast, topped with Fresh Whipped Cream and Blueberries, Strawberries, and Bananas, and finished with a lazy drizzle of Blueberry Sauce. (See Photo) The toast was hot, the cream cool, and the fruit cold and juicy.  The tastes and textures were fun and delicious.  It was one of those meals that I did not want to end.  

Old Croydon Café has definitely made my very short list of favorite breakfast nooks.  I will return to explore the menu, and even come back for lunch when possible.  

This place is a hidden treasure.

"Welcome to Nirvana," he said with a open faced smile that hinted that he had practiced this line many times as an owner of Nirvana Fusion.  He waited for his words to penetrate and for our reaction.  

Magically, we were transported to the Himalayas in Nepal, where we would dine this night.  You see, the "fusion" in Nirvana Fusion comes from the fact that the owners and chef of this mountain house are from Nepal, where they are at the cross currents of north Indian and southwest Chinese culture.  Fusion comes naturally when you grow up in it.  Both cuisines roll over each other, mix and retreat with each human tide; leaving behind something that is both informed by their neighbors, and creative of a new reality where turmeric and curry meet chili and dragon fruit.  The similarities are undeniable.  The uniqueness, extraordinary.  

The menu read differently than those of similarly named restaurants.  Extra time was needed to penetrate, and many questions had to be answered by our hosts.  We were curious.  They were patient.  We ultimately ordered the Chili Chicken (Dry) and Gobi Manchurian (Dry) appetizers, the Chicken Zafrani traditional Indian dish, and the Vegetable Hakka Noodles from the Indo/Chinese/Thai Fusion section, to try a cross section of their offerings.  

Both the apps were spicy hot and looked surprising similar in deep red amber sauces.  The Chili Chicken tasted of both Chili and Tumeric in the thick sauce coating the small morsels of chicken.  It was very good and left our mouths burning without reaching numbness.  The Gobi (deep fried cauliflower) in another dark sauce with pieces of clumped spices sticking to everything, was excellent in that the vegetable flavor and texture remained although bathed in the heavy float.  The cross fertilization of cultures was most evident here.  The Chicken Zafrani was more straight forward North Indian with a softer curry infused with the sweetness of Almonds, Cashews and Saffron.  There were also Kashmiri Chilies in there, but they did not dominate.  Finally, the Hakka Noodles really seemed more a straight up Chinese dish very akin to a chunky Lo Mein.  Very nice. 

Nirvana Fusion took me by surprise - a pleasant one.  It is definitely deserves returning for more adventures.  

We weren't in Hatboro anymore, Toto.

When all the other historic sites in Philadelphia were closed because of shut downs and furloughs coming from the nonsense in Washington, alone in staying proudly open was Carpenter's Hall, much as it has since its founding in 1770.  

An excellent example of Georgian style architecture, it was built by the first trade union in the United States, The Carpenters' Company.  It was here that the American Revolution really began with the First Continental Congress in 1774, when delegates from 12 colonies (nee Georgia), met to decide how to respond to the mounting British oppression.  They voted to boycott all English goods, and to meet again the following year should this not be enough to solve the problem.  The rest, as we all know, is our history.  

Ben Franklin opened his Library Company on the second floor.  The first and second National Bank of the United States used the first floor for several years before grander quarters were built nearby (and ultimately failed when challenged by Andrew Jackson years later). 

The building is set back from Chestnut Street, and approaching it gives a perspective of how it much have felt to do so in the 18th Century on cobblestone, horse manure, oil lamp streets.  It has a modest nobility for a structure so old and prominent in our nation's struggles for freedom.  Its larger grander cousin, Independence Hall, soon overtook it as the symbol of this fight and the center of courageous political discourse on the path to nationhood, but Carpenters' Hall continued to play a significant role as a meeting house for rebels and spies, the Philosophical Society, hospital, and Franklin's Library. 

In a time when the struggle to birth a nation was very real and daunting, and men had to seriously pledge their sacred honor and very lives to take a stand, it is a sad comparison to realize how far we have fallen as a country this very day. Those people knew the meaning of what they were doing, and went ahead bravely. 

 Where are those leaders today?  

Carpenters' Hall awaits their awakening and offers a reminder of what true patriotism means.

How to account for the two entries for this wonderful blue bridge on Yelp?  
From the Philadelphia side it is called the, "Benjamin Franklin Bridge."  The Jersey Strong side in Camden has named it the, "Ben Franklin Bridge."  Seems more reviews use Ben. 

I guess Jersey has a more casual relationship with this Founding Father.  But, we must ask if Benjamin would have anything to say about the 19th Century propriety of calling this prodigious and glorious old boy, "Ben," as opposed to his given name?  

I'll stick with Benjamin until he and I are formally introduced and get on a first name basis.

As a sister city gift from Tianjin, China to Philadelphia, the Friendship Gate was the first of its kind in the USA. Engineers and artisans from the old country designed and built it on 10th Street at the corner with Arch Street.  When freshly painted (as it last was in 2008), it is a beautiful reminder of the cultural ties between two grand cultures, one very old, and the other quite new.  It is an accurate representation of a Qing Dynasty city gate that would historically be placed in an opening in the wall surrounding a city, or an approach to a holy site.  There is also magic spread over the structure with the carvings, painting and Chinese proverbs placed on it.  So, with a little belief and a lot of imagination, you can feel the changing atmosphere when entering or exiting Chinatown through this portal.  That is part of the reason why being in Chinatown feels so far away from the rest of our urban world. 

Chinatown has suffered at the hands of last century's urban planners, as first one piece (Ben Franklin Bridge), and then another (Vine Street Expressway), and yet another (Philadelphia Convention Center) cut away at the neighborhood.  What was once a 12 block enclave, is now only 7.  Gentrification north of Vine will only make matters worse as the value of real estate skyrockets, forcing old owners out as taxes raise and rents follow. Luckily, the Phillies were not able to build their new ballpark where originally desired just off 12th and Vine. 

Although I usually approach Chinatown from the north (as the Mongols did), I try to make it a point to walk through Friendship Gate (driving under it does not provide the special spell).  Either before or after a great meal, haircut, or shopping adventure, a moment within its aura seems to lighten my load, and give a sense of connection with a 5,000 year old culture. 

Walk under it next time your in town.  Tell us how it felt.

I am normally not a fan of prix-fix menus, as they tend to be too limiting of choice, and suggests a kitchen unable to handle more options.  But, when that standard menu comes in 7 courses with additional vegetarian alternatives, and is packed into a Bedouin's tent of a restaurant, complete with belly dancing, baklava and honey tea, I can make an exception.  

This is multiplied many fold when your 40 closest friends are packed into a carpet clad room with barely enough room to sit down, and an ambient noise level loud enough to make talking to anyone but those right next to you impossible. Yet, with enough wine and North African music to alter consciousness, this becomes an all-consuming environment that transports you out of South Street and into the dark, mystic souk casbah of one of the ancient cities of Morocco. 

Marrakesh takes finger food to the ultimate.  From cool salads, to roast chicken, cumin lamb and grilled beef, cous-cous with veggies, the only thing between your fingers and the searing meal is the thin pita used to pinch, lift and stuff in your face.  Failing that, be prepared for first degree burns.  

The large metal serving trays kept coming with more food.  We all appreciated the concession to the use of towels to cover laps and wipe hands. Some of the braver souls accompanied our graceful dancer as she gyrated her hips, abdomen, shoulders and arms with cymbals ringing. Some of our folks really knew how to move.  Impressive.

Stepping back out onto Leithgow Alley after 4 hours within this transporter, it took a few moments to reorient myself to being back in Philadelphia after our wild ride.

Marrakesh is not just a restaurant, it is a magic carpet.

The other reviews capture the essence of State Street Kitchen.
The owner and creative force, Micha, is a work of art. This is HER place.  She knows everyone by first name, and genuinely makes you feel you are her best friend. You might be!
The food is fresh, and tasty.  There are standard menu items found in any comfy neighborhood cafe, plus specials that show imagination.  Yes. There is a Korean twist to many dishes, and most of them work well. 
The dining area is smallish, so come early or late or be prepared to wait.  You will find it worthwhile. 
There are many locals there every day.  If you are one of them, you don't need to read this.  For everyone else, don't be put off that we know most of the people in there. It happens because of the food quality and creativity, and the warm personality of the owner. 
Order something unique and off menu, and you might find it on the menu in the future and named after you.

It was good to be back in the old neighborhood again up along Baltimore Avenue in West Philly.  Things have changed around my old home at 48th and Balto, mostly for the better.  I was here a few months ago sampling the heat at Chili Szechuan, and this time I was back to meet up with Yelp friends at Mood Café, the Chaat & Lassi emporium on the point at 46th Street.  Lucky for me, they were delayed arriving, and I had an opportunity for a long talk with Hasan, the owner/chef/creative genius behind the concept and the counter that is Mood.  I got the $.50 tour, and an autobiography worthy of Horatio Alger. 

While I had eaten Chaat (pronounced, "Chart") before, it had never been like this.  Hasan has taken what is basically a common street food in India and turned it into an adventure in eating.  It comes at you in several dimensions - taste, texture, hardness/softness, shape, spice, food group, color and surprise.  It sat before me the most colorful assortment of edibles imaginable.  I had the Salad Chaat with Chicken, but there was so much happening inside that take out container that the meat was forgotten in the exploration of what was going on with all the reds, yellows, stars, logs, crispies, noodles, dried fruit, nuts, fresh mango, greens, feta cheese, chili sauces, curry notes, etc.  It is difficult to describe all the hyperactivity in that bowl.  Imagine an Indian version of Trail Mix thrown into a salad rather than croutons. If he had tossed in some M & M's I would not have been shocked.  This baby was Buh-Buh-Buh-Bizzzeee!!!

And, bottom line, it was awesome. We tried each others dishes, and all were unique and captivating. 

And, that does not even get into the Lassis.  More than 60 varieties of cool, creamy yogurty, sweetness.  Mine?  A Rose Lassi, complete with Rose Petals! Not just amazing, but fun!  If this wasn't enough, Hasan brought us samples of other Lassi combos in small cups to try.  This man knows how to seduce with great taste. Oh. And did I mention the Kheer and Rice Pudding he gave us at the end? 

Over the Top!

As good as Mood Café is, it is a very small shop.  Four tables with bench seats along the wall and plastic stools for everyone else.  So, not the most comfortable arrangement.  It is geared as a take out place, with everything served in take out containers and plastic utensils.  I would be willing to pay more for comfort.  

The sheer enjoyment of the event (yes, this was more than just a cool meal) kicks the experience into 5 Star territory.  In truth, there should be another category available on Yelp that addresses the euphoria and exclamations needed for certain special foodie moments.  

Mood Café would reach that level of extreme amazed unadulterated satisfaction. 

Yeowee!!!

The first thing I noticed in the shop was the great renovation done to this old wooden building on Newtown Creek.  The owner put love and attention into the atmosphere she wanted to create, as well as her business plan for all organic products, showing commitment to a successful business and a healthy planet. 
Did I mention she cuts my hair very well?  I know such salons are primarily for women, but men should feel comfortable taking a seat there.  They also do a great job on my 12 year old son who is very particular about the bushel of hair on his head.

If you grew up with Dairy Queen as your special summer sweet treat, then this classic free standing shop on the south end of Morrisville will bring you back in time.  It has the iconic architecture of those build in the 1940's and 50's, before DQ became of burger joint that sold soft serve ice cream.  

This is the place to bring the kids and grandparents on hot August nights, stand in line at the two small windows, peruse the now expansive menu, and walk away with your favorite vanilla or chocolate swirled cone, sundae, or Blizzard.  The look and taste is exactly as it was in the early days, and a wonderful trip down memory lane.  

Don't worry about the sketchy neighborhood.  Stay alert, but know that you are "under the dome," and security of your childhood reveries.

If you know Trenton, and particularly the Hamilton Avenue/Trenton Central High School area, you know it has a small commercial zone with a bunch of divey restaurants, only a few of which would you think to visit. The oldies but goodies (Eddie's Donuts, Chuck's Chicken Wings, that great cheesecake place), are either long gone, or hanging on with other outlets out in the burbs. 

But, along comes Halal Brothers, with its bright red, white and black logo, sparkling clean shop, friendly, accommodating ownership and outstanding Afghani menu, and all those preconceptions are thrown out the window. This place is inviting and its food is top notch delicious. I was there for lunch recently and almost fell in love.

At the counter I admitted to my first time there, and was offered a sample of their chicken and lemon chicken over rice. A minute later I was handed a small bowl of the two finished with white sauce and a touch of chili sauce. Diminutive, it was still beautifully presented and terrific. I sat down to eat it and tasted the panoply of flavors dancing on my tongue. Both the straight chicken and the lemony version were tender, moist and a mouth full of interesting exotic belly dancing.

From there I decided on their chicken salad - the same regular chicken morsels with a load of salad (lettuce, tomato, onion, cheese, white sauce and spicy red hot sauce) in a bowl. With a bottled drink, $7. Quite a deal! And, it was as great as the sample. With check in on Yelp, a free triangle of baklava joined the party. Mine had a cream filling, rather than the better known honey nut stuffing. It was also very good, like a Bavarian Cream donut made with philo rather than cake dough. 

All I can say is that such surprises deserve return visits and five star reviews.

Definitely one of the best burger joints in Philadelphia, especially if price plays into your taste appreciation. What used to be a food truck operation has now taken root on West Girard Avenue (2800 Block). Although, small in stature, their burgers, cheesesteaks and roast pork sandwiches are worthy of being called, "Philly Prime." At less that $10 per, they offer a strong value compared to some of the expensive burger houses. 

My Ponderosa Burger with grilled onions & mushrooms, Swiss, and fries inside the potato bun, topped with a drizzle of their secret steak sauce, was both a sight and delight.  Although slightly beyond my requested Medium finish, it remained juicy with a great taste profile from the added ingredients. The first bite told the tale.  It exploded in my mouth with so much forceful flavor, that some of it squirted out from my loosely closed lips. Glad I had grabbed enough napkins at the counter to deal with it. 

My lovely companion sampled the Manayunk Roast Pork Sammy (pork loin topped with American, coleslaw, pickle and BBQ sauce).  She could barely finish half!  Too, their fries were copious, crisp and freshly cut. 

Service, friendly and engaging. Order and pickup at the counter. 

Excellence all around.

Ariana's store front dining room may be long and narrow, but there is still plenty of room for a small intimate party with 40 friends, belly dancing, and all around carousing with interesting cuisine and effective service. 

As with many such get togethers, the food takes a backseat to the festivities, but it refuses to be completely overlooked.  Our limited Prix fixe menu was part of the standard faire and was quite good across the board.  We all shared Aashak (dumplings) and Sambosa (Samosa), which while distinctly unique from what I was familiar with from a Chinese and Indian kitchen, were still quite good. Too, my Badendan Chalow (Chicken & Eggplant Curry) was tasty and the sauce worthy of all the excellent rice used to absorb every drop.  

The entertainment was top notch and most of us got up to attempt to move our body parts in unison with our exotic dancer.  Impossible, but oh, so much fun. 

I would def return to explore the menu of this house down at the bottom of Chestnut Street.

I confess to being a first generation Eagles fan, as I've lived in the Philadelphia area for only 30 years. That makes me a newbie. Still, it is long enough to understand the long, disillusioned wait become elated jubilation that folks who live and die Eagles football feel now that we have climbed to the mountain top and see the world from this new and pristine, exhilarating perspective. Dare I say we see the world through the eyes of a soaring eagle? 

Hell, yeah!

We wander in the desert no longer. We have paid whatever penitence was due by our generations seeking the promised land. We have breached the palace walls and stand among the kings of football. The trials and tribulations, as painful and soul torturing as they were, have made us stronger.  We were the barbarians at the gate until Sunday night. Now, we are the new Eagles Empire, prepared to take our rightful place in the pantheon of football gods. 

Move over Willie Joe. Move over Johnny U. Stand aside Terry B. Step to your left, Joe M. Make room Bart S. There's a new QB in town, and Nick F. be his name. Tommy B. be damned! We got this now. You want it back? Come and try! 

We like the top of the mountain, and we are not about to give it back without a mighty battle. 

The Great Eagles Nation arise! It is our turn to bask in the sunshine of a new day, and fly ever higher on the winds of Championship.

Just visited Burns Auto Repair for the annual inspection and an oil change.  

In at 8:00.  Out at 9:15.  Dave Burns, himself, drove me to my destination, and called when the work was done. 

Still a complete 5 Star experience in automotive maintenance excellence. 

Glad Yelp finally accepted that this shop is in Newtown, Bucks County, Pa.

Russell Gardens Center in Churchville, Bucks County, Pa., may not be the largest nursery garden plantation in the region, but in my estimation it is one of the best. I have been shopping here since moving to Bucks and starting a garden around the house (The enterprise is never done).  Originally, I was tipped off to its existence by a nurseryman friend who helped me with design and bare root tree planting.  He swore by Russell's for perennials and colorful annuals and shrubs that most other dealers either lacked, or only possessed in inferior quality.

As an example, twenty years ago I bought a small pot of Coreopsis, a hardy fern-like leafy base with yellow star flowers that bloom in late June/early July, and spread to fill any space they are in.  Yesterday, I returned to see what was new in this native American beauty.  Now, they are available in a few shades of red/orange, and most strikingly, in a red/yellow flower that is breathtaking in its simplicity and kinship to its elder cousin.  Love at first sight. It is now planted across the walkway from the original, and it is easy to imagine its growth over the coming years.  

We purchased 3 other low growing, shade loving varieties to replace the old builder's grade junipers that had run their course.  Three Heuchera with rich dark maroon/gray foliage, two Veronica (Speedwell) that push up spikes of pale blue to indigo flowers in early June, and three low dark green/purple grasses that spread through their roots to cover bare soil and need little maintenance. They are all happily in place beneath the living room window. 

Always more work to do.  Plans call for a redo of the west side foundation plantings.  Russell Gardens will get the call as we lay out our plans.  Their inventory, knowledge and understanding of gardens and gardeners, makes it the place I trust most with suggestions and products. Prices are about the same as the other shops. 

Russell Gardens is why we dig in the earth.

Dave Burns and his crew are highly reputable and spend the time necessary to find what is wrong with your vehicle and make the needed repairs after discussing it with you.  They have the integrity to tell you up front if they think they can't do the work as well as the dealer. How often have you had that happen? Well, Dave apologized that he thought he should pass on a particular problem I was having with my car, and recommended I take it to a dealer for the specialized treatment required.  I truly appreciated his honesty and directness.

For that and everything else he has done for me, Burns Auto Repair is deserving of 5 stars.

I still wish Yelp would get his location right. Newtown, Bucks County; not Clifton Heights. 

Jeesh!

I have returned several times during the year for "a trim."  Both my son (now 13) and I enjoy the casual, yet well appointed atmosphere of Sycamore Salon.  It is nice to see more people working there, a sure sign of growing reputation and success.  

It is well deserved.  If you want your hair and scalp treated with care, kindness and only organic products, your best choice in Newtown remains Sycamore Salon - The Organic Option.

Stopped in to get myself my usual Carmel swirl latte... I was told that the Caramel was on recall. Funny, the next one down the road didn't have that issue. I dislike being lied to. REALLY dislike it. Consider that I won't stop at this particular location.

Ok, the ONLY reason I stopped at Burger King was to get a Diet Coke. 

First things first: A medium diet coke was $2.63??!!!  Holy cow.

Secondly: When I paid, I asked for a receipt. I don't know why, I just did. I'm glad I did. When I got to the expedition window the girl, Mariah handed me a COKE. I asked, "Diet"?  and the conversation went like this? "No, Coke, you didn't order Diet." I looked at my receipt, it said DIET.  I showed it to her. "What number is that?" "15" "Huh.. " she speaks indistinctly to the manager in the background.. "What else did you order." "Nothing, Just the medium diet coke, lite ice." She looks confused. Clearly they have both paper and monitor to look at the order, I' not sure where the issue is coming into play.. but there was an issue. 

FINALLY I'm handed a Medium Diet Coke, that I paid $2.63 for and GOOD God, it has lots of ice in it.. *eye roll* for the love of all things holy...

Do not stay here... ever. Not all RRI's are bad, but this one is disgusting.

If I could give less than 1 star, I would.  This place was a hell hole.  Let me begin by saying that when I checked in, the person behind the desk was OK. She was very nice.  The first room I checked into was absolutely DISGUSTING. The wet, heavy scent of mold permeated the air. There were stains on one of the bed covers. They weren't small stains either, they were the size of a dinner plates.  There was also a blood stain on one of the bed covers the size of a dime.  Yes, a blood stain. 

The bathroom was equally disgusting. The cover was off the fan unit on the wall, and the innards of the fan were exposed, everything covered in a thick layer of dust and who knows what.  Inside the bathtub there was a wad of hair and god knows what else.  I was skeeved.  This was intolerable, especially when they say that these are "All New Rooms". Clearly the NEW only means the paint on the walls. 

I went up to the front desk and let the clerk know of the situation at hand. She moved me towards another room. This room also smelled of mold, but not as badly. The beds were at least clean, but the big issue with this room was... ABSOLUTELY no towels. How did this happen? All I had was a single washcloth.  So once more I had to walk up front and speak to the clerk. I realize that it's not her fault, but she didn't have any towels to give me, save a small stack that had been sitting up front.  I ended up getting 2 towels and 3 floor mats. 

This was such a disastasterous experience that I ended up putting the chair before the door and hoping that I wouldn't end up dead, and this is where we ended up getting our final surprise: there were a pair of panties on the floor. They didn't belong to me or my room mate, so apparently they'd been left beneath the chair, along with the dog kibble.  Clearly, Housekeeping has failed to do their job here.   

I will not be staying at another Red Roof Inn again.

If you've been following me for -any- length of time, you know I love to shop. 

Man, this store was a deplorable experience. Granted, it's less than a week out from Christmas, but there is NO excuse for a store to be this disorganized, this picked over, and this utterly disgusting. The merchandise was scattered willy-nilly over different departments, the employees that I encountered, all three of them didn't appear to want to be there, and there appears to be a high rate of theft. 

In the accessory/jewelry/makeup & gift department department I found more open products, more missing items and more slippage (Aka THEFT of items) than I have ever seen in one location. 

The only good thing was that they had MY size bra in the lingerie department. They've been the only location to do so. 

I will -not- be coming back.

It really saddens me to write an update like this. I went in this evening because I've been having trouble with my phone ever since there was an Android update 2 days ago. Since it went into effect, my phone fights powering on. If it DOES power on, it doesn't stay on for long. Essentially it's become absolutely useless. 

I looked up on line how to do a hard re-boot, but the phone wouldn't get to the code screen. It was being obstinate and simply refused. It would come up to the actual usage screen, but then in a short matter of time.. go away once more.  It was frustrating to say the least.  In the past, I've been able to go to the stores and one of the people working there either knew of a fix or knew someone who could help me. NOT TONIGHT.

I walked in at 8pm, an hour before closing, and got Shae, a bespectacled, pinup banged young lady with a very blasè attitude. "How may I help you" she asked as we looked around.  So I came over to where she was.  As I settled into what was wrong, I explained the situation, that I -COULD NOT- get to the hard re-boot screen, and I needed help because of the issue with the recent update. She was NOT actively listening. 

She took the phone, turned it over in her hand, looked at it as if it were a piece of offal and then set it on the counter, she asked my name, asked for my phone number and ID to make sure that it cleared and then she scanned my account. "Well You don't have insurance on the phone." Ok.. what?  I've had insurance on the phones - all of them since I've been with T-mobile. I also had just been here recently to check on something and KNEW that I had insurance, so when I was told this, I took exception. "I pay for it." So she looked deeper. "You have it on XXXX, But not this number." Uh huh.. My husband came over to find out what she was saying. He got a touch heated, "So what your saying is that We don't have insurance on the phone, even though I know we pay for it?" She looked at him and said, "That's not what I said." (Actually it is just what you said.) And so she looked a little deeper and Guess what? We have insurance on ALL THREE LINES!  

"Well, your choice is you can Pay off the phone or you can invoke the insurance but your deductible is $175."  Wait, wait wait.. You're expecting me to pay off a phone that's busted due to NO FAULT Of my own, due to a softwear push?  "Well, there's nothing that I can do, I'm not allowed to take back phones that aren't in working order."  I didn't ask once to have the phone taken back. I had asked for HELP. To see if they could get the phone back to the hard reset screen.  This is when she told me what she "thought" she heard. Clearly the girl didn't care, didn't want to know how she could truly help. 

She simply wanted us out of there. She had the flat, monotone tone of boredom. We weren't buying anything and all we were doing was taking up her time now, and clearly, she'd screwed up, and she wasn't going to take any responsibility for it. There was no apology for the misinformation. No, "I'm sorry, I read that wrong." Only an "I'm just reading what I see on your profile." Really? I suggest a remedial reading course.   

So now, I have a conundrum: I have a phone, with a $400.00 balance. I can pay it off. I can invoke my insurance (Though I'm not sure why, since NOTHING I DID effected the phone) and get a new one. OR I can call the customer service in the morning  and talk with them to see what will happen. Since frankly, I'm a little underwhelmed by the level of non "Customer service" I've received.  Do I want to continue this 10 year+ relationship? In the past they've done right, but this one employee has put a dark coloration over my eyes. I know that this branch won't see much of me from now on. I don't trust the competency of their employees.

I came in to have my knee looked at. They weren't particularly busy,  but the doctor seemed to rush through his exam. He did a basic palpation of the area, asks me if I could bend it, but didn't really engage me at all, didn't ask me what I was doing to help relieve my own pain. He saw me for about 2 minutes. In that time, he speed talked, he asked if I had a primary care physician, and that I should really see her.   He said I should probably see an Ortheapeadist, and I should, but all he wanted to do was get me the hell out of there. 

I'm glad that I didn't have a huge co-pay on this visit or I'd be highly upset by the lack of care I received.  The last time I was here they at least took an Xray and checked to make sure nothing was wrong.  This guy didn't even compare the swelling to the other knee.  Like others before me, it seeems like this might just be a mill. Especially when it comes to prescribing RX's. I had to remind the Physician about my own drug interactions based on what I take and that he can not prescribe anything with ibuprofen. He seemed put off by that. Oh well, at least I know what I'm OK to have.  

WOULD NOT RETURN.

i remember when this place was the tops. 

But that was back in the early 1990's. Fast Forward to 2013 and boy how the mighty have fallen. It was a derelict relic of the past.  Some flea markets are fun to dig through, this one was nothing but a sad shadow of what it used to be. So many empty stalls, so much malaise, that it seemed as if the whole place were looking for someone to pull the plug.  The one thing I noticed was the "Dollar Tree" mentality. There would be these large swaths of booths, all grouped together - a store if you will, of cheap imported merchandise, and they were in every section of the market.   They were selling the same things - exactly the same things. NO variety in item or price. It was really rather pathetic.

11 pm, I drove though to get myself an Iced tea. Since I had heard their commercials about their new Mozerella sticks at 3 for $1 I decided to try those. I wish I hadn't.

What I got was... revolting. The sticks weren't fried. I think they were microwaved. They were not at all crispy. The cheese had probably been melted at one time, but not now. They were pretty nasty in truth. The breading was limp and tasteless.. other than garlic. That was heavy. The cheese was like glue. I wasted a buck. 

Their iced tea was old. I was a wasted trip.

Man, I hate giving poor reviews but when one is needed, I have to give one. 

So after going to the Casino, Mom and I headed home by an unusual route. She wanted an Iced tea, so we went through the drive thru. We placed our order and drove up.  There was no greeting, no total given, just a hand thrust out the window. I put my money in said hand, and a few minutes later my change was literally thrown into my palm. No "Thank you, have a nice day" no "Here's your change, pull forward to the next window." And most importantly, NO RECEIPT.

At the next window, as I waited for my order, a part of it was handed out. The expiditer turned away, when he turned back he looked surprised to see us still there.. "Um, the rest of my order, please?" Oh.. yeah.. and he handed it out to me as well. 

Again, no pleasantries, nothing to say "Come back again." nothing. Clearly this store needs re-training. Needs to know that even a smile at the window makes a difference.  I will NOT be back if I can help it.  This store is in need of something, perhaps new management - she was in her office near the drive thru, stuffing her face, and sucking down a drink.  - yes you could see her.  No it wasn't a good look.

I dislike when I have to down-grade a review, but tonight I have to. 

Tonight the husbeast and I went to Bob Evans because I was craving Soup. I've been Ill for about a month and after a lady's day out, the soup sounded soothing.  We arrived, we waited a few minutes and we were seated. .... and then we waited, and waited.. FINALLY about 8 minutes after being seated, our waitress cheerfully apologised for the wait - Even though she never acknowledged us after taking the order from the table behind us - she could have let us know she'd be right with us, but NO. nothing, no eye contact at all.  When she finally did come over, we placed everything at one time. 

We placed drink orders: Iced unsweet tea, ice water and coffee, Apps of Twisted cheese, and mains of Soup and salad (veg beef) and soup (veg beef) and burger. 

Our meal came out as follows: The appetizer. Which was good, but with nothing to drink it was very thick and cloying. We then noticed that one of our setups had jelly stains on it and the knife was dirty.  When the waitress came back to the table behind us, she took care of them, DIDN'T check on us.. so I raised my voice and asked her if we could have our drinks.. "Oh yes, I'm sorry.." We heard a lot of I'm sorry tonight. 

When she came back with the drinks, no ice water was had, I pointed out the stained napkin and dirty knife "Oh my, I'm sorry about that too.." she came back with both the new set up and ice water.  

"Your soup and salad is up, I think we're just waiting on your fries..  I'll go check." I'm not kidding when I say I timed her. It was another 7 minutes when she came back.  The soups, which were identical orders were NOT identical soups. One was rife with meat and veg, the other was mostly broth and veg not so much beef. There were NO soup spoons, no saucers under the soups, no crackers.   The salad was the last thing to come out and it was right. 

I'm not sure if our waitress was new, but when I was asked how the food/service was when I checked out, I said that the food was ok, but the service was not. I didn't receive an apology or anything, just sympathetic eyes and a nod.  REALLY??

10:08pm Wednesday
Generally I don't like giving low reviews, but this one is for the service.  When I walked into Applebee's, there was no one at the host/ess stand. I waited, and I over heard a conversation about "How a family was supposed to get their friend out, since he was in a wheel chair." I stood there, shifting weight foot to foot, for four minutes, FINALLY I was seated, after being asked if I wanted to sit at a high top or a booth. 

I looked at the time and noticed that 10:12 when I was sat.  I was given no silver, my table had no set up on it, but the guy who sat me asked me what I wanted to drink and assured me that my server would be with me soon.  I even saw him chase after who I think was supposed to be my server, as she headed out to the patio section, to let her know she had a table. 

Time passed, as a single diner, it's boring, I got my tea but did not drink. At 10:23 a gentleman approached and asked me if he could help, I did ask why it took 9 minutes for a server to approach. To his credit he apologized and then told me that there were only 2 people on tonight - the place was rather busy, so under staffing seems like an issue to me, and he asked if I would like to speak to a manager. At this point I wasn't hungry but more irritated, Seriously, 2 wait persons for a place on a busy night is .. silly. I told him That I wasn't going to order that I was going to leave, and I did. 

You only handicap your wait staff and provide bad service when you under staff.

A friend of mine came into town from Wisconsin.  He didn't ask my input on his hotel reservation, so when He told me where he was staying, I immediately YELPed the Hotel to see what the reviews looked like and my eyes went big. Oh this wasn't good. But I hoped for the best. 

Sadly, my best wasn't good enough. 

Yes, they've recently done some renovation, but a coat of (poorly slapped on paint) and (misplaced) Memo board in the room do not justify the $55 a night room rate.  The bed is on rolling casters with a Good Will bed cover complete with cigarette hole, but don't worry, the pattern is so damned distracting you won't notice it.  

There are 2 lights in the room, one above the door, it's bright and glaring. The other is a standing lamp, over by the wall, close to the bed, but not NEAR the bed. The lamp shade is caked with dust.  There is an old THRIFTed wing back chair that I wouldn't sit in, and the desk has a rickety/rockety chair that looks like it may fall apart at any minute. 

The black out curtain has.. it's tie back SEWN to it so it wont be lost. The TV gets 5 channels poorly.  The bathroom has sub par soaps and watered down shampoo, thread bare towels and a bath tub that looks like it hasn't been cleaned in YEARS.  The shower head is set... so low that I'd have to be 5'2 to use it.  I honest was waiting for someone to come in and kill me while I was in there. At least the toilet was clean. 

I would ---NOT--- recommend this place to any one or stay here in the future.

...well that was less than inspiring. I went with friends and the Beau. It was a lovely, but COLD afternoon in Tampa, with a biting wind, and I'll be honest, I didn't know what to expect, but I certainly expected MORE. 

When We arrived, we were lucky and found parking about a block away.  Having been to several events at the Red Rockstar bar, we knew that parking would be atrocious, so we tried next to the bakery and found a spot there.  I had hoped that we'd find some vendors of ephemera, not just food.  Sadly this was mostly a food truck rally. 

Since we got there just after 2 pm, we got to see the Tampa bay Kendo club (I'm sure it's a different name, but that's what's in my head) do a demo from across the parking lot while we dodged cars pulling in at all angles, and we played with people's pooches.  

The offerings of food were a few. At 2, the lines were 30 Minutes long and terribly unorganized, feeding into one another across the cement square area. There were a few smaller vendors like Hot Sauce, flaming fruit sauce and cheese cake in a jar that weren't as busy, but they too, were swamped because that's all you could get to. 

The food vendors that I did notice were: Moca Loka, Pho Truck, Flip'n Tasty, Mmm BAP Korean Cuisine, Tongue Thai'd, and Kona Ice - why that truck was there I have no idea... It was 48* outside and no one was going to it. I felt kinda bad for them. 

We left after 2 hours because of the cold. We didn't want to fight the crowd and honestly, there was nothing to do. There is -so- much room for improvement, and the space need to be MUCH larger for this event.   At least the company was good. I adore my friends!

How is it possible for you to lose the same luggage on the same trip?

On my way out to LA, I understand it, I really do. My first flight had a delay - something the airline didn't notify us of until 15 minutes before departure. But HEY! That's ok. We're not boarded yet. We're all still planeside, None of us could POSSIBLY have connections right?  There was a "sand storm" outside phoenix the previous night and the flight crew hadn't gotten in until the wee hours and so they hadn't gotten their prescribed rest. OK, I get that. HOWEVER, That's no excuse, the Airline had plenty of time to notify the passengers that this would be a delayed flight. They did not do so. 

They tried, unsuccessfully to get another flight crew to man our flight, so they gave us cards and had us all call in to a "special number" and re-book our flights. When I finally got through, Someone picked up, said something and I was put back on hold, and eventually the line went dead.  I had to call in again! This time someone picked up quickly, was very brusque and informed me that I was already rebooked and going to Texas! This was the first thing I knew about it. (GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE HERE!  /sarcasm)

When I got to the new flight - through no help from ANYONE on USAIR, I was assured that my bags would be transfered over to the new plane.  So you can imagine my chagrin when, at LAX I stood around waiting for the baggage to come off the carousel, and it didn't.  Mind you, I was in LA for a HUGE party that -REQUIRED- either black tie formal wear or Costumes. I had several thousand dollars worth of costumes in that bag.   Yeah.. the bag didn't get to me, it had gone to my original destination of Pheonix - except my destination was to be LAX.  Again, great job USair.  

I had to rely on a friend for costumes that night, this made me VERY angry since I had costumes that I'd worked on for over a month in that bag.  It did arrive in 24 hours though so bully for that. 

On the flight home: I checked into LAX 2 hours before my flight. I sat at the Counter for a good 8 minutes waiting for someone to take my bag. When the girl finally saw that i was waiting. She asked me if I was checking a bag. Yes.  Well it hadn't printed out anything. (I'm sorry, the big pink hard case is too big for over head bins) So she "unjammed" the kiosk and handed me my baggage slip. I didn't even look at it. (MY FAULT, I know)  So when I landed, I expected my bag to be on the carousel...

And .. it never came. So I went to US AIr baggage service and found out that my bag was now going to be in another city in Arizona. - It gets to travel more than I do! When Faoula checked on it, though.. It had not actually left LAX. So she was going to have it sent to me here in Florida, by way of Charleston (See, it sees more cities than I do)  and I should have it here today.

Really though, Totally unacceptable, the only person who was in anyway apologetic was Faoula, She was pleasant, She offered to refund me the bag handling charge, and she understood how angry I was. How can you lose the same bag on the same trip coming and going? I wonder if this merger was a smart thing? Did you can all the good employees and keep the inept ones?

We stopped here because we saw the sign for Food & beer/wine and though we used to have a membership to the wine of the month club (Thanks dad) we'd never actually been to the Keel & Curly Winery.

When we entered, no one was there to greet us, we didn't quite understand.  So when I finally could get the attention of the woman behind the wine counter doing a tasting, she acknowledged that we could sit anywhere.. our waitress would be with us momentairly. 

There were 3-4 groups of people actively engaged: 1 large group of 6 people, one couple at a table, one couple at the bar, and another small group of 2 or three, but I think they worked there. All in all it didn't look busy. 

The bar tender was getting flights ready for the couple at the table, when she handed them out, she literally slammed them on the table, no smile nothing. There was a look of avarice on her face, when the guy asked a question. It was then she shot us a look and said "I'll be right with you."   

She then went to the kitchen got an order for the large table and passed it out to them.  We still were not addressed. She went back to the bar and chatted with those folks some, relaxing a bit.  By now more than 10 minutes have passed since we entered, we have read the menu over by 3 times.  Since this is the "Service" We see being offered, it's not something we want part of, and we left. 

This was Thursday July 5th at approximately 3:30pm.

This started out GREAT! The place smelled wonderful, and the food, Pretty darn tasty. The price was good, and food was plentiful and hot. 

When we arrived there was one table of a mother and daughter, and our table.  After we arrived another couple arrived. There was 1 waitress.  While I can't say it ever got truly busy, I can say that she never checked back with us after the initial "How's everything?" never asked us if we wanted more water. After we were clearly finished with our food, she never came back to see if we needed boxes. 

At this point 2 more groups came in, one group of 4 and one group of 5 and they sat at the back of the place, those seemed to take up her time. This was about 6:30. My friend and I were done by now, we were looking at our watches, commenting that it was relatively early. By 7pm, though we were still talking, the waitress still hadn't checked on us, when we would try to get her attention, she never did seem to make eye contact with us, she simply ghosted to the back areas of the eatery. 

At 7:15 we had to verbally signal her to get us boxes, and to ask for the check. She then didn't remember them for another spate of time, we finally got out of the establishment at 7:44.  The times are known because I made note.   I would come back for the food, but the service was pitifully slow. Need more help in there.

A friend won tickets to see Gary Valentine at Side Splitters and asked if I wanted to join, and since it was a Thursday night, I said SURE.  I've not been to Side Splitters since the late '90's and thought why not. 

The place really hasn't changed. The waiting area is still predictably small, and the seating area is still a bunch of small (VERY) small tables pushed together onto a small floor where the comedian stands on a stage and does his/her schtick. They have a 2 drink minimum, and prices are... well, they're not cheap. 

The entertainment we saw, The first, a local fellow from NPR (poor guy - I grew up there, I KNOW all too well the tribulations of Redneckville) was decent.  I liked him, but I think the crowd didn't know how to react to him.  The headliner? He was funny. I'd honestly not heard of him, but recognized him when I saw him. He was on King of Queens, and he had us ROLLING. 

Over all, the show was a fun outing.  They did say there would be trivia after the show to win prizes, I waited around.. trivia never happened.

***EDIT TO ADD***

So a friend of mine just related this to me:  "I had paid by credit card, left "in Cash" on the tip line and left her $3 bucks in cash at the table.  When I checked my statement, I saw that she added a $5 charge for the tip, to a $14 bill?  I don't think so."  This was on Tuesday.  She tried to get a hold of them, but no one answered. Finally she got through and she was supposed to hear back from them on Wednesday. Of course, she never got a call back. Today, she received a message from their Manager stating that a mistake was made and that $5 would be credited back to her card. 

I find this slightly shady, honestly. Not everyone checks their bill, and $5 here and $5 there adds up quickly when you're padding your tips.   BE AWARE.

The name is no longer Holiday inn, but rather Tampa Stadium Hotel. I showed up because a friend let me know about an Estate stale that was going on here. 

The hotel itself is in need of some repair, and the little out building smelled of mold.  But the sale was decent, I was able to pick up some much needed things. And some wanted things.

I -wish- it was non smoking.  The moment you hit the door you can smell the smoke and the stuff they use to cover up the odor. It was rather.. strong. 

Inside though, the light is phased out and the bells and whistles of the machines come up, There is an odd sense of euphoria that seems to weigh over you as you approach and you sit down at the slots.  I played the $0.02 machines (Really more like $0.40 -$0.80 machines based on the bets you have to play) and did fairly ok. 

The one thing I can say that I do not like is the inconsideration of the staff when they stand RIGHT behind you, quite literally nearly touching you when they're helping someone out. This happened twice to me. It makes me very nervous and very .. uncomfortable.

Typical Wendys.

I used the drive through on my way home, and grabbed their 4 for $4 with the Crispy BLT Chicken Sandwich, nuggets, fries and a drink.  I asked for the crispy chicken BLT to have no mayo. When I got my order, the fries were not hot - not cold, more of a kinda UH.. not tasty and there was Mayo on the chicken. Meh.

Large WalMart, got what I needed and got out. 
I dislike this walmart because on Thanksgiving 3 years ago, someone tried to use our "Credit Cards" while we were out of town. We don't know how they got our numbers, but they used them here.  Not the cleanest store.

I was not happy with this visit to Dunkin.  I was on my way to the Airport when the husbeast and I stopped. 

I get it, they were busy, but they messed EVERYTHING up. I ordered a combo, and while I got a combo, it wasn't the one I wanted. I wanted a Bacon/egg/cheese on bagel, but I got a sausage/egg/cheese on a croissant. Not that it wasn't tasty, but if I'd wanted that, I would have ordered it.  The combo comes with hash rounds, and I can never eat them, because frankly they never feel/taste cooked through.  And my coffee.. *sigh*  No, just no. I'm not sure if it's because the ratio of their caramel to coffee was off or something else was, but it just wasn't satisfying. 

They missed my husband's order for a large coffee but at LEAST they got his order for his sandwich right.  He didn't want to waste any more time there, else we would have said something to the window.

Decided to go here today with a friend. Now I'm kind of sorry we did.  The food was OK. At least they got our -special- orders right.  So why the 2 stars?  Our waiter was S-L-O-W.  And I don't mean slow.. I mean, he took our beverage order and then disappeared for the next 10 minutes.  He didn't come back to take our order for a long while. It was quite frustrating. Here we were, ready to order, but we had to wait... and wait.. and wait. 

When we did order, the food came out fast enough, and it was just how we ordered it, but the service just took away from everything.

Drive thru ATM... this was the 2nd location I visited this evening, because the first was down. Apparently it was sytstem wide, because YEP.. the lady before me had the same issue as the one in Palm Harbor. You could enter your card, key in your pin and even enter what you wanted to do. If you wanted to get cash out though.... You weren't getting it. So Sorry.. The ATM was timing out on you.

I stopped in to get my eyebrows waxed. Granted the experience was good from the beginning until mid way through the waxing, when my waxing professional stated she'd been sick not but the day before "REALLY SICK" and that her 3 year old daughter was still ill. Here she was, in my face, sniffling every few seconds and doing my brows.  This isn't acceptable. I was going to be traveling in a few days - not to mention it was just before the final weekend of the Halloween Season for the Vault, and I am immuno compromized, and she was not wearing a mask.  I left, and looked at the makeup she'd done on my brows, without my glasses it seemed ok. Once my glasses were on, I had two big red commas on my face. Again, not so good. I do a better job on my own.  I'm glad I didn't pay for the service, because they have the first service free offering. I can't say I'll be back.

This is the most unorganized, erratic and least staffed Burlington I've had the displeasure to be in.  The floor was... disorganized, it was hard to tell what clothing sizes were where. When looking at dresses they were quite litterally all over the place. 

The wallets and gift sets were strewn about, many were missing pieces. I know that this isn't the store's fault, that this is LOSS, but the associates should at least cull those that have been rifled through and remove them from the floor for mark downs. 

This is not a place I will be visiting again.

This is the first time I've been to the new location since they moved down to Largo.  I'll be honest, I wasn't completely impressed. They do have quite the selection of things, but it's a jumble. There are a lot of things that are of good or decent quality, and then there are things that are kind of questionable. 

I saw retractable power cords, like the one I was using at that very moment to charge my phone. Theirs was $14.99. I'd bought mine in Georgia at Fry's for $6.99, that's not a deal.  They'd had argyle socks for $3.00. This is about the price I'd pay at Target. Speaking of Target. They had a Mossimo purse from Target, black leather, for $25.00.  Doesn't sound bad, until you know that the price tag from Target was still on it, and it was originally $26.99. *SMH*

I did buy an ergonomic stool from them for $40 - with 20%off. Currently the same model is being sold on Amazon for $79.00.  I also got a pair of knee high boots for $20. They usually run about double that. So it is really hit or miss with what you find. If you know what you're buying, if you know the average of prices, then you know what you're in for. It is all Buyer beware. 

My biggest complaint though: The movie section. There is no rhyme or reason to it. There is a HUGE selection but it is all thrown together. Frankly that's too much work even for $2.00 a pop.

My friends have all talked up Aldi, and this evening, I thought we could check it out.  It may just be this location, but WOW, It was not at all what I was expecting. 

This store was a MESS. There was seemingly no rhyme or reason to the way it was laid out and the way the stock was arranged. It looked and felt very chaotic.  It also felt very much like a Sams/BJ's on the inside, cold and impersonal. 

The prices were fine, the products look good. And the location was fine too. Though one cashier at 7pm probably was a bad call. There was a decent line the entire time I was there.  I don't think I'd return.

Recently opened in the old Barnhill's location on SR 54, My husband and I decided to check it out. Truth be told, I was hankering for some Peanut Chicken and didn't want to drive down to Chopsticks.  We were surprised when we walked in. They have gutted the old building, taken out about 60% of the seating and put in a LOT of buffet tables. The food variety is there, Hot and cold, including a hibachi and sushi. However, the turn over that I've seen at other places like Chopstics & Super Buffet isn't there. The greenbeans were wilted and cold, with about 5 in the pan. So when things were running out they weren't being re-stocked.  They had a mystery meat-type loaf that scared me. THEY called it a pork loin, but it was simply pressed meat. I didn't try it.  The husband said the sushi was fresh and tasty. Their chicken on a stick was delicious and their desserts were copious, but  overall, I wasn't terribly impressed. Prices were decent, $6.99 for lunch 11-4pm on M-Sat. Drinks at $1.49 seems to be a bargain.

Saturday, 11:15 and we're waiting for a table? Not because they're busy, but because their hostess isn't behind the stand, she's in the back, behind the bar, doing other things, not doing -her- job.  It wasn't just us, it was two other groups too.  

When we were sat, we had an excellent waiter. Seymour (yes, the "little Shop Of Horrors" jokes were not lost on us either) made sure our orders were taken and our food was gotten to us quickly. After all, we had a movie to catch. 

Since the menu change, Ruby Tuesday really is nothing more than mediocre. The food was tasty but nothing to write home about.

I was craving MEAT, roasted meat.. and this was half way between mom & I so I took her here for lunch. 

We both ordered a pulled pork plate, 2 sides and the endless salad bar. 

The service was good, if a bit slow. I'd blame it being on Sunday, but the place wasn't busy. 

When we did get out plates for the salad bar, I kinda wish we didn't. First, the salad mix was Ice burg lettuce, and there was a side bowl - the size of a soup bowl- that was of another mix and it was almost empty. I took those mixed greens. I added a bit of the cucumbers, some egg, some black olives, and when I went to get the corn, it was.. Goopy. Yes goopy, like it had gel in it. It was.. Gross. The other offerings from the salad bar were equally disappointing, the Tuna salad - lumped together and discolored, the potato salad, not even going to try it. Only the macaroni salad.. it seemed edible. 

The rest of the food came quickly, it was tasty and fresh, but the Salad bar was disgusting.

Mall food. But it was quick and reasonable. I ordered the bourbon chicken plate, with two sides. What I ordered was supposed to be "Mixed Vegs" but it turned out to be cabbage, green beans and the bourbon chicken. The green beans seasoned with garlic but there was no actual flavor. The Chicken was tasty and the cabbage was.. it was cabbage. 

I would not eat there again.

Recently I received a notice in the mail stating that my card was to be suspended due to the activities of some unscrupulous lout on Black Friday.  But I shouldn't fear! No!  I would get a new card in the mail by 2/18, and until then my compromised card would still work.

Here we are on 2/18 and I've still not received my card.  So I did the dutiful thing and called the bank. According to them, I have an OLD ADDRESS on file. 

 How can this be? I changed my address IN PERSON at the local branch when my last card expired 8 months ago and I'd not received the replacement.  I know that it was changed because not only did I receive the NEW card then, but the POS Verification for Zip code now works with the proper one.   

After explaining this to the girl on the phone she had no answer.  She will send me a new card, shipped via Fed Ex to the Proper Address. It should be here by Friday morning and someone will have to sign for it. I'm OK with that.  I just don't get how their systems aren't communicating with each other. 

The address was changed, I did it in person. I know that I've received a replacement card at my current address before... so... the issue is on their end. They need to work harder at making things seamless for their customers. I don't like having to wait now for my card to come in.

This was a spur of the moment decision to go to by friends. We'd been out all afternoon and they were heading over there, and said "We're going, ask the hubby if he wants to join." So I did. He'd join us there in about 30.  IN the mean while, the three of us (Plus infant in carrier) waited in the bar.  

In the bar, the bartender was .. OVER ATTENTIVE. She had baby lust. The woman didn't allow us to have conversation because she was all over us like white on rice (pardon the pun) She didn't know how to stay away from our little grouping. We were engaged in a quiet conversation at the bar, and every few moments she was interjecting her opinion about SOMETHING about the baby. How she wanted a baby - never mind that it would be a miracle for her to have one at her age - her words.  She fawned over the little one overly much, and her hovering was bothersome.  The adults were -trying- to have a sort of intimate conversation, but it was hard to do so with this woman lingering in our space.  

 When we were called for our seating, we informed the hostess that we were still waiting on our 4th person, and the bartender shot her mouth off with "Don't you hate it when someone is late, that is So rude."  My friend and I both looked at her a bit incredulous, "He's not late, this wasn't planned." we explained. But there was no apology from this woman. I personally found her behavior invasive, excessive and overtly offensive.
