For Dinner, we were taken to a corner area, where the seats were chairs that the legs had been sawed off, and placed on a table riser, we were sat here because they don't have a baby chair or table sling for a baby seat - they used to but they're all broken. (um, it would be time to replace such things, don't you think?) The table was hard to get in and out of, but we managed. We were joined by another family celebrating a birthday and sat down to enjoy a nice meal and conversation. 

The meal, it's nothing to write home about. The show, what little there was of it, wasn't impressive. I'm sorry to say, that like other reviews, they seem to be going through the motions. There was little passion in the way he did things.The table cook was understandably flustered, we had a few picky eaters at our table. *chuckles* But the food was well cooked, tasty and we all brought home extra in our to go boxes.

I know it's a fast food place, but seriously, how many times must I -repeat- my order to the 2nd window, while I'm sitting there waiting for pick up? You've already handed me my drink, why are you trying to hand me -another- drink? I don't have kids, I didn't order a kids meal.  I'm waiting on the Mc Nuggets for the 4th time. Perhaps you forgot your AdHd Medication? Or you're just not paying attention? Either way, Look at the screen, See the one with the Iced Tea and the Mc Nuggets? Yeah? that's me. *facepalm*

I stopped at Walgreens in hopes of seeing the new ELF Villain's collection. Sometimes Walgreens gets them before the holidays. Sometimes they don't. This particular one doesn't ever get them according to their cosmetics person. SAD. Really sad. I suppose I'll have to skulk other Walgreens to find them.

It's been a while since I've visited BayWalk... that I call it BayWalk tells you just how long it's been.

Re-branded the Sundial, it city center has undergone an overhaul and is quite lovely! From its open air design, to its stunning sundial sculpture with dolphins surrounding it's base, you can tell that there's been a small fortune sunk into the over haul and its well worth it. 

High end shops line the promenade, A lot of restaurants have decided to populate this popular destination and of course Locale Market has finally opened, this means more foot traffic! This it certainly is a good thing for Down Town St. Pete.

Ice creamery outside of the Cobb theatres at Countryside.  I'm giving this a 3 because the girl who tended, Sarah, us was good but she was left to flounder due to poor scheduling. She was in the weeds. I felt bad for her. 

The ice cream was good, especially when she blended in the toppings I requested. But there was a line building up and there was only one girl, a new menu and she was new there. She kept her cool and di just fine with us.

Lunch after a massage is always something that I crave. So since this was in the same plaza as the massage envy I go to, I stopped in for a bite. 

The locale is large, it's spacious with nice seating. I was even greeted by the company dog outside.  Once inside, I realised I was the only person there on a Monday Afternoon. Sad really.. 

I placed an order for water and a small pizza, this way I could take most of it home and eat it later.  I ended up getting the margharita pizza, and it came out rather quickly. The ingredients were fresh, large slices of tomato topping it with lots of basil and some garlic and oil. Tasty. But a touch underdone. 

I'd go again.

I've never seen a "super center" that is this small. 
It lacks a cohesive plus size clothing center - heck what used to be their plus wear is mostly clearance now.  They do have a decent electronics department, if you have an Iphone. A fairly OK selection of Health & Beauty.  But this is mostly a Walmart if you need to quick stop. There's a real super center 20 minutes away on SR54 or JUST up the road on Alderman.

Long drive home and I needed sustenance... I don't generally care for fast food, and since Steak 'n shake is a step above most places, I opted to stop there.  Where else can you get a triple patty steak burger and fries for $4 bucks? 

In general, the food is good, the burgers are fresh, even if the service is NOT the fastest.

I remember when these apartments were horrid. 

Now they're kind of passable. I had to drop a friend off here after she stayed the weekend with me. Gated entry and exits keep this from being the suitcase city of old.  (and yes, way back when, I used to .. well not live here exactly, but spend a LOT of time with my then boyfriend, now ex husband - ahh good ole college days..AHEM)

They've done a lot to clean up the place, given it a complete over haul, even though the apartments still look like boxes on the inside.

If EVER there was a store that had -too- much, Bed, Bath and beyond is the perfect example of that store.  They have floor to rafter and just about every square inch of floor space - save that what you would call isles filled with merchandise. 

And given that this is Christmas shopping season, well, it's doubly so! Yes, if you've seen it on TV, you can find it there. Do you want the Veg-o-matic Spaghetti maker? They have it.  Do you want Poo-Pouri?Its there too, and in multiple scents. The sweeping craze of Adult Colouring is big as is STAR WARS. Oh lard, lets talk about Star Wars. If it's got Kylo Ren or the Chrome Storm Trooper on it, its there. 

They have pillows and comforters, they have everything you need. It's packed floor to beam with everything and more. I don't enjoy the pace, or the place, but it is what it is, and they will print you out a Gift receipt if you forget to ask for one when they're ringing things up.

Contrary to other reviews, this is NOT the worst Ross out there. Sure it has it's issues, and yes, like any other major discount retailers, the clothing is a bit jumbled and discombobulated. But for the most part it's an OK shopping experience. 

The Loss Prevention person hangs out near the door, is more like a Walmart greeter, if you ask me. Yes, their presence is seen, but what do they actually do? Not a lot, really. Nothing they CAN do, honestly.  Since the holiday hours have been extended, they're currently open til 12:30 am or 1:30 am on any given night. This means, no long waiting lines to check out. 

Heck! I walked away with 4 new dresses last night, all of them looked great.  I'll continue to shop here when I can!

I was meeting a friend here because I remembered the last time I was here, they had a coffee shop attached.  It wasn't busy, but lawdy, Clearwater was sure hopping. After fighting for a parking spot, I finally gave up and paid a pretty penny $10, for a spot behind CVS across the street and walked to the destination.

As I said, it wasn't busy and that was good. My friend and I placed our orders, I got the Steakhouse burger - sauces on the side, and He got the All American burger. We upgraded to the combo for $3 more, and got a drink (Soda for me, coffee for him) and a side, rings and fries respectively. I paid the $27 and we got our buzzer and took our seats. 

Five minutes later, we were called up and our food was given. They were good sized burgers, however, i took the bun off of mine. They weren't over done, they were cooked just over medium. The toppings were done too. The rings and fries were tasty. 

I'd come back.

During Third Friday I decided I just NEEDED to stop in. They have such great displays that I wanted to see what else they might have. Lo and behold, they had a picnic basket just outisde the door, and it was a whopping $5. I bought that! It will make a fantastic Ren Faire basket. 

Inside, its a bit cluttered, there's a lot to look at, a lot to browse, and you can't forget to look up at the walls near the ceiling, as there's stuff up there too! The prices are reasonable, and all in all, its a fun afternoon to poke around.

Came here with a friend of mine before doing a salt float. We chose it because it was close and our original destination was closed because it was a holiday. 

Chili's wasn't busy, and we were seated rather quickly. Both of us perused the new menu, neither of us saw what we really wanted but did notice that there was a lunch menu that offered relatively cheap food for a low price.  

The server was concientious and quick, but the food was mediocre at best. My friend opted for the fajitas on the lunch menu with the side of rice and beans - Cadillac style, and was disappointed to find out that the rice was hard, as if it was old and had set out and dried.

Took a class here, so this is only for the Meeting room.  The staff was friendly enough, and directed me to the large room where the CPR class was being held. The room had one small issue, the AC was either too hot or too cold, there didn't seem to be a happy medium. I would certainly take a class here again.

Friday night is a busy night... and when it's cold outside, it's even busier since they can't use their outside seating. 

The food is -good-, VERY good.  The husband and I decided to try a little something from every column.  We tried the Caprese salad, two different kind of wings: The fire side and the Garlic/parmesan wings and a small margharita pie. 

Everything was delivered relatively quickly, the caprese salad was very fresh with nice big leaves of basil. The wings were tasty, but the garlic/parm wings were missing something.. salt.   And the pizza.. THE PIZZA was delicious! Absolutely tasty. Would certainly come back for that any day.

I usually REALLY like Applebee's. But this time, the resturant fell flat. 

Mom and I came here for lunch before going to Joanne's fabric and crafts.  We ordered an appetizer of the beercheese bread sticks before our mains.  When it came to the table, I noticed that the cheese was unmelted, so I tried to stir it into the gloop and see if that made any difference. Sadly it did not. The sauce was cold.. like someone didn't even TRY to heat it up.

Mom and I both ate a bread stick while I tried my darnedest to flag down my server, but the server was handling so many different tables. When she finally came to me to see what was going on, I pointed it out and she took it away, letting me know she was going to make it right.

Shortly, our mains came out and those were ok.  A few minutes later the Manager came over and apologized - he said that the appetizer was on him. At least this time the cheeze was crusted and piping hot, even if we didn't get to eat it because our food was with us now. 

Over all, it wasn't a great experience, but they made it right.

So when I first visited back in 2013, I gave them a 2 stars. They've improved but not a lot.  I have found the non smoking area, but found that many of the machines there were in need of repair ( a whole bank of wheel of fortune machines was cordoned off with tape and half taken apart) and many were just not up to snuff - by sound not working or just having the blue screen of death. 

Quite honestly, the area needs to be larger, as it was the most crowed area of the casino.  I did not appreciate the people who walked towards the bakery STILL SMOKING. That was wholly inconsiderate of the non-smokers. 

Also noticed that they are now charging a $10 parking fee for every car.  Your first half hour is free, but "All day" which lets be honest, can be 2 hours or 12 hours, in my opinion the $10 parking rate is ... kind of steep, especially for those who are there frequently (Daily) or those who come only for a little bit of time. Let's also talk about the issue the parking meters have on getting into and out of the parking garage (South), there is inevitably a hold up because they're new, and it takes folks some time to get their ticket and get through the barrier.

I'm not sure I know what they're doing with this fee, but sure, it's a revenue generator. Yet I think it will limit people coming as well.

After going to the Neiman's in San Fran, I was So hoping to find that they too carried a great selection in bras.  Sadly, they do not.  They have a fabulous collection of clothing, great designers and what have you, but their foundation selection is paltry and very slim. I am saddened by this. I mean, really! There were no bras over a DD cup even offered. THIS.. just is not acceptable.

I generally don't rate low, and had the service been better, I would have given this 4 stars, but when the waitress forgets to put your order in, yeah.. it's bad.

The hubs and I went in yesterday, as we were on the way to picking up friends to take them to the airport. We had a half an hour to kill and from his previous experience, this should be enough time to get our food and eat it.   We got there at 1pm on the dot, and while there were a few tables that were full, and the counter had 1 person at it, they were no where near slammed.

Our waitress came to us, told us she'd be with us in a moment and walked past to deliver drinks to another table.  When she did come back we placed our order for drinks and food and thus began our wait.  The counter filled up, and they were served. Food was coming out all over the place, and the minutes kept ticking by. Our waitress didn't come to check on us, when 10 minutes had passed by, I looked at my husband and he shrugged.  At 15 minutes i had almost finished the little oyster crackers in my bowl. When 20 minutes came, the waitress finally came by and checked on us, I asked her if we could just get our food to go. 

She blinked a few times and went over to the line cooks and checked on our order, then came over to us. "I'm sorry, I didn't put your order in, I'm going to jump it ahead of everyone and you can eat it in if you like." I then explained what was going on, that we had to pick friends up to go to the airport and she nodded, our food was ready to go in 3 minutes and she apologized profusely.   Everything was bagged up and we were given our drinks to go as well, and sent on our way. Yes, we left her a nice tip too.

When we finally did get to eat it, at a lovely little beach near Tampa International, the food was good. I had a Chili 4 way with beans and the hubs had the Chili 5 way.   For me, I am not a fan of Cincinnati chili, but the flavour was good, you could taste the cinnamon, the beans were good, it had a richness to it. The pasta was tasty too, and there was the cheese! So much CHEESE!!!

I needed to grab food on the way home from a play date. This was just up the street and on the corner. Having never been to a Culvers, I wasn't sure what to expect, however, After a quick read through of the menu, I settled for a combo of their Bacon cheese burger, fries and a dr. Pepper.   

When I pulled up to the window, I paid, was given my soda and a number, the kind of number that you'd put on your table to wait for someone to deliver it to me. I sat there. No one told me to pull forward. After a minute, the girl looked out the window and I asked. "So, did you WANT me to pull forward?" she nodded.  Great, be clear. that's the important part, I've never been here before. 

I pulled around to the very first (last) parking spot and waited.. less than a full minute for the person to bring me out my sack of food.. I'm sorry to say that i was disgusted when they smiled because they had what you'd say was meth mouth.  It was disconcerting to say the least. But the fries were hot, if over cooked, and the burger was YUMMY.. I might come back.

The chocolate covered strawberries are what called my name, but I didn't end up getting them. Sadly the service was terribly slow and I didn't want to wait. They are always busy!  There's a reason for that though! Godiva chocolate is GOOD chocolate and people want that stuff!

I love shopping at Ross Stores. I stop at every one I come across. Yes, much of the merchandise is the same, but once in a while, you find a gem. It really is a treasure hunt. 

They carry a selection of "as seen on Tv" stuff, a slew of Jr's clothing, a decent selection of ladies and missy, but they generally fail at plus, men's and petite.  These markets are woefully represented. Sure they have a men's section, but looking through the stuff, it's crappy t shirts and fubu jeans. Hardly anything the men in my life would wear.

This particular store's selection of lingerie/under garments is sad. They don't have a good variety of lingerie other than bras and panties.  Their home goods is very nicely situated as are their bed and bath items ... and their shoes!! My goodnes, their shoes are to die for!

One rhing I've noticed recently is that they are carrying many more high end designers: Michael Kors, Calvin Klein, and others at decent prices. So it does pay to shop at Ross.

Tried a Flat White for the first time on the recommendation of a friend (Thanks Amy P!) The first location I went to said no, I couldn't because they were out of whole milk. This location though, they were more than happy to oblige. The service was quick and efficient. The barista was both bubbly and sweet as she made my drink order. 

The drink itself was tasty, not sweet but rich on the tongue. Next time I get this, I'll see if they can add vanilla to it.

It was whispered this was some of the best Ice Cream out there. I can NOT dispute this fact.  I splurged and got myself a single scoop of Mint Chip. The scoop was HUGE. I mean -HUGE- The flavor was delicious and it was so creamy! It was a delight in my mouth!

I also ordered a large cappuccino. While it wasn't the perfect cuppa, it was a decent cup of rich java, and that's just what I wanted with my ice cream. I would reccomend this place to anyone.

Had dinner with a friend here, before going out shopping.  

The service was quick, efficient and friendly. I ordered a pick two of French Onion Soup and a 1/2 salad.  I asked for extra croutons and dressing on the side. My requests were easily made and cheerfully done.  My friend ordered a special sandwich on white bread.  They did that for her as well. We were quite pleased.

Tasty, tasty, tasty! 

For a fast food option, they're relatively healthy. The pulled pork was delicious and moist. The black beans were delightful, but the salad was over dressed. I'll come back when I get the chance, since it's on the way to work, but now I know it's a great choice for protien.

What a neat little shop! I don't get down to South Tampa to shop, but when my fellow Massage Therapist invited me out for a shopping party, how could I resist.  I made my way down and parked near the little ravioli shop and walked into this warm and inviting little storefront. 

She has -everything- you might want. Some great fashion, some very ecclectic styles, but her size range really only goes from Xs to Large.  As a woman who currently fits in 3 size ranges (Yes, I can wear a Jr.s XXL, A Womens XL or a 1x) this can be a bit disconcerting. But I did find a thing or three that I just needed.  I didn't buy them, NO, I bought accessories. She has SO many pretty sparkingling and shiny things, that I couldn't keep my hands off of them!

If you need dangly necklaces, Tassles or shiny stones, this is the place to come. Her prices are just about average and her service is right on the money. The only reason she's not getting 5 stars is the music, It was NOT the choice for me, and it might have just been for that night but hearing the rap and hip hop was off putting to me, so that MIGHT make me not come in on some days. Other wise, Great selection, great accessories and over all an excellent shopping environment.

In a food truck food court, one food truck stood out in stark contrast above the others, it was Twisted Iron. Why? they had a line.  We were at the front of this line and I was happy for that, because it was chilly under the Bridge at Pierce street market. 

Both the husbeast and I got Chicken & Waffles. The wait time was short but the food portions were large. 3 juicy pieces of chicken atop a large waffle, a serving of smuckers breakfast syrup and I THINK It was honey Mustard, but since I don't use it, I gave that to the husband. 

The chicken was good. VERY VERY GOOD. it had a nice flavour and was perfectly cooked.  THe only thing about the waffle I can say negative is that it wasn't light. it was very heavy and dense, and that's not the way I prefer my waffles. Bt the flavour was spot on and yum to my mouth! 

I ate all the chicken and 1/4 the waffle. The husbeastie was a member of the clean plate club!

So I came back to Tin Drum on my own, and I have to say that I'm pretty impressed. I walked in after the lunch rush, so there was plenty of parking, and there was no line!

I ordered one of the main dishes we'd had at our event, which was the Tin Drum Curry. It was the first time I'd had curry, and it set well with me. I did ask that it not be too spicy, and as I made that request, they brought me more rice so I could thin out the sauce.   When it was brought to my table, after very minimal wait, I was pleased. It wasn't terribly spicy at all. 

It was incredibly good. There was just enough chicken, sauce and spinach to make me happy.  And a few minutes later, Kaitlyn brought out the bowl of extra rice, apologizing that it didn't come with the meal. I thanked her. 

The staff was very proficient about keeping the place clean and neat. The tables were wiped down and dishes - if you were eating in - were never left on the tables long. 

My only complaint? No Jasmine tea! It had been there for the event, and wasn't there when I went back. *sad*  Ah well, I will be back, I truly enjoyed my meal!

I LOVE me some Zaxby's Zalads.  Their House Zalad is fantastic, with cucumber, tomato and crispy onion, it makes for 2 delicious meals. Add to that some zesty fried mushrooms and life is good! 

The seasoning on their fries is perhaps the best around - though I've noticed that Universal uses something very similar!

This isn't my first go with a Korean BBQ. I've visited one in Hawai'i, and it was a similar experience. 

We had a large group, 10 people. When I say this is both a labor intensive and confusing experience, I mean it.  It could have been our group, or it just could have been the night, but though the food was endless - most of the group ordered the hot pot/bbq all you can eat combination for $30.

The meat for the hotpot came in frozen roll ups and the meat for the BBQ came in slabs of marinated meat, but the seafood and meats were combined and you only got one or two pair of tongs. I was exceedingly concerned about cross contamination.  We had one person allergic to mushrooms and ask that they be separated out, they were not. We made sure to cook his food separately for him since we didn't want him getting sick. 

I will say they are concerned about how they are perceived. I ordered the Honey dew water (?) A frothy, almost sweet but very light drink. It was delivered, but shortly after, the waitress came by and delivered another saying she'd given me the wrong one, she'd given me a cucumber, I honestly couldn't tell them apart.  I noticed that the glass was split - broken down the side, but not enough to leak, just enough to shatter if it clinked against another, when I was 1/3rd the way done with my drink. I pointed this out to the waitress on her next pass, she immediately took that away, and brought me a 3rd. All in all, I got an apology from the owner/Manager for the inconvience, and we only paid for one of them. I understand things like that happen, and I didn't ask for a replacement as the drink was already consumed. 

We were there 2+ hours, the food was plentiful and they kept coming around filling our pots with broth, and asking if we wanted more meat.  I assure you we got our money worth.  I admit that when I got home, I stripped and put everything in the wash and immediately set to shower, because we smelled like food. Something that you remember from working in the food industry. 

While it was an alright experience it was more labor intensive than I want my dinner to be. Would I do it again? Maybe.

I've been meaning to come here since they opened. Today afforded the opportunity. 

I've been to Oahu, I've had Mac Nut Pancakes and I've been craving them ever since.. and today, I had them again. they were Ono Grinds! The weather was perfect for sitting outside on the patio deck, listening to the conversations that flowed around me while I ate my food, and sipped my tea. 

The service was attentive and the food was fresh. The menu was a bit daunting for a dyed in the wool omnivore like myself, but if you're a vegetarian or are health conscious, visit Ohana Cafe, Give a little Aloha and Mahalo to the wait staff.

I will be back!

Stopped in today after finding out that my favorite Thai place didn't open until 4.  Since Red Robin was close by and I had an errand to run at the mall, the husbeast and I decided why not. 

What we first noticed is that they've got advertising up for their new autumn menu, including the Sam Adams Oktoberfest beer and their Pretzel burger.  This piqued the husbeast's interest and me, well, I'm a simple creature, I just wanted MEAT! 

We perused the new slick menu layout - instead of being a fold out menu, they've now got newly photographed food offerings in a book style menu- and i chose to have the French dip, as a starter, we chose their pretzel bites. I've had them in the past and they've been delicious, today though, they were a disappointment. The cheese was clumpy and the bites themselves tasted microwaved and over salted. 

The way the food is presented is much prettier now. Gone are the plastic baskets, now food comes neatly arranged on plates, fries come served in hammered steel buckets. Everything looks slick and delicious.  They even offer 7 different sauces for your fries that are standard, and a few other sauces that are premium for an up-charge. This is something new.  Our entrees were served quickly and as ordered. They were delicious! The food and the service was excellent. 

Since I've been on a restricted diet, I ended up having to take half my meal home. Its days like today that I wish I could order off the kiddie menu!

I'm not a huge fan of Chick-fil-A, but I will say that they are always courteous, quick and the food is always good, if you order one of their value meals. You certianly can't beat the waffle cut fries or their grilled nuggets. Seriously, if you've not tried the grilled nuggets, do so, they're the tastiest thing on the menu!

I went all afternoon without eating. This is a dumb move, so finally after my trip to Kohl's was done, I stopped in at Tijuana Flats fo fill my neglected tummy. 

This is a new store, the windows really provide for a very bright, airy feeling to what are usually dark venues. The bright "comic book" style art on the walls always makes me smile. This store's, in particular was crisp and fresh, even the ceiling, which was not yet tiled in painted tiles, had ones that were neatly done. 

The Manager, himself waited on me, he was polite and funny and made sure i got just what I wanted, including the Diet coke, topped with cherry coke for sweetness. *grin*  He came out to check on me a few times to make sure that everything was ok, and that I really enjoyed things.  And I did. His competency was excellent. He was really personable and told me about how the training of the stores were done, how quickly the stores are growing and how they manage to keep quality even across the board.

Popped in to Hot Wax but briefly last night. I didn't get a chance to do more than just peruse while my friend was on a call out side. 

The store is beautiful, well lit and kept very clean. The staff seems friendly and knowledgable. I love that there's a glass blower right there making pipes right in front of you. That's so neat.

Honestly, I'd normally skip this place because of the way it looks like. But as the adage goes, don't judge a book by the cover. Once inside, I placed the order for a Margarita pizza and took a seat outside with my friend.  

Our pizza was delivered shortly, it was topped with fresh tomato, LOTS of fresh basil and garlic, and a white sauce. THe crust was perfection, toasty and tasted wonderful. Everything was just right. 

We had discussed knots but in the end decided not to order them, imagine my surprise when an gratis order was delivered to us. You can bet that we will be back here again. Perhaps not to eat in, but certainly for carry out. I really want to try their wings.

Crockett's towing was the service that the FHP used when my mom was in her accident. At first, we had no idea where her car was at, so it took a little detective work on my end, but we found it. 

The people there were awesome, caring and understanding. There was a hold on our car and the others involved in the multi-car accident so I had to wait to get the important things out of our car.  Those things included the hearing aids that she was wearing when the airbags went off. So for a week she was deaf as a door nail. Ah well. 

When we were able to retrieve things, the Crockett's team was there to help me with getting the license plate off, made sure I had what I needed. All in all, they did a great job with helping me.

Stopped here because there was an ETSY craft show.  The only other time I'd ever been to the Coliseum was a Cat show nigh on 20 years ago. Nothing had change except what they were showing. The floors are still lovely wood and highly polished, The accoustics are great and the stage calls to me. 

This particular show was set up as any craft show is, with rows and rows of people selling things, the Venue itself was selling hot dogs for a buck and they were tasty.   The only complaint I had was that parking was scarce and hard to use.

A Tampa classic. 

I've stopped in here so many times. It's odd that I've never given them a review.  I find them best for late night bites and cups of coffee, when you want to linger with the person you're with, but don't want to deal with Denney's or Village Inn. 

Their food is damned good, and the waitresses work hard to get you what you want.

Popped into Glossy 130 Nails & Spa by chance. My nails needed done, but I wasn't keen on making the drive all the way down to Countryside.  On a whim, I turned at Glossy nail and went inside. 

Almost immediately I was take to a seat, a gentleman named Deon started to work. He commented on how shiny my current nails were (the other place does great work.) and asked what I was looking for. I want the SNS Dip Polish and was given a display of colors to choose from. 

Once I chose what I wanted, he started to work on removing the old nail polish so that the new could be put on.  He really didn't let the nail polish remover sit on long so there was a lot he had to remove via dremmel. 

Once the color was off, he set to trimming and shaping my nails. He was very gentle and kind while he was working. He made sure that I was happy with the length and the shape. The last time I left that up to the technician, this time I asked for a specific look. 

When he was done, about 45 minutes in total, my fingers shone prettily in the light. A sparkly blue that will look fabulous for my friend's spring wedding.

We saw Jessi at one of the most derelict events I've ever been to. I only say this because I've been to a few and My husbeast and I were the only people who weren't vendors at the Glorifying Women's Expo, that Say's something. 

I'd seen Jessi and her Product on Monday at the Moonlight Bazzar at Red Rockstar Bar, but since I don't like hot things, I had avoided her. HOWEVER.. This time I had the Husbeast. and he is an avid consumer of all things HOT and spicy.  This was a good match. Jessi was awesome. She allowed him to sample each sauce, telling him about the components behind them and even offered some to me. Sharing with  me a brownie bite that was decadent and made with her blueberry ginger sauce. 

In the end, we liked them So much that we bought all 6 flavors. Yes, You read that right all six bottles now have homes in my kitchen. We will certainly be new customers as long as she's making these delicious condiments.

Totally a gorgeous venue, if you're looking for a place to have your wedding or other special event. What is not to love about floor to ceiling windows draped in diaphanous curtains, or marble floors that are originals to the building. The Vault is steeped in History, and will make your event something so very memorable.

I have driven past this TBBCW a few times and wondered what it was. Was it just a brewing company, or was it food too? Since the husbeast and I were both out and about, we decided to stop in and check it out.

The evening was absolutely mild, so we opted to sit outside in the bar patio area. With the fire tables and the over head bulb lighting, it was fun and festive. And of course, it was just beautiful at sunset.  Our waitress was perfect, she was quick, friendly and informative, and I especially loved her backward written tattoo. Great message to one's self. 

We ordered our drinks and placed our order for Hummus and Lebeneh with naan. It's been AGES since I've had Lebeneh - a tangy goats milk cheese with a yogurt like consistency, that's absolutely decadent to the tongue. I was Thrilled that they had some and even happier that it was well made and came with a really flavorful hummus. The naan was crispy perfection. 

The husbeast ordered a steak and bacon chop salad, and I ordered the Rat something shepards pie, with a side salad,  the side salad... I should have stopped there, it was HUGE. A meal in itself.  I couldn't finish it, so it went into a box.  The meals themselves were tasty and good. Both portions were large and yes. VERY VERY yummy. 

Will we be back? Sure will!

A friend told me about the Honu last night on FB, given that I adore Hawai'ian inspired food, I made the decision to go today! I'm really glad I did. 

It's located right off Main street in Dunedin, in an adorable cottage/bungalo that is very welcoming and bright. Parking might be difficult at first, but Dunedin has plenty of street and public parking so that's that. 

Once inside, I was seated and the specials were gone over.  The menu itself was quite extensive too!  I decided I wanted to do things the Hawai'ian way, and went for the plate lunch: Agave Pork, green goddess slaw and potato mac salad.  The table next to me, three wonderful ladies also made the same order, so we shared in the community of the same food and chatted while we waited. 

When the food was delivered, it was obviously made fresh, smelled great and tasted even better! The green goddess slaw was unlike anything I'd ever had before! It was light, fresh and tangy, the flavor was bright on the tongue and I really couldn't get enough. The Potato-mac salad was out of this world.  The agave pork was a bit on the sweet side, but I liked it fine. 

I actually ate every scrap of food on my plate, the portions were JUST right!  I opted for dessert, because really who can resist? I chose their "that's how the cookie crumbles" Which was immense! warm chocolate chip cookies, fresh whipped cream.. all served sundae style. Honestly it would only be made better if they sold it WITH their macadamia nut ice cream!

Over all, the food and the service were absolutely amazing! I will most certainly be back

I found this shop completely by accident! I love spice shops, I love the way they smell, I love the way they have their displays.  This store was special in the way that they will let you taste the blends as well as smell thing. I've never encountered that before. 

Service was impeccable. The gentleman running the store too an interest in what I was needing, how It could be used, and showed me some recipes I might be interested in.  He even had a powdered chili pepper that my husband would love.  I will -certainly- be back.

While checking for new places to eat, I stumbled across Caposey's by sheer accident. No, it's not new by any measure of the scale, heck it's been in New Port Richey for as long as I can remember, but as far as I can recall, I've NEVER been there. 

By happy accident, the husbeast and I arrived on the coldest day of our Winter - so far- and we were able to be seated immediately, according to the owner, it had been PACKED but the lunch rush had just ended. Normally she had more seating because of her outside seats, but due to the chill, she couldn't in good consciousness offer that to us, and thankfully she was right. It was COLD. 

We were seated right by the door, but that was fine, and our waitress came to get our drink orders, Both of us ordered coffee and ice water, and that was returned to us quickly. When she came back, we placed our order for our meals, I placed an order for the french toast combo based on the recommendations from other yelpers,  and the husbeast got the Chicago sandwich, with the soup of the day - stuffed pepper. 

We didn't wait very long, my Scrambled eggs with 4 pcs of bacon and 2 generous slices of french bread dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar and served with warmed syrup.  The husbeast's sandwich was brought out with his peppers and his soup and a side of au jus. Everything was REALLY tasty. The bacon was perfect, they offered me a side of salsa for my eggs which I happily took and the french toast was divine!  THe husbeast was a member of the clean plate club so I'm guessing he liked everything too! 

Will we be back? You betcha! This is the Kind of place you want to become a regular at.

Came here on a date with my Darkness. We opted because it was nearby where we were staying.  It was close to closing when we walked in, so it was quiet and not at all heavily occupied.  

We were seated and our waitress was over almost immediately.  We perused the menu and the chips and salsa were laid down. I have to admit I LOVED the sampler but the best part was the black bean dip, that was my ultimate favorite. 

We weren't terribly hungry, so we ordered the Nacho Appetizer, the Guacamole and the steak tacos.  We'd share it. We had NO idea how big the Nachos were.. LAWDY! That was such a huge portion, we didn't finish it. The Guacamole was Delicious, especially topped with the roasted corn.  The only thing we were disappointed with was the steak taco, and that was because of the masa shell. Took that off and the flavor returned. 

The service was perfect, the food was great and the company was better than anything else.  We will most certainly return.

I've driven past the Golden Spirit Alpaca Ranch a lot, and I never knew it was an agribusiness. But when my friends returned home from Scotland and wanted to see if we could check in on them, I was game. 

We bought our tickets on line for $30, 8:30 am tour on a Saturday morning.  The house is set back from the road amid old oaks. The inside is now a gift shop with a taxidermied Alpaca when you first walk in that is so wonderfully done.  Up stairs is a bathroom with a door that does not lock.  

The tour guide (I didn't get her name) was very nice, knowledgable and friendly, she gave us the history of the ranch and info on how to tell a llama and an alpaca apart, as well as the different types they have on the ranch. 

We then set out to feed the alpacas.  They each have different personalities and while most were skittish, several were sweet and loved their necks and bonnets pet.  We even got to see Simon up close, though he didn't want to eat from our hands. 

It was a lovely way to spend the morning and support agribusiness in Florida.

The heart of the Tarpon Springs sponge docks holds Hellas' bakery and Restaurant. It's a great place to dine, to people watch and to grab a cup of coffee and a slab of bakalava. There really isn't anything better to do on a Saturday afternoon, than sit at one of the outside tables, sipping your java and licking honey off your finger tips. The food is fantastic! Opa!

This is a Tampa Icon, and sadly it is soon to be closing it's doors forever!

A comprehensive costume house, Features offers you the ability to rent or buy costumes that run the gamut from your most basic tunic and fabric shoulder piece for your Christmas padgent as a wise man to the most ornate Lady in Waiting to a Queen.  Each costume is marked with a rental/purchase price and all are fair. 

There is a HUGE makeup selection, wig and accessories are all available. The customer service is always helpful and friendly. 

If you're looking for a good sale, right now absolutely EVERYTHING is 50% off while they liquidate their inventory. I suggest if you're looking for theatrical makeup, you go and invest in some quality Ben Nye product! Their lipsticks DO NOT MOVE, not even through eating fatty pork! I know, I tried it this weekend!

I've driven past here many times but since I was with a friend and we were looking for things to do, I figured why not. 

The place is bright and clean, but older. They aren't brand new and have been serving the area for a while, but that's ok. They serve the community with love. 

My friend and I walked in and were seated immediately. We had a very friendly waitress, and our order for Coffee and water, as well as a Reuben and a Hamburger club were taken right away. 

The food came out quickly as the place wasn't terribly busy at 1:45 pm, and what came out was HOT and delicious. My Hamburger club was delectable, It was tasty and fresh, the bacon really added a lot of flavor.  

The only "complaint" I have is that there were too many fries.  How is that even possible? It was, but that's not a complaint, it's really a good thing. Keep up the good work, I'll be back.

Stopped here for breakfast as i was headed out to Spring Hill to go get my Mom's car.  

It was a sit anywhere kind of place, and the service was beyond good, it was by far some of the best I've ever had. The waitress was wonderful. I told her I hadn't had any sleep the night before, so she took the small coffee cup off the table and replaced it with a big mug. 

She took my order, and within minutes it came out. The food was DELICIOUS. I ordered the ham and cheese omelette, with breakfast potatoes and an English Muffin. I think I age just about every scrap. Ok, so I was hungry. 

When I asked for my check, my waitress asked if i needed a coffee to go, I said yes, and she came back with her largest cup to go.  She was AWESOMESAUCE.

I drive past this place frequently and finally decided to stop in.

They have La Segunda Bread. That's some damn fine Cuban bread! 

Feed the cows! For a small price, they will give you a helping of veggies they've cut up for the bovines out back and you and your littles can go feed them. They will thank you, your kids will thank you and you, might just enjoy the break from being on the computer. 

Get some local produce, fruits and veggies, some herbs and meat too.  THey've got hives now, so Honey is there as well. 

This is a nice agribusiness!

Review #3000

I gave my former CM a choice as to what would be my 3000 review and this is the business he chose (It was waiting in line to be reviewed).

I visited Haslam's Books in early March, before the big worry about Covid struck, so I had a chance to browse the stacks and enjoy the scent of old books and paper.  I'm a HUGE bibliophile! 

I looked through the voluminous stacks of old books, through the new books and even the huge children's section because why not! Everything here is pretty special if you ask me.  Haslam's is an institution in St. Pete.  It is the epitome of a bookstore, complete with ghosts and cats. 

While I was there, I caught myself in the Metaphysical section and found a book that predicted this whole current situation. I REALLY should have bought it. I'm kind of kicking myself now, I could have seen how everything turned out. 

TL/DR  If you're a book fan, if you like reading or just LOVE the smell of books (Because that is a thing) Go to Haslam's (when quarantine is lifted) and give them some of your money, You'll thank me later. This place is the utter bomb!

Fellow Yelper, Stacy Z recommended that I stop in and check this place out. She wasn't wrong. 

First thing out of the box is this store is clean, it smells good and they have a huge selection of merchandise. 

They have all the tobacco for all your smoking needs. There's a respectable sized humidor with a good selection of varied sizes/style and quality of cigars. 

They have all your assorted smoking parephenalia, from rolling papers to lighters to the occasional (or more frequent) water pipe.  Their selection is quite nice. 

They also carry CDB and Kratom at this time. 

Join the VIP program and get 10% off your purchases each time you come in  -simply mention it.

After trying out a disappointing cupcakery in Orlando, I was happy to find this little shop in the strip mall near where I was eating lunch.  The cup cakes were fresh and lovely in her display case, each one marked with a Heart, noted a filled one. All cup cakes were $1.50 save for the canolli cup cake and that was $1.75 because it was real canolli filling and a bit more expensive to make. 

The shop smells wonderful upon entering. It is a bit no frills but over all, that's fine. It's the product that you're looking for. The cup cakes are small, but GOOD. Moist cake, good icing, not too sweet but very tasty. The husbeast had the blueberry filled one, and he said it was amazing, I opted for the Salted Caramel cupcake and it was DELICIOUS. 

I will come back when I'm by this way again. This is the kind of place that needs to be heard about. They're a little off the beaten path, but well worth the journey.

The crown jewel of Tarpon Springs. 

If you're coming to the sponge docks, make time to visit Hellas too. The food and service are genuinely impeccable. The gyro's are flavourful, the souvlaki is tender and the flaming cheese is, well, in a word  HOT!

You can get all your Greek cuisine favorites like: Skordilla, stuffed grape leaves, Avgolemono soup, spanokipita,Horiatiki Salad, Greek Salad, a broiled octopus and even a whole fish that is then deboned at your table side. 

And while you're there, don't forget to visit the bakery for even more absolutely decadent treats, the bakalava is some of the very best you'll ever eat. 

OPA!

A town and country institution. I've driven by this place a thousand times and never once gone in.  So one Sunday morning, after staying at the Beau's home, we opted to go here for breakfast.  He apparently used to go here when he was a kid. 

Opening the door was like stepping back in time. It is most certainly a greasy spoon, but that's fine.  The place hasn't been updated in 30 years but the food is good and the service is amazing. 

We both had breakfast food, I ordered their skillet and ate nearly every bite of it except for the potatoes, the man ordered eggs, bacon and french toast.  Mind you, it said 3 pieces of french toast. Most places that'd get you three triangles, right? Nope here, it was 3 whole pieces of french toast and that stuff was amazing. 

The coffee was kept full and hot. 

Will I be back? You know I will.

If you are looking for something COMPLETELY different than your ordinary Halloween Experience, The Vault of Souls is it. 

This is -not- your daughter's theme park experience, this is an Upscale experience that you won't find anywhere else. An elegant night of fear.  Don't come with the expectation of lines, of others body to body with you as you're herded though some chintzy maze, because that is not here. 

What IS here?  It is a lush party in the arrival, where you will be given your number. While you wait, you can enjoy ghostly music and dancers as they float through the room. Have your aura cleansed and be read by the resident ghost hunter.  Enjoy hand passed appetizers or a drink from the bar as you wait for your time to come. 

When your number is called, you will be brought down to the Vault, here you will be given a choice of which path to choose, and that choice is WHOLLY up to you. This is a nonlinear event. There is no ONE way to go. 12,000 sq feet of space for you to look through. You are encouraged to open drawers, read everything and touch.. just not the spirits, though they MAY touch you.   Each vignette is special, there are spirits in each room that will speak with you or not. They will interact with you in a different way. Your goal, to find the way out. They are just happy to see you. 

It may take you as little as 20 minutes to get out, if you just briefly look things over, but it can take 90 if you thoroughly investigate and immerse yourself, and this is something you DO want to immerse yourself in. The scenes are beautiful, the Spirits are engaging and it is a world that has been masterfully crafted by a Storyteller who is beyond comparison. 

When you do find your way out, you can wind down a bit in the Gin joint, enjoy the music and dancers that perform for you, and of course the delectable libations. Or have your tarot read as well as desserts and gelato up stairs in the reader's clearing. 

A couple of things to note: the event starts at $100.00 per ticket, and goes up to $400.00 Each ticket tier has it's benefits, and it is reservation only.   HOWEVER Each ticket comes with valet parking - in downtown Tampa, this benefit alone is amazing.  There is a dress code, Please don't come dressed in sneaks and a Tee, Come dressed to be immersed in the event, as if you were going out to the theater, Just, Please Ladies, no High Heels. The vault contains uneven floors, so spike heels are not suggested. The event is for 18+ and up, no children will be allowed.   -YOU- will be wearing the masks and asked to not speak while in the vault, this is so that the spirits do not follow you home. 

Come enjoy a night of paranormal fun, a night of elegant fear with a sinister twist. The spirits are expecting you.

I'll admit, I've not stopped in here before because I wasn't sure how it would be. I was skeptical, because it looked sketchy to me.  But the beau was craving BBQ and we agreed, it sounded good and was pretty close to home. 

We arrived around noon on Saturday, we sat and our waitress was there quickly. She was friendly and welcoming.  We took a few minutes to look over the menu and when we were ready, we placed our order - All of us getting the brisket and each of us choosing a different 2nd meat: I got the chicken quarter, there was pulled pork and sausage.  Sides ranged from Okra to cole slaw, Mac and cheese to green beans. 

When we were done, there wasn't Anything left. We consumed it like locusts. It was THAT good. Everything had so much flavor, good texture and the sauces were really good too. 


Now that we've tried it, we'll certainly come back. The guys didn't get to try the amberjack spread, and they're really wanting to.

So upset I do not know where to begin.
I will call the store later today and try to get my issues resolved, but basically they wanted to do $1300 - $1400 worth of (according to my dealer) un-needed repairs and they did a shoddy job on my oil change.

I would up paying for a 2nd oil change and a completely different roster of repairs at the dealership.

I am very hesitant to ever come back here.

OK, This review is based on my U-haul rental in February...

wait for it...
1993.

I was a student at Penn and moved out (one way) to San Francisco.  (Wow - I can't believe I came back!)

The entire experience was a miserable wreck - literally and firguatively.
The truck was filthy and had a governor (speed max) on it so we could not go above 55 - which on cross-country 60 mph roads (where most travel at 70-80) was downright dangerous.

NEVER AGAIN!

I received a flaming email from someone at this restaurant immediately after I posted my review.

My review stands and I stand by what I experienced.  I had a horrible time at Mixx and now, after being harassed online there is no way i will ever return here.

Nope.
After I wrote my last (negative) review of my once-loved Qdoba, we went again.
I needed a catering size Pico and a catering size Guac and chips.

Every time I do this (and I have now done it 3 times) I get charged a different price.
This time the manager (who was running the register also) tried to charged me $8 for a catering size bag of chips (enormous) which is not what I wanted or needed.

I forked over the $10, took my guac, pico and chips and left.

Not happy.

Twice in a row now.

Not coming back.
So sad. My 12 year old loves it here and I used to like it, too, but no longer.

My bad.  My mistake.  I shoulda known better.
I stopped in for a "squagel" (whole grain with cream cheese).
I was given a number (73) and told to wait.
I waited about 3-4 minutes.
Not worth it.

Sat like LEAD inside my stomach.

I did it before a few years ago, and I guess I forgot.
Now I remember.

I will not be back to Cosi.

Just had an amazingly AWFUL experience at Mixx.
It was about 7 PM on a Friday night - but the place was slow (about 3 tables occupied).

I ordered the sushi/sashimi combo.
When it arrived (After the iceberg lettuce salad) the "white tuna" (likely escolar - certainly not albacore) sashimi tasted fishy.

The server had it replaced with yellowtail - which was good.

Then I tried the tuna, snapper and salmon.
All were cut poorly and less-than-fresh (not spoiled but certainly not prime).

I ate only the sushi and left most of the sashimi behind.
What happened next was really weird.

The $23 platter came to $24 and change - so I looked for cash and decided to leave a horrible tip.

I left $26 and proceeded to leave the restaurant.  Then a lady came out (not my server) and chased me down to give me my "change".  I said (over my shoulder(, "No, it's for him".

She thrust the change at me and said "No!" "I'm not a beggar."

She was really pissed off at my horrible tip.

Oh well.

There is no way in hell I will return here.

There's a reason most of the maki is covered in mayo, spicy sauce or crunch.  You can tell the quality of a place by its sashimi - and this place is sub-par.

Do not get the "new" Shrimp!  Ick!!!

We came in at a time when almost every item on the hot bar was running low.  I tried the Surf & Turf bowl for the first time the the shrimp were old and rubbery.  There was hardly any steak left so the lady scraped out the "required" amount of dried out beef cubes.  The black beans were also old but then they brought more and she plopped a scoop of "new" beans over the dried out old ones.  I thought about asking her to re-make the dish but did not.  I should have!  

Awful!!!!  
Waste of $8.40 plus tax.  Cold items (Salsa, etc. were fine).

So sad because I often really enjoy Qdoba - for those fast food times in my life.

On its literal last legs - everything is in disrepair/neglect due to the impending closure.

Good news?  Cheap ticket prices and no crowds.
Bad news?  Don't eat any of the stale old food and do not use the rest room if you can avoid it.  Ick!

It's like viewing a movie in an abandoned, decaying theater.  Sad, sad, sad.
Depressing.

I loathe McDonald's and fast food in general, but I did go here once out of sheer desparation, hunger and broke-ass-ed-ness.  I got a $1.00 McChicken Sandwich, no pickles - It came to $1.07 and I just barely had the change scraped together.

What a humbling experience.

I pray it won't happen again.

OK, as many of you know I loathe chain restaurants, but I tried (I really did) to keep an open mind when a colleague of mine - who likes it here - wanted to have lunch here.  (She also graciously paid for lunch - and she is a good friend.)

After our server took our orders she quickly brought drinks and water.  The Philly-tap water tasted just awful.  So I drank my diet coke and kept quiet.  (I am a big water drinker and had a bottle of brita-ized water with me.)

We passed on the 2 for 20 deal and both got salads. I had the Shrimp/Avocado salad and the salad, was really not good.  Strangely enough the lettuce was just fine, but the shrimp were so oversalted/seasoned.  Also the avocado had obviously been chunked much earlier in the day as it was brown and slightly dried out.  Eew.

And thank god I got the gloppy green avo-based dressing on the side.  It was awful.

Thus, my faith in Applebee's has yet to be restored.
Next time I'll go to Shiroi Hana across the street.  What possesed me?  Oh yeah - a colleague wanted to come here.

We were here for a corporate event and the place really needs some SERIOUS help.

Disgusting public restrooms.
Shabby, dated ballrooms.
Mediocre service.

I bet it was the cheapest place the group could find - so that's why they chose it.

NOT recommended.

ZERO Stars for what we referred to as McDEATH when i was a grad student at Penn.  There have been shootings, stabbiong, roberroes and muggings here over the many years.

Yet somehow - McDeath remains open.

Let's not even talk about the "hood" demographic servers and patrons alike.

And of course the scads of loiterers and homeless, down & out West Philly types.

AVOID.  AVOID.

I was dragged here by 2 coworkers who actually LIKE it here - I think because it is very cheap - $4.50 - $5 for a personal pan pizza at lunch - and quick.  I have never been a pizza hut person and have not eaten Pizza Hut food at all in the past few years - except for once when My (then) 9 year old demanded it.

Blargh.

First of all the service is non-existent - Gail tried her best but even with only 2 dine-in tables everything from ordering to serving food to especially getting our credit cards back was painfully awkward and slow.  Gail is a sweetheart - and has good taste in 70's music (which, by the way, was blaringly loud - not at all "background" music) but she can't handle the lunch crowd all by herself.

The toothless guy making the pizzas was also pleasant but left to fend for himself.

Not a fan.
And I will only go back when dragged back.

The good part?  Super cheap - even with tip.
The bad part?  A greasy, salty MESS of a pizza.  

Maybe I could attempt wings next time?
I am frightened.

Pretty awful.
I have tried it twice - once back in abour 2008 when I worked nearby and got overly doughy steamed dumplings for takeout (filled with a greasy mystery meat).  YUCK.

Aside from the grotty digs and crappy location - next to the XXX rated theatre, I ventured in again.  And I will never do this again.

I played it "safe" with chicken and brocolli.
I have had better food from a cart.

Never again!

Oh lawd!  I just ate the most horrifc lunch at E & C.  A meatloaf sandwich - wherein the meatloaf contained multiple bone fragments.

Sooooooo disgusting,

Fortunately they took it off the bill.

I used to tolerate E & C - I will now NEVER go back on my own accord.  (Alas, some co-workers insist on dragging me here.)

BLECH!

Epic fail.
I should have known better after my kinda-sorta-bad experience the first time.

I stopped by to pick up a toasted english muffin.
I saw a sign for grits - $1.99.  So I ordered that too.

The lady scooped and scraped the grits from the bottom of the steam-pan and then shouted, "Guys, we're gonna need more grits!".
But she had enough for my order.
When I ate it back at my office the grits were so salty I literally spit out the first bite and trashed it.

Meanwhile, the english muffin was barely toasted and flabby.

I called them - and they have agreed to refund my $1.99 when I stop in tomorrow - but that will be the last time I come here.

So disappointing.  Many of my colleagues come here every day and love it - but they are now 2 for 2 in the "bad" category with me.

You're kidding?
Based on grungy digs alone my family (of 3) walked in and out.

This is clearly a take-out only place (a few card tables and zero atmosphere for dining in.)

The sushi case was empty.
Empty.

There is no way I would get sushi here.
I am reticent to even try the Chinese food.

Maybe it is, "all that".
But I was scared to even go there.

Dayum!  I wish I had read my old reviews.  I got the schwarma - again pre-cut meat (at lunch - 11:50 AM) and bone-dry and COLD.  So I had a salad with cold, dry meat on top and threw away most of the meat.  Just icky.

I added some sauces and toppings but was told hummus is $.79 extra.  What???  And the have no baba ghannoush.

There are so many fast-casual Med spots (CaVa, Naya, Naf Naf) that I will not be returning to Zaffron.

Just skip this place and eat elsewhere in the Liberty Place Food Court.
There is a reason their line is shorter than the others.

Not happy.
Not happy at all.

OMG!!! It's awful.  Maybe I just hit 'em on a bad day/time -as it was on a weekend at about 4 PM - kinda between the lunch & dinner crowds.

Place was empty - so service was quick.  I ordered 1 item - a steak taco.

Then I noticed the fruit flies.  Swarms of 'em - near the "hot sauce" bar area.  Ugh.

Appetite destroyed.  I paid for my taco and took it to go - and ate it next door at the Dunkin' Donuts while my 4 year old stared at the donuts and decided which one she wanted.

Taco?  Inedible - and the vision of those flies was dancing thru my head.

Chucked the taco.

Don't think I'll be back.

I hate to give 1 star reviews unless a place truly sucks - and this place...
OMG it's awful.  I walked in (I was meaning to go to another place nearby but they were closed) and it was so unbearably hot in there - no A/C in July and all the refrigerators and freezer units give off additional heat)  I had to walk right back out. (After taking a good look around.  Ugh.)

Not goin' back either.

A McDonald's seems so out of place here amogst the shi-shi shops on Walnut Street.  That and it is a haven for local down & outs seeking a $1 McChicken and a coke or coffee.

I rarely ever set foot in here. (But admittedly I have once or twice.)

Yick!

I'm sorry - but ANJOU is WEAK!!!

From the outside it looks appealing.  The menu sounds like it's gonna be good - if a bit pricey.

MEH.  MEH. MEH.

Sorry.  Nothing special here.  Go to Pizzicato, Mizu, Uzu or some other nearby place.  There are oodles of them to choose from.

You'd think for a place called "Brodo" that you'd be able to get a decent cup of soup.  Well, you'd be wrong.  I stopped in today after trying to get into Nom Nom (which was mobbed and they don't offer take out.  WTH?  But that's another review...)

Brodo looks very sleek, new and nice.  Prices seem low enough - but it ends there.
I got a 1/2 sandwich (Veggie) and a cup of soup (their version of Italian Wedding).  I asked if I could substitute cheddar for the American Cheese (which is a waste of tasteless fat/calories) and was told they only have shredded cheddar - but i could get swiss or provolone.  So I opted for no cheese.

Meanhwile, I start to eat it back at the office and there is a weird horse-radish taste to the mayo.  I think they goofed and put horseradish mayo on it.  Weird - but not bad.

The soup was salt-laden and NOT even close to being delicious.

Not goin' back.
Sorry.

I spent $8.40 for the combo (no drink).
Oh, and the line waas not bad when I went - but if there is a long line, don't wait in it.  NOT worth it.

So sad, because it looks very nice.  I sure do miss the Naked Chocolate Cafe though.

Read Catherine L.'s review - and my sentiments are echoed.

A close friend and I came here  for dinner.  When we had trouble finding the place (we were at the "A Full Plate" end of Liberties walk, we called on the phone and a nice man came out to get us and walked us over.  This, alas, was the best part of the meal.  Things got progressively worse and worse.

First we were seated (inside - at our request) and our drink order was taken by a clearly overworked, spread-too-thin male server (who was very nice and tried his best - 3 stars for him).

After taking our meal order we waited, and waited, and waited...

And waited some more...

And finally asked harried server to please bring our chips and salsa (as he had just brought some to another table nearby).  We were starvin'!

The smoky salsa and salsa verde arrive - in hot bowls "fresh from the d/w" and thus we had warm salsa.  Yech.  And the salty chips were "chipettes" (or to be mean - crumbs.)  smashed to smithereens.

OK, things aren't so great - but we await our entrees.
Wow - Impressive looking - I order a single beef shortrib and feel like Fred Flintstone.  This thing is HUGE.   Gi-normous!  Like a brontosaurus rib.  Alas - there is no sauce.  My friend orders an "OK" pair of Chicken burritos that are no better than Qdoba.  

So here's the kicker...  About 3/4 through the entrees, frantic server appears again with a six-pack of sauce.  He gives me a bottle of HOT and a bottle of SWEET.  I pour out a bit of the sweet onto my plate (disregarding the crust around the rim of the squeez bottle) and dip my meat in.  UGH!!!  Racidity Central.

The HOT sauce is not rancid - and has a nice flavor but it just to hot for me.

My appetite is now officially GONE.

And shortly thereafter, so were we.  I will not return.

Such a disappointment.

Selection and location 4 stars, Surly/Bitchy customer service - 1 star.
Price 3 stars.

I stopped in here looking for leotards (hopefully something sparkly or USA themed - they had none of that) for my 8 year old's recent gymnastics obsession.

Now, part of this was my own damned fault as I was talking on my cell phone (engrossed actually) as I entered the store and basically waved at the woman and pointed to my phone.  I tried to wrap up the conversationbut the person went on and on and I dd eventually hang up.

By then the woman had wrttenme off - which kinda sucked, because I did end up finding 2 "close-out sale" short sleeved, solid-color, basic leotards at VERY inexpensive prices (and thus non-returnable).

This place is Kickin' it old-skool - literally.
Leos, skirts, ballet shoes, tap shoes, costumey things.
A dancers paradise - save for the surly service.
Glad they are still around - as this type of place is a dying breed.

Do not multi task in this store!!!

Not sure why so many raves.
The place is so dingy and needs a good cleaning.
They do offer many authentic dishes like Duck Tongue and Frog, but we were not interested.

We got the ($32) Peking Duck and the meat was dry.
Eggplant with garlic sauce (the best dish of the night) was so hot we could barely eat it.

Food is very spicy - even dishes marked mild (but that is also part of the Szechuan experience).  Compared to Han Dynasty in Philly - this place is awful.

Not coming back any time soon.

Not good, Temaki.
I am sorry to report that our last visit (albeit it was "Dining Under the Stars" aka "Chaos out in the Heat") the service and food quality both were Just "Meh".

Mike tried hard to please us but after receiving 2 warm and watery diet cokes (they were, thankfully, removed from the bill) and cold, soggy sweet potato tempura rolls - I am not a fan.  Also, this is now the 2nd time the salmon tasted "fishy".  Fresh raw salmon should not taste this way.

Unfortunately for me, my 8 year old ADORES the place - especially the tasty shrimp shumai (served with a saffron cream sauce and fresh sweet corn kernels) and california rolls.

We'll be back - and pray you won't take it out on us, but food and beverage quality needs to improve.

The female manager is very sweet.
I think the guy hates me.  (He might really hate me now.)  

:(

Ook!  I am close to giving it 1 star only.
Dirty, nasty store.  Dairy is unreliable.
Produce is Questionable.

Cashiers?  What Cashiers?  When yo9u can get a register open there is a huge line and the lady looks pissed off.  (I would be too if i had to work here.)

YUCK.

Packaged goods only.
I would never buy veggies, meat or dairy here.

And it's a shame - bordering on a sin.  This area of Philly NEEDS viable grocery stores - and this is all we've got.

SAD, SAD, SAD.

Meh.
You get what you pay for and they do go crazy with the Kewpie Mayo here - so either avoid rolls with mayo or ask for sauces on the side.

I had seen the place (walked by) and read the other yelp reviews - but for $8 (2 maki - you can get 3 for $12) I figured I'd give it a shot.

Service was icy-cold at first (one lady was kinda mean - she was prepping a table for a large party that was not there yet and clearly did not want to stop to help another table) but then my "real" server showed up and was very sweet. Vibe is kinda icy too - with colored LEDlights that change color and rock-hard banquettes that are straight up & down and not that comfortable to sit at.  Water was brought instantly (YAY!) and green tea (which I had to ask for) was free.

I ordered a yellowtail scallion roll (had decent yellowtail but hardly any scallion in it) and a roll with salmon and grilled onions (loaded with mayo blobs on top which I scraped off - seriously, at least 3-4 tsp. of mayo.  Eew).  It was also supposed to have masago but there was NOE in there - and when I asked the (sweet) girl about it she said they don;t include masago on the lunch special.

These people are certainly cost consious - as the lettuce & dressing salad indicated (no tomato, no nothin').

I am in absolutely NO HURRY to come back here - yet - oddly enough - I ran into a friend here with another aquaintance and the LOVE it here.

Meh. Meh. Meeeeeeh.

Sorry.

Doma and Vics cost more - but are sooooo much better.

Nope.

Ok, I came here on the advice of co-workers who basically said "Don't eat at Long River" - which is across the street from my office.

So I trudged over the 2-3 blocks to Golden Chopstick, stood in a pretty long line and ordered a Chicken & Stringbean lunch special with brown rice to go. "Light on the sauce", I implored.

Service was friendly and the order took about 6-8 minutes to come out (not bad considering there were 7 people ahead of me.)

Walked the take-out grub back to my desk and voila.  Tasteless - abut thankfully not greasy due to the lack of sauce.  Beans were the best part - crisp.  Chicken (thankfully white meat) was bone dry and flavorless.

Not sure If I'd ever come back.

Now I am really in fear of Long River.  This is supposed to be the "good" Chinese place near my office.

Oh well.

This ain't my bag, baby.
The free one hour of "build your own" martinis was great - for FREE - and then it was $5.00 apiece after 9 PM.

My husband got completely hammered by downing 3 of the candy garnished concoctions is 55 minutes.

It was just way too frat-boy in there - and the lack of waitress servce made it impossible for us to even order food.  (Thus we were both pretty trashed while drinking on an empty stomach.)

The cute bartender-boy made me a very tasty cosmo - but I was just as happy with my cranberry, vodka & lime.

If it were not for the "free" ploy marketing - we'd never have gone in.

And unless there's another freebie - we won't return.

OK, for some reason I could not get the name "Beefsteak Charlie's" out of my mind - and indeed, this place takes me back to 1984 - but not in a good way.

The good parts?  Our server Brian was attentive and kind - and took the overly-salted French Onion Soup off our tab without hesitation - nor us asking.

The salad bar is also nice - and very '80's - one whole section is mayonaie-based salads (pasta, potato) so I skipped that part.

My friend ordered a "Queen Cut" prime rib - and I had 2 bites of it - he ordered it medium and it actually came out rarer than I had thought it would.  It was OK but no flavor to it other than (you guessed it) salt.

Do NOT order the French Onion Soup here - it looks great and the cheese/crouton are good - but the beef stock is like eating a salt lick.  I could not eat more than a few spoonfuls ($4.99) what a shame!

Just OK.  Not in a hurry to go back.
Strangely enough - with the exception of no "pick and peek" shrimp on the salad bar and no "Free Sangria" (remember that???) this place could be a Beefsteak Charlie's.

Ah, the '80's.
Childhood.
Recaptured.

I guess...

Nope.  Now we go tot he Giant in Aston which is far better - albeit more crowded.

This Giant has out of date dairy products (have seen that twice now - so READ THE DATES!!!) and a picked-over produce department.

Step up your game, Giant in Brookhaven!

Meh.  2.15 for a bottle of Dasani?  I shoulda gotten a latte for $2.19 instead.

Mediocrity at its best.

I am so NOT a fan of Cosi.  After eating in them in NYC in the early 2000's when this chain emerged - it seemed cool at first.  And - if the bread is fresh and hot (before it solidifies into cold cardboard) it actually tastes pretty good.

The hungrier you are the better it'll taste.

Meanwhile - the overpriced sandwich fillings are mediocre at best.
There are better places to waste (I mean spend) $9 bux.

Sorry.  Not a big fan.

Well, I got dragged back to "the pube" for a free event for a charity that I support.

While I love the charity and am thankful to the Public House for sponsoring the event, the food and beverage service here is sub par.
Mediocre chicken wrap (with an odd mayo-ish sauce) was inedible.

Hummus and veggies were safe - but blah.

It's still not my thing.

Sorry - but i have had way, way, way better Afghan food.  I love Afghan food - the bread is usually sooooo good.  Sansom's was dry and re-heated in a toaster oven.

The rice (reheated as well) was good, but not great.

The salad - scooped out of a tupperware - obviously pre-prepped way in advance was wilted and over dressed.

The Chalaw Kadu (Normally a fave) was so greasy I had to pick out the chunks of pumkpin from the sauce and discard it.

I was the ONLY person in here on a Thursday night - and finally another single diner came in.  The place was dead - and I bet I know why.
Get it together, folks.

I'm sticking with Kabul. (And oh, how I miss Pamir - now closed - in NYC)

Well, Jay was not here tonight and I bet he'd freak if he was.
The place has gone downhill - and quickly.

My tuna dumplings were stuffed with Kani Salad (fake crab) not lobster as shown on the menu.  The weird, overbearing, barely-english-speaking waitress leaned in sooooo close to me it was a BIG violation of my personal space.  To top it off, she cleared my plates and brought a check - assuming I was done.  I was actually contemplating ordering 1 more roll or a piece or something - but i was so put off, I just paid the bill and left.

The 2 sushi guys behind the counter were friendly enough - but they were so busy filling takeout orders (dead for eat-in, busy for take-out) that their work was just SLOPPY.

I am unimpressed, Jay.  Get it back together!  You have some great items on the menu.  They need to be executed better - less kani stick and more REAL seafood, please.

I came here out of sheer desperation and they carry Eukeneuba small breed senior.
What I noticed - the place smells AWFUL and there are tons of puppies and PIGS ($399) for sale.

This ain't right!
Stop supporting puppy mills.

2 young adults (late teens?) seemed to be running the place.

I generally hate Cosi - the bread is like hot cardboard - and the food is not my thing, but I stop in to this one every once in a while for iced coffee.  A good friend lives near this one so we'll meet here, grab some iced coffee and hang out with or without our kids in tow.

The restroom is abhorently filthy though.  Yick.

I am so not a Cosi fan.
The bread tastes like stale cardboard a minute after it cools - and g-d know what its doing inside my stomach.

The prices are high as are the caloric contents.

This particular location - inside 30th Street - is often crowded and the service is awful.

Not my thing, baby - and 2 stars is being nice.

I like the Neuvo-Latino-Americano grub here.  The place has moved locations and is now a bit larger.  Chips & Salsa are always fresh 7 tasty, too.

I wish I could give a more substanital review but I ate here so long ago - and at the old location - so I'd better just keep my mouth shut.

This is the City Nails in Penn Center - the yelp map is incorrect.  Meanwhile some of the City Nails are good and others are disgusting.  This one is in-between.  The Guy who runs the place is very nice.

They still use sub-par base & top coats and will try to pass them off as Essie or OPI.  

Come during a non-peak time and get better service.

My daughter loves it here - but she's 6.  Meanwhile they have always been very kind and generous to her.

It's hotel food - and usually I might give a place like this 2 stars - but I am giving 3 due to VERY nice service and we lingered a very, very long time.  The main dining room was nearly empty (but the bar was hoping for happy hour) on the week night we went.

A good friend of mine who is vegetarian got the pasta with goat cheese which looked very good.

The female server was superb!  Very attentive and brought us apples and nuts (with a nut cracker) to snack on.

While there are far better choices nearby - this was a warm safe place to kill a few hours on a bitterly cold afternoon.

On the scale of Chuck E. Cheese's this is a solid 2 stars -maybe 3.  We attended a friend of our child's birthday party here and it was typical chaos. Many of the games were broken and the place was clearly understand.

However, the staff that was there was very attentive and the lady who helped our party was great/  Very patient with the kids and the birthday girl got the "1000 ticket" ticket in the ticket blaster.

 I generally loathe Chuck E. Cheese - but my kid loves it - and we did have a good time.

We bought our 2007 Hyundai Sonata from Fred Beans.  Over the years my family and my husband's family have each bought many different cars - new and pre-owned - of different makes from Fred Beans.

Between them and Foster & Kardane (and we were friendly with the Kardane clan back in the '80's) they pretty much OWN the D-town automotive scene.

Competitive prices and salespeople who don't make you feel like a target.

Good repair work, too.

I'm sorry to hear that Sub S. had a bad experience.  Ours has been fine - and we still have and love our car 4 years later.

I had not been to a benihana on over 20 years - and back then ist was teppanyaki only (no real sushi). Ah, the '80's - and we all owe a debt to Rocky Ayoki.

The sushi selections have improved a bit - although fish selections are limited and the Hamachi Hand Roll I had was sub-par.  (Tamago was froze - for $2.75 a piece).  Prices were too high for that sort of mediocrity.

Service was harried - we were seated on a rainy Sunday at 7 PM in the bar area, albeit with our picky 7 year old who did not care for her $3.90 Strawberry Lemonade.  (She had water instead.)

Edamame was boiled within an inch of its life.

My MIL had a tasty steak teriyaki - surprisingly yhe best of the lot.
Oh and for $4.00 a single round blob of chocolate Hagen Daaz was unceremoniously plopped in a dished and thrown at my child.

Not in a hurry to return.

OMG I practially live here. (And not just as a commuter rushing thru every day.)

Every 2 weeks I have a 1-2 hour wait here to pick up my little girl.  It's always iffy as to exactly when her deadbeat dad will return her safely home - so I know every cop in the place.  (Alas, they are rarely there when you need them.)


I also know the Amtrak red caps Rich & Rich (the cigar smoking one is our fave) who work weekends.

We also know the nice Korean lady who owns the flower stand with her husband.  They give my little girl flowers every so often. 

And the lady who chops the fruit at the Smoothie stand is nice too.

Oh, and Susan with the hairy upper lip who man's (or wo-man's) the Hertz rent-a-car booth is a godsend.  She allowed my daugheter to play with the (broken) yellow hertz phone and "call" people.

There is good and bad in every situation and I sure am making lemonade out of a BIG Honkin' Meyer Lemon that life handed to me.

Service was excellent from manager (owner?) Melinda and our server Ledesha.
