Food was just OK. (But I am pretty spoiled from NYC and Philly.)  The sashimi platter I had ($26) had some winners (fluke and sea bass) and losers (paler, poorly cut tuna, odd tasting salmon and cheap escolar "white" tuna).

DH ordered a specialty roll (called the "Thank You" roll) for $18.  Oy vey.  Strange "crunchy" fishy topping that we did not like.  Lots of fruit -mango and strawberries.

That said, we will be back - but try more affordable, conventional maki next time.
There is no way I would get sashimi here again.

High prices (2 roll lunch combo is $12, 3 roll is $15.  I pay $12 for a 3 roll combo at Vic's in Philly.).

I am not sure how I feel yet - so 3 stars for now - and hopefully it will go up - not down.

Standard Starbuck - mid-size location (Not huge and not tiny).
Decent service - youngish staff of disinterested baristas just "doing their job".

Efficient but not warm nor friendly.

Drinks were fine - I got my kid a decaf frappucino so she was in 11 year old heaven.
Ice tea was fine.

No big whoop.
Glad it's here to get our four-bucks fix.

Had dinner here last night and it was just OK.
Greek salad that came with dinner was good but lettuce was overly wet.  (Odd.)

Chicken Francese was swimming (drowning) in a heavy buttery sauce.  The chicken itself (I pulled it out of the sauce and put it on another plate) was good though.

Not a holy grail, but a much needed place in a culinary wasteland.

I received help over the phone and it was fine - I signed up for a 2 year membership for myself and my husband.  We got the cheaper one with 3 miles of towing.  There is also a more expensive membership with up to 100 miles of towing.

We shall see what happens if we need these services over the next 2 years.

It's just OK.  And I always forget it's there - but I have a friend who works in the design center - so we had soup 'n salad there for lunch.

Oh - and now they charge for bread.

Food is OK, Service is OK.  Not super and not awful  Just middling.

Oh well.

We have been here Twice over the past 18 months that we have lived in the area.  Our 8 year old loves Friendlys - but my husband and I are not big fans.  This location is relatively clean - but the service is sooooooo slow.  I mean bordering on ridiculously slow.  We came last night for a late dinner - around 8 PM and did not get our food until 8:40.  Kiddo was getting a little shiny by then - but finally it came out.

Meanwhile my husband's salad was "blah" and my "build your own" burger was actually pretty good.

Not a holy grail by any means - but with kids in tow it's a safe option.  Just don;t come here f you're in a hurry.

Single surface ice facility for USFSA (Figure Skating) plus a few public skate times each week - call first to be sure.   No real seating.

A few minor level competitions per year.

They have a 1/2 day skating camp in the summer.

Locker room is very old, Training room is small. We are spoiled by Iceworks.

Very nice lady runs the skating program. 
Apparently, Scott Hamilton trained here for a while, decades ago.

Better.  The new server/hostess Brianna (sp?) is lovely and we were warmly welcomed at 8:50 PM on a Tuesday.  (Our first choice was CLOSED.  Ouch.  Again, I ask - don;t suburban folk eat dinner?)

The secret?  Order cooked items.  The sweet potato roll and Shrimp Tempura roll were absolutely fine.

I stay away from sashimi, nigiri etc. here.  Been burned too many times.
Meanwhile my 10 year old gobbles up the shrimp shumai (frozen, I think) in a delectable saffron cream sauce with fresh corn.

We had a fine experience here with our (then) 3 year old - but it was about a year ago so maybe since then it has gone downhill?  We had burgers and chicken sandwiches and my daughter's kiddie meal came in a paper car.  She loved it.

We had a nice lunch here and would go back.

I have passed this place many times over the years but it always looked creepy to me so I never ventured in.  Well, today I HAD to get breakfast stat - and decided to go inside.

Good food (solid diner fare) to go, nice ladies at the counter.

I'll be back for a lunch soon!

Odd.
Tacos & Donuts???  

I did not have any donuts but they looked good.
I got a Chopped Salad with overcooked (but tasty - great spice on it) steak.

Would have been great if the meat were at least pink.  (It was well, well, well done.)

$8.47 for a cheap lunch.

Not rushing back though.

This is more of a friend-with-an-expense account place.  The faux shi-shi atmosphere is really getting played out.  I enjoyed my meal - the tiger shrimp were flavorful, but I would have prefered the heads to have been removed.

I also thought the prices were not worth it for the quality and quantity of the food.

Pearl is nice - not bad, really, but there are much finer dining experiences to be had.

Went here today for lunch with an old, old friend who I haven't seen for about 15-18 years.  (Really.)

We both had lunch specials - He got a 3 roll for $13 and I got a 2 roll for $10.  Both came with a choice of soup or salad and we both had a good (albeit generic) fresh salad with tasty dressing.

The Ginza roll was excellent - cooked salmon, mayo, oinion and tempura flakes.  Crunchy and very Americanized - but good.  My yellowtail roll was just OK.  I can tell the quality of this place is not high end - but for a cheap sushi lunch I would, in fact, go back.

Service was unassuming and prompt - the large dining area was not even close to busy - maybe 4 tables occupied.

I would never waste my money on all-you-can-eat sushi (or all-you-can-eat anything for that matter) since I don't go for quantity - I need quality.  This place is OK - but no holy grail.

Our 7 year old is a crafting wiz - albeit I am inept at such things.  We visited Jo-Ann on a surprisingly busy Sunday evening.  4 people working in the IMMENSE store (understaffed) but still, friendly and efficient service.  Amber (??) who was running the show, cutting fabric, re-stocking bolts and cashiering was great.

They honored all 3 of our 50% off (single item) coupons.
We got alot of needed fabric, notions, needles and supplies.

LOVE IT.

This is the location in the Pennsport Shopping Plaza - right next to SuperFresh.  I actually have had great luck in here - and especially during the semi-annual sale events.  Candles for $5.00, old packaging designs for body wah & lotion for $2 or $3.

The sales associates greeted me and were friendly and helpful.

Sometimes the store is very crowded and other times absolutely dead.  I like to shop when it's not crowded - so I like that.

Glad to have one that's not in a mall. (Especially since the one on 17 & Walnut closed).

Most choices were really great (avoid the chickenparm - awful.) like my crab-stuffed ravioli, over broccoli rabe.  St. Louis Ribs were fall-off-the bone tender.

There is a slight "SYSCO" pre-fab element to the food - but for the most part we love a nice weekend lunch here.  Burgers (patty melts, southwest style) are a solid choice.  Upgrading to Sweet potato fries is a good idea!

I jokingly call this place Oh So Mediocre - but really it is pretty good.  The Korean lady who runs the place is very, very nice and always asks about my daughter.  The hot & cold food bar is fairly clean with a wide variety of choices, some of which are actually healthy.  (Be careful - many of the hot foods are loaded with oil/fat).

If you really want something good here, though - skip the "pig bar" and head to the back for a fresh grilled turkey burger.  You'll have to be prepared to wait several long minutes - but it is worth it.  Cheap and tasty - not at all dry.  I got my T-burger with Ketchup, tomato and lettuce.  3.75.

What a deal.
Oh So Good.

Now that I am working in this area, I must confess that I am frequenting Qdoba far too often - however the Craft 2 menu allows me to eat one, save one - and thus not consume the requisite 750 cal minimum.  (Beans plus rice plus any meat choice = about 660 alone).

Also the "new" whole wheat tortilla is 270 cals (not 330).
Additionally, they introduced a slightly spicy brown rice (a few calories less per serving than the white) in February 2013.  I don;t like it though, so I still get the bad-for-you-white rice.

Still, a cheap, calorie-bomb on the go.
Oh - and I have to give a shout-out to Antoine - the cute (nearly looks like L'il Wayne!) cashier who is super cool and friendly.

My husband had a minor surgical procedure at Rothman's Surgi-Center on the 4th Floor and he was well cared for - but there was a long wait (we arrived at 8 AM and he was prepped right away but not seen by the doctor until close to 11:30 AM.  Eek.)

We got outta there just after 1 PM.

Follow-up care and administrative staff seemed good also.

There are some great little gems tucked away in this part of town.
The Clay Studio, The Wood Turning Studio - there's a bunch of artsy studios, a few BYOs scattered about and yes, tha Park-o-minium and other parking facilities.

Easy walk to Old(e) City - let's not start THAT debate again,  (Whether or not Old City has an "e" on the end of Old.  What ehvs.

Anyhow, I like this area just fine.

Great cappuccino and other espresso based drinks.  Plus good salads, hummus and snack-y foods.

Free wifi and comfy, homey seating.  Cute barristas (male & female) and well poured shots of eeeeeeeeeee.

Comfortable homey environment.  Beats the hell outta fourbucks.

I'm a fan!

Needed Urgent Care (ER/ true emergency) for our 11 year old and had 5 star treatment from all staff, however we arrived on a Monday night at 6:10 PM and although triaged right away were not seen until around 9:20 PM by a resident.  (over 3 hours waiting and waiting.)

Once seen treatment, diagnosis and medications arrived quickly.
Mikey (female) the respiratory therapist was truly exceptional and a wonderful care giver.
Laura, patient liasion, was terfic and the Doctor - Dr. M. W. Attia is terrific.

I hope we don;t need to come back but if we ever do, we'll be coming to Dupont!

Beautiful facility.

Wow - I coulda sworn i reviewed Susanna Foo a looooong time ago, but I guess not.  Anyhow - went there again (3rd time) last night and sat putside - which I usually never do.  It was a surprising lovely evening.  I had been here twice before for lunch - which was good but maybe only 3 or 4 stars.  

Last nite's meal solidified the 4 stars.  Service was wonderful and attentive (maybe because they are slow in the summer??).  We stated with virgin Golden Pineapple Mojitos which were truly delish.  FRESH pineapple juice and mint - perfectly balanced.

My dining companion was a close friend from out of town who walked by and wanted to go here.  She is very health conscious and ordered the salmon in a light (not too salty) black bean sauce over a crsip tender bed of TERRIFIC baby bok choi.  It was accompanied by a Cocunt "polenta" that was so silken it tased and felt like coconut flan.  Almost dessert like.

I had a started of an Ahi Tuna Sampler (which I have ordered before and I just love it.).  At $17 it is small and expensive - but the quality of the tuna tartare and the fabulous accompaniments make it somehow worth every delicious teeny morsel.

Instead of an entree I had the COMPOSED  $12 salad with golden beets, candied Walnuts, sliced yellow tomatoes, microgreens in a delectable, sweet but not cloying , light vinagrette.  The salad came with 5 small goat-cheese wontons - that looked like over-stuffed tortellni.

I ate 3 and gave 2 to my partner.  They really didn't do much for me.  The goat cheese inside was almost like a bleu?  Goat gorgonzola maybe?  Too strong.

But the salad and all the other compnents was terrific.

If you think Foo is past her prime or somehow not "all that" anymore - I urge you to give it another try.  At dinner.  (It was way better than the 2 lunches I had previously.)

I had a basic (el cheapo) oil change over my lunch break.  I was told it would take 45 minutes (there were a few cars ahead of mine) but it actually took about 70 minutes.

Guys were friendly and seemed knowledgeable.  Not too pushy about upgrades.

I got a $10 off coupon from the jiffylube website so after taxes and discount I paid around $40.00.

Yes, it's expensive.
No, you can;t do your "regular" shopping here but it is terrific for taking kids.

We came for the "No Kid Hungry" cupcake event (for $3 kids could decorate a chocolate or vanilla cupcake) and the kids (both age 9) loved it.

My daughter loves to shop the bulk candy department and there are some unique holiday gift ideas here also.  Look into their cosmetics (Pacifica for CHEAP!) and chocolate bar sections.

No, it's not cheap - but there are some unique items here that I can't get at Whole Foods (aka Whole Paycheck) nor Trader Joe's.

I confess, I am a Sephora and Ulta shopper - I price compare on ebay, also and it pains mne to pay retail after spending YEARS in the spa industry.  Meanwhile, I stock up on Tweezerman, NARS, Lorac, MUFE (Makeup Forever) and other staples at this Center City location.

The ever-changing line up of staff (usually young overly-made up MUAs) is friendly and usually pretty knowledgable about makeup.  Skin care?  Not as much.

Meanwhile, I love Sephora - and have since its creation.
It continues to evolve.

Upon my teen daughter's pleading request, I caved and picked up 2 take out items at the now-dreaded Qdoba in Springfield.

What'd'ya know?  Everything was fresh and great again.  It helped that there was a new (at least new to my eyes) manager and that we cam at 11:50 AM on a Thursday before the lunch hordes had descended.

Steak burrito and Steak burrito bowl (both with Guac) were both great.

I truly hope the "badness" of the past is in the past.
Management and team makes all the difference.  The female team lead (front counter) is friendly and good!  Give her a raise!

Now that I work right near this Target, I can't help but run in from time to time for household goods, frozen entrees for lunch on the cheap and of course, a latte from Starbucks.

Lunch hour can get busy - but if you go at 10 - 11 AM (sure, my boss will love that!) it's ded in there.

Weekends?  Another story.  Parking lot is big but gets full and a bit of a cluster getting in and out.

Bonus:  I can stop at Petsmart, too.  And Trader Joes' is walking distance.

Lots of shopping in a compact area.

The desserts OTHER than ice cream are so yummy here.  The gargantuan slices of pecan or apple pie (topped with yummy ice cream, if you wish) are so great.

The sandwiches and soups are good too - but defintiely save room for dessert.  That is what  this place is famous for.  In the old days we'd get cream of broccoli soup here - so good - so rich and a slice of warm pecan pie with ice cream on top.

Mmmn mmmn!

I really love Angela - the owner of the new Wings to Go on the Corner of Vine & 15th.

So, I ordered a bunch of party platters (boneless wings & buffalo shrimp) for a party I had.  Everything was piping hot, fresh and perfect.

I really want people to support this much needed busines on an otherwise "dead" block.  Need wings?  Catfish?  Shrimp?  Corndogs?  Come here to get them.

This remains our go-to Rita's and the young teen staff is friendly and polite - in the summer (evenings) the lines can get longer.  We enjoy an occasional custard or "wooder" ice treat here.

Tip:  Ask for the kiddie size to save calories and money.

Benches and tables to sit at outdoors.

This place is a strong 4 stars - maybe even 5 (but it's just not the same tier as a Nobu).  It's homey vibe and decidedly 2-3 star service (not bad - but weird service - a bit inattentive and spacey - hard to get a check - hard to ask questions) knock me down to a solid 4 stars.

Bright, homey decor and even the bathrooms feel clean and light.  Owner is very nice and has gorgeous eyes.  (Waiter was pretty hot, too.)

My good (lacto-ovo-vegetarian) friend and I had a delicious lunch there today.  I have 2 yummy glasses of the Lemonada (1/2 mint iced tea mixed with 1/2 lemonade - the PERFECT summer refresher.  My friend had Greek Coffee - made the traditional way.

For our lunch he had Shouksouka (delicious) - great for a breakfast or brunch, too.  Very rich and filling.  I had the Kanella platter and for $12 it was the perfect way to sample alot of offerings.  For me the best part were the Dolmades (stuffed grape leaves).  Now, I realize that everybody and everybody's grandma makes 'em dirrefently and Kanella's are distinctively sweet with currants and luscious Pine Nuts.  The falafel, Zucchinni fritter and yogurt were all good too.  The only thing I could not eat was the spicy tomato salad (next time I will order it made mild - if they can do that).  It was soooooo peppery with a "harrissa-like" taste to it.

Baklava was served with syrupy orange slices and was chock-full-o-nuts.  Very good for $3.50!

We plan to return.  But - please - beef uf your staff and service.

I have been taking classes at Fuel House (I buy packs of ten classes for $80) for 2 months now and I have lost over 5 lbs.  I am seriously considering the Unlimited Monthly membership.

There are a few classes that are NOT Zumba - like "Boot Camp" and Tabata (a high intensity interval training 30 minute workout).  There are also a few "easier" classes - which I like since my fitness level is low.

If you are a serious athlete - this is probably not the place for you, but if you are a middle-aged suburban mom with pounds to lose - come on by!!!  It's perfect for me.

Went for a casual happy hour and thoroughly enjoyed my $8 (normally $12) cocktail.
$3.25 for a club soda.  Ouch.

Also loved the seared tuna appetizer with - get this - portabello "fries" - so tasty.

Excellent food, service and one-of-a-kind atmosphere.

Perfect for a date or romantic dinner for two.
Great for a proposal or special occaision.
Expense-account-worthy.

Boy can they throw down!

N.B. - I can't get any cell phone service up here.  Oh well - with that view, who cares.

So glad that Angela and the gang are still going strong after 2 years, delivering wings, ribs, corn dogs and FABULOUS fried shrimp to Drexel/Hahnemann students and others.

Wednesday is 1/2 price boneless wings and Monday is the Shrimp deal.

Love to take my 6 year old here - as I, probably should not even contemplate eating this.  It's an OCCAISIONAL treat only.  And we get celery in lieu of fries - and I get a salad - so I feel a little less guilty.

Bring on the fried shrimp!
And corn dogs. (Big and slightly sweet batter.)  Umm!

Saget's has been picking up and dropping off my dry-cleaning and this service is pricey - but so worth it as a timesaver for me.  John (the Manager) is terrific and custoimer service has been gresat - they bill me monthly and charge it right to my card.

Best of all the cleaning is expertly done and my clothes look great.

Once again, Eyesite and Gene have gotten me a WINNER!!!

I am in love, love, LOVE with my new glasses.
They are from Belgium and very unique looking.
They make me feel like a butterfly when I wear them.
They are so light and comfortable - and GORGEOUS.

I absolutely love to shop for eyewear - and I go to lots of higher-end shops, but EYESITE is where I purchase my frames and lenses.

Simply the best.

Went there again tonight - and while the decor sure ain't 5 star - the food absolutely is!!!

Shrimp Scampi .
The world's BEST baba.
Simple grilled veggies with chunks of feta.

So cheap (cash only at this location) and so tasty.

Killer waitresses - they attack - beware!

Xo-Cheat on your diet!  It's Xo-worth it and Xo-great to come here.  I love the Oaxacan cuisine and kick-y cocktails with real tropical fruits used in making them.  I have been here twice already and, although pricey - and sometimes unbearably crowded, I will be back again and again.  It's Xo-Good!

The Aussie Bartender is muy, muy caliente!
Try a couple of Dona Florinda cocktails with fresh prickly pear cactus fruit.  Super Yum!

Came in for my 5-6 month prophy and saw Kara - who is a new hygenist and TERRIFIC.  She took text-book perfect bitewings (digital, baby!) and Dr. D is great as always. Plus I love LeeAnn (sp??) - the office manager.  Such a well-run place!

Plus I got strawberry prophy paste.

Wheeeeeee!

Philadelphia's Chinatown may not be the largest - but it has many wonderful things to explore.  Of course, the wonderful food - restaurants, tea houses, pastry & bake shops and grocery stores.  Also Chinese culture - and gifts galore.  Much fun to come here during the Chinese New Year - but to me it is even better to come here when it is NOT a celebration - just a "normal" day - like on a Tuesday or Wednesday in the spring or fall and stroll the streets and have a leisurely lunch.

Must explore Chinatown!

A few lucky PWCG members took part in a share of delicious, sustainable salmon from  OTOLITH SUSTAINABLE SEAFOOD in Philadelphia.  The 15 lbs of Salmon came in convenient (approx.) 1 lb portions.
 
With my first lb (I have gotten 3 lbs so far) here's what I made:
 
Karen Flam's "Grilled Gravlax".
 
Since I hadn't the time to do a proper "cure" here's what I did:
 
Dry-rub the clean, thawed salmon with:
 
1.5 tsp. Penzey's Shallot Salt
1 tsp. Penzey's Vanilla Sugar (yes, really)
A few healthy shakes of granulated Garlic
A few cracks of fresh black pepper
LOTS of fresh or dried dill.
 
Then, squeeze on the juice of one (or two) fresh lemons, or use 3-4 TBSP of bottled lemon juice.
 
Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for 4-6 hours (I couldn't wait any longer) - ideally - cure longer (and add some juniper berries - I didn;t have any).
 
Heat a skillet with 1-2 tsp of good olive oil and pan-grill (or use a real grill or grill pan).
I seared mine (First with skin side down, then flipped and seard the flesh side).
 
Slice thinly and serve.
 
Do not over cook!
 
My 6 year old gobbled up the small slice I gave her and asked for more right away.
She proceeded to eat about 4 oz!

I am giving 5 stars not so much to the coffee shop (which is about 3.5 stars) but to the FABULOUS customer service we got from Nicolas Capes at the MAIN site of La Colombe.

You see, we wanted to have individually wrapped foil pouches of coffee as wedding favors for our June 2008 nuptuals.  DiBruno Brother's couldn;t help us.  Neither could Dunkin Donuts, nor Cappriccio (though the manager tried).

The coffee favors available on "wedding" websites as favors is sub-par pre-bagged swill.

We wanted QUALITY - and with La Colombe - our guests got it - for reasonable coin, too.

We ordered a case (96 pouches) of the house blend and bagged each pouch in a cute little tulle bag, and added a Yankee Candle "buttercream" votive.  Between the coffe and the cream - our closet smelled heavenly.

The coffee favors were a huge hit and La Colombe is the ONLY Philly coffee place to come through for us.

OK, Brace yourself.  It's gonna be a long review.

3 of us went to R2L for an amazing dining experience last night.
And even though there were some problems (big ones) with service, the exquisite food more than made up for it.

Danny & Zaga - you "make your mamas proud".
That semi-open kitchen was running very nicely.  Your garnish chef, poultry man and line crew were in a good groove.

Daniel Stern's newest creation is in a gorgeous, dimly lit (and on a hoppin' Saturday night - very loud but still, surprisingly, comfortable) space.  The light fixtures, sculpture, bathrooms, stainless steel salt & pepper shakers (unused and unneeded) even the jacket of the wine list - all set off the gorgeous floor to ceiling views of the city.

Our lovely female bartender mixed us excellent drinks (brandy soaked cherries that are simply divine - I could eat a handful easily) and explained the menu while we waiting for our friend to arrive.

After we were seated our new and VERY nervous waiter (I think he had been there 3-4 days) explained even more.  We forgave him for using his notecards.

What was not so forgivable was the service snafu.

2 of the 3 of us ordered apps which were brought in short order after a delicious house-made bread.  The apps - which I truly recommend (those here with low food reviews - man, I think you may have ordered the wrong things) were the steak tartare (served in a rough chopped with plenty of shallots.  I ordered mine "not too spicy" and it was delicious.  Accompanied by crispy toasts with sort sort of butter (I think she said "beet butter" but it must have been golden beets as the color was a pale yellow).

My friend was not yet even finished his appetizer - crabcakes (which I did not try but he liked them and they looked great.) and his entree and side were brought out.

Then we sat.

And sat.

And finally said - "go ahead and eat it while it's still hot".  So he started to eat his (signature dish) Veal 5-6 ways.  So fabulous.  YOU MUST TRY DAN STERNS famous veal plate.  Accompanied by crisp butter-tossed broccoli florets.

So while he ate and my husband and I sat there and stared around - I said "This is a screw up". 

And, indeed it was.

First our (now petrified) young server came to apologize.  Next the manager came and said that our entrees were "3 minutes away" and apologized and said that they would do something "special" to make it up to us.

When our entrees did arrive - they were so worth the wait.  The filet accomanied by prociutto (I always spell that wrong) wrapped leeks (divine) just melted in your mouth - and the shortribs (want a little beef with your beef?) were good, too.

I opted to get an app as an entree - and had the unqiue -and uber-rich - lobster mac 'n cheese.  It was more like mezza-canelloni each topped/stuffed with small, buttery lobster medalions.  Served with it was a copious amount of rich, creamy cheese sauce - cheddar, gouda and something else.

WOW.  Don't miss the lobster mac!

To make up for the weird dinner service (AWKWARD!) they comped our desserts, cappucinos (delish - La Colombe)  and 2 of the 4 glasses of wine.

The pineapple cucumber sorbet was simply perfect.  Refreshing and "sang" on the palate.  Served over diced honeydew and plums.  The blackberry verjus sorbet was also good - but nothing compared to that Pineapple Cucumber.  It was capogiro worthy and obviously house made - served in perfect quenelles. (Can't wait to try the Kalamansi icecream and of course - who doesn't love a good gianduja?) Oh, my thighs!

My friend ordered the chocolate cream and apple pie (with a decadent sour cream quenelle beside it.

Also to make things "special they gave us an amuse-bouche pre-dessert of cinnamon panna cotta with a lovely rose-water sugar crysal topping and two picture-perfect fresh raspberries.

After dinner they served us each a crisp (not rock-hard) house-made cinnamon biscotti and - the best yet - buttery blueberry financiers (OK I can't spell that either).

KUDOS to your pastry chef.  He or she is a keeper.

Oh and Zaga is really a master - wow.

Such fun to watch y'all work.  If you can fix a few kinks in your service and have a more welcoming hostess stand - the 5 stars will stick!

Good work!  We can't wait to try your place in University City.

Oh - and they have a small private party room that seats 12 or so - and I hear a big one that seats about 100.  This would be a great wedding or rehearsal dinner setting.

And I bet plenty of marriage proposals will go down here.

Swanky, urban, romantic, high quality American classics with a BIG twist.

What a find!  What a lucky break!
My 11 year old recently enrolled in dance lessons and needed shoes, tights, leotards - the works!

DanceLine and their terrific staff saved the day.
They even have "Foot Undies" -  like little underwear for feet -used in lyrical dancing.

We'll be back!

OMG I echo Emily A.  I just discovered the Italian Market (I know, I know -what took me so long) and I went to Claudio's for home-made ricotta (so creamy, fresh and good - and CHEAP - $2.99 a lb.) and mozzarella.

Can't weait to pre-order a Burrate for later this month.  Burrata is Mozzarella with a creamy-buttery cream in the middle - so decadent.

I have FOUND my source for mozzarella.  Hooray!

OK, I bit the bullet and joined as an Unlimited Member for $50 per month.  My 9 year old kids loves it here too (but refuses to take the kiddie classes - she wants to take the ones I take - including Piloxing - a cross between boxing and Pilates - which is a terrific class.

I love the instructors here and many of the ladies who go here (there are a handful of men -it's mostly women) have become casual acquaintences.

I have nothing but great things to say about Fuel House.
Try the Zumba - but also try the non-Zumba offerings.

Jodi, Stephanie & the team are terrific!

Three cheers for the kielbasi boys (one of them was smokin' hot!) and their CHEESESTAK filled pierogies.

They gave our group of 11 a tour of the smokehouse - and we got to sample the turkey kielbasi, and several other varieties.

You gotta check this place out!  This is the real deal.  

$8.00 a dozen.
Cash only.

The Doylestown Farmers Market runs from late spring through mid-autumn in the parking lot at Oakland & Hamilton Streets.  There is a good selection of produce, meat, dairy, egg & beauty product vendors.  

I love coming here early in the morning when they are first setting up (don;t come too late or many of the goodies are sold out) and getting whatever looks freshest - Berries in June, Greens & Beans, and goat cheeses.

Great for kids & dogs.

Support your local farmers and farmers markets!
Bring cash - but a few places accept plastic.

Yes, they are high-end and expensive - but the frames are gorgeous.  (My French frames from face a face were 420 alone - plus 200 for the lenses and 150 for the sunglass clip which was custom made.)  Gene the Owner and Ala the optician were very easy to work with and the glasses were ready quickly.  (Just got  the matching custom sunglass clip.)

Ok that's $770 for 1 pair of glasses.  Egads! (Do NOT tell my parents who would FLIP out.)  I spent way more than I could afford - but they offered to charge my credit card in 2 installments - so that helped me out a wee bit.

I look great and am so happy.  Alain Mikli - eat your heart out.
I am so lovin' this place.  I will be back for sure!!!!

OK, I''m doin' it.

I am giving this mom 'n pop, cash only BYO the full 5 stars - based on that 5 star food.

Simple, fresh flavors - like a party in your mouth.

Yes - it's cramped and close quarters.  And there's a sign on the back kitchen door that says, "Beware Attack Waitress" and they are not kidding - those ladies can work it!  Yes - there are 3 terrific Laotian cooks, grilling up greek fish.  And it somehow all just works.

Perfectly.

A close friend and I (tip - do not come with an odd number of people - a single gets stuck at the counter, and a 3 will be forced to do a deuce with an extra chair) ate dinner here.  We split everything and ordered just right.

Mozzarella & Tomato salad was delicious, fresh, easy to eat and cut up home-style.  Perfectly seasoned.  Baba (no Ghanoush - ha, ha!) was some of the BEST I've ever had, bursting with charred eggplant flavor, olive-y richness and fresh garlic zing.  Not too oily.  Just AWE inspiring. (Great with that char-grilled pita.)

Next came a perfect Scampi (or Gambas if you were in Spain) with an abundance of fruity olive oil, garlic  and paprika.  Delish.  (Dip some of that pita in the oil when nobody is looking!)  And they are not skimpy with the shrimpies.  We had at least a dozen.

And a platter of grilled veggies - mostly Zucchini and Green Bell Peppers, but also a few red onions, pepperocini & olives.  It also had 2 BIG hunks of fresh (bulgarian or greek??) feta. I would have liked to see some RED peppers and EGGPLANT in there.

Drinks & Desserts are mothing to speak of here - and I coulda used a nice Lemonade - but the house brewed iced tea (in a teeny tiny glass) was good.  I had 2 of 'em.

I can easily seeing just giving this place 4 stars - it is NOT fine dining and there were a few service related flaws, but for pure, simple Greek/Med cuisine (and perhaps the East Coast's BEST BABA) I give them 5.

And I can't wait to go back.

And I kinda want to try the other location on 22nd Street, too.

Pick your own Strawberries in season has given me and now my little one spring after late spring of red-stained -face bliss.  None Such has great, fresh, farm-raised, seasonal produce.  (That means berry bliss in May/June and Corn late summer.)

We love it.  The same family has owned and run None-such for years!

I recently discovered the Italian Market (I know, I know -what took me so long?) and I went to Claudio's for home-made ricotta (so creamy, fresh and good - and CHEAP - $2.99 a lb.) and mozzarella.

Can't weait to pre-order a Burrata for later this month.  Burrata is Mozzarella with a creamy-buttery cream in the middle - so decadent.

I have FOUND my source for mozzarella.  Hooray!

Three Dog Night had a popular song that hit number 1 on the charts in the 70's. It was appropriately called "One". In the lyrics, it stated, "One is the loneliest number that you'll ever do". That may be true in love, but when it comes to dining sometimes you just want to dine alone.  If you do, avoid HWK. 

Not once, but twice I have been turned  away when wanting to dine here as a single person. The first time when I called to make a reservation, the young lady who answered informed me they preferred not to sit single diners at tables and that I'd have to eat at the bar.  At first I was content with that arrangement, but then she continued to tell me that  those eating at the bar can not select from the entire menu. At that point, I decided not to make the reservation.  I wanted the true HWK experience. After all the reviews have been amazing. 

The second time, I stopped in for early lunch while shopping the main drag in Maplewood.  Once again, I was told I'd have to sit at the bar and order from a "limited menu". When I asked if I could be seated at one of the hightops in the window, she told me she needed to save those for parties of two. The kicker came when I asked if they were already reserved and she said, "no".  I ate else where that day. 

What I do not understand, is why can I go to Chicago dine at such top restaurants such as; Girl and the Goat, RL, The Pump Room, Table Fifty-Two, The Purple Pig, Frontera Grill and The Publican and be welcomed with open arms. Many of the chefs at these restaurants have been on Top Chef and published cookbooks.  How is it that their establishments are welcoming to the lone diner, yet a small Maplewood restaurant is not?

I understand they have a small space, but if you are going to sit single diners at the bar, let them order from the entire menu. Before posting, I shared this review with other friends who are single diners and being women, they said for them they would not feel comfortable eating at the bar and would not eat here if a table was not an option. 

Disclaimer: I did dine here as a couple opening week and was not impressed. I contributed that to opening week jitters and wanted to give them another chance. It is a shame that I have not had that opportunity.

Oh, sad day in the land of Yelp. I have a new restaurant listing on my No-No list. 
Our lunch today at Tin Can Tavern was a total disappointment in all categories. 

We started out with chicken wings, that were rubbery and tough. It also grossed me out that I could see the yucky bumps on the chicken skin. I'm not sure, but I think they were just tossed in Frank's Hot Sauce and that was it. The Blu Cheese they served as a side, was thin and soupy. Two strikes, and we have only had our wings. 

The burgers were 5 oz of over cooked beef. When we placed our order, the server started to leave the table and Brad stopped him and asked if he wanted to know the temps for them. He said don't worry they'll be fine, we wont over cook'em. Really? 
Our burgers were served well - well done. It was like eating the leather sole of your shoe. When ordering, I did not realize they top all burgers with grilled onions and bacon. I pushed mine aside, the bacon was hard and cold.

Side dishes were equally as bad as the burgers and wings. My side was their House specialty Mac - n - Cheese. How they can call this rendition a "specialty" is beyond me. I took one bite and sit it aside. Brad took a bite and said he could not understand how a cook could taste this and say it is good to go, it tasted that heinous. Brad's side was Tater-Tots, it is kinda hard to screw up Tater Tots, but Sonic does a better job. 

The service was minimal, the two men working were more interested in watching the hockey game on the TV behind the bar.  They never even took the time to do a follow-up after we were served our food. Were they busy? No, it was us and another table of three ladies only drinking beer. 

Hell will freeze and pigs will fly before I come back to this dive bar.

I was looking so forward to my first visit Crown Candy Kitchen, after-all I have lived in Saint Louis for 33 years and had never gone. When it was featured on the Food Network for the Heart Stopping BLT, I knew I had to make time and go. I knew as soon as I walked in I had not missed much those past 33 years. 

The building outside appears so run down, we were not even sure they were open. At first I was surprised to see parking meters, in such a dilapidated neighborhood. Once inside the ambiance did not improve. The floor was in need of being replaced and the booths could use a fresh coat of paint. To be honest, the entire place felt claustrophobic and dirty. I was willing to over look those details and consider it character if the food was good, but it was horrible. 

My Heart Stopping BLT was heart breaking. The bacon was cold, rubbery and chewy as hell. I was expecting hot fresh off the grill bacon and it was far from it. Actually it tasted as if it were fried the day before. I've had better malts at Steak - n - Shake. I took a bite of the SO's Ruben and thought the Corned Beef was fatty and the sandwich had to much Thousand Island Dressing. 

I could go on about the limp potato chips, warm pickle and lackluster service, but I have got to shake this negative experience and move on. Thank goodness, we had Yelp Mints in the car to rid our mouths of the horrible after taste we both had. 

This is a tourist trap and I am embarrassed that it is representing my hometown.

Just take me out and spank me now. What was I thinking when I ordered from Imo's. I know what I was thinking, I was hungry and desperate for delivery at work. Being new to the Alton office I wasn't sure who would deliver and all I could find was Imo's and Domino's. I had two evils to choose from, so I flipped a coin and Imo's won. 

Amiee's talk thread about Toasted Ravioli got me kinda craving them, so I ordered some ravs and a 10" Deluxe pizza. Their deluxe has; sausage, mushroom, onion, green pepper, bacon & cheese. We all know which type of cheese, so I will not even go there. 

If these were my first toasted rav's, they would have turned me off and I would have never tried them again. They were rubbery, chewy and several out of the 10 were burnt. The so called "meat sauce" that was included for dipping was oily and nasty. The one rav that I did dip was spat out quickly. I only ate four of them and tossed the remainder into the circular file cabinet. 

The pizza was a major disappointment. I will be honest and say, I do like the thin crispy crust for my pizza and this was ultra thin and crispy. However, the toppings did not make the grade. The bacon was plentiful as were the onions. The green pepper was cut to large for me, combined with the sausage it left a stuffed pepper taste me my mouth. The mushrooms were kinda on the mushy side of being done. Again, we all know which cheese they use, but this was the most minimal cheese I have ever seen on a pizza. 

When I ordered I did not expect greatness, but I did want at least average.
What is sad, is my mom use to live in Godfrey and enjoyed going here for a personalized lunch pizza and a cold beer when I visited. She'd roll over in her grave knowing that this place in the last couple years has gone to hell. 

Thank goodness I keep a toothbrush & paste at work, because my mouth was in need of a good cleaning after this lunch. Also, another good thing about this lunch, I got a new addition to my No-No List.

It isn't what it use to be.  I remember when the food and service here was fantastic and breakfast was a treat. Today, the best thing we had was the Bloody Mary Bar and we made those ourselves. The pour of vodka was generous. 

We started out with the Irish Salmon with bagel. The salmon was good, the bagel was tough and chewy, the tomato a typical out of season tomato and the red onion was rather woody. 

I had the Hickory Smoked Ham & Pepper Cheese Omelet. The coloring and folding was close to picture perfect. When sliced into, is when it got disappointing. The inside was runny (the egg, not melted cheese) and the ham was ice cold. The side of hash browns were seasoned okay, but again they were cold. Either they don't have a heat lamp, or they had the potatoes made way in advance. 

My partner had the Eggs Madison, the portion of salmon was generous and the eggs were done well. The big disappointment was the hollandaise sauce. It was not made from scratch which you'd expect for the price they charged. It tasted and looked like Knoor's  powdered mix. Loving bacon, he also had a side as an extra treat. When they sat it down on table, I thought it looked like over processed beef jerky soaked in grease. 

The service was poor at best, the young girl serving us was very scatter brained and gave off the vibe that she'd rather be somewhere else. The guys serving around our table were more attentive then she was. 

Perhaps my expectations were too high, but when breakfast cost $55 I just want more bang for my buck. 

The highlight of the breakfast was running into a friend who retired from Louis Vuitton.

Yida, you haven't even opened yet and you already have left a bad taste in my mouth. Monday night we were at the Galleria and saw all the excitement around your entrance. People were hustling and bustling in and out and we thought a Margarita and Mexican fare would be a great choice for dinner. 

We entered with others and stood at the hostess stand as they organized tickets and chatted amongst themselves. Finally the primadonna host in a pink bow tie asked what I needed. I requested a table for two and this is how our conversation went:

Host: What time is your reservation?
Me: We don't have a reservation. 
Host: We only seat people with reservations. (In a condescending tone)
Me: Really? (Shocked and disbelief tone) I could see a fourth of the restaurant empty
Host: Yes. (More attitude in tone)

At this point the SO and I decided to go else where for dinner.  I looked at the young man shook my head in further disbelief and said "whatever". As I turned to exit, a manager who was standing by and heard the conversation, stopped me to explain why I could not be seated. What a shame the little host did not think to do the same.  The night was for Friends & Family of the opening staff only.  In other words, they basically were having a soft opening. 

I informed the manager that the internet stated they were open and with no signage outside or on the door stating "private party" it was misleading. He gave me a card for a free appetizer or dessert. The card was a nice gesture, but to late. With it being a soft opening, I hope that manager used this as a teaching moment for his front of the house. The young man's attitude totally turned me off from ever returning and even tarnished my opinion of your sister restaurant Black Finn.

This is where used car salesman got their sleazy reputation. 

I wouldn't shop or buy anything from this location. 

After leaving had to go home and shower to get rid of the sleazy grime feeling that I got from their sales manager and staff. 

We caught them in a bald face lie and the more they tried to save face, the more they tripped over their words. It was a prime example of the right hand not knowing what the left had is doing.

Free WI-FI and Special Menu for those who are 55+. 

Worst service I have ever experienced, or should I say NO SERVICE. We arrived shortly after 10 AM. The only words we heard from the hostess was, "Follow me". 
She walked us to our table, tossed the menu down and told us our server would be with us shortly. 15 minutes later, no one has approached our table. We couldn't even get the attention of those walking past us. We had enough, we got up and walked out.

This Denny's has been removed from my Breakfast list and added to my No-No list.  

Free WI-FI is a nice offering, but it doesn't get them any more stars.

What the Cookies?  That is a polite way of saying, "what the F". 

My advice to Grandma is to remove all those working Tuesday from her will.  I was so looking forward to her cookies after reading such great reviews here on Yelp. I was doing my "local" holiday shopping on Main Street and wanted a sweet treat to munch as I strolled & shopped in historic Saint Charles. Three times I visited her tiny shop and not once did anyone acknowledge me or offer me service. 

My first visit,  as I approached the counter I noticed there were only three (green) sugar cookies on display. I stood there reading the sign and waiting for the woman who was standing in the doorway to the kitchen with her back to the shop to offer assistance. She glanced at me once and said nothing, but continued to chat with her coworkers. I left in disappointment. 

I continued to shop and as I passed Grandma's a second time, I thought for sure more fresh cookies would be fresh out of the oven. I entered a second time, and same three cookies on display. No staff to be seen, only heard in the back. This time I was vocal and called out a friendly, "hello". I would have bought the sugar cookies. 
No one answered or responded to my call out.  Again, I left in disappointment. 

Why I gave them a third try after finishing my shopping is beyond me, but I did. 
Guess what, same three cookies on display. This time I noticed one of the booths was filled with day old  or it could have been 4 day old cookies being sold at a reduced price. Okay, I'll give them a try, only if someone would wait on me. 

There was a lot of commotion in the back and finally a man on a phone came out and sat down at the other booth that was covered in paperwork. He kept yelling a woman's name and no one responded to him. He said, nothing to me. He could have informed me someone would be out shortly, but he did not. All he did was yell her name again and continue talking on the phone. I turned and left for a third time and I will never return. Three strikes and you are off my shopping list.

Oh, Hell No. Consignment shops and places like Goodwill and Salvation Army have better furniture then VCF. 

On my mission to redo the living room, I was exploring as many options as I possibly could. Obviously I was not thinking when I made a stop here. We were promptly greeted by a "sales professional"  and I informed him what we were looking for; club chairs that do not rock, swivel or recline and no leather. 

He acknowledged my guidelines and lead us towards the middle of the store.  He then pointed out one chair that he thought we'd like. It looked good, so I walked over  and touched the arm. In amazement I said, "I can feel the frame."  His reply was an honest one, "Look at the price, what do you expect."  He was right, for that price I was lucky the chair frame was covered with upholstery. 

We should have left at that point, but we continued to follow him further through the store pointing out other selections. I did no more chair touching. As quick as he suggested another chair, I responded "No". Finally after I think the third suggestion, he politely said, "Perhaps we're not the store for you."  Wonder what gave him that idea? Once again, he was so right. 

The biggest plus of shopping at VCF is the fact that El Maguey is across the street.
After browsing through their store, I needed a Margarita.

Homer Simpson wouldn't  eat these donuts.

I never thought I'd see the day when I'd find a donut I didn't like. 
These are the most flavorless donuts I have experienced.   

I can not comment on the customer service, the box of donuts were brought in by a co-worker.

Hell No and I do mean Hell No. I will never step in to Mai Lee again and I was looking so forward to finally having lunch here. 

Strike One - We entered during lunch and the restaurant stank more then Jay's International on S. Grand and anyone who has shopped there knows that place smells bad. 

Strike Two - We tell host party of two, he says nothing, but turns around and starts to cross the dining room floor. Being educated we finally figured it out that we were suppose to follow. He tossed two menus on a table and kept walking. We seated ourselves at the table and started to read the menu. Water served without a word and server disappears. 

Strike 3 - 15 minutes pass, no one has approached us. During this time we realize the menu is for dinner and we were wanting a light lunch. As we were getting ready to leave due to the lack of service, our server appears. The SO says, "we were just getting ready to leave" and the servers response was, "Oh, you need more time." We then asked if they had a lunch menu, he responded yes and left to go get one. When he returned, he only brought one, it was a folded piece of paper and he pushed it down so hard on the table I am surprised it did not collapse. He then said, "Lunch, you only get Chinese, no Vietnamese for you." He then turned and walked away again. The point of coming to Mai Lee was to experience Vietnamese food, so we left. 

I knew from reading reviews here on Yelp that the service was bad, but had no idea it was going to be this bad. Reading more reviews before writing this one, I see others have had trouble with the "lunch menu" issue. @ Mai Lee, sorry to say with your pissy attitude I will not be back.

I was gifted Pottery Barn gift cards during my birth month of November of over $100. I was eager to spend  them, since I also became an G-Uncle during the same month. I wanted to spoil the new little boy addition to our family. 

I made two complete circles walking through the entire store and actually embarrassed for the staff. I have never seen a store so disorganized, cluttered and dirty. I know it was during the holiday season and they were most likely under staffed, but there is no excuse acceptable for how bad this store looked. I've refrained myself from posting pictures. 

Not one sales associate acknowledged my presence in the store. Also,  you could hear the frustration in the voice of one associate who was on the phone explaining to a customer why they didn't have an item in stock and most likely would not be getting it before the holiday. I felt sorry for that associate, because without hearing the other end of the conversation, you could tell in was a Karen. 

I  spent 25 years of my professional career in retail and the majority of it was in high end retail. So my I will give this store another chance, but for now they'll be added to my No-No Collection until they improve.

"Grease" is the word. Greasiest fried chicken I have ever experienced.
All the food here taste the same, like old "grease" that is long over due for a change. The cole slaw is flavorless, the crinkle french fries are mush, and Mrs. Paul makes a better onion ring.
Why people think this is the best fried chicken in St. Louis is beyond me.

Yesterday I did something that I can not believe I did. I went to a restaurant without checking it out on Yelp first and that was a big mistake. We wanted a new experience, and we got it. I also learned to not pick a restaurant by a road sign promoting what food choices are at the next exit on I-170. 

After we were seated, I made the comment to the BF that I hadn't checked Yelp. I quickly pulled it up on my iPhone and was shocked to see a 2 Star rating.  We took the high road thinking it can't be that bad and stayed. Reality check, when looking at the average Yelp ratings, they are spot on. 

When we looked at the drink menu, I got excited to see that they offered Jalapeño Margaritas. If they offer Jalapeño Margaritas, the food can't be that bad, can it? 
Yes, it can. However, the Margarita was the bomb, I loved how the jalapeño gave it an extra kick.  

They offer one serving of chips and salsa complimentary. If you want "bottomless"  you can pay $4. One serving was enough. The chips were thicker then most chips and also were over done for my taste. The salsa was chunky, but for me had way to much cilantro. It was overpowering to my taste buds. 

My entree was the Fat Taco Sampler, which included three tacos, rice and beans.
I choose the Grilled Chicken, Grilled Mahi Mahi and Blackened Tilapia.  All three tacos were topped with lime spiked cabbage, pico de gallo & homemade sauce. The amount of toppings overpowered the selected flavor/protein. The toppings were so plentiful you could not pick the soft tortilla up to eat. This was the first time I had to eat a taco with a fork. I picked through the toppings and just ate the protein.

Grilled Chicken - Huge pieces of grilled white meat, the best of the three. 
Grilled Mahi Mahi - Small broken up pieces that had little flavor. 
Blackened Tilapia - The overpowering toppings ruined this taco. 
 Rice and Beans were extremely dry and flavorless. The beans were pasty like a mud pack at a health spa. 

The service was okay, our server was attentive and did good touch backs with us while dining. However, a good Margarita and table service is not enough to bring me back to Flaco's Cocina.

Total disappointment - it was the most flavorless breakfast I have ever had. How they can mess up fried eggs & hash browns is beyond me. Over easy eggs were over cooked and the hash browns under cooked. The bacon & sausage were done well. Our side of biscuits and gravy had no flavor. Thank God, salt and pepper were on the table.
Service was friendly, but minimal. The server took our order and delivered the food, period. Which was sad, considering there were only three tables being served.

If you are a knowledgeable wine drinker, do not shop here. This wine shop caters primarly  to inexperienced young women who are drawn to "cute labels" and no substance.  Their selection of quality wines is small and limited. You are better off shopping at another local wine store where your selection of "good" wines are a smorgasbord. 
It's a shame that a prime location and presentation are wasted on such a selection of wines.

Give me the keys to the bulldozer, I'll drive. This shopping mecca should have been leveled years ago. There is no reason to come here, unless you are a "mall walker". 

How Sears survives is beyond me. 

Amanda Z., I don't think Ikea could even bring this place back to life, it is dead.

FREE Wi-Fi is available at Diner's Delight and that is the most positive point about this diner. With the majority of the reviews on Yelp being 5 Stars, I was expecting to be blown away with some down home cooking. Instead, I was served food that made me wish I was bulimic.  All the food was overcooked and flavorless. Yet it left a horrible aftertaste in my mouth. I couldn't get home fast enough to brush my teeth to rid myself of the terrible taste in my mouth. 

We had two Chicken Dinners with two sides, two ice teas and 1 Peach Cobbler with Ice Cream. Total cost of lunch $27 with tip. No alcohol, poor service and bad food. I think I've been robbed. I would not recommend this place to a homeless person.

I am happy to say, Cassy the owner and executive chef at HWK has contacted me and was in shock that I had the experience that I did. She assured me that was not their policy and was going to use this situation as a teaching moment with her front of the house staff. 

I appreciated her outreach and will attempt to dine at HWK again. Once I do, hopefully you'll see another increase in stars.

Before my last visit I quick tipped this business as a great asset to our neighborhood, I may have jumped the gun. It has a long way to go, but they are still fairly new, so I am sure they are suffering from growing pains. 
First thing that we found distracting is the big cooler in the lounge area. Find it a new home, it ruins the ambiance that you have created and it is a good feeling.
Secondly, don't down grade yourself with the Robert Mondavi - Woodbridge table tents. Your serving quality wines, and everyone knows Woodbridge does not fall into that category.  
The staff is friendly and provides good service, but while we were there they seemed to be over staffed and falling over each other. 
They've decorated well for the holidays and I love the heated front patio and the fire pit in the back patio. 
 I'll revisit and I am sure they'll pull it together so I can upgrade my # of stars.

I've tried to come back to you this year Ted, but it just isn't working for me anymore. 
Your custard isn't as thick and creamy as it once was and your staff is developing attitude. 

You are no longer the only custard in town, you now have competition and they are all serving up a better product. Even Andy the new boy in town is providing a superior cup or cone of custard. 

I know I am giving a big thumbs down to a St. Louis institution, but it really isn't that good, guys and gals.

Not impressed!!! Pissy attitude and overpriced pastries that are no better then those you could buy at your local grocery store. Perhaps after reading all the 5 Star reviews I was expecting to be blown away. Well I was and it was with disappointment.

First off the staff is very dry and look down their noses at you as if they are better then the customer they are waiting on and who is paying for their overpriced pastries. 

Secondly, even though some think the black glove they use to retrieve to macaroons from the case is cute, I thought it to be unhealthy. It is worn by multiple employees, waded up and thrown back into the drawer. It just made my skin crawl thinking how nasty and dirty that glove could be.  We did try the macaroons and for being a signature item, again I repeat, I was not impressed. 

Thirdly, the Easter Shortbread Cookies were kind of okay. The shortbread itself was good, but was ruined by a very unflavored icing. 

Best thing about this place is they serve Chauvin Coffee which in my opinion is the best coffee roaster in Saint Louis. 

There are a lot better bakeries in our city that offer more flavor and bang for your buck then this place and they will be getting my business.

Thank goodness there is practically a Walgreens on every other block, because this one is so discombobulated. It is cluttered, kind of dirty, in serious need of some TLC and has nil customer service.  I was expecting so much more being located in the Brentwood area, but once inside the store it might as well been in a ghetto. Management, you may have a high volume sales store, but do not let the small details get out of control. If this location was the one closest to my home or work, I'd switch over to CVS or drive to the next closest Walgreens. After all, there is practically one every other block. 

Also, be aware of the self important people backing out of parking spaces and arriving in the parking lot while talking on their cell phones. It makes for some defensive driving and a new addition to my Parking Lot Derby list.

I always have a basic cone when experiencing a new custard place. That way I can get a true flavor of the custard before adding ingredients  to make a sundae or concrete. The custard here was thick, creamy and no flavor.

When I returned to my car, I saw the "Colombo" sign in their window, which is a kiss of death in my book. Colombo is a pre-mix used by many small ice cream business and I have yet to see one produce a quality product. 

What a disappointment, I really needed a new place for concretes.

Big disappointment, it started out with poor customer service. The staff was just rude, and could careless that we were there.
We ordered an 8 piece box with biscuits and large side and an extra large side. Our order was carry out and when we got home, we realized they shorted us our second large side. Then when we opened our box of chicken, 4 of the 8 pieces were legs.
Stopping by the next day, to mention the shortage of a large side, we were told we should have come back that same night, that it was to late now. 
All they had to do is say sorry, and they couldn't even do that.
Our chicken business will be going somewhere else.

Boo-Hiss! Strange Donuts has lost their luster. They no longer are a shining star in my donut universe. The donuts we experienced this morning were bland, flavorless and dried out as if they were yesterdays product. Out of the four donuts purchased, not one was entirely eaten. Each only had bites taken out of them, before being thrown into the trash. These donuts were being shared between two people and both gave big thumbs down.

Banana Chocolate Peanut Butter - No banana taste at all and it was supposed to be the featured flavor. Very dry texture.  

Maple Bacon - This one could have been a winner, but the bacon was like chewing Bazooka Bubble Gum. I wanted to experience that contrast between salt and sweet.

Bart's Revenge - A chocolate cake donut with chocolate icing topped with crumbles of a Butterfinger candy bar. This was a repeat of a previous visit and it did not repeat the quality we had before. The donut was dry and the flavor of the Butterfinger could not be tasted, the chocolate donut dominated. 

Gooey Butter -  Another one we repeated and another disappointment. Again, I do not get the Gooey Butter flavor. It was more like a gas station cheese danish. 

Customer Service is always spot on friendly, but selling these donuts at $2 each is only worth 2 Stars.

Gotta give a special shout out to Sara D. for reminding me to write my review about the deplorable service that I experienced at Mi Caribe. It is a shame as a Brand & Marketing Manager she hasn't learned the lesson of, "don't poke the bear". I've been poked, so I gotta speak up. 

I'll be nice and start out with the only positive thing about the night I was at Mi Caribe. Since it took three hours to get my food that evening, I immediately had to have them put it in a to-go vessel to enjoy the next day. When I opened the container (non-eco friendly) with my Mango & Curry Chicken Wings, co-workers immediately asked me what I was eating and where I got them. Yes, the aroma was that strong and good being ice cold. Even cold, I enjoyed them. (Did I tell them of the horrible service - HELL, YES) These wings saved them from getting a 1 Star review. 

My main entree was the Chuleta. This is a thick cut pork chop marinated dominican style, deep fried and topped with onions. The seasoning was good, but I was not impressed with the cut of the chop. It was tough and had excessive fat on it. 

Now, I'll share with you the true reason for the low rating. The general manager on duty was a curmudgeon. He was rude and condescending. Our large group had made a reservation, so they totally knew we were coming and should have been prepared. Upon our arrival, Mr. Duval approached our table and gave us rules that we had to follow in our ordering. He wanted us to select from 5 or less entrees, to make it easy on his kitchen. Since he knew our group and another group of 12 were dining at the same time, perhaps he should of staffed his kitchen appropriately. Instead of putting the responsibility on his patrons. 

When I asked him, if we were 4 tables of 4 that walked in behind each other, would he be making the same request. He replied, "that would never happen". I don't know about anyone else, but I've seen it happen at many restaurants and I eat almost every evening meal out. However, I guess it doesn't happen here, since our table, the other table of 12 and a couple other small tables were the only diners that evening. Not being busy, there should have been no excuse for the length of time our food took to come out of the kitchen. 

The majority of this could have been avoided if they kept taking alcohol orders and got the appetizers out ahead of the entrees. Our group would have been content drinking and munching on our appetizers. Instead, we had to go to the bar to retrieve our additional drinks or order one from the curmudgeon and receive the wrong drink. My entree came out before my appetizer of chicken wings. 

Rude service and disorganization will keep me from returning or recommending Mi Caribe. It's a shame that their Brad & Marketing Manager is an agitator instead of one who resolves negative experiences at their restaurant. This is one restaurant that truly is deserving of being on my Terrible Two's List. 

When: August 2, 2016
Why: ISC

In all fairness, I thought I needed to give Vida a second chance. I have a friend who is leaving STL for a new job in Rochester, NY and we wanted to meet for a final lunch. With The Galleria being the midpoint for both of us, I thought I'd give them a second chance. So glad that I did, now I get to raise their score to two stars. Our waitress was so cute and perky, I just couldn't help myself from going out on a limb and giving the extra star. 

Being a Margarita lover, I know they are high in calories so I was excited when I saw that they offered a "skinny" Margarita. I would like nothing more then a good Margarita with a reduced amount of calories and my search will continue. The one Vida offers basically tasted like a watered down regular margarita. There truly was nothing special about it and it cost $2 more then a regular Margarita. 

Vida does offer a lunch special offered between 11 AM and 3 PM for $8.99.  You get to choose two from: salads, soups, tacos, enchiladas, quesadillas, taquitos and tostadas. We both took advantage of this savings and our "twos" were served with rice topped with black beans. The rice was extremely dry, but I did enjoy the black beans. They defiantly had better flavor then a can of Bush's. 

My friend is a chicken man, so for his two he ordered a taco and quesadilla. He enjoyed the taco, but left the majority of the quesadilla on his plate. I had a Fish Taco and Spinach & Mushroom Enchilada. The fish was hand battered, but a little  greasy on the inside. My enchilada was a disappointment, both the mushrooms and tortilla were chewy and rubbery. 

Our waitress was friendly and attentive. I liked how she presented the chips and salsa. When she brought them to the table she said, "Here are your complimentary chips and salsa."  We've all eaten at enough Mexican Restaurants to know, the chips and salsa are usually "free", but the verbal delivery made us feel special. 

The manager doing table touches around us kept looking at our table, but not once did he approach us. I guess we did not meet his demographics. 

I'll continue to satisfy my Mexican cravings at Milagro. Vida is pretending to be a high end Casa Gallardo.

What a major disappointment. I so wanted to like this nursery, but they dropped the ball big time.  They have Neiman - Marcus quality plants, but the customer service of a Family Dollar. 

I am working on a major landscaping project and have been visiting all the major and small nurseries through out the metro area and this one by far was the worst. On the day I visited, it was the third out of five. I normally do not like to drop $ figures, but on this given day I spent between $100 - $400 at each nursery. I did not spend a blood cent at Greenscape. 

When we arrived we asked if they had a specific plant, the two girls working the counter, were to busy talking and flirting with a young man who kept lift his shirt to show his belly. All they could do was point and tell us "down there, you'll see them". 
Wow, all the other nurseries we shopped at took us to what we wanted and helped educate us on the needs and care of each plant. Not here, they just point and direct. I guess that is why they have such good signage so customers can wait on themselves. Why not put in self checkout too. 

When we got to the area we needed, we did find another employee who must have been the "water boy" because he couldn't really answer any questions we had. He at least said, he was sorry for not knowing. We looked around a little more and left. 

As we got into our car, I looked inside and the two girls were still behind the counter. I think they are trained like a dog with an invisible fence, and they can not get out from behind that counter. Keep in mind, we were the only people there besides the man flashing his belly and got not service what so ever. 

I do not need to think I will not be back, I know I will not be back. Another addition to my No-No List.

Boo-Hiss! 

I came to celebrate, National Egg McMuffin Day and was totally disappointed. It was a time you'd think they'd have their A-Game going, but they did not. I went through the drive-thru about, 6:45AM. 

Since I was there to celebrate their special day and I am sure they're the ones who created it, I ordered the Breakfast Combo #1 which is the Egg McMuffin. 
My drive to work is less then 5 minutes from the restaurant and my food was ice cold. The Canadian Bacon was tough and chewy. The best thing out of the combo was the cup of coffee. It was hot and strong. 

The service was questionable. I wished them a Happy Egg McMuffin Day and neither the money taker or the one passing out the food at the next window, seemed to know what day it was. You'd think they would be the ones to be extending the celebratory greeting. 

I'll give them another try, because I do like their Double Cheeseburgers on occasion, but my experience on Egg McMuffin Day is a solid #2. Yes, I meant the grade school humor in closing. 

When: March 2, 2021
Why: National Egg McMuffin Day

I have been on a mission to revisit all the businesses that I have given 2 Star ratings, in hopes that they can prove themselves worthy of an increase. Today I visited Oh Lolli Lolli and unfortunately they showed me that they actually deserve a 1 Star rating, but I couldn't bring myself to lower their rating. The ambiance and location saved them, but they are still a 2. 

The young ladies working were unfriendly and when I asked questions their answers were short and curt. Once again I walked out empty handed. Later that day, I visited two other candy shoppes on my quest for a specific need and they both offered me exceptional customer service. Their excellent customer service resulted with me spending money in both stores. What a shame that the cash register did not ring at Oh Lolli Lolli - Itsy Bitsy Candy Shoppe.

Oh, Lolli Lolli you disappointed me so much. I heard and read such great Yelp things about you and was so excited to shop your little candy shoppe, that I made a special trip to the De Mun neighborhood. 

When I arrived I thought the location was cute being next to a playground, giving you an endless flow of customers. I also enjoyed the compact size, you made use of every inch. Your staff was perky, friendly and was offered good customer service. 

What disappointed me was your selection of sweet treats. There was nothing unique or special. I have a huge sweet tooth and I walked out empty handed.

Not impressed at all. Candy was boring and overpriced. I did not pay that much attention to the soda selection as I am not a big soda drinker. 

I did find several humous signs that would be great joke gifts for various friends and family members. 

Service was minimal, not even a greeting or  a thanks for coming in. With that type of customer service, I most likely will not be returning.

I don't get the love for this place at all. I have tried this place numerous times with friends and each time we all walk out scratching our heads. The service is minimal at best. Our most recent visit, we were the only ones sitting at the upstairs bar and we still had a hard time getting waited on. The young lady working that bar treated us as if we were an inconvenience and an interruption to her night.  We drank half of our cocktails, which were made very amateurish and left. 

There are too many other bars in Saint Louis where you can get a professional and masterfully made cocktail, so I suggest you take a pass on Planter's House.

WARNING: This is my harshest review to date. Some folks may be offended by some terminology that I use. I do apologize to those offended, but somethings just have to be stated openly. 


I must have hit a bad day, because the only words that come to my mind after my lunch here are, "What a dump". The service was snotty young people who thought they were better then the customers they were assisting and we had to send food back to the kitchen for a redo. The counters were cluttered, disorganized and the area around the soda/tea was yuck. 

The cashier was a throw back to the early eighties, a total "Valley Girl". I use that term, instead of the dumb blonde. She had no idea what she was selling. When we informed her it was our first visit and could she recommend something. We got the deer in headlights look. We rephrased our question, "what's popular". This time we got the look of why are you asking me questions. Finally, my friend said, "I guess everything is good" (with a chuckle). Then the light went on in the young girls empty head, "Yeah, everything is good". Well she was wrong, everything is not good. 

Now let's talk about the food. My friend had a Yellow Fin Tuna Steak Sandwich, (not on take out menu or website so I do not know the exact name) and I had the Skinny Californian. 

Yellow Fin Tuna - Sandwich is huge, served club style with three slices of bread. My friend and I both agreed it would be much better between only two slices. This is the one we needed to send back for a redo. The Tuna was nasty, huge pieces of skin hanging on to it making it difficult to chew. 
When my friend asked to send it back the young man working the tables, told her that is the way Tuna is served. My friend informed him that she was eating Yellow Fin Tuna, before he was breast feeding. and she'd like another sandwich. He went to talk to the kitchen and when he came back to remove her plate, you could tell he was not happy. 

One of the chef's brought out the new sandwich and waited as my friend inspected the tuna. It was great. He apologized for the earlier one and returned to his kitchen duties. 

Skinny Californian - How can a crepe stuffed with Roasted Chicken, Avocado, Bacon, Swiss Cheese, Tomato with Mornay Sauce be bad? By being served inside a rubbery chewy crepe. If we hadn't already sent one item back, mine would have been returned. I ended up eating only the stuffing (which was very good) and very little of the crepe. I know making crepes is an art, and you'd think a place with crepes in it's name would have mastered that art. 

As we were leaving my friend thanked the server/busboy and told him that she enjoyed the sandwich and she'd defiantly be back. His reply, "Uh-huh, sure". What happened to, "Thanks, glad you enjoyed your meal. Look forward to seeing you again". The staff (excluding the chef) need an attitude adjustment. I've gotten better service at a greasy spoon. 

Don't know what is sadder, the fact that I had a bad experience or the fact that I'm going to give them a second chance. I feel obliged to revisit since I am friends with the wife of one of the owners. 

They have free WI-FI, Yippee.

I am not a certified BBQ judge, and I do not play one here on Yelp. Nor am I an expert in BBQ. I am what I am and that is a Blue Blooded, All-American, South City Man who knows and enjoys good BBQ when he has it. In my opinion Smoking Barrels missed the mark. 

Seeing all the rave reviews on Yelp, I was tempted to try SB for dinner the other night. I am always up for supporting a business in my hood.  We opted to eat in, instead of doing carry out. The ambiance is nice. We liked the hole in the wall, neighborhood feel that it had. Also, the barrel tables gives a rustic true BBQ feel to the dining room.  

After reading the menu, our game plan was to order two, 2 Meat Combos which came with two sides each. This was our way of being able to experience 4 different meats and 4 different sides. Aren't we ingenious?  The following is how we placed our order:

Ribs and Sausage with Cole Slaw and Potato Salad

Pulled Pork and Beef Brisket with Baked Beans and Mac - n - Cheese

Out of the four meats, the Sausage was by far the best. It was a nice touch that they pre-sliced it in to bite size pieces. It reminded me of a Johnsonville Sausage that you'd do on your grill in the backyard. The Baby Back Ribs had a fair amount of meat on them, but were dried out. No tenderness or juiciness when you bite into them. 

Our Pulled Pork was tender, but had no smokey flavor that I could taste. At first look and taste, I thought it had been boiled. The Beef Brisket was the biggest disappointment, it like the Ribs was dry and tuff. I am use to being able to break off a bite size piece of brisket with a plastic fork, here I was using a typical flatware fork and had to use a saw like motion to break a piece off.  Were the ribs and briskets leftovers, reheated? Made us think. 

When the young man serving us asked how things were and the BF informed him how tuff the brisket was, he offered to bring us something else or another serving of the brisket. We opted for more brisket, but to be honest there was not much improvement. The Pit Master brought us out some Turkey Breast and it was the absolute best of all. A shame we did not order it to begin with, it was juicy, smokey and tender. 

Their sides can compete with most of the other BBQ joints in town. 
Cole Slaw was creamy, thinly chopped and a flavorful. Potato Salad was better then some delicatessens. The Mac - n - Cheese was creamy, but was in need of some more cheese and less garlic. Baked Beans were good, they did have chunks of pork, but so does the cans of Bush's in the grocery aisle.  The Garlic Bread was as good as you'd get at Texas BBQ and that is damn good. 

The ice tea was fresh and they had my favorite artificial sweetener, Splenda.
We'll let the growing pains pass and will re-visit on a weekend to see in there is a difference. 

Remember, I am not a BBQ judge. This is just my opinion on a social medium.

WOW! I cannot tell you how excited I was waiting for the Copper Pig to open. Now that it has opened, I am sad to say, it is the winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award. It is the winner of; The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015. They disappointed me with; food, cocktails and service.

Let me start off with the positive points that saved them from getting a 1 Star Review:

1) Linen Napkins - They're always give a nice upscale feeling to any restaurant. 
2) Eco-Friendly To-Go Vessels - Thinking of our planet. 
3) French Fries - European style fries & a little cup of ketchup. 
4) It's in my hood - Brings variety and vitality to the neighborhood.
5) Girl with water pitcher always made sure your glass was full. (Also see negative point)*

Now the reasons why it was The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015:

1) Service - Very rushed. We ordered cocktails and three appetizers. When our drinks were served, waitress asked for the rest of our order. We stated we wanted to wait until our small plates arrived. Later when the small plates arrived, she again asked for order. When we ordered a second round of drinks, she responded, "I meant your entrees".
