Loving my Old Fashioned's and Manhattans being made with Maker's Mark, I couldn't resist trying their signature cocktail 201. It too, is made with Maker's Mark. It then has St. Germain, orange liqueur and a touch of lemon. It is served up in a rock glass for only $10. A hand crafted cocktail in the French Quarter and only $10 was a deal. Considering how strong it was, it was also a steal. 

One of my true seafood loves is Sea Scallops. When I saw them on the menu under appetizers, I had to have them. It was two jumbo sized sea scallops pan seared and served with baby arugula drizzled with white truffle oil and shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano. It was perfection. I could have had a second helping, but I had to get going to my original dinner plans at another restaurant. It was also served with a personalized mini loaf baguette - that was boring as hell. Everyone else rave about it, but I found it bland and flavorless. 

I love sitting at a bar when dining alone and Mr B's made it very elegant. They put out an opened linen napkin as my placemat, provided me with silverware and an additional linen napkin. A classy treatment for dining at the bar. 

I'd visit Mr B's again and next time sit at a table and have the full experience. I can see now, why my friend was so adamant that I go experience this restaurant. 

When: August 27, 2016
Why: A friend insisted that I go

The Good Pie in my opinion is, The Best Pie in Saint Louis.  I agree with Karen G., in loving this style of crust. The bubbly edges with charred spots not only add character to your pizza, but flavor as well. I too tend to eat each slice with a fork, but at times I just fold it half creating a Stevie B Calzone and take a big bite of the chewy pie. 

Today for lunch we shared a Chopped Salad, which they were more then happy to divide on separate plates. When we saw our split portions, each were a hearty serving.  The dressing was a little heavy for my taste, but the flavor was rich and creamy.  I loved the burn that was provided by the pepperochini. 

I took advantage of the Pizza Del Giorno which was; Spinach, Sausage, Roasted Peppers topped with a dusting of  Parmesan Cheese. Spinach is slowly becoming one of my favorite vegetables and combined with roasted peppers and sausage made me wish this was a regular feature and not just today's special. 

The SO ordered the Atina and if a picture is worth a thousand words, look at the picture I posted. It will show you how over the top good this pizza is. The roasted mushrooms alone were worthy of their own pizza and when they got combined with tomato, prosciutto di parma and pecorino my taste buds danced for joy. 

The finale of our lunch was the most incredible Salted Caramel Gelato. Creamy and the perfect blend of caramel and saltiness. Service as always, friendly and attentive.

If you don't follow your favorite restaurants on Twitter, I highly recommend that you do. If I were not following, Farmhaus on Twitter, I would have never known that they were preparing one of my favorites on Mother's Day weekend. When they sent out the tweet that they were serving, Soft Shell Crab that week-end, I responded back with a simple, tweet. "I'll be there." 

Arriving on Friday night, I seated myself at the bar. Being a lone diner, I hate tying up a two-top table from the servers. Besides, other fun people also dine at the bar and I like a good company. Sitting at the bar, I of course had to start my evening out with a cocktail. I'll have a, Manhattan, please. Farmhaus is not known for its' cocktails, but I will say they do an excellent job making a classic Manhattan. 

As I read the menu, I got doubly excited. Not only were they serving one of my favorite seafoods this evening, they were also serving one of my favorite vegetables - asparagus. Life is good and I know this dinner is going to be delicious. If that were not enough excitement, on the dessert menu was, Lemon Poppy Seed cake with vanilla ice cream. I am so glad I am a Twitter follower of Farmhaus. 

My asparagus was served, "loaded". It had prosciutto, Gouda Espuma, Shoe String Potatoes and Spring Onion Ash. The asparagus was prepared to the perfect tenderness. To my delight, I enjoyed two soft shell crabs split in half and corn flour fried. They were served with a soy-lime aioli, pickled ramp and english pea salad. Some may frown upon eating a shell, but this is my second favorite seafood, right behind scallops and they are a very close second. 

Dessert completed the evening. To accompany my Lemon Poppy Seed Cake, I enjoyed an after dinner Grand Marnier. The LPSC was basically a pound cake and it was moist. It was served with a small scoop of vanilla ice cream and pieces of orange meringue. The fresh citrus taste made this a very refreshing and lite dessert. 

Service at the bar is always attentive. I still miss the, Blue Plate lunches of years gone by, but dinner at Farmhaus is always a 5 Star experience. 

I'll be back? - Absolutely, it's one of my favorites

When: May 11, 2018
Why: Soft Shell Crabs

I am more of a doughnut guy, but how you spell it doesn't really matter. Because, these are some of the best tasting cake donuts I have had in the St. Louis metropolitan area. They are moist and the icing is not overly sweet. As Goldilocks would say, " These donuts, are just right." 

The price point is a little higher then your normal doughnut shop, but lower than the area "gourmet' and "trendy" doughnut shops. Either way you look at it, it is well worth the money. The creative doughnuts with added toppings like M&M's is done way better here, than at other shops in the area.

One of the highlights for me being a dog daddy, is they also offer house-made dog treats. With today being, Love Your Pet Day, I couldn't resist stocking up on a very extra treats for my Fur-Babies. 

The staff is friendly and the owner himself is a delight to speak with. He made selecting and buying donuts fun. 

When: February 20, 2021
Why: Needed a doughnut and killing time.

This Thanksgiving I was thankful for J Gilbert's. I was thankful that I was able to get a reservation at the last minute at the time I wanted. Most importantly, I was thankful for an amazing Prix Fixe Thanksgiving Menu, that satisfied me need for a traditional Thanksgiving dinner. 

I liked that J Gilbert's did a Prix Fixe menu instead of a buffet like so many other restaurants that were open on Turkey Day. Buffets usually are overpriced and overwhelming. Where do you start? What should you eat? and the hardest question of them all, "When do I stop eating?" 

Our dinner was reasonably priced at $38 and included three courses. The first course was a choice of two types of salad and two soups. I choose a Caesar Salad and my friend Norma went with the Maryland Crab Bisque. The size of my salad was appropriate for a lead in to a large meal. I enjoyed the dressing, which was proportionate to the amount of Romaine lettuce. The asiago cheese crisp was the perfect carb match up to the salad. 

The second course was the main attraction; a Traditional Thanksgiving spread. When the plate was first placed in front of me, I thought it was skimpy servings. As I started to eat, I immediately realized I was wrong. I needed a to-go vessel, that provided me a nice lunch for the next day at work. 

The traditional spread included; roasted turkey (both dark & white meat), yukon mashed potatoes, cornbread and sausage dressing, gravy, glazed yams, green beans with pecans and cranberry orange relish. I had everything that I wanted and if I closed my eyes, I would have thought I was down home on the farm instead of an upscale steak & seafood house. 

The third course of course was dessert. You got to select from three of their most popular desserts and of course pumpkin pie. Miss Norma went pumpkin pie, but I had to stray off menu. I saw a Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée pass by our table and instantly knew I had to have it. When I asked our server if I could substitute she was accommodating to my request. It was so delicious with the fresh raspberries on top. Actually, the serving portion is so huge that two diners could share. 

Let me back-up to the beginning of our evening and tell you about our appetizer and cocktail. 
One of my favorite cocktails is the Moscow Mule, so I was thrilled when I saw J Gilbert's made theirs with my favorite vodka; Tito's and my favorite ginger beer; Fever Tree. Most MM's are $8, but to have my two favorites in my favorite cocktail was worth the $10. Plus, they poured heavy, it was a good strong cocktail. 

Being a fan of crab meat, I couldn't resist ordering the Jumbo Lump Crab Cakes. Excellent! You are served two huge cakes and if you order this item for lunch, for me it would be the complete meal. They also served up a small loaf of piping hot house bread with two types of butter. 

The service was; friendly, attentive and not rushed.  A couple of friends have told me J Gilbert's does a great job on lamb chops and scallops. So I know I will be back, as those two entrees are on the menu of my last meal on earth. Can't wait to give them a try. 

When: Thanksgiving 2015
Why: Thanksgiving Dinner

Gentelin's is easily the premier restaurant in Alton. If you are fortunate to be seated by their huge windows, you'll have an amazing view of the Alton Bridge. Besides the spectacular view, you'll experience white linen service at a small town locally owned restaurant. 

I've come here twice for a Saturday before Easter dinner with my favorite cousins. I apologize for not writing about last years amazing dinner, but I'm making up for it this year. Our appetizers, entrees and desserts were all amazingly delicious. Each one was plated and presented beautifully. 

There were six of us, so we started out sharing three appetizers. With my love of Jalapeños, one of them had to be, Goat Cheese Jalapeño Popper. It was three fairly large jalapeños stuffed with goat cheese. (are you surprised?) Served on top of a roasted red pepper jam with candied bacon. I got one of those peppers all to myself and loved it. 

Our other appetizers were the; Creamy Spinach and Artichoke Dip and Santa Fe Wraps. Some of the Southwest/Mexican restaurants in STL can learn a thing or two on how to make these wraps from Gentelin's. They were, crisp and full of flavor. So much so, that I didn't use the salsa for dipping. I did try the red pepper mayo and enjoyed it for the extra kick. 
The final app CSAD, was served with roasted garlic and parmesan crostini's, which separated it from other restaurants which serve just plain crostini. 

Our entrees were a good variety of the menu. I went with the Cowboy Ribeye. It was served over a Yukon Gold potato hash with caramelized red onion, red peppers, scallions, roasted garlic and bacon. I'd love to see this hash served at breakfast it was so good. My Ribeye also had Roasted Asparagus and was topped with Cowboy butter. The meat was tender and flavorful. 

Other entrees included; Aunt Jayne's Chicken, Grilled Chicken Pasta and  their famous Pork Chop. My cousin who lives in Alton and is a semi-regular, swears by it and claims it is the best PC he has had in a restaurant. 

I by far had the best dessert, Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée. The other two desserts enjoyed were, Raspberry Sorbet and Donuts and Coffee. I will say, the Donuts and Coffee was very original and creative. 

Service was great, cocktails made professionally and strong and as others have said, the bread basket was kept full. 

I'd recommend Gentelin's for a special occasion, or just an evening out. Treat yourself, get out of the city of STL and cross over the bridge to Alton for a fabulous meal.

Ok I went here after hearing from several girls I know about how great, fresh, and wonderful it is.  I'm sure the food is fresh, light, and delicious to some people but I have to totally disagree with anyone that calls it "healthy" as it certainly isn't.  They do offer lots and lots of nice looking desserts but everything on the menu, other than the soups, seems very heavy on the carbs, fats, and sugars here so I think some girls delude themselves that they are eating "healthy" here just to justify being able to order the super desserts as a "reward" for their "healthy" eating (if I ate this kind of food ratio often I would be huge!).  The menu is also a bit on the expensive side for the small portion sizes.  

They really didn't have anything I liked (I love meat but don't eat pig) but the soups were decent but not good enough for the price.  This is definitely a place for a "light" lunch.  Il Posto really just reminds me of a coffee shop that decided to throw in some sandwiches (but use some quality ingredients to make them a bit fancier).  The seating area is TINY and has very little space.  

I just find this is a place for dainty girls to eat and not men so I will never be back as it just isn't my type of food.  If you like this type of food and like light lunches this is certainly a place you might want to check out.  If I'm in this area I will be going to Pascal's Manale or Charlie's Steakhouse instead for my healthy food :)

I'm a big fan of the other two Pho Orchid locations in Metairie but this one needs serious intervention by management ASAP! I'm done with this location until at least the end of Carnival and I had been excited about it as it is near my home and I had planned on eating here often BUT this is not up to par with the other locations. They have a limited Mardi Gras menu with jacked up prices and only are doing to go orders. I wasn't happy about discovering this after walking down from my house! Next on arriving home and opening the package I find I've been given a mostly uncooked "Pho kit" with raw meat and noodles with the broth separate. I stir fried the beef and noodles as the broth had no heat to cook it. Thank God I was home and not trapped on the street trying to eat this mess but I think I need a refund after having to cook my own food. Unfortunately it seems I didn't cook it enough as I've had non-stop stomach issues since eating this worst pho experience of my life and it has ruined my Carnival fun for the weekend! I'm not happy and I hope management takes rapid action to fix the unacceptable situation at this location!

I feel so utterly betrayed as the recent law, requring disclosure of the origin of seafood from restaurants has gone into effect now, has revealed a dark truth I would never have wanted to accept.  The current menu at Slim Goodies reveals their crawfish are sourced from foreign lands even though they are literally across from the amazing seafood distributor of Big Fisherman.  I feel utterly betrayed over my patronage of this business over the years as they have proven to favor China over local Louisiana... so so heartbreaking....

The owners went on some insane rampage and fired all the long time staff in this once great joint.  The burger seems to have really slipped in quality and the meat portion has gotten smaller.  Everybody that knew what they were doing seems to be gone so the once fantastic burger seems to have died with the departing of the long term staff.  Another great thing that just ain't there no more :(

I'm afraid the only thing this place has going for it is late night hours and cheap prices.  I pulled into Nashville around 10:40PM and was badly in need of some food so this seemed to be about the only nearby option.  On walking in I quickly wished I would have skipped the nearby option and went to the late night Greek option instead but I thought I would risk going ahead with eating here despite my instincts telling me otherwise.  It was pouring down rain and when I walked in there was a leak dripping water down from the ceiling.  I at first wanted to order the country fried steak but they could only do it with white gravy and were not able to make it with brown gravy which I've never been anywhere that couldn't do that.  So instead I just ordered a cheeseburger.  Next I observed that the iced tea was that lazy processed fountain kind that comes out of a concentrate instead of freshly made tea.  Then they had no lemons for my iced tea which seemed to be a constant Nashville theme for some reason.  When I got my burger it was a pretty pathetic looking creature and it tasted even worse.  I considered trying a biscuit to maybe add some redemption to the place but again only gross white gravy could be done.  This joint is cash only but it still took forever to pay.  This was by a large margin the worst food and experience I had in Nashville during my visit.  Maybe the cheap prices and late hours make the food acceptable when you are drunk outta your gourd but other than that I just see no reason anybody would ever eat here as the food was just awful.

Dear Tips,

Raising the price of Abita Amber to $5 and the for real imports to $6 is just a rip off and pure greed!  I can go to Maple Leaf and most places Uptown and on Frenchmen and get cheaper beer and watch great music.  I simply can't afford to pay cover and then shell out $5 for a beer that I can buy for $13 a 12 pack or go to Ms. Mae's up the street and get for $2.50.  I've been a VERY good customer for years but I'm not paying that much for a LOCAL beer!  I might show up for a few shows but far fewer than in the past and I will be doing all my drinking at Ms. Mae's and not at Tip's during those shows.  Maybe if I smoked weed it wouldn't matter so much but I don't and I only like my beer.  Y'all have the freedom in our great country to charge whatever you like but the market dictates to me that you are way out of line with the value of what you're selling so I ain't buying no more.

$5 for Yuengling is outrageous!!!

This is probably the worst Middle Eastern food I've eaten in the entire Greater New Orleans area.  The few times I've eaten here it seems to be run only by a husband that does the cooking and his wife that is the only waitress/cashier/hostess.  I have found the portion sizes to be extremely small for the price and the flavors are very lacking as compared to all other Middle Eastern food I've ever had.  I've never had bad Middle Eastern food before so I gave this place several chances over the years and I hate to report that every visit was a disappointing one.  This place has always been very deserted during my visits and I've only seen at most 2 other people dining here (which unfortunately is probably a good measure of the quality of the food).  The family seems nice enough but the food just doesn't really merit a return visit from me ever again.

I've eaten here four times over multiple years since they first opened and it has been consistently terrible with basically everything consisting of just a big pile of bad-melted-greasy-congealed-plastic "cheese" over some very substandard mush of tortillas and whatever else you happened to order as your filling (and it tastes worse than it sounds and we won't discuss what it does to my stomach).  I'm not the biggest fan of Mexican food but I can't even qualify this as Tex-Mex (or really as edible food).  This is just some of the worst food I've had anyplace.  The service is pointless to even discuss because there is none.  Most of the other reviews here are just being WAY too nice or are counting in the cheap drinks BUT the drinks don't even come close to redeeming anything about the place.  I observe people eating the food OFTEN on my way to drink at the Bulldog and it looks consistently disgusting and people often leave large portions untouched at deserted tables.  

I usually wish the best for anyplace contributing to business in NOLA and want them to succeed but this place has been so BAD for so LONG they just need to close and make way for something better to replace it.  I'm ASHAMED to have this place in my neighborhood!!! This joint is a ZERO and not even worthy of 1 Star.  This is permanently on my "no go" list!

I've been nearly every year and this year was by far the worst.  The bathroom situation was out of control bad.  I've always gotten a 3 day pass or 3 day VIP pass.  I had such a bad time this year I gave my armband away and didn't return after Friday.  The single day tickets have gotten outrageous and when a festival costs more than Jazz Fest you're losing most of your locals.  Hardly any of my friends went this year and the line up was terrible other than the local bands (and I get to hear them often and for far less than what the prices at this fest are).  They had freaking carnival rides this year and it just was totally out of place along with what seemed like very diminished crowds.  I'm not buying a pass for next year and I will need to hear about substantial changes to return again which is very unfortunate as this is the best weather of any fest in NOLA.

The food is decent except when they run out of things or haven't defrosted things which has happened on every visit.  The service is just unacceptable and its a miracle if you can get your drink refilled.  I hope I don't have to ever come back to this joint and I would far rather go to the City Diner next door or Tic Tock Cafe across the street for much better food, much better prices and light years better service.

I really want this place to be good, as I frequent happy hour and the bars on Oak, and I would have loved a nice quick place to grab some food.  

Unfortunately after several visits and giving it several chances I can't see ever going back again.  Way too overpriced for what it is and the decor looks like they just ripped it off a 5 Guys Burger. On my last visit my burger and bun just disintegrated and crumbled apart as I attempted to eat it and they were completely out of iced tea.  The place was also nearly deserted on my last visit but all the tables were covered in trash.  They actually want tips even though it is exactly like any other fast food burger joint and they don't provide any "service."  Bud's Broiler is better.

They might be able to redeem themselves with some major work but it will take something major to get me back in here as Camilla Grill is a far better and cheaper burger of the same type and nearby GB's is far superior.

This review is for the now gone El Patio Mexican Kitchen and Tequila Garden.

Add this to the list of soon to be closed businesses in 2018.  $5 per tiny taco is absurd and then you get to pay for chips and salsa.  There is absolutely no way this place will stay in business with their current menu and pricing.  Looking at the menu I thought I was ordering a taco plate and not just ONE taco because NOBODY charges $5 for ONE taco!!! The dry bland taco was a .50 cent size and a Taco Bell taco would have been infinitely better.  This is the uber hipster place to go for terrible food at insane prices.  

Overall you would have to be utterly demented to eat here as this is the worst Mexican and one of the worst restaurants in NOLA.   To add insult to injury my stomach is doing salmonella somersaults from likely poor food prep...

Wake up call they need to visit Juan's Flying Burritto, La Casita, Taqueria Guerrero, Felipe's and other area Mexican joints to see how outta whack they are pricing themselves.

The only good news is they had some $4 beers.

La Casita ran El Patio but ran it quite differently than La Casita but fortunately they have recognized the error of their ways and seem to be returning this place to their La Casita model that works.

So my tenants washing machine goes out so I'm shopping for a replacement.  Walk into Lowe's and bam they have some "refurbished" appliances in the front.  "Wow that looks like a great deal on a nice front load washer," I say to myself as I look at the price marked down from around $700 to $250.  Bam! I love a good deal and I'm in good deal fever so I quickly locate a staff person and go up to a Lowe's staff lady and say, "Hey, I'm interesting in purchasing this item if it is fully repaired and you guarantee that it works."  "Oh yes they fixed that in the back it is completely repaired and should work great and we just marked it down so much because of a few dents and scuffs," replies the staff lady.  "Great I'll take it!" I say.  So it takes four of us to load this 500 pound beast into the back of my vehicle and then I recruit three more folks to help me haul this massive creature into my tenants space and remove the old broken machine.  

The next morning I get a text informing me that the new machine just fills up with water and won't work.  I again recruit people to help move it but this time I can only get two to assist with lifting the now even heavier beast with the added water weight trapped inside.  We manage to drain most of the water out of the machine but it still seems far heavier and painful to lift than when we had one more man assisting us.  Finally on returning to Lowe's I give the return lady the receipt and say, "Ok I bought this thing yesterday after being assured that it would definitely work but this thing definitely is broken!"  "Oh we only put things out for sale like that when they just can't be repaired so this happens all the time," replies the returns lady.  

Seriously if something can't be repaired what in the name of ever loving Bacchus are they selling it advertised as "repaired" for!  It is 100% that if it doesn't work customers are going to be returning such items!  If it is only good for scrap or being broken down into replacement parts don't advertise something as "repaired" when clearly it isn't!  Ludicrous behavior and poor management to ever do such a thing!

I very rarely eat fast food but Wendy's generally makes some of the better quality fast food available in the area.  Generally I see no reason to even review fast food joints as they are all generic but this Wendy's location has earned EXTRA SPECIAL RECOGNITION...  

Over the years on the few occasions I've visited this location one thing has been 100% consistent and that would be that they 100% of the time get my order WRONG!!!  I've complained to the little link/number they give you on the receipts but I've NEVER heard back.  I had some small hope that once they completely tore the old building down and rebuilt a totally new store that maybe they would be reborn as a competent establishment... Well that hope was dashed as once again and keeping their 100% FAILURE rate they once again got my very simple order completely WRONG again!!!  

Just don't go here and do yourself a really big favor if you must have Wendy's then go to the location on Claiborne where they can at least comprehend how to accurately fulfill an order.  Better yet just go to one of our much better local joints and avoid the fast food experience so you can have a beer with your burger.

I've been here several times over the years hoping that it would improve at some point but it hasn't.  The only good point of this place is they have some VERY cheap food and drink specials.  You also get what you pay for here and I've never had a good or even decent meal here.  The service has always been lacking and I've just never had a good time here.  This place seriously needs new ownership, new management, new staff, new everything in the personnel department.  Hey maybe they can get on one of those reality TV shows and improve.  Before that happens I really can't recommend anybody go here and 100% of my friends describes this place as follows: "That place sucks!"  I really wish this place could be good as it would be fantastic to have another option when R&O's has a long wait.  Please owners get yourself on one of those TV shows ASAP!!!

This place is definitely not the king of anything.  I had the single worst bowl of pho ga I've ever eaten in my life here.  The chicken pho came with the least amount of meat I've experienced and that small amount of meat was low quality and rubber in texture while the broth was blah.  My jasmine tea was nearly clear and had zero tea flavor to it.  I hope their other dishes are far better but this is the worst food I've ever eaten at a Vietnamese restaurant.

Go to Pho NOLA or Pho Orchid for much better food.

I've been several times and it just doesn't float my boat.  I've sampled multiple things and I just would much rather be at another tapas place than this one.  (I'm not sure if the same people that ran the previous short lived restaurant, Catch, at this location are still involved now but I think they are and that was some of the worst food I've ever had in NOLA.) Every time I've been I've sampled something different and found it mediocre at best and I hoped that at least the sangria could have some saving graces but unfortunately it did not.  This is now officially on my "no go" list and I won't be returning.  5 visits and 5 strikes and they are out; which is unfortunate as they are near to my house and I would have liked to have liked the food but I find it nowhere close to Spanish tapas or any other food I like (it seems generally more like Central/South American food with some strange NOLA fusion attempts).  

I can see how this place might appeal to women but I should also confess that I HATE the small plate concept (outside of traditional tapas and sushi) as I like to eat and I'm a man that needs a good portion so if the price of multiple small plates to fill me up costs more than one regular plate it makes me very unhappy.  An old caveman like me needs a big hunk of meat to be happy and a man's belly being unhappy is the source of most of the trouble in the world ya know...

I went for Saturday lunch with my sister and mother and none of us were happy with the results here.  We were served some of the worst gumbo I've ever had containing ONE shrimp along with half a tiny crab soaking in a cool rue.  The Ruby Red shrimp were ruined the way they cooked them (resulting in them being dry, flavorless and tough) and the shrimp toast appetizer was just an unfortunate choice. I tried to order one of their foreign non-Gulf oysters to see if I would like it and was informed the minimum order was half a dozen even though the menu priced it per oyster.  I can't remember EVER going to a seafood restaurant where EVERY food item I ate was so very unappetizing.  Expensive prices and food that is way under expectations.  Perhaps dinner is a much better experience but now that they have made momma unhappy nobody is going to be happy so I will not return for lunch and definitely won't be bringing anybody back here unless I try dinner sometime and have a radically different experience.

It took quite a bit of adventuring and travel time to find the location of this festival and I was really looking forward to attending it and putting down massive amounts of tasty gumbo as I do love some gumbo...  Wow what an incredible disappointment as this is some of the worst gumbo I've ever had in my life!  I couldn't believe I was still in Louisiana as the "gumbo" was such a bad watery thin flavorless concoction that it wasn't fit for consumption.  I literally ate half of it and threw the rest away it was so bad (and I was starving).  This event was one of the least favorite fests I've EVER been to.  It was so sparsely attended and depressing that I was in and out of this festival in 20 minutes and I really don't think I would ever return to this event!

I've rarely have had a fun time at the bar here but there have been a few moments that were enjoyable.  The food here used to be much better and they once had a great turkey burger BUT the food has gone WAY downhill and now I just refuse to eat here.  The last terrible meal I ate here was around Mardi Gras and two of the cooks got into a huge fight that spilled out into the street and there was all sorts of great blood and gore everywhere (this is probably an extra star for sheer entertainment).  Of course due to the fight it took three hours for us to get our food.

Decent snowball joint where you can drive through for your chill fix.  They are heavy on the syrup pour and the sizes are large and cheap.  The ice consistency just wasn't my cup of tea and it seemed more like a snow cone instead of a snowball but that might have been due to the very heavy syrup pour.

I discovered this super hidden bar during an adventure to the Homedale Inn with a group of friends.  This bar is further down behind Homedale Inn and we just saw it as we were turning around and decided we had to check it out.  We came in here and there were only around two people in the entire place so it seemed a bit spooky.  It looks like a place that only people that live in the immediate area would even know about or go to.  I've never met anybody else that has even heard of this place or been here.  It looks like a decent place to hang out but it is just very far off the beaten path.  If there were more people here and I would have stayed for longer than one drink this might actually have been a fantastic place but from my short visit there wasn't much going on here.

Beer was drinkable but probably doesn't inspire me to want to drink much of it.  The biggest challenge here is that the interior warehouse space gets very hot and uncomfortable.  So far this is probably my least favorite brewery experience in the NOLA area.

This is just a place to drink as the food is completely overpriced for the boring and typical Tex-Mex crap wrapped in a tortilla of some type.  Tex-Mex isn't complicated and nothing in it is very expensive so there is no way the outrageous prices this place charges for their food can ever be justified other than  they must get a lot of tourists and locals who don't know better so they just rip those clueless folks off.  Why even bother with the overpriced mediocre food here anyway when you can just go eat awesome food right across the street at Lola's!  The owners are nice people but what they charge for a freaking taco is insulting.  Do yourself and your wallet a favor and just booze it up here but never eat.

The food consists of small appetizer portions and really didn't impress me that much.  Don't come here expecting to be able to eat a full meal as it is just snack size portions.  Nothing I ate really appealed to me and I won't be eating here again.  The beer selection was small, overpriced and not very impressive (seriously no Abita Amber).  They do have a large selection of cocktails.  The bowling alley portion is nice enough but the overall experience just doesn't rate a return visit and I'm sticking to Rock and Bowl for my bowling excursions as it is FAR superior in every way to this venue.

Tip:  You can bring children here so for those with kids this can be a spot where you can drink adult beverages with the offspring in tow.

I had great times at old Pravda and liked that joint.  This new incarnation has nothing in common with the bar formerly known as Pravda and I don't like it.  Another fancy cocktail bar that ignores the needs of beer drinkers with a very limited selection of overpriced beers.  There is nothing Russian or Slavic about this joint so the name makes absolutely no sense.  I have absolutely no reason to return to this establishment.

Hello the 1960's called and they want their bad acid trip back.  This interior of this place seems like a venue that belongs more in a Los Angeles or Austin and it doesn't evoke anything of New Orleans.  This aesthetic of this place is just gaudy and painful to the eyes with all the clashing designs.  

I've stopped in here a few times over the years when going next door to MiLa and while the bartenders often seem to be very good at what they do I'm really more of a beer or wine drinker (MiLa's bar makes great drinks too).  Generally I could care less about cocktails and while they do make some notable cocktails here they also come at a notable price as it is ultimately a hotel bar.  Cocktail fans and those who enjoy such uber tacky "hip" and "mod" designs like this joint has will probably love this place.  It exudes so much hipness here that even hipsters aren't hip enough to drink here.  Granted they do make some very nice looking drinks here but I prefer the comfort of more old school and antique interiors and just a plain whiskey will do me fine if I'm drinking liquor.  The drinks here are probably four to even five stars for cocktails but the interior is a solid one star.  I've never been in this bar when any sort of decent crowd has been present and it seems to close very early by NOLA standards so it really lacks for any type of fun social aspect.  If you only want to go drink a fancy cocktail in a hotel type bar that is nearly deserted with a psychedelic interior design then you will love it here.

I've been to a few events here but other than that this place never seems to have many people in it.  Overall its a decent place to grab a drink and watch a game but the food is inconsistent so I probably wouldn't eat here.  This is a good place to host an event as you can easily do a block party as there is usually not much traffic in this area.

This is a Chinese Restaurant with some Vietnamese dishes.  I usually just get the chicken pho here which is pretty good but probably the most expensive pho in the whole New Orleans metro area.  The other dishes I've had here are decent for the most part with the sauces being not the most flavorful to me.  They seem to give good portion sizes and the service has always been good.  My biggest negative for this place is I really find their hot & sour soup to be the worst example of that dish I've ever had and I just don't find it edible. The location is very convenient to where I live and the nearest place to get my pho fix (for now but I've seen TWO new pho places opening on Magazine so huzzah!!!)  When new pho options appear I doubt I shall be returning very often if at all...

If you're a fancy cocktail drinker this place is a four or possibly five star place.  If you're a beer drinker then this place is a bit silly as it is just another fancy schmancy cocktail bar that is just way too cool to carry Abita Amber and other well loved beers.  They do have beer here but only expensive ones and some I even like but if I want an Abita Amber I want an Abita Amber!  

The bar is pretty cool with lots of fresh herbs lined up along the bar that they use in the drinks and if I was going to drink a fancy cocktail this would be a pretty cool place to do it.  The bar is a bit narrow and small and there is a larger lounge type area with cushy chairs and couches.  There were VERY few people here for a Friday during happy hour time when I was here but it seems they don't have happy hour pricing so maybe that's why.  I liked the ambiance of this place alright and if there were actually people here and if they had Abita Amber I might even frequent it but otherwise I probably won't be back here unless I get some really unusual craving for a fancy cocktail.

Really nice folks run this place and while they have some good food they just don't seem able to produce a good brisket.  Unfortunately this is one of the worst examples of brisket currently in the area.  They do have a nice selection of sauces and quite a variety of sides.  They have some creative ideas and do a lot of things here with pickles, sides, sandwiches and entrees.  If you only want chicken or pork BBQ they seem to be far more proficient in that area of BBQ skills.  Overall this is probably a three star joint but the seriously lacking brisket is a vital component of any BBQ place outside of Alabama and the Carolinas.  McClures went to brisket school and improved their brisket offering so I would suggest a good brisket course would drastically improve the results here also.

The front of house was excellent and all were very friendly and took great care of me.  The sushi menu wasn't very inspiring and the three rolls I had were small with little fish and rather mediocre in flavor.  The only item that seemed different from other sushi options in the area is they offered "Scottish salmon" which I'm not sure if it really is from Scotland or just how they describe it as it tasted like all other salmon I've had.  This might be the only sushi restaurant in the area to only have a regular bar and not even have a sushi bar.  I think they might want to give up on the sushi idea and focus on other seafood dishes.  This would be on the bottom of my list for sushi in the area and while it's not bad it just isn't as good as the other options.  The lagniappe grilled oyster I was given was the best thing I ate and it was well executed.

This is an old bridge that shakes, rattles, and I'm afraid its going to roll over into the river.  The lanes are scary narrow and you always have the feeling somebody is going to ram into you that they are so near to you in the other lane.  If you didn't have to use complete Jedi force focus to stay within the centimeters tolerance you get for your narrow lane to avert disaster you could enjoy the nice view of the Mississippi River and the East and West banks of the river while you cross the bridge but leave that for when you're a passenger and not a driver as I don't want you ramming into me while you look at scenery.

I hadn't been to this place in several years and I had heard that the food had improved a great deal.  I had heard that the chef had gone off to Italy and learned some great new stuff so I that was a compelling thing to me so I decided to give it another try before Wednesday on the Square.  I had liked the lasagna here "ok" the last time I had eaten here so I decided to try that again to test the "improvements." 

When I walked in service seemed disorganized and inexperienced.  When I got my food I thought it looked "ok" but I've definitely seen better looking lasagna and when I tasted it the first thing that came into my mind was that the sauce on it tasted like a Chef Boyardee canned pasta!  I was also in sticker shock when just my lasagna and one Abita Amber cost $25.24 and I didn't even get a salad or bread or anything else along with my entree like EVERY other Italian place does with their entrees.  For that price their are a whole LOT of other NICE restaurants I could have had a multi-course meal at for around the same price.  

Maybe they have other items that are really good on the menu that I would like better and they did have some interesting looking pizzas but at the prices they charge there are just WAY too many other restaurants that are much nicer that I like a whole lot better.

Hipsters and assorted other grimy folks were stumbling about in here.  It was dark dank and smokey but they do sling food pretty late.  The prices were not good with overpriced $5 Yuengling so this seems to be a bar for those that don't know that this is overpriced as all they probably drink is that gross PBR poison.  The smoke fumes really left a short threshold of being able to survive in this place so I had to get out pretty fast.  Maybe I can check it out again if they ever clear the smoke out but otherwise I probably wouldn't go back.

Yet another mediocre Mexican place on Magazine where there are already too many Mexican places adding to the already overly crowded number of mediocre Mexican restaurants in the area.  The interior is interesting and they have done a unique theme inside while their tables are more form than function being a bit slippery on top but highly decorated.  The menu continued the theme of form over function as the print the menu was written in literally stabbed my eyes and was painful to read so it was hard to decipher what the offerings were. Their enchilada was not at all what you usually expect from an enchilada while their tacos were nice with generous slices of avocado.  The salsa that comes with the chips is very thin and watery along with the fact it could definitely use some spice kick. For the prices there are just many better places to go.  I'd stick with the taco happy hour and before or after that still just stick with the tacos.

The ice doesn't compare to Hansen's or Plum Street and the flavors taste like the commercially made ones.  This is about the only game in town along this stretch of Jefferson Highway so unless you're willing to travel about three miles further in either direction you won't find another snowball treat.  I've only ended up here due to the fact that a Concentra drug testing lab is next door where yippee ki-yay I get to pee in cups for drug tests due to the line of work I'm in so after I pee I saunter over to this joint to get a snowball.  The good thing about the remoteness of this place is I've never had to stand in a long line or seen a long line here but that could be due to my timing.

Blah boring chain burger place that's slightly higher quality than McD's.  A much better restaurant is deserving of this prime location and this place would be better served next to some other fast food places.  I really could do without the steel cage basket they serve things in.  Maybe this place will do ok as there isn't any other fast food joint within eye shot of this place other than Subway but I think a local joint would have done better business and fit in much better with the neighborhood.  Personally I could do without it and probably won't be back as there are much better burgers for a similar price nearby in the bars.  I guess this would be a good spot to bring kids.

Typically long lines and the food just doesn't have a whole lot of flavor to me.  The tortillas are very "gummy" and just don't have a very good consistency to me while at the same time being too dry and often falling apart.  I'm just not a fan of "better" fast food that takes a cafeteria line approach and then just doesn't taste as good as Taco Bell.  For the same price I can go to an actual Mexican restaurant and get better food with actual service while actually being able to enjoy my dining experience.

This place has decent Chinese food at reasonable to cheap prices.  The location has been multiple places and was most recently a vegetarian Indian establishment.  You can easily drive past this restaurant and not even notice it.  There has only been one person working the front of house during all my visits and it hasn't ever been crowded during lunch so this has been a quick lunch spot.  It's a pretty bare bones and basic place without a lot of atmosphere but that seems to be reflected in their affordable prices.

This place has just "ok" BBQ in the realm of brisket and chicken.  They really focus on the pig to the exclusion of the other meats and I like the beef better so I feel discriminated against.  The brisket is pretty tender and has "ok" flavor but isn't my preferred style of brisket here.  They are pretty generous with the chicken and a bit less with the brisket if you get a combo plate.  They are also very guilty of one of my biggest pet peeves at BBQ joints in that they dole out the sauce like it is made out of plutonium and I'm not allowed to have too much for fear I might build a thermonuclear BBQ device.  Seriously one little baby container of sauce isn't going to cut it!  Really the sauce isn't even all that great so why dole it out like it is made out of ground up million dollar bills.  The sides here are alright and the service is decent.  They have a nice location on Oak Street but with Buddha BBQ closed it looks like I still have to head to the Joint to get my main brisket fix in the NOLA metro area...

Ahhh it is ok but nowhere near the ambiance of Cafe du Monde.  I've never seen this place crowded so you do get super fast service.  I really don't care for beignets but they have those here too and it is all very similar to Cafe du Monde EXCEPT they also have a decent small menu of some New Orleans classic dishes so I would say the dining options here are far superior to Cafe du Monde (but a terrible location in a strip mall).

This is a small bar with a large gangster theme.  I really like the tommy gun decor but I wish they offered it with some bullets and a range to go along with it.  This is a nice spot to grab a quick drink right off Bourbon Street when you are on your way to or from dinner or some other activity in the Quarter.  I've never seen it unpleasantly crowded here so it seems to be a reliable spot to have an enjoyable experience with breathing room and a sound level appropriate to have a proper conversation.

It is connected to the original Galatoire's and so in some ways this is sort of just extra space for the original restaurant but they do offer a different menu.  The steak is good and the service is professional.  The downstairs bar here is large and comfortable so it might be a good place to drink if the upstairs bar at original Galatoire's is full.  Generally I would prefer dining in the original Galatorie's but if it was full I wouldn't mind eating here again.  You can also access Galatorie's 33 from the upstairs bar at Galatorie's.  The dress code here is more relaxed than the original so if you find yourself in a more business casual mood then this might be a better choice than the original Galatorie's.

This is probably the least interesting putt putt golf course I've ever played but its the only putt putt in the city.  They do have some nice New Orleans specific learning information and icons for kiddos.  I just like my putt putt with more crazy stuff like whirling windmills and other such obstacles.  They have a few interesting water hazards and a few trick shots you can attempt but most of the holes are pretty basic.  I wanted the Mr. Bingle and other figures to be part of the actual course play and not just static decorations.

This is a very authentic Mexican and not Tex-Mex restaurant.  With that being said the majority of the stuff is the same old tired Mexican theme of things wrapped in tortillas.  They have decent tacos and have the great authentic Mexican spicy green sauce that burns so hot and tingly.  They do have some sandwiches and other assorted items not found in the typical NOLA Mexican place.  The area where this restaurant shines is in its selection of soups.  They have a large selection of many types of soups and stews that you just won't easily find anywhere else in the area.  The caldo de pollo (they recently have cut back on making this) and caldo de camarones are two of my favorites here but they also offer lots of other meats and different combinations.  The prices are generally a decent value and they have a large selection of Mexican beverages (but no booze).  A decent stop for a quick meal before heading next door to Brocato's for a bit of dessert.

This is a nice little indoor snowball spot where you can sit and eat at a table if you want.  They specialize in stuffing their snowballs with cheesecake here and have come up with some really interesting combinations.  They use a Snowizard machine so the ice isn't quite as fine as Hansen's but the cheesecake addition and the creative flavoring twists make this a worthy place to grab a treat at.

This is a good place for bread and desserts but the sandwiches are just NOT so good.  I'm not a big carb person and prefer the protein parts of my meal the most with lots of veggies on the side so this place isn't my optimal feeding spot.  Better to grab some bread to go and work your own magic on it.  They also offer some traditional Jewish breads that you might not find anywhere else in the area.  I never tried any of the Jewish breads and don't have any point of comparison to know if they are good or not but they looked nice.  The desserts here look pretty tasty and I had a cherry mini-pie that was pretty decent.  Overall I just wasn't that impressed and haven't been back for a long while now.

I used to have lots of friends that were members here and I would visit this venue often.  This can be a fun place with its Asian theme and lots of nooks and crannies to hide away in.  They have some nice wooden carvings of naked ladies in here that are cool.  This place is alright but there are certainly better private clubs in NOLA.   As time passed most of the people I know realized that they really didn't get a lot of value out of their memberships so they dropped out.  Personally I prefer being on the ground floor for shows at House of Blues and I really don't like being stuck up in the balcony area.

This is a much nicer park than I expected and a lot of time has been taken with the decorative foliage planting.  The view of the river isn't as nice as other spots along the river as there is a fence blocking access.  This park is all shiny and new and certainly doesn't look like your typical New Orleans riverside venue.  The access bridge could be a challenge for some but it is also one of the best places to train running up and down a significant elevation in NOLA.  The biggest downside is this park closes relatively early and they lock everything down so no later night running which during the Summer months is the better way to go in our heat.

So far of all the beer I have tasted at the NOLA breweries this brewery has the best to my taste.  The space is pretty cool being in an old movie theater while the geographic location can be a bit on the shady side and challenging to find if you don't know where you are going.  The Kristalweizen and Scotch Ale were my top choices and I would enjoy drinking mass quantities of those.  The space is set up much more like a bar than a lot of the other spots with indoor bench seating like a German Biergarten but no outside patio seating.  They also have some random food pop ups.  

Beer prices start at $5 and go up from there which I found pretty pricey for a beer in this locale even if it is some craft fancy stuff it is still just beer in the end and I would drink a lot more of it at $4 than at $5.  Maybe give locals and beer professionals that commit to 6 or more beers a quantity discount?  Maybe sell in a proper Bavarian liter glass for a better quantity and discount for those dedicated to the beer consumption arts?

Convenience store with a Vietnamese restaurant inside that also does traditional NOLA po boys along with banh mi and NOLA's own yaka mein (aka "old sober").  The chicken pho is a flavorful version in a a good size bowl that is not too small or too large.  There is a dining area in the front with tables and chairs and then a lot of folks get things to go here.   Prices are quite affordable for many things and a good value for what you get for some items and less so for others.

They give you large snowball sizes for little money.  They have a selection of ice cream, hot tamales, burgers, hot dogs etc. in addition to just snowballs.  The ordering is very quick but then you often have a very long wait to get your order as many people are ordering for MANY people and get a big box full of snowballs.  Overall its a good snowball at a value price for the larger sizes they offer along with a good flavor selection.

This is a convenient location for me as it is near my home.  They have some of the most flavorful chicken meat in their chicken pho here.  Generally the food here is decent to good but it doesn't seem to always be as good as their other two locations in terms of service and consistency of food.  In this area I generally prefer Pho Cam Ly, Lilly's and Mint Modern over this place but you can certainly satisfy your Vietnamese cravings here.  They don't seem to stay open late here usually and tend to close right at 10pm or earlier.

I've been in this store a handful of times and it has a much better selection than the Breaux Mart I'm much more familiar with on Magazine.  The location is a bit problematic depending on which way on Severn you need to go as the traffic is almost always terrible.  This grocery is very near Whole Foods so if you need items not carried there you can add Breaux Mart to your itinerary and complete your shopping in a more timely manner but items here are often more expensive than at Rouses.  They often have great prices and specials on beer.

This is the seafood market side of Harbor Seafood & Oyster Bar restaurant.  They sell boiled crawfish, shrimp and crabs along with fresh and frozen of the same along with fish.  I eat at Harbor Seafood & Oyster Bar all the time and it stays open later than the market side but if you want something boiled to go or to take home and cook yourself the market can provide you with most of the seafood items you can eat on the restaurant side along with quite a few they don't.

This is a pretty nifty bar for watching live music and they also have a kitchen putting out some decent food.  The people that run the place all seem very nice and they want to run a quality place and seem to constantly work on improving it.  I'm really happy that this is a non-smoking venue so I can actually breath oxygen instead of poison and even smell something other than smoke.  The main problem here is that parking is a bit tight in the area and Mid-City tow trucks are always on the prowl these days.  They have a very long bar but when it gets crowded they seem to need more bartenders to cover the area so it sometimes can take a bit longer than I like to get a drink but usually they do a good job.  They have a really cool small courtyard area that is "hidden" away that you might miss if you don't know to look for it.  They often get bands and music that you won't see elsewhere in the area.  This place is always a great place to check out as they always seem to have something interesting going on.

They have "Ghetto Punch" (AKA Red Drank) what more can you ask?  17 flavors of wings, crab cakes, chicken tenders, fish strips and crawfish balls.  Where else in the world but New Orleans would you find such a place?  Let me tell ya:  NOWHERE!  Go Ghetto and go to Wing Snack Express!  Take out ONLY!

This place has some of the best vegetables of any restaurant in NOLA.  I really love the mashed sweet potatoes, the creole okra with shrimp, the collard greens, and the green beans.  I used to work across the street from here before Katrina and I ate lunch here everyday so this place really does hold a special meaning to me.  

I really like the daily specials (with a choice of yummy veggies) which are pretty much the same goodness as they have been but the new training format they have started since Katrina has resulted in substantially decreased and consistently bad service (where before Katrina I always had great service).  I understand that this is a training ground but the training used to be much better and they need to institute more discipline and control to get this ship running right again.

I recently returned for my first visit since they completed the massive renovation of their location and it has been transformed into a very nice space with a much larger seating area.  There is no longer the dive feeling with the kitchen thrown out into the the side of the dining room but now it looks like a modern full fledged restaurant.  I sort of miss the dive aspect but the layout is far better organized and the bathrooms are exponentially better.  Service has improved some since my last several visits but it still hasn't gotten back to what it used to be before Katrina so the trainees definitely need more supervision and guidance.  As an extra bonus they are now selling a cookbook so you can learn to prepare their great veggies on your own.

This is a spacious place for watching live music and other NOLA events (I also usually end up here for MOM's Halloween Ball most years).  The bar has developed a clever system of using number cards that you have to show when you run a tab as it can get very loud when music is playing so that makes it easier to get your order in.  I've always had great service and the crowd has always been interesting.  They have adequate bathroom faculties for men but I've seen some shorter lines form outside the women's before.  They are usually very good about stamping you and letting you go in and out as you please.  The have a "set" behind the stage that has several "houses" giving it the look of a New Orleans neighborhood so that gives it a unique NOLA spin.  As with many things in the area it can be challenging to find parking at times so plan accordingly.

This is a great locally owned and operated sporting goods store that focuses primarily on hunting and fishing.  They have a limited selection of clothing items and frequently offer great sales on Colombia fishing shirts.  If you need anything in the area of firearms or fishing equipment this place often has items that are difficult or impossible to find at other area stores.

Gambino's is famous for their Doberge, Red Velvet, Wedding, Birthday and King Cakes.  They are also noted for their French bread and muffuletta bread.  In addition to their cakes and breads they have great pies, cookies, petit fours, cake balls, cannoli, pastries and all sorts of other delicacies.  The one thing they've really dropped the ball with is that with their olive salad they don't use 100% olive oil and they dilute the mix with cheaper vegetable oil.  They have a great website where you can order many of their products and have them shipped all over.

This place usually has very good food but the portions are on the smaller side and the prices on the higher side.  The biggest challenges with dining here are that they only take cash, there is usually a wait to get in (on the weekends), and they are only open for breakfast, brunch and lunch.  Service can also be inconsistent and the tables for two are cramped.  

I really like the selection of fresh juices and it is one of the very few places you can get a wheatgrass juice shot in NOLA (but it ain't cheap!!!).   Granted I'm not a big breakfast person but I do like the sandwiches, fresh juices, and other specials.  The fresh quality ingredients are noticeable and substantially add to the flavor and my enjoyment of their food.  They have been opening up several other locations that I haven't been to and I've only been to the original spot at 1418 Magazine so I'm not sure what the other locations offer but they could help some of the congestion that has grown up during the weekends for brunch and lunch.  This place is especially recommended for those seeking lighter and "healthier" fare that might have burned out on our normally "heavy" traditional creole cuisine.

This place was crazy happening and busy on a Thursday night when they run a great 2 for 1 drink special.  They have a really smart system I have seen a few bars use where they give you a token for your second drink so they don't just throw two drinks down at you so one gets hot. 
Their food looks interesting but leaning a bit on the overpriced side for what you get and I had already eaten so I never got to sample any food.  I really had a great fun time hanging out at the bar and there were a lot of other folks also having a great time.  The bartenders were probably some of the most professional, calm and collected I have ever seen dealing with such a large crowd.  I was impressed at how quickly the bartenders were able to quickly serve me and still provide polite, friendly and professional service the entire time on such a crowded night.  This place was right next to my hotel and was an awesome place to have so nearby.

For historical significance alone it gets 4 stars along with being one of the best ways to see the Mighty Mississippi as our ancestors did.  The steamboat trip is a slow journey that can be a relaxing experience as you watch and hear the repetitive cycling of the steamboat paddle churning through the water.  You can easily imagine a time not far gone when "Mark Twain" would be yelled and inspire Samuel Clemens onto adventures and writing.  This is more than just a journey down the river but a journey in time to experience what travel was like just a few lifetimes ago.  The loud blaring whistle may awaken you to the fact that you're back in the present for a moment but you can swiftly find yourself drifting back into a slower time as you watch the banks of the river drift past.  Yes the Steamboat Natchez is more than just a steamboat as its also a time machine.

I really like Pal's and I love the "special" wallpaper in the men's restroom here.  They often have cheap and free food specials.  They have outstanding bartenders that always make sure you have a good time.  They have a security officer at the front door and you have to get buzzed in by the bartender (as the neighborhood used to be a lot more shady and might still have some shady characters occasionally but it seems to be getting better and better around the area all the time).  I've never had any problems in this area and I've been here at ALL hours.  I've always had a fantastic time in this bar and they are always making some very creative cocktails.  They also have all sorts of fun games in the back and an awesome jukebox.  I wish this place was closer to my house and I would be here even more than I already am.

This is a really tasty Middle Eastern restaurant specializing in Greek and Lebanese cuisine.  They have some very generous helpings on their entree plates and they have some nice combinations not offered by similar restaurants in the area.  The food is delicious and the service is excellent.  On my last visit my drink was kept full even though the restaurant was packed to capacity and there was a line of people placing take out orders so that says a lot!  Keeping my drink full doesn't seem like a big deal but some restaurants really seem to have service problems with waitstaff just doing that basic task to actually earn their tips but Albasha took excellent care of me in that regard and these days that impresses me.  I was also asked multiple times how my food was and my order was delivered very rapidly.  This is a thoroughly experienced and professionally run restaurant that does good quality so even though they are a local chain they perform where it matters.

This is quite an interesting dining option in the area now.  The vibe reminds one of a techno dance club or stripper joint when you first walk in so you aren't quite sure if you are in the right place but you are.  They have a really extensive menu with a nearly overwhelming and sometimes confusing array of choices including à la carte along with all you can eat lunch and dinner options.  Regardless of the ultimate choice you make it is highly unlikely you will leave this establishment hungry and most likely you will be bloated to maximum capacity.  You get unlimited banchan and the serving portions of the main dishes are all generous.  The experience is one of the best for the Korean BBQ concept in the area currently.

This is a great location overlooking City Park.  I've been to a few private events here and many dinners.  The ambiance and location are my favorite things about Ralph's and it is a very relaxing spot to enjoy fine dining.  I've always enjoyed the food, service, and atmosphere of this place.  They often have different specials throughout the year.  They currently have lunch Wed-Fri with brunch on Sunday and dinner 7 nights a week.  They also have a nice bar here that can be enjoyable just to hang out at.

They have a plumbing supply business and also a retail display store with bathtubs, sinks, faucets, lighting and other associated home decor items.  They seem to mainly carry higher end items in the retail store but some things can be ordered in a cheaper configuration.  They want you to sign in when you first walk in the retail store and the wait for a salesperson can be a much longer time than you would expect so they use the sign in list to determine who gets the next available salesperson.  The plumbing supply business can get really busy especially in the morning as they carry one of the largest selections of plumbing supplies in the area.  I have been given some incorrect parts before but they have always been easy to work with to exchange them.

The Fly is a bit of a locals secret that sees far less tourists than many other areas of the city.  Being hidden back behind the zoo also makes it more fun as you get to get high up on the levee and look down on the zoo below.  There is a good amount of open grassy space to play games, picnic, throw a Frisbee, let your dog go for a good game of fetch or otherwise enjoy a bit more open space than a lot of other areas in the city.  It is also a great space just to get a bit of sun or watch the Mississippi River pass by as you sip on a daiquiri or some beers.  This is a very relaxing spot or a great spot for activity depending on your mood.  Unfortunately they keep building more and more stuff out here taking away from the open space and natural beauty of the area and that development has drawn enough complaints that it seems they have at least paused most additional development for the time being.  Overall this is one of the nicest spots to kick back and have fun outside in the Uptown area.

Perlis is one of the better clothing stores in New Orleans.  They primarily focus on men's clothing but they do have some women's and boy's items also.  The Perlis brand is most famous for their crawfish logo items and you will see many local folks proudly wearing these clothes.  In addition to crawfish logo items they also specialize in fleur-de-lis and Mardi Gras items.  Perlis is also noted for their selection of suits, ties, and shirts with the suits coming with their offer of free lifetime alterations.  The prices often do seem a bit expensive but they do often have some good sales and also have things you can't find anywhere else in the area.  They will also special order items and will really go out of their way to search for things for you.  I have several of the Perlis polo shirts and I like them "ok" I just wish they fit more like Brooks Brother's which I find more comfortable.  They thing they provide better than just about any other area clothing store is service!

They have some wacky flavors in this place and just their chocolate flavors take up an entire corner.  There is almost always a line to be served here and they offer free tastings of their many and varied flavors.  I'm all old fashioned and mainly just stick to my strawberry but I sometimes mix it up with one of their chocolate flavors or anything else that might catch my eye.  The only big negative about this place, other than the sometimes long lines, is that they only take cash.  They also have the infamous Tchoupitoulas Sundae challenge, that consists of 8 scoops of ice cream and then a huge onslaught of toppings, and completion of this challenge gets your name on the wall (I've never achieved this accolade but I could certainly eat the eight scoops but all those toppings just gross me out).

This is a great little park in the CBD that is host to YLC Wednesday on the Square and the Harvest the Music series of events.  Many other festivals and events are held here and this is a great location for such celebrations.  When events aren't going on this is just a nice park spot just to enjoy a picnic or anything else you might want some green space for such as frisbee etc.

This is one of my secret hide aways that I like to go to for cheap but great raw oysters and good seafood options.  They do good boiled seafood and grilled fish (or you get several other options on how you want it cooked).  The po boys are good yet smaller than I like but that leaves room for some of the other good options (like the delicious fried seafood appetizer, gumbo, or turtle soup).  Sunday through Wednesday ALL DAY they have 50 cent oysters (used to be 25 cent until BP) so I like my $6 a dozen deal.  

This place can get crazy crowded with a substantial wait on the oyster special days so there might be a line out the door waiting to be seated sometimes.  I've always had great service and I prefer to sit at the bar to enjoy my food.  There are always some interesting characters in here and this is certainly a great spot to see and hear things that you are hard pressed to find elsewhere.  I find the oyster size more consistent at Luke but generally more interesting people here.

This is a great old school Mid-City steak house that has barely changed over the years and is a New Orleans icon.  I've usually had good food here with a few inconsistent and less tasty visits but always good times.  I've often gotten the Porterhouse for 2 and found that to be one of my favorites here (and sometimes instead of eating it all myself I actually share it with someone).  The sides are pretty simple and basic here and I rotate between the sauteed spinach, broccoli au gratin, spinach au gratin, and peas. Most people usually get an order of onion rings and a salad but what Crescent City does better than any other steakhouse is give you an amazing assortment of potatoes to choose from: au gratin, french fried, German fries, Lyonnaise, Braebant, cottage fries and shoestrings!

I really like the booths with the curtains you can pull shut and plan to take over the world with your co-conspirators.  The service has always been great here (except for the abrupt opening of my tightly closed curtains).  I know they need to bring stuff to me but maybe they should have some kind of signal system to let you know they will be entering your private cocoon soon so you won't be so surprised when they yank it back and reveal the glare of the outside world. It can be a bit expensive for what you get but ambiance like this is nearly impossible to find outside of New Orleans!

This is a great place to get your wine or beer fun on when it is nice outside as there is only outside seating.  They have some great cheese plates and the outdoor chef's are usually making some good food with some good music playing.  

The good news & the bad news is the outdoor seating as it gets really hot and rains a lot in NOLA so there are definitely better times of the year to experience this place than others.  Another growing problem is the popularity of this place is making it harder and harder to actually find a seat so you need to get there mighty early to secure a spot and finding parking is never an easy task.  The only other thing to watch out for is there are sometimes some people with really stinky BO in there that need a good hosing off (I'm not sure when it became fashionable to avoid bathing) so that could be the benefit of going after it rains as maybe those folks will smell better.

Another benefit or problem depending on your point of view is that folks will often bring their children with them to hang out on the patio.  I don't have  any problem with kids and find them nicer than most snotty adults that don't like them so I think it just adds to the entertainment and flavor of the place to have entire families enjoying themselves and to have a place I can go with my friends that have kids that want to go somewhere like this.  I wish we had a place like this closer to Uptown so I didn't have to go so far to enjoy it.

This is a nice addition to the expanding Vietnamese restaurant scene of Magazine that I have been eating at for several years now.  This is a nice spot for a quick and delicious meal with their offerings of a variety of rice dishes, noodle dishes, spring rolls, pho, Vietnamese po boys/banh mi, Vietnamese tacos/sliders/banh gap and many other delicious items.  Their stir fried beef banh mi is one of the best beef po boys in the city!

My video review of Pho Cam Ly is here:

https://youtu.be/E2TfP_bLwBg

This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options which has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  Generally Porter & Luke's averages a bit over a 3.5 star mainly due to consistency issues as they absolutely can put out some four and five star food when they are firing on all cylinders but they seem to often have misfires.  They have a decent LARGE private back room and smaller private side room for meetings, events or other private dining groups.  The location is in a strip mall on Metairie Road which leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save.  My most recent visit was during St. Patrick's and the special was corned beef and cabbage and the corned beef was on the tougher side and certainly could have been better while the gumbo I also got was good.

Overall this is USUALLY a nice spot to get a good lunch or dinner and I've been to some good events here.

My video review of Porter & Luke's is here:

https://youtu.be/uLEkT9jOf28

Excellent Service!!!  I had a lot of problems with my Jeep Grand Cherokee and the security interlock that shuts down the engine stopped recognizing my keys and would shut my engine down and make it very difficult to start along with frequently locking the key and steering wheel.  I took the vehicle to numerous Jeep dealerships and other repair shops but NOBODY was able to fix what I thought was a pretty basic problem.  What I needed was a WOMAN running things just like the owner of EFI Services does.  She immediately knew what the problem was and fixed it FAST.  Every other place I had taken my vehicle to took WEEKS and still didn't fix anything.  I returned for many other repair issues after this and EFI Services was always fast and fair.  They know what they are doing here and don't give you the run around of incompetence that I found at every other place I went.

This is a great locally owned old school grocery that has lots of fantastic classic New Orleans food!  Their prepared foods and deli are great, the bakery is amazing, the meats are high quality and they have a wonderful cheese selection.  They also have one of the best wine and liquor selections in the area and carry things you won't find at any other local stores with great prices to boot!  This is one of the best grocery stores in the entire metro area.

This is the premiere Arby's location in the entire world.  Arby's makes a decent roast beef for a disgusting fast food chain.  Most of the sandwiches and the curly fires are a cut above your typical fast food selection.  On the edge of the French Quarter, which is home to some of the best gastronomic delights in the world, one would ask "why" people eat such drudge as fast food?  Well generally I would say they are drunk or otherwise under the influence of some mind altering substance.  I believe I should confess I've eaten in this Arby's a grand total of one time in my life, back during my college days, when I was in just such a beer induced altered state and I sorely needed some curly fries.  

In any other context, location or realm I would most likely rate Arby's around a 1, 2 or 3 star joint and I'm known as a rather strict Yelp reviewer so you might ask yourself, "why 5 stars?"  Well for one reason and that my friend would be the prime location of the bathrooms in this establishment!  During Carnival season when the biological urge to release the bladder invariably happens after drinking fermented beverages this Arby's has prime real estate on the parade route to assist you from exposing the public to your desperate need to relieve yourself.  Public release of the bladder in New Orleans is one of the most frowned upon offenses by the officers of the New Orleans Police and they are well known for arresting offenders and then with the sheer volume of offenders jailed during Carnival people have been lost for weeks in the place that nobody wishes to experience that shall not be spoken of.  So yes my compatriots this Arby's can save your reputation, your festivities and your bladder from exploding so blessings be upon this Mecca of Burt ("Where the Locals Eat ® ©").

I've eaten here many times and had many private events here.  I have always had a great time with outstanding service and food.
