Muriel's has some amazing gumbo and they usually have a special for around $30 for a 3 course meal.  Some people don't know you can usually get a drink downstairs and go and enjoy the balcony upstairs and this is one of the best places to people watch all the interesting things going on down around Jackson Square below.  They also have an interesting "Egyptian" themed room upstairs. Always a great place to go with a group, book an event, or just eat by yourself at the bar.

If your looking for a quality smaller gun store with a reliable and straight shooting owner that knows what he is talking about then this is the place for you.  Meplat Group is an FFL with a small but notable stock of firearms and is happy to do do transfers for $20.  They buy, sell, trade, and transfer firearms of all kinds including Class III weapons like machine guns, silencers, short barrelled rifles and shotguns.  They also provide training through their NRA certified instructors and give a great level of service and knowledgeable advice to help customers in the selection and acquisition of firearms that meet their needs.  The owner, Kenneth Bossetta, is an attorney and can also set up NFA trusts to assist with the process of acquiring NFA items.  Mr. Bossetta is also a great person to do business with and is definitely a step up from your average gun store interaction.

This is a fantastic park and they have several distinctive areas.  The Carousel Gardens Amusement Park is one of my earliest and most enjoyable memories featuring the fantastic antique wooden carousel along with several other rides such as a ferris wheel, the Red Baron mini-plane and, another of my favorites, the miniature train ride.  Storyland is another great area for kids with 25 storybook exhibit play areas.  You can also rent boats & bikes, play golf & tennis, or enjoy the equestrian center.  People also fish, play rugby, soccer and all other manner of sports on the park grounds.  There are also the attractions of the Botanical Garden, the Sculpture Garden and the New Orleans Museum of Art.  I've got many memories of the Museum of Art with the earliest being making multiple trips to stand in LONG lines to see the King Tut exhibit and after many attempts FINALLY getting in.  There are also several other areas and spaces available for rental and hosting of events.  Christian Brothers school, Tad Gormley Stadium and the Pan-American Stadium are also located on the park grounds.  There are many festivals and events that are hosted here with Voodoo Fest probably being the largest.  They even have a dog paradise for your pet to enjoy at "City Bark."  

This is a great park!

This is one of the best hotels in New Orleans and is home to fantastic pieces of NOLA history and legend like the Sazerac Bar.  This hotel would often donate food to the place I worked prior to Katrina so I often got to take the elevator deep down into the bowels of the lower levels of this place which was fascinating as there are many functioning antiques down there that still keep this place going.  I've been to many Mardi Gras balls and other fun events here over the years and it was a sad time after Katrina when it was closed for so long.  It was a happy day when they finally reopened and added even more new restaurants and reinvigorated many of the traditional spots.  The most special time here is during Christmas and they do some serious decorating above and beyond nearly any other location in the city and it is a definite destination during that time of year!

One of the oldest Yacht Clubs in the USA the SYC has a long and distinguished history in the annals of yachting.  This is the epicenter of sailing for the NOLA area and the club has some fantastic programs.  They have a nice pool area with a smaller kid friendly splash pool.  The clubhouse has nice facilities overlooking Lake Pontchartrain and the food is generally good to excellent depending on what you order.  This spot is always a hub of activity and it is certainly a popular venue for many events and activities.

I'm from the South and this is my General Robert E. Lee on his prime pedestal in the center of our Lee Circle looking defiantly Northward at you invading Yankees with your dirty hipster and sloppy tourist ways!  Verily I say unto thee bathe thouselves well and learn to behave in decent civilized ways to dress appropriately for dinner.  Truly do not arrive wearing shorts or jeans to present in our fancy eating establishments.  Do not whine, balk, or complain about not being allowed entry due to your lack of appropriate regalia when such dress codes are clearly posted on websites and the exterior of establishments.  

Appropriately honor our monuments to the War of Northern Aggression with due historical respect and leave your snide comments about Southern culture and peoples back in your frost laden Northern lands.  Repent of your Californian attitudes of despising our heavy use of butter, cream, and deep frying in making things deliciously decadent.  Imbibe in the holy consumption of alcohol to achieve the nirvanic state of inebriation so that you might fully embrace all that our Southern hospitality has to offer and join us in the revelry that we freely share.  Releasing your preconceptions and fully embracing living in the space and time that you're in New Orleans will unleash a multitude of  delectable possibilities.  

Now salute General Lee and march on to eat something scrumptious!!!

I've been going to Tips for many years and I've seen many shows.  I've had friends in bands and gotten to hang out backstage.  I've been to many a New Year's Party and more special events here than I can even begin to count.  I've even seen midget wrestling here.  Ultimately Tips is just a fantastic venue and has some fantastic bartenders.  They often have shows that will run until dawn so make sure to pay attention to the music schedule.  The bathrooms can get nasty as there are some nasty people out there but thankfully it is now non-smoking and you can breath fresh air in here.  This is a place to dance, drink, and enjoy yourself in a crowd so don't think you will be sitting down and having lots of personal space to yourself.

If you grew up watching the Dukes of Hazzard like I did then there is only one way to review this place.  In summary:

KICK ASS!!!

This place is fantastic for all things about those Duke Boys and sometimes ole Cooter himself is around to further kick this place up to Infinite KICK ASS levels of AWESOMENESS!!!

I'm going to go shoot my bow now (obviously with some arrows attached to dynamite) before I call it a day so I can then start hitting up some of Uncle Jesse's special distilled magic and just wait for Daisy to show up and demo some wrastlin moves with me before we take a romantic ride off in the General Lee to ramp off some dirt embankments.

For my 1000th review I want to give a big loving Yelp hug to my neighborhood.  Yelp gimped up my 1000th review and put it under a place it did not belong in its quest to associate everything with a business but this is a neighborhood not a business.  I had to delete that review and yet again add my neighborhood.  The Garden District is my home and where I live.  This is one of the most beautiful areas of New Orleans and has some of the most amazing architecture.  There are amazing restaurants and fun bars.  This is a prime place to catch Carnival Parades and St. Patrick's events.  There isn't anywhere else like this neighborhood in the world and I love living here!

Jacques-Imo's is one of the most fun dining establishments to enjoy in New Orleans.  I have often waited 3 hours or more to eat but you get to enjoy the bar (or even the bar next door at Maple Leaf).  Chef Leonardi is often at the bar (and at Maple Leaf) and he has often bought me drinks as my group waited.  Many people from out of town seem to get irritated with the wait but most locals find it just gives us more time to enjoy our drinks.  Just use some common sense and if you don't want to wait then make sure you go early!  

The worst thing I can say about the place is the bathroom situation is "challenging" in that they are small, often a wait, and a bit hard to find.  Some of the tables can also be cramped and a bit close to one another but that usually just helps you meet new people (so if you're anti-social this probably isn't your place).  Chef Leonardi sometimes has a bit too much fun and gets a bit too tipsy for some peoples comfort but that only seems to bother tourists for the most part (so just enjoy his exuberance and merry making).  The only other problem here is that Jacques-Imo's is only open for dinner (but you can find the fried chicken and some tasty po boy's at Chef Leonardi's lunch time venue Crabby Jack's).

The food is fantastic and great value for what you get!  The menu is very comprehensive and has a great selection of meats, poultry, seafood, and vegetables (and probably a few other food groups that we only eat in Louisiana).  Jacques-Imo's also has some of the best fried chicken of anyplace in the South (much better than Willie Mae's Scotch House).  I do have to seriously caution you about the deep fried roast beef po boy (it is listed as an appetizer) in that you should probably only eat one in your entire life as it is so much fried goodness that it certainly has to have fatal levels of grease in it.  I've always had great service, great food, and great times here so it is ALWAYS a great time to go to Jacques-Imo's!!!

P & J is a New Orleans institution that has been around for generations!  Almost all the best restaurants get their oysters from P & J.  The BP oil spill hit them hard but they're back up and roaring.  These are generally among the highest quality oysters available anywhere in the area.

Falafel King looks a bit like a dive outside but is much nicer inside and they really offer a LOT above and beyond what most other Middle Eastern restaurants in the area are doing.  Falafel King has a brick oven fired up slinging their delicious flatbreads and then they also are surpassing most other places in Metairie by offering some really amazing fresh fruit slushies that really need to be experienced to fully appreciate how delicious they are.  Falafel King also is the only Middle Eastern/Mediterranean restaurant I know about that offers consistent daily specials every day of the week except Sunday.  The thing that Falafel King really dominates in is their AMAZING table service if you dine in they really treat you as an honored guest and your drink will certainly stay filled during your visit.  All of the food I have had so far has been really delicious and they really use quality meats along with seasoning the dishes to have fantastic flavor.  They also have a great selection of sauces they serve with your food that take a lot of things to a totally different level with their garlic sauce, yogurt sauce, tahini sauce and spicy pepper sauce.  Their bread really is a step above the typical pita most of the other Middle Eastern/Mediterranean places serve and they have a flat bread that is NOT pita and much more delicious.  They really treat you like an honored guest here and often they give out free samples of many of their amazing food offerings to tempt you into indulging more while also teaching you how GOOD so much of their food is.  I got a free sample of one of their fresh fruit slushes made with fresh watermelon and it was AMAZING and totally convinced me to add their slushes to the items of MUST have at Falafel King as I had pre-conceived notions of a Slush-Puppie or Icee which the Falafel King's version is NOTHING like those as they are real fruit and some of the best frozen things I have ever samples so you have to try them!!!

Do yourself a favor and try this place out as they really take great care of you from my experience.

Check out my video review of my experience here:

https://youtu.be/Iogkjx2STcU

The most dive of dive bars and it is ALWAYS Christmas!!!  The dedicated don't even go til 4am but happy hour is 9pm-Midnight.  It is a glorious dream & dank nightmare that blurs and melds into an alcohol induced numbness of sensation that both terrifies and fascinates all at once (damn that tiny evil Santa!).  Always an interesting crowd and the most unusual things to see and hear going on.  Usually some pretty good music being played by the bartenders and somehow shots (usually Jager or Jamison) always end up being put in front of you whether you ordered them, want them, or even run from them.  I've seen & experienced some very strange things in this filthy glorious place but I don't recommend sitting on the couch just from what I've seen.  Sadly when the sun comes up they kick everybody out and make them go home (or to Ms. Mae's or Brother's Three but that is another story).

This is just a magic Willy Wonka candyland!!!  They have some fantastically decorated desserts and sweet treats in here that are nearly too pretty to eat but they taste mighty good when you do!  

They generally have a nice selection of good but not fantastic gelato (as several of the flavors are very mild and if you were blindfolded you might have problems discerning some of the flavors from the others).  I'm also not the biggest fan of their espresso (I much prefer Angelo Brocato's).  Sucre is also a bit pricey for what you get but they do give very large scoops for even their smallest size of gelato.  

It is hard to find anywhere else that has such beautiful presentation and artistically crafted deserts along with the fact they stay open very late (especially on weekends) so just for that they rank 5 stars.  They recently added alcoholic concoctions and I haven't yet sampled any of those so that is an adventure still to be had.

Mardi Gras is one of the things that New Orleans is famous for and arguably something that New Orleans does better than anywhere else.  Mardi Gras strictly refers to Fat Tuesday but in common usage it often refers to the entire Carnival Season which starts after Twelfth Night, on Epiphany (Jan. 6th). It is a season of parades, balls, and king cakes.  Celebrations are concentrated for about two weeks before and through Fat Tuesday (Mardi Gras in French), the day before Ash Wednesday.  There is generally at least one major parade each day and many days have several large parades. The biggest parades take place during the final five days of the season. For the last week of Carnival events occur EVERYWHERE in New Orleans and the surrounding area.  Parades in New Orleans are organized by Carnival krewes and the Krewe float riders toss "throws" to the crowds.  Throws include beads, doubloons, plastic cups, and toys.  Living in New Orleans and experiencing an entire Carnival Season is an unmatched experience and makes life anywhere else during that time painfully dull!

Its a holiday that I get the day off for that folks in other parts of the country have no real clue about.  This is the end of long and amazing Carnival season that really distinguishes New Orleans from the rest of the United States and most of the world.  Being virtually anywhere else on Mardi Gras day but New Orleans is a terrible idea as this is the center of an amazing celebration that is roaring to its conclusion until next year.  There are so many activities, king cakes, parades, events, balls, parties, dinners, lunches, snacks, excessive costumes, total lack of clothing, elegance, decadence and sheer exuberance.  There is just nothing else like it!

Simply the best snowball ever!!!  Once you have a Hansen's you just don't want any other snowball as the Hansen's ice is the best thing ever!!! They make all their own flavors and focus on quality.  I usually get one of the delicious tart flavors or coconut and actually there are a few of the regular flavors I'm actually not very fond of.  If you want a completely different experience get one of their cream flavors and then the snowball takes on the characteristic of an ice cream cone that banged a snowball which then gave birth to the cream flavor snowball!  The regular strawberry flavor here really doesn't taste good to me while the cream strawberry is awesome and has real chunks of strawberry in it so definitely make a point of trying a cream flavored option at some point!  The only bad thing is the sometimes very long line in the very hot heat as they don't have air conditioning here.

I rarely give a 1 star rating but if a place deserves it, that's what they get.  So when I heard about this new discount store opening on the south side of Mooresville, I felt I should check it out even though I am not a fan of discount stores in general.  This place was below my expectations!

The premise here is that each week, a couple semis will unload their items into aisles of bins.  On Friday and Saturday, everything is only $5.  They are closed on Sundays, but on Monday, the prices start decreasing.  So Mondays, everything drops to $3, Tuesday to $2, Wednesday to $1, and for a couple hours on Thursday mornings, everything drops to $0.25.  It sounds like an interesting concept but that is where it ends.

On opening day, photos were posted of people getting 32" televisions and drones for only $5!  However, all sales are final as is.  If there are no instructions, you figure it out.  If it simply doesn't work?  Too bad.  No returns.  

I decided to go on Monday after knowing they were closed on Sunday.  What I walked into was a place where shoppers with giant carts (most left them angled in the aisles so it was hard to get by) and bins of random items:  some in boxes, some without markings (but you can't open them to look.) Some items were in plastic bags and others were just loose.  No sense of order.  Even though there was an entire day for the staff to straighten things out or group items.  No effort at all.  I guess when you charge so little, they don't want to pay anyone to actually make it seem better.  

When I compare it to a discount place like Ollie's on the other side of town, this place makes Ollie's look like an upscale experience.  There you can find things by type and orderly.  Here, it's just like going to a hoarder's place and wading through it.

Unless you are so desperate to spend a little bit of money, I would suggest staying away and wait for a nice garage sale.  It will be interesting to see if more televisions and expensive electronics continue to show up each week of if that was just a ploy to kick off the business.

By Monday, all the high end items were gone.  I'm curious how long this place will last.

Review #3434

I stopped in for lunch on a Sunday back in March.  Construction was still going on for the new outdoor seating, so I took a seat near the front of the restaurant.  This sister restaurant to Bakersfield (just a few doors down on Mass Ave.) had minimal decor making me wonder if the main restaurant was still being worked on or if it was their choice.

Based on the waitress' recommendation, I went with the fried chicken, cole slaw, fries, and an Abita Root Beer.  The food was brought out quickly and I began dining.

What I was immediately aware of from the first bite of the plentiful chicken is that it was very salty.  I found out afterwards that the chicken is brined before deep frying.  That saturates the chicken with salty taste instead of just on the surface.  So, I was surprised at how salty the breading of the chicken was too.  It was just too much salt and overloaded the chicken flavors.  I tried eating the chicken with the cole slaw and/or taking a quick sip of the root beer, but all that did was make them salty.  

I can't comment on their evening atmosphere or beverage options, but based upon my lunch experience, I probably won't be back for the chicken.

Review #50

I dropped in for lunch on a Thursday (4-14-16) after seeing Tropicalismo make the Top 15 new restaurants of 2015 in Indpls Monthly.  The restaurant is located on the north end of a strip mall, so there was plenty of parking, but minimal effort of creating any atmosphere.  Basically, some music and a large mural were the most significant contributors.

As I walked in, I couldn't see anyone in the place except working back in the kitchen.  I finally was able to get someone to greet me who seemed to have very little command of the English language.  So, I sat myself and received a nod.

I placed an order for Empenadas to start with and then the Costillo a la BBQ which came with white rice, a small salad, and beans.

For an appetizer, there were three Empenadas (enough for an entree) along with some delicious, but unidentified dipping sauce.  The turnovers had a pulled pork center and the dipping sauce was very complimentary to the flavors.  The ratio of pastry to meat was a little heavy on the pastry side.

The barbecue was okay, but nothing unique or especially tasty.  The beans were heavily seasoned (more than I would like) to the point where the bean flavor was minimal.  The salad and white rice were basically flavorless. 

To sum up, I was hoping to experience some unique and delicious flavors of another culture.  I came away disappointed and wonder how the restaurant was staying afloat.  During the entire lunch, not a single customer came in for seating.  Only a single person came in for an order to go.

Review #29

I was very disappointed with my most recent dining experience at the new location of Chef Mike's.  I had enjoyed my visit when it was in that hard to find location, so I thought having this new location would help business bloom.  Sadly, everything was disappointing.

From the sign out front painted over the still legible Abuelo's (the former occupant) to the cone in front of the door (Why was that in the way?), we questioned whether the place was really open for lunch.

Inside, the place still looks like a Mexican restaurant but with a few flags and football pictures on the wall.  And my wife and I were the only ones n the dining room at noon.  That didn't say much for such a huge place.

Our server did a good job of getting with us, but the kitchen let us down.  First, they didn't have the fish (trout) option available.  So I ordered a Mandarin Salad and a tenderloin.

The salad lettuce was brown around the edges (which I removed) and just lacked freshness.

The tenderloin was seasoned well, but the first bite I took was a glob of sinewy fat. YUCK!  Nothing like having to remove food from your mouth and stash it on the side of your plate.  Fortunately, the rest was pretty good.

When you are the only dining customer in the place and the kitchen sends out food that is sub par, that means somebody isn't paying attention.  I can't see coming back after this disappointing experience.  

Rev. #50

I was hoping there would be a lot to find in this over-sized warehouse, but I found the place to be congested and messy with the quality of items you might find at a garage sale, not an antique store.

Lots of booths were in disarray, over packing their space with everything they could instead of trying to showcase their best stuff.  I walked through the entire building (except for the food and electronics places on the periphery) and felt there was little stop and look at.  I did notice that the back and east side of the floor space seems to feature more large pieces of furniture if that is of interest to you.

I probably won't return.

Review #2055

I had intended to try out the food trucks each Friday during the summer that locate on Georgia Street, so even though I was running late in the lunch hour, I noticed there were still about a half dozen options lined up serving customers.  After finding some metered street parking near Union Station, I walked the block over to the trucks and decided to try out NY Slice (it is based out of the south side restaurant).  

I saw there was an Italian Sausage Combo option available and went with that.  The menu states that the sausage comes topped with peppers and onions, as well as with a beverage, chips, and a cannoli (all for $11).

So I placed my order, paid, and waited a few minutes for them to call my name.  In fairness, it was after 1 pm when I placed my order, so it is possible that there had been a run on that choice.  But for whatever reason, instead of telling me they had run out of peppers and onions, someone in the truck decided to add the chili sauce instead.  I carried my meal when called back to my car and realized that I didn't get what I asked for.  I understand that if they run out, they can't go get more, but they should mention it to the customers.   Otherwise, you get bad reviews.  See how that works?

The sausage itself was fine.  Not very spicy.  Just enough to tell it wasn't a hot dog.  But without the blend of flavors that the peppers and onions would have provided, the sausage was disappointing.  The chili sauce was supposed to be spicy as well, but it wasn't.  And the flavor was not the great when paired with the Italian Sausage.  

Overall, just a disappointing meal for the price.

Review #2864

My wife and I went with another couple to a local gathering of food trucks for lunch.  Because we are retired, we were able to be there before the crowds got too big.  So, we had very little wait in getting our order turned around.

I ordered the Scratch Burger - 1/3# ground beef, bacon marmalade, arugula, & gorgonzola cheese on a toasted bun as my sandwich.  I ordered it medium (cooked correctly to order).  Having read the excellent reviews, I was disappointed with the results.  I took two bites before I tasted the bacon marmalade.  I also noticed the gorgonzola had not melted at all, so the flavor didn't blend as smoothly as I had expected.  Finally, the burger had no sear for browning, so the beef was rather bland as well.  I didn't add any condiments because all the other reviews had cautioned not to.  Just a miss for me.

I also tried the Poutine de Peru Fries with Peruvian yellow pepper sauce, queso fresco cheese, and cilantro.  Unfortunately, this was another miss for me.  I accept this as partly my fault for ordering it since I am not a banana pepper fan, but I am trying to expand my palate to include the wave of world cuisines that have come to Indy.  I own that, but the fries quickly became soggy and flimsy.  Just not worth the upgrade.  I should have just gone with the traditional fries.

I did order a Strawberry Basil Lemonade which was really delicious.  Too bad it was the highlight of my meal.

My wife ordered the Scratch Grilled Cheese - with red wine braised short ribs, caramelized red onion, muenster cheese, arugula, & colby jack cheese on toasted honey white bread.  This sounded fantastic, but was another disappointment.  When described as grilled cheese, she expected the sandwich to have enough cheese so that it would ooze when bit into.  Frankly, there was so little cheese that it appeared spread on with a knife.  It should have been called a short rib sandwich.  That was disappointing enough, but the flavor of the ribs was completely different than what she expected.  They were just bitter!  I took a bite and noticed the odd flavor, but was hard pressed to identify it.  Later on, I tried more since my wife didn't even want the second half of the sandwich.  The only thing I could come up with is that the red wine had reduced to concentrate the tannins bringing the bitterness as the strongest flavor of the sandwich.

I am not sure if we just caught the truck on an off day or if my tastes are that different from those who gave this truck high ratings.   For me, I am not sure that I would give the truck another chance with so much competition out there.

Review #84

It was over seven years since I last dined at PF Chang's, and this latest visit will probably be my last.  The food was okay, though some of the pairings were odd.  It was mainly a management and service issue that made for an unpleasant visit.

I hate going to meals in large groups because it always, ALWAYS brings out the worst in service.  Our group of 13 which had reservations, was assigned a single waiter to serve us on a Sunday afternoon.  (He also had a 6 top and two 4 tops as well.)  No busboys.  No one to help on water glasses.  Just a little help when the food was brought out.  This is bad management to not have anyone help on a large group.  

And as much as I wanted to have sympathy for our server, he made a lot of mistakes in his organizational skills that kept putting him farther behind and keeping our table waiting so that our lunch took a full two hours.  We tried telling him at the beginning who was on the same bills.  He didn't want to hear it until the end.  We couldn't even get water until the last couple arrived, so we then had to wait for our beverages.  (I got one replacement glass of water in the entire 2 hours.)  We asked for our bills, he had them in his hands, and without delivering them, went to take another order, then logged it in, then brought out our bills.  Why didn't he drop off our bills, then go take the order while we filled out the tips and payment?  Items like additional drinks or "to go" boxes were just not delivered.  We ended up having to go to the bar for additional drinks and get our own boxes from a service counter.  Just horribly inept service and no clue that things were going bad. 

It's sad when you go out to celebrate an occasion and all everyone talks about is how bad the service was.  I never did see anyone from management come by to see how things were going.  We were just glad to get out of there before dinner.

Done...finished...won't be back.  And I think I'll turn down any invitations to large gatherings from now on.

Review #2348

I feel bad for the guys in the kitchen.  I stopped by for lunch and after seeing the sign to seat myself, waited a short period for someone to stop by.  A guy from the kitchen informed me that he was sorry, but there were no waiters working that day.  He would try to do his best if I wanted to stay.  I had traveled over 45 minutes to Irvington, and doubted I would be back anytime soon, so I decided to give it a shot.

I received a menu and some ice water and when I found what I wanted, went up to the order counter and let the guys in the kitchen know that I was ready.  

A short while later, the same kitchen guy apologized that neither of the kitchen workers knew how to make a boba tea.  So, I settled for the water.

While waiting, I noticed the continual assault by houseflies buzzing around the window and occasionally annoying me.  I've seen this issue commented on before and it made me wonder why this issue isn't taken seriously by the owners.  I've dined at over 700 restaurants and have never experienced a problem this bad.  The guests sitting on the other side of the room didn't seem to have the problem, so it must have been something about the windows attracting them.  A quick look at the floor let me know that it could use a deep cleaning as well with a buffer.  Very dingy.  I wondered if the kitchen was in better shape and if I should leave.

Fortunately, the banh mi I ordered arrived and was amazing!  Fresh ingredients topped the toasted sandwich.  The crust had a nice crunch and the pork n' shredded pork was delicious!  I would gladly recommend that to someone.  But I would suggest getting the order to go....the inside looks unfinished (abandoned murals, open holes in the air system) and questionable at best.  Sad.

Review #1123

Pancake house by day, steakhouse by night!  If you have read any of the other reviews (particularly for Gaucho Steakhouse), then you will see there have been a number of bewildered guests that have dined here.  The family that owns this brunch restaurant closes the place at 3, cleans up, and then reopens as Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse at 5 pm.  Both restaurants use the same entrance and space, but the signs over the entrance make it look like the pancake house is on the left and the steakhouse is on the right.  Just go to the left, regardless of when you dine here.

Okay, so the space inside is not designed for clearing things up.  There are large murals on the walls celebrating breakfast and area sports teams.  And there are posters about steak as well.  The space is broken up into two shotgun style dining areas.  The one on the entrance side has a number of tables and a bar area towards the back.  The space to the right is divided by a mirrored wall that is lined with booth seating for the tables that are located there.  Pull out chairs sit on the opposite sides of the bench seating.   

Anyway, I ordered my brunch selection and a bottomless cup of coffee and was generally pleased.  The "Original Benny" came with two poached eggs, a buttery Hollandaise sauce, English muffin halves, and Canadian bacon.  Pretty well executed and tasty.  On the same plate, some crisped hash browns came with the order to help mop up any of the sauce left over.  On a side plate, a colorful fresh fruit plate offered melon, red grapes, and orange slices.

The service was okay....efficient comes to mind.  Not a lot of interaction or welcoming attitude.  I could understand if it was a busy day, but the room seemed less than half full.

Overall, if you are hungry, the food is good and you just have to trust the staff to lead you to seating.  Don't over think it.

Review #503

For lunch on Saturday, my wife and I headed to Irvington to try BitterSweet.  Having lived on the east side for eight years, we were really hoping that this restaurant would be another link in the restoration of the Washington Street area.  Sadly, we left a bit disappointed.

Arriving just after noon, we found parking behind the restaurant.  We followed directions and seated ourselves.  Our waitress greeted us and saw that the table needed a bit of cleaning, so she took care of that.  When we placed our beverage order, she brought my wife's iced tea, but forgot the lemon.  Then, my wife had to go ask for silverware so she could stir the tea. We noticed other tables correcting the service as well.  Little things, but clearly the lack of mature leadership on site let quality control slip.

After placing our orders, we took in the atmosphere of the place.  As described in other reviews, it is rather stark.  Also, half of the flourescent light fixtures were missing their coverings and a fair amount of those had bulbs burned out.  It just looked like it needed one good day of maintenance and decorating to be appealing.

After a reasonable amount of time, a different waiter took over and brought out our food.  He was much more attentive, i.e. experienced.  My wife ordered the Cuban sandwich, while I went with the Caprese Grilled Cheese and Mediterranean Orzo as a side.

The Cuban was pretty standard:  pork tenderloin, ham, swiss, dill pickle chips, and dijonaise on a pressed bollio roll (with seasoned kettle chips).  She let me eat about a third of her sandwich and we both felt the sandwich was rather bland.  The dijonaise was spread very thin and was barely detectable.  There were probably only two small pickle chips per half, so that many bites missed having the complimentary acid to round out the flavor.  The ham was far less in proportion than the tenderloin, so any saltiness that would be expected was reduced as well.  Simple adjustment to this sandwich could have made it delicious.

My Caprese Grilled Cheese sandwich was loaded with lots of cheese (provolone, fontina, and mozzarella) so that it had that oozing gooey texture that I expect in a grilled cheese.  It also came with roasted tomatoes (delicious!), fresh basil, and a touch of balsamic glaze on grilled sourdough bread.  Much better overall than the Cuban, but the bites of tomato were not evenly divided so that about half of my bites got no tomato at all.  The cheese and basil were fine, but the bites with tomato were fantastic.  So, what could have been a home run, was hit and miss depending upon the bite.

The Mediterranean Orzo side dish was served and upon the first bite, we realized that this was a cold salad, not something freshly cooked and tossed.  The salad came with spinach, sun dried tomato, red onion, kalamata olives, artichoke hearts, and feta cheese.  It was okay, but labeling it as a side instead of a salad led me to believe it would be warm. 

I am giving the restaurant the benefit of the doubt since we didn't order any of the tasty cakes in the display case.  I hear they are delicious, so I will give them a third star for potential.  

I don't think this restaurant would have much difficulty raising my rating with a bit of oversight and care, but I probably won't drive 45 minutes again to give them another chance.  If any of their regulars are on Yelp, please post if you see the management make an effort to fix up the decor and the service.

Review #94

Timing might be the biggest cause for my mediocre rating of this nature preserve.  I expected there not to be many flowers in February, but the recent rains really curtailed my enjoyment of exploring the trails.  So, I only visited the prairie side of the park.  There are lots of bird houses on poles throughout the prairie side.  There is a covered kiosk area near the pull-off (not really a parking lot as just a patch of gravel by the roadside.)  The kiosk had plenty of room to display information , but what was there looked aged and didn't really catch my attention.

So, I hope to get back this spring, after a dry spell, to check out the flowers and greenery as well as the back woods beyond the prairie while taking a long hike.

Review #610

I was really surprised by how much there is to do at this park.  There are baseball and basketball areas, an aquatic center, a few shelters, a playground on the north end and a Play 60 Colts inspired playground/fitness equipment area.  But try as it might to be inclusive, the park needs some capital investment in basics like walkways that aren't broken and sadly, more surveillance in the parking areas.

I had been here before about a year ago to take photos of the Thomas Taggart Memorial.  Taggart was the Mayor of Indy from 1895-1901, became a Senator in 1916, and founded Riverside Park.  The Memorial was built in 1931 and was thought to be a treasure of Center Township, but has fallen into disrepair and has been closed off by fences to prevent further vandalism.  A study was done around 2005 to spend $1.3 million to restore the stability of the Memorial, but even now there is little evidence that anything is happening.  This could be a great location for all types of events if restored.

There is another building that hosts functions, but it seems rather mundane compared to the Taggart.

One of the newer additions to the park was the Play 60 inspired playground/training equipment that is on the 24th street end of the park.  Colts logos and colors are prevalent throughout the area since the NFL is behind the Play 60 (minutes of exercise/activity each day) program.

I will admit that most of the equipment and shelters appeared to be in pretty good shape.  But like I've seen mentioned in reviews of other city parks, the convenience of having parking lots away from busy streets can attract adults engaging in inappropriate activities.  As I was driving by on a Sunday afternoon, a group of men had gathered in one of the street side lots and their behavior was offensive enough to keep me from stopping.  There is no way I would have wanted to take my grand kids to the park after seeing that behavior.  I can only hope it was an isolated event, but the fact that none of the other men stopped the offending individual was deterrent enough for me.

I truly believe this park has the space and basics for becoming a really good park.  But in the meantime, a little more police presence might be needed to make the park a bit more family oriented.

Review #714

My wife and I stopped by for lunch on a Saturday and arrived just as they opened. One of the employees was still mopping the floor while we waited for our server to arrive to take our orders.  Since our order was first in line, we had great turnaround on having our food brought out.  We started with an order of gyoza (5 dumplings) which were crisped and served with lemon slices and a small amount dipping sauce.  The flavor was good, but the serving tray reservoir for the sauce was too small for the dumplings to be dunked in so about half the sauce went unused and too little got on the gyoza.

We each were brought a side salad before our entrees came out.  The iceberg lettuce was crisp and generally bite sized and loaded with the house dressing.  The flavor was quite good, but they could have used less dressing.

I also got a bowl of Miso soup which I found to be one of the best I've had!  As I stirred it, the soup went from a mostly broth like appearance to a more cloudy look.  The flavor had a more salty taste than most versions I've had elsewhere.

But then the entrees arrived and the disappointment arrived with it.  My wife ordered the Beef Teryaki and she might as well have ordered an ill prepared liver and onions.  The pre-sliced beef was served with a teryaki sauce on top, while presented of sliced white onions.  There was nothing about onions in the description, so she was surprised.  The beef was over cooked and dry, especially on the outer slices to the point it was tougher and chewier than it should have been.  The plate came with some unseasoned white rice.

I had ordered a Bento box and it came with more of the plain white rice, some orange slices, and my choice of roll (avocado), and meat (teryaki shrimp) served over the undisclosed sliced white onions.  The shrimp was also over cooked so that they were rubbery.  The flavor was good, it's just the texture was unappealing.

So, some of the apps were good, but both entrees were misses.  Having read some other reviews, I was expecting much better quality.  

Note:  The approach to the restaurant out front could use some cleaning and the stairs were quite steep.  If you have trouble with stairs, I suggest approaching from the rear where the parking lot is the same level as the restaurant.

Review #771

If you love disc golf, you may love this park.  The full 18-hole course is nearly a mile in length.  It has holes that are in the woods as well as ones on the open green space.

If you aren't a disc golf fan, there isn't much else for you here other than walking the course and a few narrow trails along the river.  There are a few picnic tables and grills, but no shelters or restrooms.

And if you're concerned about your car hitting potholes as you drive in, you may want to look elsewhere to visit.  The gravel road was in bad condition and made it challenging to get back to the paved parking lot...which has its own roundabout!

Review #738

This place was by far the busiest of the three gift shops on Mass Ave that my wife and I explored.  With a name like Silver in the City, she expected it to be more of a jewelry store.  When she passed by that section of the store, no one asked if they could help.  There was a lot of stuff, a wide variety actually, but the place felt cramped and crowded with a line stretching back from the pay counter like you would see at a department store with kids waiting to see Santa.  Either not enough help or enough registers...not sure, but I found the experience difficult to maneuver and actually look at the goods.  Maybe I will have better luck on a weekday when the crowds aren't so large.

Review #1834

After taking photos on the Monon, I stopped in for a late lunch at Bub's.  I liked that they had a patio with a view of the Monon and inside, colorful small rooms create more private dining experiences than the big open air dining places elsewhere.

And the service, though quite active, managed to be friendly and keep delays to a minimum.

The only problem was the lunch was nothing to rave about.  I ordered a pot roast sandwich that comes with potato salad.  The meat was tender, but only lightly seasoned.  There is a house horse radish sauce, bacon, cheddar, and pickled onions on mutli-grain bread.  First, the onions were very tart which threw off the balance of the sandwich for me.  Nothing exactly wrong, it just didn't appeal to me.  There was also a texture problem.  The bacon was thick and chewy while the rest of the sandwich was tender.  So, biting through the bacon was awkward.  I often pulled the bacon part way out of the sandwich while eating.  Maybe a little thinner bacon would work better here.

The potato salad had bacon pieces in it and was okay on flavor, but the consistency was too thick/dry.  I like it a bit more creamy and less clingy.  

To be fair, this place specializes in breakfast and I just don't get up to Carmel for breakfast very often.  If I do, I will give Bub's another shot.  But, at least on this visit, the food left me without anything to rave about.

Review #3125

After having such a pleasant experience at the Mass Avenue store where we made some purchases, my wife and I made a point of exploring the Nora shop to see what else we might find.  Sadly, this store doesn't have nearly the diversity of items that the other store has.  And though there were three staff working (two were behind the counter without customers) and one was doing inventory), it wasn't until we were getting ready to leave that the one doing inventory greeted us.  So unlike the store on Mass Avenue where they asked if we had shopped their before and took the time to explain the fair wage system that they use, we could have come in and never known anything about the items on display.  I will stick to the Mass Ave store.

Review #2051

This park is nicely maintained and has a shelter and playgrounds with some open spaces for active sports.  It is on a hiking/biking trail so it makes for a decent rest area.

But it is a cookie cutter park lacking restrooms and running water that visitors (both park and trail types) could benefit from.  The mature trees are at the perimeter and so shade is limited to the shelter or sitting in your car.  Not much for older kids to do unless they have enough for a team activity.

Review #768

I went on a Sunday afternoon to this beer garden in Irvington.  There wasn't any special event going on, so there wasn't any food available, or entertainment like a party or movie.  Just a nice open space with pergolas, a variety of tables, and a fire pit.  I will also say that going by myself didn't help any since there was nothing going on but people with their dogs drinking beer.  

Getting here is also odd.  You can see the venue from Bonna Avenue, but you can't drive straight back to it.  There is a fenced off private parking lot directly north of the garden, so you have to enter on the gravel (and somewhat bumpy) driveway on the east side of Coal Yard Coffee and then drive back behind that building to use the gravel lot east of the garden.

There is a metal ramp to get up to the garden level and then most of the patio area is a wooden deck.  I did find it odd that the area by the fire pit is not level with the deck and has a different base.  I wasn't watching and nearly stumbled when I stepped off the 1 1/2" drop while going towards the pit seating.  

During my visit, I didn't notice any wait staff, just a guy sitting inside the building behind a counter.  I couldn't read the handwritten names on the taps, so I had to ask what they had available.  After I learned that they don't do flights, I settled on trying their Oktoberfest (a German Marzen ale).  They serve in plastic cups and I noticed a number of covered trash cans around the patio for convenience.

The beer was okay, but not my favorite.  The patio was nice, but I could sit on my own porch and drink a beer.  I thought the bartender would be a little more welcoming when I mentioned it was my first visit and when I asked about flights, he said I should just go to the regular brewery on Washington Street.  They had no intention of serving those here.

My advice?  Watch their Facebook page for an event.  Go with some friends and bring your own food to snack on.  Otherwise, it is just a nice place for the locals to hang out and gather with their dogs.

Review #3178

This small Asian restaurant is tucked away in a stripmall on the north end of the International Marketplace.  I found plenty of parking out front and entered for lunch just before the place started getting busy.

The restaurant offers Vietnamese and some Chinese food items.  I decided to go with the Yelper recommended Bun Bo Hue (Spicy Noodle Soup) with lots of long thin noodles, beef, "beef tender" and pork.  While waiting for my entrée, I ordered a small batch (3) of Crabmeat Rangoon.

The rangoon came out soon and were still steaming hot inside.  Although the wrap was generally crisp, there was a slight chewiness to it.  The flavor was quite good, but the chewiness was enough to detract my attention from the flavor.

Before long, the soup arrived and Wow!  What a huge bowl!  The bowl was a full 9 inches across three inches deep.  It was filled with a spicy broth, long thin noodles, and cuts of beef, beef tender (?) and pork.  On the side comes a small plate loaded with bean sprouts, a lime wedge, sprigs of purple basil, and sliced jalapeno peppers with seeds.  I asked the waitress and she said to squeeze the lime into the broth first, then add the sprouts, basil (leaves only), and pepper a little at a time to allow them to cook/infuse more flavor.

The Positive:  The broth, once it cooled a bit, was excellent!  It had a bit of heat that I would rate about medium, so a bit spicier than I normally get.  The noodles were tender like the noodles you get in canned soup.  The noodles also didn't have much flavor on their own.  The sprouts added a bit of savory and the basil seemed to take on a bit of licorice flavor.  

The Negative:  In their defense, the waitress asked me if I minded that the pork was fatty.  I figured that the fat would add flavor to the broth.  However, the pork was thick cut and not only had fat, but also had the rind (skin) which was tough and chewy.  I basically chewed the pork meat from the fat and set the fat aside on the side plate.  That was manageable once I realized that every piece of pork was like that.  What was bad was that the pork and the beef pieces were completely overcooked and tough to chew.  And, instead of picking up flavor from the spices, seemed blanched and flavorless.

So, I'll settle on an average score for the excellent broth and the disappointing meats.  I hadn't seen any comments about the texture problems of the meat in any of the positive reviews of the dish on Yelp. Maybe it was just a bad day in the kitchen.

Review #569

I'm trying to figure out what the big deal is about another franchise coming to town...especially one that specializes in hot dogs. SMH

I've heard people rave about the original in Chicago and about the crazy lines in Fishers, so I decided to avoid the things that make for a bad experience (long lines, long waits, no parking) and come for lunch during the week well after their grand opening in Avon.  

There seemed to be plenty of parking here and we were pleasantly greeted by a man passing out menu flyers so that we could look over their selections while we waited in line.  It looked rather long, but to their credit, the line moved quickly.  By the time we reached the bend, we had our selections in mind and another employee asked us what we wanted.  She wrote our order on a paper bag and when we got to the counter, gave the bag to the cashier who repeated our order and asked any pertinent questions related to our order so that we knew what our options were.  We paid and were given an order number on our receipt before being directed to the other end of the building to pick up our lunch.  

I suggested my wife pick out a spot to sit while I waited about ten minutes for my order number to be called.  There was a slight mix up, but it was corrected in less than a minute, so overall, things went pretty well.

I stopped and picked up my napkins, straws, ketchup, and salt at a counter near the entrance and then hunted down my wife to join her with our meal.

She picked a spot, but it hadn't been wiped down completely between guests, so we sat to the other side of the table (4-top).  She ordered the Jumbo Hot Dog which it truly was.  It came with a host of toppings including mustard, relish, celery salt, chopped onions, tomato, a pickle spear, and sport peppers on a sesame seed bun.  She liked the flavor of the dog, but thought the onions a bit strong and wasn't sure why the relish was a bright green....had to be some artificial coloring since I've never seen pickle relish that color.  Okay flavor, but not something she would order again.

I got the Italian Beef (I went with the standard presentation) and selected the sweet peppers.  I also ordered a small fry.  The fries were good and salted ahead of time.  No problem there.  The beef was juicy and very tender, and had a decent amount of meat in the French bread bun.  The pepper was very mild as was the beef flavor.  I kept wondering what I was missing....it just didn't have much flavor.  I think everything was cooked properly, but there wasn't any "wow" to the sandwich....just very ordinary.

So, back to my original question....why all the fanfare?  I doubt I will ever understand it.

Review #1355

I made my first trip to this buffet after having lived in town for over six years and I will say that the food is pretty good, at least it's as good as the stuff you can buy prepackaged at the grocery (from the freezer section.)  I was surprised at how large the dining area was and how many buffet lines (five in total) were available to choose from.  But I found the staff a bit difficult to communicate with and maybe it's just a cultural thing, but they don't interact with the customers any more than the minimum.

When I entered and let the hostess know I was by myself, I was directed to follow a server who showed me to a table.  She provided my napkins, utensils, and asked my drink order.  After bringing my drink, she then disappeared.  I have been to restaurants that have buffets as an option, but also allow you to order from a menu.  No menu here.  I've also been to buffets where they charge you by the weight of your purchase.  No scales here.  And in almost every case, the server/hostess has directed me to help myself when ready or at least asked if I had any questions.  I tried talking with the server and she thought I was asking her to get the food for me.  Again, difficulty in communicating.

So, I helped myself to one of the five buffet lines.  I started with a salad.  When I finished, I left my used plate on my table and grabbed another plate to try some Chinese foods, including the egg drop soup (help yourself to additional plates and bowls as needed.)  By the time I got back to my table, my old plate was cleared.  Yeah!

What surprised me was that none of the other reviews have mentioned that there are quite a few American dishes to eat here:  pizza slices, fish, chicken wings, Texas toast, and a separate line devoted to desserts.  Who knew?  It appears that you can continue going to get more food until you pop or decide you've had enough.  All for under $10.  Just amazes me how people think it's too expensive. 

Anyway, now that I know they have a wide variety of food options and that you help yourself whenever you are ready, I would probably have a better experience on a return trip.  

Oh, I also recommend flagging down your server when you are ready so that she can bring your bill.  You pay at the front desk when you are finished.

Review #1992

My wife and I stopped in for lunch in this restaurant located on the end of a mini strip mall along US 36, just west of Ronald Reagan Dr.  Plenty of free parking in the lot outside this shotgun set up restaurant.  

We were seated promptly and had good service throughout the meal.  We had very small wait times between courses, the table was cleared quickly and water refilled.  The service was really good and kept the rating from going into the negative zone.

Some of the food was really good.  Although they use imitation crab, the crab rangoon which came with a crushed peanut dipping sauce was the best I have had!  It was filled with a generous amount cream cheese and a blend of flavors that made for a great start to our meal.  

The edamame, however, was a little under cooked and needed a bit of work for the beans to "pop" from the shell.  They were also salted heavily on the top, but not much on the pods lower in the bowl.  

My wife's Thai Dumpling were made from ground chicken and shrimp which were on the bland side when compared to the flavorful pork options I have had elsewhere.  The Ginger Soy Sauce that accompanied the dumplings was a thick sauce that helped, but my wife is not a big fan of ginger, so she wasn't thrilled with the selection.

The soup course (clear chicken noodle for her, Miso for me) was okay.  Since I ordered a Bento Box for lunch, my soup and a salad selection came with the Box.  I ordered a Mixed Seaweed Salad which was more salad greens than I have had elsewhere that features the seaweed in a thread like prep.  The seaweed here was in thin ribbons atop the field greens and dowsed in a salty soy and ginger dressing.  Can't recommend this.

The Bento Box came with a choice of about a half dozen sushi rolls (8 pcs), Seafood Tempura (4 pcs), and a choice of a sashimi or nigiri option.  I went with the really good "Philly Roll" with cream cheese, avocado, seaweed, and a choice of meat (I chose eel) wrapped in a sushi rice.  Very creamy and tasty!  The seafood tempura had two pieces of breaded shrimp and calamari that had a rather bland coating.  I went with the Salmon Sake Sashimi which came with three pieces of salmon served on what I think was chilled radish threads.  The salmon was fine, just not on the same level of what I have had at my favorite places.

This is a nice place and I have not had a chance to try the Thai side of the menu.  However, when it comes to sushi, I cannot recommend this as my first choice.

Review #306

Based upon my lunch time visit, I was expecting a fabulous dining experience with my wife and our friend.  Sadly, all our entrees were improperly flavor balanced.  Maybe it was the chef's night off.

We arrived on Thursday evening and were seated promptly.  The room was very dark, relying mainly upon the natural light at the front of the restaurant and some dimly lit hanging lights that were more ornamental than functional.

Our service was friendly and efficient throughout the evening which started off well.  We put in an order for the Bacon Wrapped Apricots - tequila soaked apricots, hickory smoked bacon, jalapeno kumquat honey glaze.  These were tremendous!  There was a bit of sauce on the side that added an extra layer to the flavor!  Definitely get these!

We also shared the Foie Gras - sauternes, charcoal honey, espelette jelly, pistachios, country bread.  I really liked this, especially the bites where I got a whole pistachio.  The ladies thought it was good, but thought it a bit light on flavor.

I then ordered the "Toad in a Hole" - toasted brioche, egg, asparagus, prosciutto, roasted peppers, poached pears, shaved brussel sprouts, brie, truffle mushroom puree.  The way it was served, I ended up cutting up the entire serving first so that I could get multiple flavors in every bite.  Otherwise, there would be some bites that were mostly bread.  If you look through the ingredients, you can easily see that lots of flavor combinations made this a delicious meal.  My only complaint was that the tableware knife was too dull to cut through the prosciutto.  

Our friend ordered the Harvest Salad - endive, roasted beets, goat cheese mousse, portobello, blackberries, buttermilk vinaigrette, pistachio granola.  She raved about how good it was.  My wife agreed.  They both thought it the high point of dining.

And then the entrees came out.  

There was no balance to my Pork Belly - red chile glaze, bacon braised swiss chard, smoked onion rings, white bean puree, sweet corn relish, peach coulis, arugula salad.  Again, I needed to cut the meal completely because the plate was stacked high.  The pork was very salty.  The chard and arugula were clumped and had a more intense flavor than expected, overwhelming the rest of the ingredients.  The bites without the greens were overwhelmed by the saltiness.  It just didn't work.  I could see promise in that the pork was cooked tender and the plate looked rather nice, but the balance was wrong.

My wife had the Beef Brisket - sweet corn pudding, roasted creamer potatoes, heirloom tomato puree, baby carrots, hickory gastrique, pickled mustard seeds.  She found the brisket on the dry side.  

Our friend ordered the Fettuccini - crushed tomato sauce, roasted garlic ricotta, pancetta.  The restaurant does offer meatballs for another $3.75, but since our friend is usually a light eater, she passed and just went with the basic plate.  Sadly, the flavors were basic.  She thought spaghetti at home had more appeal than what she was served.  I get it:  If you want spicy, get the meatball.  But if they are going to offer a meatless version, then the flavors should stand on their own.

We finished sharing a creme brulee with pear sorbet and candied rice krispies.  The brulee was good, but the sorbet was teeth chilling cold (I wonder if they used liquid nitrogen?)  Uncomfortable to eat, and then it tasted like juice.  Not much flavor complexity.

I don't like writing negative reviews or down grading from excellent ones.  But I could see the disappointment in my guest's faces.  Since we traveled nearly an hour to dine, it is unlikely we will be back any time soon.  Maybe we were just a few years late catching this place when it was one of the best in town.
Rev #17

Truth time:  I didn't make a purchase, so I can't say how the service is.

What I can say is that for being a Movie and Music store, I was surprised how much of the store is devoted to other kinds of merchandise, like t-shirts.  I remember going to the mall and buying CD's and movies and having tons of options.  Maybe it's because so much streaming / downloading is going on that these types of stores need to carry items that aren't electronic.  

But I can only base my review upon what I know has gone before and though they have a nice selection, I wasn't impressed.  It's Okay, not anything unique or enticing.

Review #1907

For those of you who are familiar with my reviews, you know I try to capture the first time experience of visiting a business with an optimistic point of view.  Unfortunately, this review takes a hit to the rating because of some confusion that I was unable to clear up as well as taking place during the recent pandemic which I am certain affected product availability as well as customer service since everyone was practicing social distancing.  When employees are not actively seeking out customers to make sure they are finding what they need lessens the shopping experience for me.

I had become a bit of a hermit during the pandemic and when my wife heard a news report about this nursery becoming a part of the Sullivan's Hardware family (I really am a big fan of the main Sullivan's store with all its offerings and great service), we made the trip from the opposite side of the metro area to check out this business.  I had read several articles online that Sullivan's had purchased the business, but when we arrived, we found no signage (not even on the receipts) that indicated Sullivan's had anything to do with the business.  In fact, if there hadn't been the Big Green Egg ceramic section of the store, I might not have any idea there could be a connection between my high hopes and what I found here.  

The feel of this place, though it does offer a variety of interior decor items and plantings as well as having a large outdoor showroom of plants that include shrubs, annuals and perennials, didn't carry the hardware options and definitely lacked the charm of the main business.  This was more of a help yourself location.  If you are already knowledgeable of plants, it was fairly well marked to find what you are looking for, but if not, then a sense of bewilderment and frustration sets in.  My wife wanted some specific plants and just couldn't find them.

She did end up making some purchases of floor mats and checked out some of the wall hangings which she found many that lacked prices and others that were hung too high to read.  I was looking for a new rain gauge instead of just ordering one online but the selection was disappointing.

Unfortunately, since this business is so far from my home, I am not likely to return to update my review any time soon since there are probably a dozen other lawn and garden centers between my home and this location.  Without the special charm and service that I expected, I can't say that driving all the distance was worth the pay off at the end.

Review #3763

I'm not sure what has happened to this location.  Maybe they are struggling during the pandemic with help or maybe there has been a change in management.  This used to be my wife's favorite place on the southside to grab a burger when in a hurry.  

But on our most recent visit, we both were disappointed.  I ordered a mushroom burger with curly fries.  Both were quite bland tasting.  I did eat my fries, but only finished about half my burger.  My wife just ordered a burger and it didn't stay together and made it kind of messy to eat.  She also thought it not as good as usual.

As we pulled in to place our order at the machine (which did work and we could hear clearly), she noticed that the lot surrounding the building had not been cleaned in some time...trash, mainly from customers, was all over.  Just makes you wonder if the inside is maintained any better.  We didn't go inside, so we can only wonder.

We both used to enjoy this location when we lived in Greenwood and lived much closer.  But over the passed five years or so, something has happened.

The woman who took our order and got our food was courteous and efficient, so no problems there.  The wait time was not that long either.  She even remembered to offer condiments which so many places seem to not think of on to go orders during the pandemic.

Here's hoping that this place can find the magic in the kitchen to make their food taste good again.  Just very disappointing, though quite filling.

Review #3788

This small Chinese restaurant has low prices and quick service.  Their small shop is in a strip mall just south of Main St on SR 135 in Greenwood.  

What I liked:  Convenient parking, quick service, and low prices.  The crab rangoon was crisp and had a fair amount of crabmeat inside.  The sweet dipping sauce was tasty without making the rangoon loose its crunch.

The Beef with Broccoli had a nice flavor.  The beef was tender.

What I didn't care for:  Their is an $8 minimum purchase to use a credit card.  Not bad, just awkward to find something to add since I was low on cash.  Their plastic ware is flimsy and made cutting the hot, but barely tenderized broccoli difficult.  I couldn't spear it through the stalk with the fork.  I ended up stabbing the crowns of the stems.  

Problem:  I got an order of egg drop soup.  It was generously sized and served piping hot!  However, the flavor was generally bland, even for egg drop soup.  And there was a trace of soap/chemical in the soup.  I would have mentioned it to the staff, but since I paid at the time I ordered, I didn't see anyone after they brought my food out.  No follow up on their part and no opportunity for me to call attention to it.  

Rev #395

My wife and I enjoyed good food and service in this quirky new pizza place.  I really liked the breadsticks and the Sidekicks Supreme pizza.  

  I was surprised to find street parking just around the corner at lunchtime on Saturday.  (Free is good!)  Anyway, we walked past two other restaurants/bars in the Action Bowl building and saw the sign/stand in front of the entrance.  (It still says Shelby in bold letters over the doorway.)  As we entered, we saw the sign to seat ourselves and our waitress noticed us and greeted us, echoing the sign to sit wherever we liked.  We chose a window seat so that we could see the fountains and people watch.

  Our waitress was over promptly and maintained good service throughout our lunch.  She kept busy doing prep work while not attending us and managed to deal with carryout orders as well.  I noticed another sign that they now have Uber Delivery available.

  While waiting for our food, I noticed they have pictures of sidekicks all around the restaurant. I recognized many of them. There is also a pinball game to help pass time.  A long bar is available for patrons to order one of the bottled beers or local brews (I think there were 8 on tap.)

 Our breadsticks came out first.  We ordered 4 sticks which came with two choices of dipping sauces.  (Breadsticks can be ordered in 2, 4, or 6 and there are six varieties of dipping sauces to choose from).  We ordered the marinara and the nacho cheese.  The nacho cheese comes with red peppers diced into the sauce.  Both sauces were tasty and the sticks were flatter than I have had elsewhere, but that was a good thing.  They seemed to have a little more crispness than most I've tried.

  Our pizza arrived and was very good!  This thin crust pie had plenty of mozzarella that stretched when I lifted each slice. The green peppers were cut large, but were cooked thoroughly, so that was a nice surprise.  Plenty of flavor.  The crust itself was crisp around the rim, but just a little soggy in the center which made it hard to pick up at first.  There was just a little grease from the pepperoni, but just enough to lick my fingers, not make a mess.  Overall, I would order this again and since there were 8 slices, I had to get a box for my leftovers.

  I haven't tried their salads or sandwiches yet, but based upon my experience, I would gladly bring friends here to eat and maybe grab a brew.

Review #341

p.s.  This is the third restaurant I have been to in this location.  It is quirky here on its own, but seeing the same basic layout with new decor just adds to the oddness of the experience.

The Stutz, much like the Circle City Industrial Complex, is one of those repurposed industrial complexes filled with as many twists and turns as shops and businesses.  If you want to visit the gallery in Stutz, I suggest street parking (southbound on Capitol).  You can either walk through the gated alley from the east side of the complex or from the 10th Street alley on the south side to the outside gallery door.  

  The gallery door lets you into another grouping of business, including a loading dock with an antique fire engine.  But if you take a right as you enter through the second door of the entry, you will find the gallery just passed the elevators.

  The gallery itself has two show rooms connected by an annex that features other artists not part of the show.  The gallery is open Wed-Fri from 11 to 2 and is free.  It is also open on the first Friday that the new exhibit opens.  Most shows run a month, but it is best to check the website for specifics.  

  There are also open houses where most of the artist's studios (around 70) are open to check out and purchase art pieces.  The studios are located upstairs during the open houses.  The next open house will be April 28-29, 2017.

  During my visit, the artist had pieces from five decades of work on display.  She had acrylics and watercolors, hand cast ceramics, and drawings.  Overall, the exhibit was interesting to view, though I wasn't moved to make a purchase.

Review #247

I had good food, beer, and service on a Sunday afternoon.  Stopping in for a late lunch, there was plenty of room inside and out.  There is a small parking lot for customers and some free street parking across the street on Cornell.

Inside, the pub is quite dark.  On the north end of the pub is where you can see the brewing tanks behind glass next to the bar.  I grabbed one of the smaller tables in that section and ordered a flight of their in house brews.  The flights are about 5 oz each and were only $1.50 each.  I opted for four:  The Cerveza de Sol (a Mexican style lager 5% 10 IBU); the Nice Weiss (Hefeweizen 5.25% 14 IBU) with a mild banana/clove taste; To Helles With It (German style lager 5% 17 IBU); and I Got Rye on It (a malt liquor 9% 28 IBU).  I enjoyed each of the samples and recommend trying the flights to get a sense of what you might like best.

I was drawn in by the Indy Burger Week promotion, so I went with the tasty Cheese Crock Bacon Burger with a side of brewpub "chips" and cole slaw.  The burger can be ordered to "doneness" and since I always order my burgers with a nice char, I was really pleased how great the kitchen did the grilling.  They then dunk the burger in cheese and serve it on a thick pretzel bun with bacon, lettuce, tomato, and pickle.  I have to admit that this was one huge stack of sandwich!  I ended up squishing the bun down to fit the sandwich in my mouth.  The taste was really good.  The cheese doesn't go on in a thick sheet like when a processed cheese is placed on top.  Instead, the heat of the burger melts the cheese so that you can see the cheese down in the crooks and crannies of the burger, but see mostly burger on the top.  Still, there was plenty of cheese flavor.

The cole slaw had a bit of a pungent taste.  I couldn't tell if it was the vinegar, but it may have had a touch of horseradish inside..not the heat, just something in the taste made me think of it.  It worked really well with bites of burger, but a little stronger than expected when eaten alone.

The brewpub "chips" are the English style thick sliced potatoes, not the crispy type we normally think of here.  I think there may have been a little bit of seasoning on them for additional flavor, but I didn't notice it throughout the batch.  

This service was attentive and helpful.  Although my waitress had customers in other sections of the pub, I never waited more than five minutes once I finished a glass or my meal to have them cleared.  Checkout was fairly quick too.

As Indiana's oldest brewery, they have a number of quality ales to select from their own tanks.  They do offer a few other brewery/cidery options along with some wine and cocktails.  

Overall, I had a very pleasant time at Broad Ripple Brewpub.

Review #324

I stopped in for lunch and had a really good experience.  The restaurant checks all the boxes for expectations from a local Mexican restaurant:  colorful interior, Hispanic music in the background, complementary salsa and chips (a little spicier than most places!).  In addition to these, I was greeted immediately and shown to my booth.  The chips arrived while I was perusing the menu.  When I put the menu down, my waiter made eye contact and came right over to see what I needed.  

As soon as I finished my bowl of salsa, he brought out my entree and asked if I needed more salsa since there were still chips left in my basket.  Fast service and kitchen!

The entree (Fajita Quesadilla) appeared neatly plated on a 16" oval platter with the folded 10 or 11" tortilla stuffed with cheese, green peppers, onions, and my choice of beef (steak).  The rest of the plate was filled with shredded lettuce, sour cream, pico de gallo, and guacamole.  The steak was quite tender and had a nice flavor that went well with the other ingredients.  I quickly piled all the external ingredients atop the quesadilla and dived in.  Very tasty and filling.  The lettuce was thin cut (shredded) and not too long.  I appreciate when veggies are prepped bite sized.  Overall, as appealing visually as it was to my taste buds.

Really good flavor and great service.  Parking was free down the street and the atmosphere was clean and welcoming.  Though it has a lot of competition in the neighborhood for customers, El Arado is a strong contender!

Review #447

This combo candy shop and gift shop has some delicious confections to test your will power.  Though I noticed the variety of gifts and cards, I had my attention drawn to the chocolates counter.  (They have a variety of other types of candies including a jelly bean wall and some other fruity type treats.)

After looking over the displays a couple times, I asked and found out that you can buy the chocolates by the piece or by the pound.  I thought it best to go with individual pieces and limited my purchase so that my waistline stayed relatively the same size as when I started the day.  I decided to get a pecan snapper in milk chocolate (snapper = turtle), a cashew snapper in milk chocolate, and a dark chocolate covered pretzel.  
Because the pieces are handmade, they are on the pricey side.  (After tax, it was nearly $8!)

The flavor was really good.  The snappers were fairly large compared to the ones you see in those assortment boxes.  They were filled with nuts and creamy gooey caramel.  The only problem was that since it was a hot day, I had a bit of a mess as the chocolate melted.  (Fear not, I am not above licking my fingers to savor the last bit of it!)

Overall, I would recommend this place if you have some will power or otherwise, a very deep wallet!

Review #1214

Once I walked in from the patio on the north side of the building, the first thing I noticed was a wall loaded with awards for the prize winning ales that this place has won at the Indiana Brewers Cup.  Since 2012, it seems Bier Brewery has had prize winners.  So the bar is set pretty high for your drinking experience.

I have had a number of their canned beverages around town.  They make a variety of brews including Special K (kolsch), Weizengoot (Hefewizen), and PDG ("Pretty Darn Good" American pale).  I have enjoyed them all!

The interior is dim and filled with assorted tables, chairs, and a lounge area.  The restrooms have been designated as Stouts and Blondes, so I guess that is understood to be gender neutral (I hope so since I am neither stout, at least not yet, or blonde!)

In the back corner is the counter/tap area with a list of the current taps artistically displayed on the chalkboard.  One thing I liked was that the counter has several laminated flip folders describing each of the featured brews.  I am still learning about craft beers, so I enjoy reading the details of each brew when available.

My only negative was that the brewery doesn't have flights of beer to sample.  Instead, they give free samples in small plastic cups.  In fact, you can try everything they have on tap!  But I found the samples too small (they said 3 oz, but they actually were only partly filled so about the size of a shot) to be able to distinguish the uniqueness of each brew, especially if you don't get a glass of water to clear the taste of the previous sample.  Of the four samples I tried, only the seasonal pumpkin ale stood out and the spices overwhelmed the beer and pumpkin flavors.    For me, I would prefer a legitimate four or five ounce sample to see how the flavors hold up to appreciate the nuance of each selection.  That's why I like the flights.  I don't want to buy a whole pint and find out that I may not like how the taste develops.  

I know the brewery makes good beer, so even though I was disappointed with my visit to the brewery/taproom, I don't need to see the awards to know this place will continue on the right path.  I simply wish they would add the option of flights like so many of the other breweries around town.

Review #390
