The newest addition to the regular features of the Indianapolis Museum of Art (IMA) was very cool!  While checking out the spring gardens and greenhouse near the Lilly/Oldfield mansion, I stopped by the new beer garden.

The Beer Garden came to fruition as the first phase of the museum's plan to make the museum more approachable.  Sun King Brewery continues its support with the museum, first providing beer for last year's mini golf exhibit, and now by creating an exclusive Farmhouse Ale called "Among the Leaves" (5.1%, 23 IBU) for the Beer Garden.

The seating area is just east of the greenhouse on the north end of the IMA campus.  A pergola covers most of the seats.  There are additional tables out across the driveway for spill over crowds.  

You place your order at the outside counter where a menu board lists the ale, a German Pilsener, and a dry Riesling wine.  There are also a Root Beer from Triton Brewing, a giant pretzel, cheese Dippy, and a snack mix available along with coffee, tea, bottled water, sparkling water, and lemonade.  I ordered the giant pretzel with mustard to go with my beer, paid, and took my number to one of the long tables.  Before long, my beer and pretzel arrived and I then had the choice to eat it there, or walk the grounds with my food.  The only restriction is that you can't take the beer into the museum or off the grounds.  The beer comes in a glass so if you do wander, you need to return it to the beer garden.

As far as the quality, I really liked the beer!  It was a clear amber color and had a full flavor that I expect from a Farmhouse Ale.  And the pretzel was easily big enough to share, but I managed to devour my warm and salted pretzel on my own.  The mustard is a basic yellow, not a spicy brown or horseradish style.

The only knock I have is that the selection is rather small.  I realize it is new and they are limiting their exposure while trying to offer something for a large range of people, but when I compare it with other beer gardens, it simply isn't on an equal basis.  Sure, it has probably the best surroundings of the beer gardens I have been to, but I am trying to be fair.

  I will give them a pass on being a bit expensive since I realize the museum is trying to make money (I don't believe they receive any tax dollars, so I don't mind paying the extra amount.)  

  Note that the only way to get to the beer garden is to go to the museum first which now has a fee of $18 for non-member adults.  So, it isn't a place to go just for a beer.  But, if you want to check out a great museum and gardens, it's nice to have a casual option for grabbing a beer and a snack for strolling around.

Review #262

Wolf Run has the potential to be a really great park on the south east side.  It is easy to find just off Thompson Road and has a paved parking lot near the shelter and playground.  There is a paved walking path oval around the park and basketball courts on the west end, away from the playground.  There is no parking/street access for the courts without hiking or biking, but it offers a distance which keeps older kids from the younger ones.

  The playground has two sets of equipment:  one for bigger kids and smaller equipment for the tykes who might not be as safe on some of the bigger pieces.  They are conveniently spaced for parents who need to watch both.

  There is a large lawn area for playing athletic games, but very few trees for shade.  Maybe future plantings can be arranged to offer a break when the hot days of summer approach.

Review #676

I generally enjoyed my visit to Deviate Brewing.  The interior is a bit crowded and dark compared to a number of breweries I have visited, but the bartender was friendly enough and mentioned a couple brews that were available even though they weren't listed on the chalkboard behind the counter.  

I decided to go with a flight (4 five ounce selections) which have varying prices dependent upon the brews selected (anywhere between $8-14 for the four choices).

Lots of Stouts and IPA's are featured.  The four I chose were full flavored and I enjoyed 3 out of 4.  The PB&C, a peanut butter imperial stout was full of peanut flavor and was quite good as a special choice.  The Color Blind (blonde stout 7.8%) was another smooth and full flavored choice.  I also enjoyed the Kuppa Kopi (coffee porter 5.7%) for its smooth coffee taste without the bitterness.  I would drink each of these again!

My only choice that didn't taste quite so appealing was the Victimless Crime, an oatmeal stout orange zest.  Something about it seemed like an odd pairing the more I drank.  Even though it was only 5.3%, it seemed more boozy than the others to me, and the orange flavor when paired with the other flavors in the profile, just didn't appeal to me.  Still, 3 out of 4 ain't bad.  

It can be a little tricky getting in and out of the parking lot since it is located at such a busy intersection (96th and Michigan Rd).  I managed to time traffic okay to head west on 96th to leave, but trying to get back on the interstate or to head east on 96th during rush hour would seem difficult due to excess traffic.  Enjoy the beer, but keep your wits about you when you head out!

Review #426

I am not generally a fan of buffets and cafeterias.  Like most, Gray Brothers does tend to overcook a lot of their foods like the pork and roast beef entrees.  The green beans are also "well done" instead of al dente.  And their pies have several inches of rich meringue that overwhelm the otherwise delicious pies.  So, why four stars?  There are a number of items available that are really good!

  I like to get the dark chicken for an entree.  Lightly breaded and seasoned, the chicken is tender, juicy, and lets the flavors of chicken and a bit of salt come through.  The light crunch of the breading is a nice touch.  They are generous with the portions as well.  I got 2 thighs and a leg for under $5.

  I also like the pasta & broccoli salad.  Nicely balanced between spiral pasta and veggies, there is a sweetness to the side dish and the diced red onion makes a nice savory addition.  I definitely recommend this.

 For a side, one of my favorites are the beets.  These small whole baby beets are cooked thoroughly and are bathed in a semi-sweet sauce.  There is enough beet flavor to avoid being masked by the sauce.  Give it a try!

  The line workers are more efficient than friendly, but the staff attending the dining area seem to be a bit more welcoming.  Although you usually carry your own tray of food and beverages, the staff will clear your empty dishes, refill your beverages, and fetch a "to go" box if your eyes are bigger than your stomach capacity.  

  My wife and I don't usually dine in.  We prefer to go to the west end of the building where there is a carry out section.  It does have fewer options than the main restaurant, but most of the favorites are there.  The carry out is a great place to stop and get "home cooked" quality food without any of the fuss and dishes.

Review #445

Of all the parks I have reviewed, this one stuck in my mind that I needed to return to and see it once the flowers and greenery were peaking.  My previous review in February was when the paths were muddy and there was little sign of life.  Now that it is July, I found the trail wide and grassy (though still a little uneven under foot, so pay attention or you can stumble).  All around were wildflowers, birds and bees in motion, and a general sense that the prairie was alive and doing well.

I was able to work my way to the wooded area to the rear and right of the prairie. The path, sometimes mostly earthen, was narrower with a bit of an elevation change so that emerging from near the front required going up about a dozen steps to reach the prairie near the road.  Along the way, there were squirrels, a small creek, and lots of new forest trees that animals could be heard more than seen.  Though the day was hot, the shade and the breeze reached through the woods to make the journey pleasant and biting bug free.

The park is something that is well maintained and should be a point of pride for the community.

Rev. #35

I enjoyed my visit to Phan's Kitchen for lunch on a weekday.  The restaurant is tucked away inside Washington Square Mall on the wing nearest to Target.  There are a few decorations on the wall, but the general condition of the dining room was a bit worn.  (Hopefully the place will be successful and can invest in new chairs.)

There is a row of four-top tables on the left side of the dining room as I entered.  The order counter/grill are on the right.  I asked about seating/ordering and was told I could grab a menu and have a seat while I decided and then should return to the counter to place the order and pay.  During my visit, there was one guy handling the phones, the grill, and the cashier's duties.  So, even though I was the third customer, the order for my appetizer still took about 20 minutes (the entree came out much quicker as the boss arrived to help pick up the tasks.)

I started with the suggested Lao Beef Jerky.  Served on two green leaves, the jerky was tasty and had a nice chew, without being dry and tough.  Not exactly a Wow! moment, but still quite good.

I also ordered Pad See Ew which I've had many places that serve southeast Asian food.  I had read that this place can really crank the heat, so I played it a bit too safe and asked for it mild.  I think that robbed the dish of the fullness of flavor that I might have had if I had cranked it up just a bit more.  It was okay, just a little bland.  They do carry three sauces on each table, but I was afraid I would mess up what was a perfectly fine meal if I tinkered with it.  The only real negative about my meal was that most places I've had this dish use the wide noodles that are a bit thicker and shorter.  I checked and even the menu called for wide noodles.  But my plate arrived with what looked like very long egg noodles (maybe a half inch wide and much too long for my limited chopstick skills to securely tug out from under the beef, onions, and broccoli.)  The noodles just didn't have that texture and taste that I've enjoyed elsewhere.  

Overall, the staff was pleasant and took care of my requests for a fork, more water, and even a to go box since the portion was huge!  I hope they continue to do well.

Review #701

I stopped by to see what this location had since I had enjoyed my stop at the Keystone at the Crossing location.  This place is noticeably larger with more room to move around.  The inventory seemed to be different here.  More focus on home decor (serving dishes, rugs, etc) and less of the cute stuff that I liked at KatC.  The price is upscale which is expected on this side of Indy, so I wasn't too shocked at anything.  

They do have some whimsical items like the stuffed penguins & flamingos, but not much variety. 

The man behind the desk greeted me when I came in but wasn't intrusive as I browsed, staying at the counter while I was there.  

I didn't find anything to buy on this visit, but some things did catch my eye and made me pause to consider them.

Review #2022

I enjoyed my visit to this clean and inviting place on 38th Street.  It is located on the north side of 38th between Moller & Georgetown at Kevin Way.  There's a stoplight making it easy to get across traffic and if you make an immediate right on Kevin Way in front of the Planet Fitness, you can drive straight to this bright yellow restaurant.  Although it is elevated with several steps to climb, there is a ramp for those who need it.

  Inside is quite open and spacious.  I was seated at one of the raised booths (They do have some tables located in a section that do not require stepping up.)

  The hostess/waitress was pleasant and efficient.  She took my order and within about twelve minutes, I had my small order of Jerk Chicken.  Wow!  The flavor was fantastic!  I got eight small wing halves served wet with lots of napkins.  The had a built in heat, but not overwhelming.  They also had a nice tangy flavor that was similar to a barbecue sauce, but with a bit of additional spice to lift it to another level.  Definitely try these if you visit!

I also tried a housemade sweet drink called Byssop that is made from hibiscus flowers.  The drink is very sweet for someone who doesn't drink soda.  Once I got passed the initial blast of sweet, I adjusted my expectations and noted that it was both fruity and floral.  The deep reddish violet color was appealing and the beverage, served over ice, was transparent.  Note that an order of the beverage does not come with refills.

My main course was from the dinner menu:  Oxtail stew which comes with a couple side courses.  The stew is made with tail meat which is "bone-in" and floats in a dark brown gravy with stewed carrot chunks.  The gravy can be eaten like soup, but note that you may get pieces of thyme stem as I found several lengths in mine.  The carrots were tender and tasty.  The beef itself was very tender, but because it is submerged in the gravy, becomes difficult to cut off the bone.  I suggest asking for an additional small plate that could be used as a cutting board.  Good taste, but not a "wow" combination.

The only real disappointment was from the sides.  I got the mixed veggies since my meal was meat laden.  The veggies were colorful, but thoroughly cooked, so they were limp and not as flavorful as I hoped.  The Jallof rice was served in great abundance, probably close to three cups worth!  The rice was a bit overcooked and had become dry.  I probably could have added some of it to the gravy from the stew, but I didn't.  The rice, though bright orange in color, was a bit on the bland side as well.  I believe they add tomato and onion (traditionally), but any pieces included were unnoticeable.

So, like many restaurants that are open all day, you have to choose carefully to get the best flavor for your dollar.  Definitely try the wings and if you like sweet drinks, get the Byssop.  Otherwise, read the reviews and see what others recommend to maximize your visit.

Review #487

I stopped by here on a sunny winter day and was amazed at how bright and cheerful the place looked.  I totally respect my friend Richard P's opinion that it doesn't match well with the neighborhood in colors, but I think the target audience, i.e. children, will love it!  It's very bright in primary colors and the play area is a checkerboard of padded squares that are slightly raised to help with drainage.  There is also a grill with some bench seating and a permanent ping pong table for folks who bring their own paddle and balls (the net is metal and stays up year round.)

The playground is located on the busy one way eastbound New York Street.  It is fenced to offer a bit of protection to keep the little ones from running out into the street.  The equipment is packed closely together which makes it easy for parents to keep an eye on them, but I can see it becoming congested if a lot of kids are here.  

The playground has all kinds of unique pieces too!  I've not seen anything like the pieces here.  They still have similar functions for climbing, swinging, and sliding, but look different and less boring than most.

Parking is limited to street parking along the north lane of New York or along Jefferson.  The neighborhood is undergoing a transformation and the proximity of this park to Westminster Greenspace and a pocket park on Parkview is helping to make it more visually inviting.

Review #2302

I stopped in for a burger during the opening week.  This spin-off from St Elmo's/Harry & Izzy's is located on the street level of the Circle Centre Mall with access from Georgia Street, or from the south escalator if you are coming from the parking garage in the mall.

This is a full service restaurant, so they take reservations and have you wait to be seated by the hostess. They have multiple bartenders and have waiter staff.    The bar is in the center of the dining space, with four top tables lining the outer walls.  Multiple televisions play silently while you wait/dine.

Overall, I would rate the waiters/bartenders to be very good.  They were friendly and maintained my water glass throughout.  However, the kitchen was running behind for a place that specializes in burgers.  It took a full 30 minutes from the time I placed my order to get my food.  I get that it's their first week, but most folks working downtown cannot afford a lengthy wait on their lunch hours.  So, definitely room for improvement there.

As far as the food, let me suggest ordering the Zucchini Straws.  Yum!  Long strips of zucchini are lightly breaded and fried to a delightful crunch on the outside with a light airy filling on the inside.  The aioli dipping sauce is perfect for the side.

I decided to try the pricey Prime Degree burger, which is basically a burger with BLT ingredients and cheese (plus an aioli sauce for a condiment.)  The flavor was good.  My burger was a little more done than I ordered but close enough to not take points off.  Now here's the takeaway:  I don't know if their beef is that superior to other high end burger places, but at the end of the day, the more ingredients you add to the sandwich, the less burger flavor comes through.  My burger had a nice char flavor (as requested), but when all the other flavors were added, I couldn't really taste a difference.  I can't recommend spending $19 for a burger (without sides). 

Review #399

This new shop in Mooresville looks like it's off to great start with a beautiful collection of house plants and artisanal pots/accessories.  For a small shop, I was impressed with the variety they offered.  

In addition to the house plants, the office part of the shop carries Indie Coffee Roasters coffee (Carmel) and a selection of oils, including CBD oil.

They have a few parking spaces out front and some additional spots behind the building.

Unfortunately, the current business hours are limited to a lunch time window three days a week and only extend into early evening hours on Thursdays.  Hopefully, they will be successful enough to expand the store AND the hours if they want to compete with all the big box discount plants in the area.

Review #2109

I enjoyed browsing through Papyrus inside the Nordstrom wing (east hall) of Keystone at the Crossing.  They had a really nice window display with painted wooden holiday items that caught my eye.  Inside, they had a number of greeting and holiday cards, some games and books, and accessories for wrapping. There were even some small gift items too.

The shop was full, but not too crowded on a weekday.  Seems like a great place to grab some last minute cards/wrapping paper if you did some shopping in the mall without having to stop someplace else.  Good location!

Review #1963

I've been meaning to stop by Mudbugs for quite awhile, so on a rainy Saturday, I finally made it.  Inside, the dining area is filled with color.. bold color.  The walls are covered with images and decorations to make you think of Mardi Gras.  A small tv in the corner was playing an episode of "Swamp People" that was a bit creepy for me to think that people make a living, by choice, to hunt snakes and crocs for income.  

Anyway, there is an order counter with a chalkboard menu to the left.  There are a variety of entrees, sides, Po'Boys, and a combo platter.  

I decided to give a Chicken Po'Boy a try.  It comes with a choice of hush puppies or potato salad (I went with the potatoes).  They have some bottled beverages, but there is also a self help soda fountain to the right.

I grabbed a 2-top after being given my order number to set on my table.  The food took about 10-15 minutes to be brought out.

The flavor of the chicken sandwich was really good.  The chicken was moist and had a crispy crunch batter.  I also liked the cajun sauce that was added for a perky flavor.  The lettuce was crisp and added another bit of crispness.  Really tasty sandwich!

The potato salad was topped with paprika and was fine.  It was generally cubed potato with a mustard based cream.  A little on the dry side, but okay.  I've had similar texture from grocery brands that were also chilled.

I've not been to New Orleans, so I can't comment on how it compares, but the meal was modestly priced and had a pleasant flavor.  It's a nice alternative to the burgers, pizza, and Mexican restaurants that fill the area.

Review #2494

I stopped in this new sandwich shop which is part of a three business cooperative located midway along a row businesses in an industrial area on 79th, just east of Zionsville Road.  There are two doors leading from the parking lot:  The left one opens to Wabash Brewing; The right one opens to the adjoining space and holds Liberation Roasting Company (coffee) and this aptly named restaurant.  Note that this place is open to all ages (only the brewing area is off limits to minors.)

They have a menu board and table pamphlets to help you choose your food items.  There are sandwiches, salads, and flatbreads which are made fresh when ordered.  On this visit, my wife ordered a wedge salad while I went for the Peppa Pig flatbread and a half house salad.

While we waited for our food, I strolled over to the brewery to pick up a beverage.  My wife decided to go with a Coke which was only $1 and served in a chilled can.  No ice is available yet, but they do offer cups and straws if preferred.

Before long, our food came out and the portions were quite generous!  My wife's wedge was a full quarter head of iceberg lettuce topped with tomato, bacon bits, and a Gorgonzola cream.  Everything was fresh and crisp.  She thought the size was almost too much and that if they continue to use a full quarter, then more cream would help.  She also thought a bit of bell pepper would perk up the flavor as well.

I went with the half salad and was surprised that it was as large as a full salad most places.  I went with the Balsamic Reduction as my dressing and it was delicious!!!  It had a great combination of savory and sweet flavor along with the mixed greens, grape tomato halves, and shredded cheese.

The Peppa Pig flatbread features peppered bacon, garlic aioli, small tomato slices under the cheese, loads of fresh mozzarella, and topped with chiffonade basil.  The flavor was nicely balance and the cheese was pleasantly gooey.  My only negative was that the scratch crust was a little on the soggy side and could have used just a bit more crispness to give a nice texture to support the cheese.

Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced.  One of the three sister owners was on hand to greet, prepare, and serve us.  I like being able to support new businesses, especially where a family is so active in running the place.

Review #498

If you like quality food, then you will like Turchetti's!  I went to the grand opening and was fortunate to get there just before the lunch rush.  It's located within the former "Marrow" space, so parking is limited to street parking in the area.

Inside, there is a window processing area at the front, and once you get into the main area, the order counter/cooler/bar are on the left side; the two-top tables are in the middle; and the 4-top tables are on the right with the curing meats in a windowed room beyond those.

While waiting to place my order, I noticed the menu boards for sandwiches, burgers, and sides posted above the cooler filled with packaged meats to go.  I picked up a pack of beef franks and one of beef summer sausage.  

I was welcomed by the cashier who explained a few things to help make the visit informed.  I started with a double order of N'Duja Deviled Eggs (they come as half eggs) and went with the Pastrami (Reuben).  They also have a variety of beverages including Pepsi products, sparkling water, and a few beer selections.

After paying, they gave me a card to place on my table so that the server could bring out my order.

After a brief wait, the eggs were delivered.  Wow! The flavor was great.  I ate each half like it was an amuse bouche.  The yolks were flavored and though I can't tell you all the ingredients, the creamy texture and the light bite of the egg white added to the layered flavor (definitely an hint of vinegar & mustard seed).  They aren't filling and are worth a taste.

The Pastrami was delivered soon after and was excellent!  The rye was lightly crisped for that satisfying crunch.  Inside, they have the pastrami layered with Swiss cheese and "gardenkraut" topping and a bit of 1000 Island dressing for more flavor.  Simply delicious and it paired well with my Central State IPA.  

The only negative I had was that the place was getting quite busy since it was opening day and the line was backing up.  I think once the cashier doesn't have to take time to answer a lot of questions about the place due to all the new customers, things out to go more quickly.  Still, the line was moving pretty well while I was there...maybe 5 minutes from door to placing your order.

Review #1265

New Day has been serving meads and ciders in Fountain Square for about seven years.  So, I thought it about time to stop in and see what I was missing.

The shotgun style shoppe has a serving room in the front and a gathering place/gallery in the back half.  The serving room is lined with tables on the left.  The right side is made up of a display area for merchandise and a long bar area that has blackboards for upcoming events, beverages, and menu items to enjoy while sipping your drinks.

Since it was my first time here, I went with a flight (6 selections for $8).  They hand you a flyer that you can fill out and indicate your selections.  On the back is a listing of custom cocktails that are available made from the house beverages.

Okay, I will admit that I had no idea what mead was other than something knights and commoners drank while roaring about their conquests.  So I asked.  Basically, it is similar to wine, but made with other fruits instead of grapes.  They can also use honey instead of sugars.  However, like craft beers, the drinks can have a variety of ingredients that can take them into a wide range of flavors.

My flight had three hard ciders and three meads.  The Gold Rush (6% ABV) is a dry, champagne like drink.  The South Cider (6%) is more of a gateway beverage for someone who is used to commercial apple ciders sans alcohol.  It is sweet with the taste of apples and honey.  I also tried the seasonal Barrel Aged JC (Johnny Chapman) that is deep in flavor due to the black strap molasses (12%).  This is a drink for those who like their drinks to kind of slap them in the face with flavor!  Surprisingly smooth, it is very complex and somewhat herbal in aftertaste.

The meads I tried had a variety of flavors.  The Washington's Folly (6%) is a cherry mead with fresh tart cherry notes.  The Shelby Blue Ribbon (6%) is made with Strawberry and Rhubarb.  The aroma of rhubarb adds to the enjoyment of this one.  My final selection is another seasonal selection called Breakfast Magpie (8%).  This is a black raspberry mead with a strong coffee (espresso) infusion.  The coffee taste is strong and dominates the raspberry flavors.

As for the rest of the business, the staff seems friendly and well informed.  The merchandise ranges from t-shirts to glasses and growlers.  There are several selections available year round, but the seasonals come in roughly each quarter, but last only as long as the supply lasts.  

Overall, I really enjoyed my beverages and the experience here.

Review #251

I noticed the sign for the business on the side of the building and thought I would check it out.  After all, a name like Fancy Fortune Cookies has a certain appeal to it.  Seemed like my lucky day!

The business, located on 65th between Allisonville Rd and Binford, is clustered with a number of small businesses that use a common entrance, parking, and are grouped into a few buildings.  This business has been around for about 30 years and makes fortune cookies for special occasions.  

The entrance was colorful and featured a lot of gift ideas for presenting fortune cookies.  Once you walk into the center of the shop, there a small gift bags and sample bins of individually packaged cookies.  There were plain and chocolate covered ones.  There were flavored cookies in bright colors.  On the wall was a price list for ordering cookies (minimum order of 50) if you want to personalize the messages and the assortment you need for your special event.

If you are like me and are just looking to getting a package of a smaller quantity, they had plenty of options.  The basic fortune cookies (multi colored/flavored) sell for $8 per dozen.  The chocolate covered cookies go for $12 per dozen.  I have sampled some of each and can tell you that the flavors are fantastic! 

Oh, and if you check in with Yelp while there, you qualify for a free sampler bag of the basic fortune cookies with a purchase on your first visit. Such a deal!  

Review #389

My wife and I brought some friends to Delicia for dinner on a Thursday evening (6-2-16).  We were the first to arrive, so we were immediately seated in the area across from the bar.  The restaurant was very stylish yet inviting.  
  We also had great service with a combination of friendliness and knowledge that I wish more restaurants had.  After all, the social aspect of dining with friends can be as key to enjoying the evening as the food.
  After ordering our beverages, we were brought a small cup of Sancocho as an amuse bouche.  I am not familiar with the item, but the flavor reminded me of tasty bean broth.  
  We then shared a guacamole for the table.  Excellent flavor combination in the guac.  My wife, who normally doesn't care for avocado, even thought it was good!  The chips that came with the guac were light, but crisp enough to scoop.
  I ordered the "De Palmitos" salad (hearts of palm, field greens, roasted walnuts, butternut squash, hibiscus-lemon vinaigrette).  It was my first time trying hearts of palm, so having all these other delicious flavors gave me confidence to try something new.  I was very pleased.
  Finally, I ordered the Pescado Zarandeado (it comes without the fish head....I asked.)  The sea bass was colored/flavored with green and red achiote which made for a nice presentation.  Very tasty.  The fish came with black beans and white rice to fill out the entree.  
  With the great atmosphere, service, and food, it was plain to see why this restaurant was voted one of the Top 5 restaurants in Indy.  I look forward to my next visit.

Review #6

While on the west side, my wife and I decided to give Pho 36 a try.  I must say I agree with a number of reviews that mention that the service is friendly and pretty efficient (even though the owner/waiter was the only one covering the front including the cash register.)  The food we ordered, and we ordered a lot, came out pretty quickly and I enjoyed everything I tried.  

I started with an order of Egg Rolls (3) that were nice and crisp and filled with ground pork, egg, long rice, carrots, and onions.  There were a couple types of veggie strips along side and a dipping sauce.  The sauce was on the thin side and didn't add a lot of flavor, but it was enough to add some depth to the taste.

I also had the Vietnamese Chicken wings which had five pieces of crisp breaded chicken drumettes or flat/tips and covered with a sticky "fish" sauce which tastes like a combo of sweet and savory flavors. (I didn't find it pungent, salty, or hot.  The flavors seemed like honey and sesame seed to me.)  My wife liked these too!

I also ordered the "Special" Bahn Mi - a baguette sandwich with sliced pork, pate, mayo, carrot, daikon, cucumber, sliced jalapeno, and cilantro.  My wife thought it tasted hot, but I didn't notice the heat at all.  The ingredients are served cold, but the flavors were refreshing and quite good.  The bread was very fresh too.

My wife was new to the cuisine, so she played it safe with the stir-fried chicken with mixed vegetables.  The dish was plentiful and the rice with chicken and shrimp stayed moist, not overcooked.  Plenty to eat for the money.

I also sampled a bowl of Pho - Chicken Noodle soup.  I noticed a small plate of sliced jalapeno, cilantro, and bean sprouts, but completely forgot to add them into my bowl.  The bowl itself was huge and was loaded with noodles and large (almost more than bite-sized) pieces of chicken.  The soup itself was on the bland side, like broth with just a hint of seasoning.  Maybe if I had remembered to add my side veggies/herbs, the flavor would have had more depth to it.  

On the fun side, I ordered a strawberry bubble tea.  This was very cold and I did get a bit of brain freeze.  The bubbles are black tapioca beads that have the texture of gummy bears and were odd to watch slide up through my straw.  The flavor was exceptionally good and the drink stayed icy throughout the meal.

Overall, it was a fun place to stop and try another cuisine that is hard to find around town.  Although it has items that are similar to those offered at nearby restaurants, the business did a brisk business the entire time we dined there. it must be the service and food being a high quality.

p.s.  For additional flavor, they have Sriracha sauce and Hoison sauce bottles on the tables.

p.s.s.  Although the website leads me to believe this is a franchise of a chain, the ownership appears to be local and works in the restaurant.

Review #376

I stopped in here for lunch on a Tuesday (4-12-16).  Although it is part of a strip mall with plenty of parking, the interior is anything but typical.  A wall sized mural and elegant tables await the diners.

I was a little disappointed that some items are available in the dinner hours, so I ended up choosing a couple other items and relying upon getting a to go box for what I didn't finish.

My first item was the Grilled Shrimp with Wild Mushroom Risotto, braised tomato, ratatouille vegetables, Broccoli and Crispy Onion.  This was a nice sized portion for lunch and the flavors were well suited for accompanying the shrimp.  I would definitely recommend this.

I also ordered the Chicken Almond Croissant with roasted rosemary chicken, toasted almonds, celery, onion, tomato, bacon aioli, petite greens and barbecue chips.  Again, this was a delicious combination.  (I saved half the sandwich so that I would have something to eat later in the evening.)  

I plan on returning with my wife and friends soon to be able to sample some of the evening menu.

Review #31

After catching a quick bite for lunch on Virginia Avenue this Friday afternoon, I headed north to Shelby Street to try a flight of brews from Indiana City.  A few snacks are available at ICB, but mainly they rely upon using ClusterTruck delivery if anyone wants something more substantial to eat while sampling the local brews.

This was my first time at ICB, so after parking outside in their lot, I sat at the bar.  The flight ($7) comes with the customer's choice of four varieties.  Since I am not an experienced craft beer drinker, I went with some of the lower IBU options.

I selected the Sister City (Kolsch) as my first sample.  This was a great intro beer coming in at 4.7% ABV with only 20 IBU.  Very smooth for someone trying craft beers for the first time.

Next, I went to the Son of War (Blonde Ale) which was a very hoppy tasting Belgian style ale with a bit of citrus flavor on top of the hops.  Definitely a stronger flavor, especially after the swallow than the first brew. 4.5% ABV and 15 IBU

As my third selection, I sampled the Yacht Rock (Wheat Ale) with hints of orange peel, coriander, and fermented with witbier yeast.  The drink appears to resemble orange juice as a cloudy deep yellow color.  The taste was very pleasant though a bit higher in alcohol content than the first two choices.  6% ABV and 19 IBU.

As my final selection, I went with one recommended by the bartender based upon the information I had given her about what I liked.  She suggested the Shine (Dampfbier).  Dampfbier or "Steam Beer" is an effervescent ale brewed at warmer temperatures than most of the other ales.  This version had a hint of banana and was quite good as well.  

The bartender was very friendly and was able to carry on a conversation between dealing with customers and posting info on the blackboard behind the counter.  ICB beers are available in cans at many liquor stores around Indiana, but not groceries.  There are also a variety of options for getting beers to go in growlers and bullets as well.

Review #93

This is the third of the 5 local (soon to be 6 when the south side branch opens) Books & Brews I've been to.  Like the others, it has a book theme, a section for families to dine, and a separate bar area.

The have the five core brews on tap (also available in cans), and there are a number of smaller batch brews that come from the "mothership" location in Fishers.  So, this spot doesn't actually brew, but is a more like a pub than an actual brewery.

The staff seemed to be friendly and good at making conversation when they weren't busy helping customers or cooking.  And I must admit, the chicken wings I ordered were expertly cooked with a crispy outside and a juicy middle.  The price was a bit high for the serving size, but I found the serving to be right sized (8 pieces) for me when paired with the fries that come with the order.  (I had the "Where the Wild Wings Are".)

I like the clever names they have for their brews; all have some connection to a book title.  The available brews are posted on a chalkboard behind the bar and can be amusing to read through when seen gathered like that.

On my visits, I sampled a couple choices before ordering a Shogun Soba Ale (5.1%, 23 IBU).  It has a dark color from the buckwheat and has a somewhat buttery taste that paired well with the heat of the wings.

Books & Brews is expanding rapidly in the Indy and Denver areas while looking forward to opening in Ohio soon.  They seem to look for spaces that are already set up for business (not new construction) and can keep their start up costs lower than from building dirt up.  Nothing wrong with filling an empty space with a place providing tasty beer and some food to go with it!

Review #645

This park is dedicated to the mountain bike riders of central Indiana.  Here, the riders have right of way on the 127 acres of park trails.  Seriously, if you are a hiker or walker, please find some place else.  

The park is on the south side of 96th, immediately east (about 50 yards) of Hazel Dell Parkway.  (Hint:  It is much easier to find if you are approaching from the west so that you don't have to turn across traffic so close to a stop light.)  Inside the park, there is plenty of parking, some picnic tables, and a small shelter.  From what I saw, the trails are narrow and have some serious drop-offs along the way.  There are ponds and the river along the trail as well. 

Please note that if the trails are wet, the folks who oversee the park want to avoid damage to the trails from ruts that harden and make the trail lose its accessibility.  So ride when the trails are dry.  Pretty simple rule to comply with.

I am encouraged by the information on the Indy Parks website that there are plans for a skill and challenge feature for developing the skills of the riders in a controlled environment before confronting those challenges on a trail.

Review #736

You know, when your server greets you with a smile and goes about her job with a positive attitude, it can make your whole meal experience go well.  And when you top it off with a delicious sandwich and side, you earn a 5-star rating.  So it was with La Mulita.

I grabbed a spot in the lot behind the building and when I entered the restaurant, the sign directed me to seat myself, so I grabbed a spot outside the "bar rail" and sat in the dining area.  My server was busy delivering someone else's order and I soon realized she was not only doing the waiting, but running the bar too!  She went by dropping off a glass of ice water, apologized for the wait and said she would be back in a minute as soon as she delivered the drinks to the couple by the window.  She immediately returned and took my order.  Efficient and friendly.

In relatively no time, she brought out my Cubano and my side of sweet potato wedges served with a serrano aioli.  The first bite of the sandwich let me know the bolillo (bread) had been toasted with the crispness of the bite.  Then Wow!  The flavor of the combo was great!  There was a delicious grilled flavor in the ham & pork.  There was also a pickled tomatillo and Chihuahua cheese adding to the blend.  

I then tried a sweet potato wedge which was lightly crisped and salted.  The sweet/salt combo was good.  Then I dipped one in the savory serrano aioli and that punch of flavor was all it needed to take the flavor to the next level.  Simple flavors, but in the right combination, can make for a nice surprise.

All too soon, the meal was devoured and I thanked the server for a great experience.

Review #682

As a fan of public art, I would like to point out that the outside of the Children's Museum has a number of pieces that are probably overlooked by most visitors.  The parking in the garage is free, so I took the opportunity to stroll around the outside.  

Before you exit the garage, there is a 26' tall statue of Anubis overlooking the parking area.  This statue has been here before, but has traveled following a number of Egyptian exhibits.  Now, it is a permanent addition.

Once you cross Illinois St, there are a number of bronze statues of children playing and reading.  Two of the three are designated as memorials.  Each is a reminder of yesteryear when kids got outside to play or read a book.  

Breaking into the top of the museum, a mother brachiosaurus lifts the roof allowing her offspring to climb in.  Purely fantasy in staging, the sheer size of the dinosaur is quite impressive.

As you work your way around the building to the south, there is a series of miniature recreations of the great architecture of the world.  Kids can play/climb all over these constructs or read about the originals on conveniently placed plaques.  The last is a tribute to Anne Frank.  Anne used to look out over a tree and dream of freedom as she wrote in her famous diary.  There is an art piece that features an open diary and a young tree grown from one of the actual nuts of the original tree outside Anne's window.

On the southwest corner, another grouping of dinosaurs (Alamosaurus) is seen escaping from the interior of the building.  Fantastic coloring and lifelike (as imagined) recreation of these beasts can be quite surprising as they appear to be running towards the street!  During certain festivals and holidays, these dinosaurs often are decorated with party hats of whimsy.

Often overlooked, Beyond Spaceship Earth shows a pair of astronauts working outside their point of entry (to the planetarium a located at the back of the main floor of the museum.)  I remember being fascinated by the spacewalks of the 1960's, imagining how courageous those early astronauts were, trusting their limited technology to keep them safe in the vacuum of space and to return them home safely.  

On the north side of the grounds, there is a small mural on the building that shows a number of the exhibits within the museum.  

Of course, I have been inside the museum numerous times.  I really appreciate that they continue to bring new exhibits to capture the imagination of visitors like Avatar, Transformers, and Hot Wheels.  But they also have a number of keepsake exhibits that keep drawing me back as well (Merry Go Round, the Trains, Beyond Spaceship Earth, and the Dinosaurs.)

Science and Fantasy...high tech and primitive...activities and quiet observation are balanced within.  And quality time with the kids that grow too fast can be as treasured as any of the exhibits.

Review #141

FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:

http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

I stopped by late in the lunch hour after roaming around in the January chill.  I wanted a simple cup of coffee and noticed an eye catching array of large muffins sitting on the counter.  So, a cup of House Blend coffee and a giant crumble topped apple (caramel?) muffin for under $4.  Very cool.

The shop was being manned by the owner and he was very pleasant and helpful.  We chatted a while since the morning rush had passed.  I headed upstairs and was glad to find the coffee was served at the right temperature to drink right away.  No scalding!  The house blend was a bit stronger than I usually like, but the flavor was deep and rich and I quickly adjusted.

Oh, and that muffin was phenomenal!  Light and cakey inside, but with chunks of seasoned apple inside.  And the top was crumble topped with a slight crunch and drizzled with a hint of frosting.  One of the best muffins I've had!  I'm not sure if they make them or buy them from someplace else, but I will find out the next time I return.  

Review #2094

This museum is truly unique and has a wonderful collection of paintings, sculptures, tools, and apparel from the "Wild West" to numerous tribes of Native Americans.  On each of my visits there is a balance of reverence for the determination of early settlers heading out into what was (to them) an unknown territory and a sadness for how shamefully our country has handled dealing with a proud people indigenous to the land.

Growing up in the 60's, I had an idealized vision of the west:  Good guys wore white hats and had a loyal horse.  Gun fights happened at noon but no blood was ever spilled, and only heroes took awhile to die.

So going into the first floor exhibits of the Gund Gallery and Art of the American West was very nostalgic.  Fantastic pieces of sculpture like "The Broncho Buster" by Remington and "Chief Crazy Horse" by Baur are masterfully crafted.  Paintings like "The Twins" by Hennings and "Crippled but Still Coming" captured the flavor of my memories of cowboy life.

"A Secret Cache" by Buxton and "Blessing From the Medicine Man" pay reverence to the native peoples of the land and their lives.

Fantastic vistas captured on canvas like "Mount Wilson Winter" by Chavez and one of my favorites, the triptych "October Suite, Grand Canyon" draw you in to a world where the land was majestic, not littered with highways and oil rigs.

It is truly unique to the midwest and worth seeing for these pieces on their own.

But when you get to the second floor, and enter the "Mihtohseenionki" (The People's Place) that reality replaces the nostalgia.  There is an extensive display with timeline boards that tell the history of the Native Americans, primarily the Miami tribe in Indiana.  There are numerous artifacts to see, but the recurring theme is the numerous treaties that were negotiated usually after some bloody conflict in which the settlement meant pushing farther to the west.  Compare the rich, lush landscape of the east with fresh water rivers and great soil for crops to the desert lands that have become the last resort for many and you will understand my impression.

The remainder of the second floor is devoted to the Native American Galleries displaying pottery, clothing, utensils, and religious artifacts of the diverse societies of the West.  From desert to the Great Lakes to the northwest and beyond, there are numerous examples of artwork in the everyday lives of the people.  

The collection is truly remarkable and are fortunate to have access to it.

On a lighter note, there is a cafe on the canal end of the first floor, a family activity area on the canal level (lowest level), and for Yelpers who check in before paying, a $2 discount.  Also, parking in the garage is free if you ask for a validation pass at the time you purchase your tickets.

Review #202

This park is a truly great park on the near east side for anyone who wants to take time to visit.  It is conveniently located on the south side of Washington Street (a turn lane is there for anyone who has to cross traffic.)

I used to drive by this when I lived on the east side and drove local streets to downtown.  I wasn't impressed.  But in the time between my last visit and now, the park has undergone a half million dollar makeover (Wow!) that has made it a go to place.

  Do you want a place with shade and a shelter with picnic tables, quiet places with benches to relax, open space for activities on the far east end?  They got it here!  Do you want basketball courts, an aquatic center, and a cool playground right near the shelter?  They got it!

The park has a lot of paths (grit based) to travel on your way to the different amenities.  The playground and aquatic center (pool, slides, splash pad) are separated by the common parking lot so that the end of the lot fill faster than the center.

  Note:  There is also a memorial to Sylvia Likens on the southwest edge of the park.  If you are interested in learning more about the memorial, there is a great review by Richard P that has all the information you would like under the Sylvia Likens heading.

Review #678

What a cool venue!  My wife and I stopped by for lunch on a Saturday and the place was pretty quiet.  We sat in the bar area on the left (there is a larger seating and lounge area to the right).  

Before eating, I browsed some of the A J Foyt Memorabilia gathered along the walls and an actual race car over in the lounge area.  I then tried a flight of the white wine samples:  Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, and Chardonnay.  You only get a small pour of each, but enough to get a few sips.  I really liked the Riesling (my favorite of the three).

Our lunch arrived and I got the BBQ Chicken Flatbread while my wife ordered a salad with an upgrade of chicken strips added.  The salad was large and only loosely chopped, so she did need to cut it into smaller, more bite sized, pieces.  They also brought her a couple types dressing on the side since they didn't have exactly what she wanted.  She enjoyed her meal and there was enough for a to go box.

My flatbread was about 8" x 12" cut into eighths.  The BBQ sauce was sweet and tangy and the chicken was cubed, still moist, and warm.  The flatbread was also topped with sliced red onion and cheese.  Very good!  I thought the crust had just the right amount of crunch and held its shape despite the toppings.  Definitely recommended!

Overall, we had a fun time and enjoyed our meals and the wine.  Be sure to check their hours since they are somewhat restricted.  Also, be aware that the space is sometimes reserved for private parties that you may not be aware of until you arrive.  (Hopefully they can add a calendar to their website to show blackout dates.)

Review #2138

The City Center Park is a great playground area for children.  It is located just a block south of Main Street between US 31 and Madison.  You can tell it is well maintained and has a lot of great ideas built in.  For instance, the playground areas (one for toddlers, one for older kids) are elevated and have padded squares underfoot that provide good traction and a soft cushion if a little one happens to tumble.  The elevation allows the runoff water to go to good use by collecting in a couple rain gardens.

The trails/walkways are all paved and even though I visited on a rainy day, the paths were puddle free.  

There are several seating areas for parents to stay close to the playgrounds without having to stand the entire time.  There is also a permanent restroom and water fountain area, so no port-o-lets on site.  Parking is located along the north side of the park and there seems to be plenty.

In summer months, a splash garden is also available and tennis courts are fenced in to keep stray shots from traveling too far.  Overall, I think it is a great addition to the local parks in Greenwood.

Review #504

In the passed year, I have been both a patient and the designated driver for a loved one undergoing a procedure at St Francis/Franciscan Health Indianapolis Hospital.

In both cases, admissions made the process easy and the staff were friendly and helpful.  In my case, I had to transfer from a smaller satellite hospital that was unable to handle my needs.  This location got me in immediately and although I needed to stay overnight, was in fine shape to take off the next day.  When I compare the procedure I received to those of friends who had it done 15 years ago, mine was minimally invasive and required a minimum of pain relief in the following days.

In the case of my loved one, she had undergone the procedure at another facility and was dreading having it again because it is quite painful and requires the patient to be awake.  But this time, the process was greatly improved with far less discomfort.  Good quality surgeons and specialists to handle the procedures go a long way in the healing process.

I also found the waiting areas of the hospital to be clean and open, not cramped and uncomfortable.  There are even places where you can walk inside to stretch your limbs if the procedures run a few hours.  That was a relief to me!

I have had great results when dealing with this location.

Review #2274

What a great place to get out for some exercise and to reconnect with nature.  The park is 127 acres and has multiple foot worn trails that total about 2.25 miles!  The northwest corner of the park is a state nature preserve which is densely wooded  with most of the trails.  It features numerous small creeks with small footbridges over most and a few larger ones when necessary.  That doesn't mean you won't get mud on your shows, but at least you probably won't need to change your socks!

The rest of the park is under DNR oversight and features prairies, wetlands, and a swamp!  I really appreciate that parks don't turn everything into a lawn.  Creatures need habitats that they are used to, so when there is space, I applaud efforts to provide sanctuary to them.  The trails in those areas are limited and the wetlands have an observation platform to make it easier to see what surrounds you.

There is a grit packed pathway that leads from the parking lot to the two shelters which are less than a quarter mile from the parking lot.  There are permanent restrooms that are maintained as well.

If you are going here to hike, I highly recommend stopping by the little building at the parking lot and grabbing a pamphlet about the park.  Within it, there is a map showing color coded trails and lists how long each trail is.  This can be really useful since the trails seldom go in straight lines.  Each trail intersection has a post with a sign showing which trails head in the corresponding directions.  That is great for first time visitors like myself.

Note that the trails wind through the trees, so roots may become tripping hazards if you are looking up all the time.  There is also a limited amount of elevation change especially on the Creek Ridge Trail.  That's a good thing or else the park would flood out.  At least the wooded and prairie areas stay mainly dry.

Review #801

As I get older, I have trouble keeping up with all the fads in dining.  So when I heard about a "Paleo" diner, I wasn't sure what it meant.  But, being a fan of good food, I thought I would give it a try.

Nook has expanded their hours to include lunch, so I went the day after their first lunch serving.  As my waiter arrived, he explained how people should eat like "cave men":  no artificial sugars, no gluten, and no dairy.  Now, I have no animus against any food group, believing in the basic food groups and moderation to be my golden rule of dining.  But any given meal for me may step out of the pyramid.

So I gladly accepted the complementary sip of olive oil to start my meal.  It is supposed to be good for digestion.  I noted a hint of peppery flavor which was actually rather pleasant.

I started my meal with a beef broth bowl.  The bowl is huge!  They start with 200 pounds of beef bones and slow cook it down to extract the rich flavor from the marrow.  The broth has daikon radish, shiitake, shredded beet noodles (yellow), onion, shredded cabbage, and topped with fresh herbs.  Yum!  Note:  You can make this a full meal by adding beef to the bowl for an additional $7.

I also ordered a side of Brussels Sprouts which are shareable in size and un-shareable because the flavor is so fantastic!  I devoured the whole dish by myself.  The sprouts are halved and are grilled with shishito peppers, candied (turbinado brown sugar) bacon, and topped with a smokey paprika aioli.  The flavors were nicely layered and makes me wonder if people who say they don't like Brussels Sprouts had any idea how much they are missing.

As an entree, I ordered the short rib taco.  Instead of a flour or corn tortilla, they use ground almond which adds a nice flavor and a bit of crispness.  The short rib beef was juicy and tender, but maybe a tad under seasoned (they do have salt and pepper on each table, but I refrained from using it since I wanted to see how the flavor combos worked without it.)  The taco also has scallions, shredded napa cabbage, teriyaki, and sriracha (not very hot with all the other ingredients).  They also added shredded carrots and herbs on top.  The herbs were fresh and gave a pungent fragrance as I folded and lifted the taco for a bite.  Note:  although the tortilla holds up to the juices, some will drip out onto your plate with the orange color of the sriracha....be sure you have your napkin in place so that you don't get stained. (Whew!)

The staff was very friendly and even though they left an iceless carafe of water on the table for me, frequently did the pouring when they passed.  The front manager stopped by to see how I was enjoying the meal and even the owner came by.  I like when the folks who are supposed to be overseeing the operation actually care about listening to my feedback and don't just go through the motions.  Everything ran smoothly and the waiter even checked on a couple things for me with the kitchen to answer my curiosity.  (Note:  I go at non-peak times, so staff may have a little more time to answer.)

I doubt I will switch over to becoming Paleo.  But I will definitely be back to try some of Nook's other options soon.

Review #689

I stopped in for a bite and brew after a morning of hiking around Central Park in Carmel.  Since I was dining alone, I grabbed a spot at the bar and was impressed with the giant row of taps behind the bar.  The menu for drinks is large and two sided with all the fun stuff about the craft beers that I like:  ABV, brewery, location of the brewery, and sorted by beer type.  And I also like that they offer flights of 5 oz beers just like a number of breweries do!  So, that was the route I headed.

I also wanted to get something to eat and saw the Crab Cake Melt listed under the sandwich section.  Served on an oversized English muffin, the crab cake is covered with melted Gruyere, arugula, crispy onion strings, a tabasco mayo, avocado, and roasted tomato.  And though it looks like one of those giant monoliths that you wonder how you can fit it into your maw, relax....you can simply smash/squeeze the sandwich down to a smaller size without it shooting out the sides.  Oh, and the flavor was fantastic!  I was really surprised by how well the flavors worked together and the tabasco was tempered by the cool of the avocado.  Just lots of layers of flavor.  

With so many beers to choose from and a few hard liquors for those die hards, this is a great place to sample a large number of brews from around the state and around the country.  And the food was even better!

p.s.  The service was very pleasant and efficient.  Even though all those working in the bar would disappear at times, there was always someone back within a minute or so to make sure nobody was left unattended.

Review #944

My experience with Pacifico Hyundai was not a positive one. I was working with a negotiator who I hired to help me through the buying process. My negotiator set up an appointment for me through the manager of this location. I was supposed to go there for a test drive, plus an assessment of my current car's value. Easy in, easy out, and with intentions of buying a car if everything went smoothly. 

When I arrived and asked for the manager, he immediately passed me off to a sales rep and I knew things were not going to go as planned. When I sat down with the rep, she asked for my phone and email address, which I did not wish to give as I would not be doing any of the negotiation for the sale. This did not go over well. My test drive was pretty awkward and very short - I was reminded more than once that it was the last day of the month which made feel uncomfortable. I brought up the fact that my car was also supposed to be assessed and that was quickly shut down. 

After leaving, I immediately called my negotiator and asked that he find my car at another dealer; I simply did not feel comfortable there. One week later, I've got the car I want at the best price possible (spoiler alert: not from Pacifico).

On more than one occasion, I've found myself so frustrated by this particular Acme that I vowed to never return.  Nevertheless, its close proximity to my apartment has lent itself to repeat trips for the sake of convenience.  I can't think of a trip to this store where the experience has not been flawed in some way.  Basic grocery items are often out of stock.  There are hardly any workers so the lines are always long and there inevitably ends up being a problem at some point that requires the involvement of a manager.  Worst of all, the produce department is horrendous, and it just so happens to be the straw that broke this camel's back.

Last week I bought a bag of baby carrots.  When I got home and opened the bag, they were slimy.  

Yesterday, I bought some pre-husked and packaged corn on the cob.  Naturally, it was twice as expensive as the unhusked fresh corn, but I was in a hurry and I wanted a healthy snack (corn on the cob + spray butter + Frank's buffalo hot sauce + seasoned salt = food of the gods).  I also bought a large container of watermelon chunks, to bring to a pool party.

When I got to my apartment, I threw a pot of water on the stove and tore open the corn.  I was immediately met with a weird smell, which seemed to coincide with the slime that was now on my hand from a piece of the corn I had just picked up.  A whole lotta' cursing started going on at this point in time, as I disgustedly threw the cobs into the trash and frantically washed my hands with pink grapefruit soap, hoping to erase the association of Elmer's glue with my favorite summertime produce.

The watermelon was sufficient later that evening, but the damage had already been done.  I will not be returning for any reason in the future.

The words "ice cream" and "water ice" usually fill me with happy thoughts, but when combined with the word "Cabana," my mood sours.  One night last summer I had a craving for vanilla custard (that's "soft serve" for those of you who don't speak South Jersey) so off to Cabana I went.  Now, I get that "soft serve" is supposed to be softer than hard ice cream.  But is it supposed to be so soft that it starts melting all over your hand as you pay?  No.  Is it then supposed to implode into a hidden ice cream cavern before falling off the cone and onto the asphalt before you even reach the car?  No.

Vowing to boycott Cabana, a full year passed before I found myself giving them another chance when out with a group of friends the other night.  Had we not been pressed for time, I would have happily driven us all to Maple Shade Custard Stand, one of my favorite places on Earth.  However, Cabana was on the way and it had been a while since the mishap so I figured, why not?

This is why not.  My friend stepped up and ordered her hot fudge sundae.  They were out of hot fudge.  At 7 p.m. on a Friday night.  Two minutes later, a guy came in requesting blue raspberry water ice.  They were out (natch), and when the guy left, one of the Bratz dolls behind the counter remarked that water ice is artificially flavored anyway so it all tastes the same.  Awesome.
 
Luckily I had not already placed an order, so I hit up the McDonald's drive through for a $1 hot fudge sundae that kicked the ass out of anything they hadn't already run out of at Cabana's.

Does someone mind explaining why the apocalypse hit this Walmart location a long time ago? 

Walking in, I'm like a deer in headlights with the absence of neck tattoos, tight polyester clothing and loud, screaming children. I quickly scurry past the masses at customer service and Subway, trying to avoid eye contact while planning my attack. The faster I get to the items I need, the faster I can just get out of there already. 

Problem is, the items I need never seem to be in stock, or available at all. Something as basic as plastic cups was too much to ask on my recent visit. I secured small cups but, other than the giant red Solo cups, there were no other options for something in between. 

The only redeeming thing about the place is the body shop, which unfortunately means I have had to endure many an hour walking around the store while my car received an oil change. There aren't even any decent stores in the strip mall that shares the parking lot to escape to. 

I do believe I made my final exit through this Walmart's doors the other day.

Just thinking back on my limited experiences at this establishment gives me the creeps.  At the time, I worked at a nearby law firm and this was a favorite for support staff members and alcoholic attorneys alike (sorry for blowing up anyone's spot).  It is one of those places that you sneak off to for lunch to have a beer or four, and if you see anyone from work, you silently acknowledge them and immediately forget that you saw them there.  So I guess it's cool that this unspoken code exists.  

However, the place is downright nasty.  Cobwebs hang in the corners and every surface has that sticky feel to it.  You know what I'm talking about.  Mace's Crossing is as close to a dungeon as you can possibly get in the middle of Center City.

My dad has always talked about the Trolley Car Cafe as one of his favorite spots for lunch. Today, I met him there, and we both left in agreement that our experience was terrible.

There is outdoor seating in the back but we chose to sit inside since it was a hot day. Unfortunately, the amount of flies that were buzzing around the restaurant was probably more than we would have encountered outside. It was disgusting. They absolutely should put one of those double door hutch thingies leading to the patio to help prevent this. 

Service was bad. There's no other way to put it. Our server was nice enough, but she didn't attempt to relay our orders with any sort of accuracy to the guys in the kitchen who did more talking than cooking. My dad asked for a blackened salmon Caesar salad and I asked for the buffalo chicken wrap to be made into a salad (so basically, same ingredients, on a plate, minus the wrap). 

My dad's salmon was not blackened (he says he's had it that way on other visits without a problem). My salad wasn't remotely close to a buffalo chicken salad. There was grilled chicken (I was expecting breaded but wasn't bothered by grilled, even though it still seemed rather greasy), asparagus (what?), barbecue sauce (what?) and ranch served on the side instead of blue cheese dressing. The rest of the salad was pretty sad - just some romaine and a few dices of pale tomatoes. I'd rather not have any tomatoes than be served non-local tomatoes in the middle of August in an area surrounded by farms. 

It took longer than it should have to get the check and get out of there. I absolutely will not be going back, and I've already tipped off my dad to another nearby restaurant that I think he'll enjoy far more next time.

I received a thoughtful message from a Saxbys' manager after my previous review. So when a friend of mine suggested we meet there for coffee based on the fact that they have high chairs (she had her one year old in tow), I was down with the plan. I arrived moments after my girlfriend accidentally left the key to the bathroom in the now-locked bathroom. As I ordered our coffees, she apologetically told the cashier that she had done this and asked if they had another key. The cashier made a few unnecessary remarks about the fact that the door locks automatically and that's why they have keys. Thanks, genius. Regardless, the key was left in there by mistake, my friend was apologetic, and then she was subjected to some embarrassment handed down from the cashier. In the end, a large handful of extra bathroom keys was brought out and we got the door open. It didn't have to be a big deal but the entire experience was really off-putting. 

I went over to the creamer station (still in the same congested location as before), and literally had to swat away fruit flies while grabbing my sweetener and getting away from there as fast as possible. Obviously, something isn't getting cleaned properly and no one is doing a thing about it. 

This was my second visit to Saxbys and also my last.

I'm embarrassed to admit that I stepped foot in this place over the age of 25.  Alas, it was a friend's 24th birthday and the decision was not my own.  

There are two parts to this establishment.  The downstairs is a sports bar/restaurant and the upstairs is a club.  After hanging out downstairs for a while, a few of the girls decided to check out the upstairs.  Two bouncers made a huge production of searching purses and patting down all guys.  A sign that read "NY Style Dress Code" was posted nearby.  This should have been my signal to turn around but curiosity won out and I paid the five bucks to get in (it's ten for guys).  We proceeded up the steps... and straight into a code-red situation: popped collars, wannabe platform dancers and more hair gel than a mid-nineties LA Looks campaign. 

A few girls wanted to stick it out and dance but I made my way back downstairs to watch the Flyers' game.  My experience was severely hindered by the constant opening of a side door that let in a very cold and smoky draft.  Apparently, the patio area that is open in the summer also doubles as a smokers' lounge.

While the building itself certainly holds many memories of my past (under 18 dance parties back in the day at The Iguana, my first real bar experience after my 21st birthday at Top Dog, etc.), the ship has sailed.

In the span of a 15 minute train ride, PATCO made me vow to start saying my prayers again every night, and possibly even start hitting Sunday mass again. Let me explain. 

Last Friday evening around 5:30, I boarded a westbound train with two other people. The train car was surprisingly empty, but I made a mad dash for the only seat that had a sports page sitting on it. Just as I started to get into the Flyers' injury updates, the lights went out. This seemed odd, but the train was still moving so I didn't think much of it. 

We went underground in Camden, and the darkness in the tunnels was quite spooky. As we approached the first underground station, the train slowed, but did not stop. Same with the second. So the lights were out, we weren't making stops and no announcements were being made. As we made our way out of the tunnel and onto the Ben Franklin Bridge, I text-messaged my sister about the situation and said that I was a little freaked. 

As we went back underground in Philly, I thought we would surely stop at 8th and Market, where I was supposed to get off the train. Again, the train slowed but did not stop. At this point, it is safe to say-- I WAS LOSING MY SHIT!!! Worst-case scenarios featuring gunmen and hostage situations filled my head. 

I abandoned the sports section and made my way closer to the other passengers. A lovely woman by the name of Susan comforted me when I expressed my concern for our safety. For that, I am eternally grateful. 

When the train started slowing to what appeared to be a stop as we got to the 12th/13th & Locust station, I stood up and announced that I was going to pry the doors open with my bare hands if I had to. Which is exactly what I tried to do-- only, the doors were locked. I felt like I was in a horror movie when suddenly, the lights went on and we could see the conductor walking towards us from the car in front of us, a confused look on his face. He opened the door and said, "this train is out of service!" To which all three of us replied (i.e., screamed) something along the lines of "well then why were we let on to begin with?!" peppered with many expletives (mostly mine). 

I shakily made my way above ground, grateful to be alive, grateful for the kindness of strangers and grateful that some taxi drivers don't mind driving drunk girls home to Jersey at the end of the night when they decide to pass on the train.

I'm amazed at the positive reviews for this dentist because my experience was anything but positive. I reluctantly started searching for a new dental practice when my go-to for the past several years reached out to say they were no longer accepting my insurance. Due to the great reviews and proximity to where I live, I made an appointment quickly and easily with this office. I received texts leading up to the appointment which prompted me to confirm. 

I arrived a few minutes before my 1pm appointment. The waiting room is very small and you can basically hear all of the procedures as they are taking place a few steps away. I filled out some forms on a computer and waited about twenty minutes or so before being called back. I was seated in the first patient area closest to the waiting room. The only thing separating me from the patient right next to me was a small half wall - there was no privacy and I could see my neighbor's procedure as it was happening. I know dentist offices are always kind of open (which I think is incredibly strange) but this was really open and made me pretty uncomfortable. 

A dental hygienist came over to give me a dental bib and some protective glasses and I thought we were about to begin, but then she walked away and I just sat there, waiting. The sounds of Christmas carols and dental work filled my ears while a TV played some sort of dental demonstration, adding to my unease. As an entire hour of waiting came to a close, I removed my bib, grabbed my belongings and made my way to the door. The receptionist was apologetic but, truthfully, I was happy to leave. The search for a new dentist continues.

Yeah... no. The first thing I noticed upon arrival to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge, airport version, was the distinct and slightly unpleasant smell. The second thing I noticed upon sitting at the bar was the disgustingly dirty floor. Why did we stay? I guess the live music had something to do with it. That was the only redeeming quality about this place. 

It's a shame that a place as iconic as Tootsie's would put their name on this extremely sub-par restaurant, even if it is in an airport. The rest of the airport seemed very clean and well-kept, so I'm not sure why the ball was so majorly dropped here. 

Service was extremely slow and you really had to speak up to get someone's attention. The food was pretty awful. I also witnessed a bartender pouring a drink with one of those liquor measuring devices, but he would pull the bottle away before the pour was complete which amounted to spilled liquor around the drink. I would veer towards fast food or eating before the airport when given the choice again.

Should have checked the Yelp app first. Tsk, tsk.

At Nail Polish, $18 (plus tip) will get you a run-of-the-mill manicure, a beating while your nails dry (which they refer to as a massage), and wide-eyed comments and titters about your height, if you are a statuesque woman like myself. I'm 5'10" before heels and have no issues with my tall-ness, but I felt kind of like a circus freak with the number of questions I had to field in front of an audience while selecting my polish. 

I actually had to walk outside and catch a breath of fresh air while waiting for my friend's mani to finish up. This was probably the least relaxing manicure experience of my life. 

Also, what is up with the mini-convenience store going on along the wall? Pregnancy tests and sample-sized shampoos were among the items available for purchase.

I went to Baja Fresh for the first time today at lunch, armed with a printout of the nutritional info as I'm preparing for the upcoming bikini season.  My plan was to order the Baja Ensalada and Original Baja Taco, which are BY FAR the only selections that are a reasonably healthy option (check the website if you don't believe me).

After watching the BF employees prepare the food, which a blind five year old could have done faster, I was on my way back to work with my to-go bag.

"I can't wait for my chicken taco!" I thought.  I almost, ALMOST, tore it open on the car ride back (have you ever encountered a hungry girl on a diet at lunchtime?  No?  Well then get the eff out of my way or you're gonna get hurt.).  

FINALLY I was seated at my desk, diet coke open, salsas at the ready.  I opened the taco wrapper and saw... two (two???) tortillas with one, maybe two, chicken chunks and roughly half an onion scattered about.  Ohhhhkay.  "That shit cost me $2.25?" I thought as I tossed the onion taco with chicken flavoring in the garbage.  

Salad time.  To be honest, the salad didn't look half bad, but the cotija cheese that was promised in the ingredients list was nowhere to be found, and though some of the chicken was okay, a lot of it had that fatty fake-chicken consistency that so many fast food chains try to pass off as "chicken breast."  It was pretty disappointing, considering how much I've heard people rave about this place.  I guess the food that makes this restaurant the "Top Mexican Chain in America for 2007" lies within the menu items that are covered in cheese and deep-fried, aka, every other item on the menu.  Baja "Fresh" my ass!

I've had it with Capital. They used to be so reliable about a year ago but lately, not so much. It seems like every time I call for a cab, I end up waiting outside as the minutes tick by, growing more and more anxious as I realize I may be late to whatever meeting, appointment, etc. I may have. 

This morning was no different. I called at 8:37 for a cab to 30th Street Station. Twenty minutes later, still no cab, we started walking towards busier streets so that we could simply hail one. While in transit, I received a call from Capital that my cab had arrived. It was 9:04. Thanks. In the past I would have called to cancel, but this has happened so many times that I have come to expect that a cab may not show up in a timely manner, or at all. Bottom line, if there's a delay, people need to be notified. I will not call Capital again.

The boyfriend usually swears by Olde City Taxi, but these guys sucked it big time when we called for a ride to 30th Street Station last week. I don't know why, but every time we call a cab (from any company) specifically for 30th Street, they never seem to show. For now on, Uber will be my go-to when it comes to time-sensitive rides. 

Back to Olde City Taxi: we waited for thirty minutes and even logged a follow up call during that time to ensure that someone was on their way. Ultimately, we trudged down the street with our rolly bags to hunt down a cab the old-fashioned way.
