Another Philly cab company on my do not call list.

I had the unfortunate opportunity to go back to Champps for a friend's birthday.  The bathrooms seemed cleaner this time (although I lucked out on door #1 so who knows what was behind doors 2 through 5) but the experience as a whole managed to bring the place down to a one-star level.  Our server was terrible.  It was crowded and we had a big party, but the guy would take drink orders from two people and then scurry off, completely ignoring the other people at the table.  It took him twenty minutes to tell me that the wine I wanted wasn't available and another ten to bring me something else, which I didn't like (not his fault, I know, but frustrating nonetheless).  I flagged down a manager and calmly requested that he exchange my glass of wine for a 22 ounce beer (bigger is always better, but especially when you have to wait a year for your next drink). I made it clear that I was asking him and not our server because I didn't want to wait another twenty minutes for my first drink.  Perhaps a little harsh to get the manager involved, but when I spotted my rejected wine on our bill at the end of our visit, I felt it was even more justified.  The next time my friends want to hit this place up, I will NOT take it like a "champ" but will instead meet them at the after-party.  Harumph!

NEVER AGAIN!!!

Actually, I'm pretty sure I said those exact words several years ago when I was last at Mad River.  However, it was my sister's 23rd birthday, so I had to suck it up and go with the program. We arrived around 9 or so on Saturday night, thinking the bar would be relatively empty since the Phils game was postponed.  Not so much.  There was a Penn State alumni event going on, so the place was packed and we had to wait in line in the rain.  We should have known right then and there to cut our losses and go elsewhere.

Once inside, the bar was so packed with people that I started planning out a fire escape plan.  It was nearly impossible to get anywhere near the front bar, so we made our way to the back, where there was more room.  Only thing was, the floor was covered with puddles of beer, plates, napkins and food.  What the hell happened before we got there? Employees were trying to clean up the mess but it was a lost cause.  Nearby, I witnessed a guy spitting on the floor. I started to pray, knowing that only a stronger force than myself could get me through this night.

The $2 domestics that were being featured were actually plastic cups that were filled 60% of the way if we were lucky.  After a while, the back bar ran out of draught beer completely so the only option was to either pay for bottles or attempt to get to the front bar without getting felt up by every drunk guy in the place along the way.  I still can't believe we each paid $5 to get in.  The stamp should have said "sucker" because that's exactly what paying for anything in that dump made me feel like.

Not awesome. 

That's how I'd describe my experience at Five Guys tonight. I was so pumped for a Five Guys burger, since they are Whole30-compliant. The young lady who took our order was friendly and seemed to understand exactly what I wanted - a burger in a lettuce wrap, with grilled onions, tomato and pickles. 

When our number was called, my mom and I grabbed the bag and went back to her house to dig in. I opened up my container and couldn't believe it: two grossly overcooked patties, no lettuce whatsoever, a couple slices of pale tomato, a couple pickles and a small pile of grilled onions. Where was the g-d $&*# lettuce wrap?! In that moment I was Nancy Kerrigan. Whyyyyyyyyy? 

My stepdad said the Cajun fries were really good, but his burger, and my mom's, were also majorly overcooked. The fries I couldn't have, because, Whole30. Nine more days. French fries of the world, you're on notice.

At first, I defended this store because it's the only affordable grocery option for anyone south of South/north of Broad. But after several visits, I've realized it's okay for picking up a few items, but not a replacement for my regular stores (Shop Rite in South Philly/Jersey or Wegmans in Jersey). Yes, I still make regular grocery runs to Jersey, because the quality of the stores is so much better. I digress. 

The guy who works the seafood area seems to hate life and he takes it out on the crustaceans he haphazardly throws around. My first and only encounter with him was when he made me feel as if he was doing me a favor by using the same gloved hands he used to slop around a bunch of fish guts to handle the cooked shrimp I requested. (I ended up not purchasing them.)

Panhandlers set up camp outside the store and though there are security guards just inside the doors, no one does anything. 

On the bright side, mostly everything is priced competitively and I can generally find what I need (though it takes some searching since I never remember the layout of the store). The rotisserie chickens are tasty as well. I'll return if I'm too lazy to drive all the way down to Shop Rite, but I'll try my hardest not to be that lazy.

Maybe Top Tomato does some menu items right, but my turkey and cheese hoagie was pretty weak yesterday. They didn't have American cheese listed on their menu when we ordered online, so I had to get provolone. No big deal. But the turkey definitely wasn't high quality deli turkey and the tomatoes were a tad mealy. If you're going to have the word "tomato" in your name, at least get some tasty hothouse varieties. 

My sandwich was sliced at a really weird angle and not all the way through, so when I tried to pull the sandwich apart the bread ended up ripping at the wrong place. I realize this is the whiniest of all complaints, and I probably sound like a total brat, but if I'm going to order a sandwich from one place over dozens of others in this city, at least try to sell me on it. 

My friends seemed pretty happy with all of their selections (cheesesteaks, some type of chicken sandwich and an eggplant parm). I'll admit, there was some food envy. But I'm not sure that I'll be giving Top Tomato a second look the next time I want a sammie.

Thanks, Jay's, for helping me out with my diet today. How did you know I don't like salmon sushi? You must have had some idea since you replaced my California roll with a spicy salmon roll in my take-out. Clearly, my eyes were bigger than my stomach (yet again) when I ordered the three roll combo instead of the two roll. However, in the future, I'd like to make that decision on my own. Because you still got me for the cost of three rolls even though I only ended up receiving two out of the three that I ordered. 

Who knows what that poor guy who walked in after me ended up with. Five minutes after placing his order, he was asked for his order... again. 

For average-at-best sushi, awkward service and the California/salmon roll switcheroo, I bestow two stars.

It's pretty bad when, a short time after "checking in" to a bar via the yelp app, you get a text that says, "What the heck are you doing at Paddy Whacks?" 

Trust that you better have a good answer lined up, in the interest of saving any remaining street cred. My reason for being in this self-titled Irish bar last night was for one thing and one thing only: cheap beer. Paddy Whacks is an official sponsor of the Philadelphia Sports Network and, more specifically, the Wednesday night coed floor hockey league which I participate in. This means our team gets 10% off our total bill, half price appetizers and three dollar drafts. 

The decision to take this offer up was met with a collective groan amongst teammates, but we decided to scope out the sitch anyway. We entered to the pulsating bass of hip hop. The DJ spun to a room of about ten uninterested people. Poor guy. We grabbed a table on the opposite side of the room and struggled to hear each other over Nelly lyrics. Do the sentences, "Andele andele mami E I E I uh ohhhhhh! What's poppin' tonight?" mean anything to you? Spend one Wednesday evening at Paddy Whacks and I guarantee you they will play on a repeat track in your head the entire next day. 

I love some hip hop, but only at the right place at the right time and in the right mood. What kind of responsible person shakes it like a salt shaker on a Wednesday night, anyway? 

One beer (Victory pale ale - props for that) was all I could handle before turning in for the night. A couple teammates shared some boneless chicken wings that looked and smelled pretty tasty, but it's unlikely I will be back to try them for myself. The unanimous decision to find a new team bar was made in silent acknowledgment.

Every time I walk into the Foodery, I'm excited by the well stocked beer selection, which I am confident has been handled with care to avoid any possibility of spoiling.    

Every time I walk out of the Foodery, I feel like I've been robbed in broad daylight in front of a police station.

Why did two bottles of Stillwater Ale cost almost TEN DOLLARS more at Foodery than at a competitor (ahem, Food & Friends) across town?  I get the convenience factor of the location, and the fact that Foodery started the trend, but come on.  Maybe the price gouging works on the clueless but I'll mix my six elsewhere.

After getting totally lost via crappy directions from Google, my mom and I finally arrived at Sam's for a bridal shower - a half hour late. Fortunately, the bride was even later, and we didn't ruin the surprise. 

Sam's needs a major update, stat. The air smelled of old carpet and everything had kind of a sticky feel. The room we were in for the shower was decent enough, and a bartender kept soft drink pitchers filled, with plenty of glassware and ice available. 

We had a choice between chicken parm and crabcakes. Chicken seemed like the safer option, which is what I ordered. To start, a round of garden salads with just about the palest iceberg I've encountered. The dressing was tasty though, and there were black olives (bonus points there). Entrees were better than expected, although not super flavorful. The crab cakes were more filler than crab, but my mom liked the veggies served alongside. My side of pasta was weak, but the tomato sauce was decent and the chicken itself was fine. 

I most likely will not return to Sam's on my own volition, but I'm not super familiar with the area to know how it compares with other spots. I'd recommend using the Yelp app to find alternates if I had to offer advice to someone passing through.

I feel bad leaving two stars for this place because my lunch partner recommended it, but I wasn't impressed. 

The restaurant was nearly empty at lunchtime on Friday, which seemed odd. There was one server working and he was running around the whole time so we didn't see him very often. We had to call out for water refills and flag him down for the check. 

I ordered a special roll with spicy tuna inside and torched salmon outside, plus a king crab roll. It's pretty unlike me to not plow through my sushi, leaving no trace, but I actually didn't even finish my rolls. They were fine, but not exceptional. My friend had a few of the larger special rolls and the pieces were cut so large she actually ended up choking on one - thankfully, she was fine.  

The final nail in the coffin was when I went to wash my hands in the restroom and saw how filthy it was. I will not be returning, or ordering from this establishment, again.

Glasses of wine priced at $8 - $12 and a happy hour that consists only of reduced-price domestics? Playa, please. Public House no longer has the cool cred that warrants this type of inflation. 

I revisited Public House to meet up with some old friends from a previous job. It had been four or more years since the last time we all got together in the very same space. The crowd at the bar was smaller... much smaller. Gone were the lines at the door and, with that, the obnoxious bouncers. 

The bar food that some friends ordered looked pretty standard. I stole some housemade chips and a pickle from my friend's plate and the chips were solid but needed salt. After a few rounds, we all looked at each other for that crucial moment where you have to decide to either go home or make a move, the later of which will inevitably turn into a 2am rager. We decided for the safe option, with promises to meet up again before the end of the year, somewhere other than Public House.

I've been on a bit of a bagel kick recently, and Spread has been one of three shops I've visited in the past month or so. It was the most expensive of the bunch by far, and also the most underwhelming. 

I'll never understand the pricing structure at Spread; it's laughable how much a bagel with a few toppings can add up. I often enjoy my bagels with cream cheese, bacon, tomato and cucumber. This combination breaks the ten dollar threshold at Spread (and by the way, their tomatoes were pale and hard - Wawa has better tomatoes). 

I used to frequent the Spread in Rittenhouse but stopped going because of the cost to quality ratio. Still, I wanted to check out the UCity location, which always seemed big and bright from the outside. 

We sat at the bar counter after ordering and receiving our food. As I was eating my bagel, I was visited by an insect that scampered out from behind some type of coffee apparatus. My reaction sent the insect scurrying back to wherever it came from, but I was ready to get out of there after that. I know bugs happen in restaurants, but it was still a pretty big turn off. 

I think I'm done with Spread. Their bagels are good but not three times the cost of everyone else's good.

The official after-party spot for Opening Tap was PBR. Since my crew was in the mood for a few bites, we stopped by The Khyber first and made our way to PBR a bit later. 

I've walked by the place several times and have been looking forward to checking it out. The space is really pretty, and a lot bigger than other Old City spots. I love the windows that surround the outer walls. 

Unfortunately, my single experience with one of the tall male bartenders left a really bad impression. I had a coupon from a beer rep friend for $1 off a draft beer. I wasn't really paying attention that it was only for two different brands (like hers - duh! Sorry, Suzy!), and I ordered a Flying Fish Exit 11. When I passed the coupon over, the 'tender pointed out (not really nicely) that it was only good for the two other brands. Okay, no problem. I asked what I owed him, thinking the last seven bucks in my wallet would cover my drink plus tip. I thought I heard incorrectly so I asked the guy to repeat himself. EIGHT DOLLARS. For a Flying Fish draft, brewed not fifteen minutes away. Stupefied, I pulled out my credit card, and the angsty bartender whisked it away without even bothering to ask if I wanted to keep my tab open. 

In a place crawling with beer reps and other industry types, I'm actually pretty shocked at the 'tude that I - and others we were with that night - received. Not even a fake smile. I'd be hard-pressed to return for that kind of service, not to mention the overpriced beer.

So disappointing! 

My husband and I went to Yeeroh on Sunday evening for takeout. It has been on our radar for a while and we were stoked to try a new-to-us Greek restaurant. He ordered a lamb gyro while I had a salad with chicken added. Total with two bottles of water was around $25. 

The restaurant smelled delicious and our to-go bag was heavy so we were ready to chow down when we got home. I opened my salad box and was really surprised to find no lettuce at all. Worse, the tomatoes were so mealy, and the red onion was overpowering! The chicken was the shaved gyro kind, not pieces of grilled chicken as I expected. 

My husband was also unhappy with his sandwich. It was constructed sort of sloppily and all of the cheese and tzatziki was glopped in one section so the ingredients didn't really mix together. 

I'm really hoping our bad experience was a fluke, and I'm willing to go back for another try sometime. I really want to try those zucchini fries!

Sorry everyone, but I just don't get the warm and fuzzies for this place.  Don't get me wrong, the store itself is nicely laid out and very cute, but the items are priced at highway robbery levels.  The free yoga classes do nothing to add to the appeal for me, because I don't live in the city and I'm not a big fan of yoga.  Lastly, and many will find this statement upsetting, I found the sales staff to be downright annoying.  One girl sang along to the background music at full volume (am I the only person who finds this awkward?) and another asked a customer "what was wrong with them?" when the woman decided against whatever it was she tried on.  As if there couldn't possibly be a reason for not loving every piece.  

You may be wondering why I didn't simply leave the store to save myself this aggravation.  Well friends, my New York brother must have decided back in December that this trendy athletic wear store would be the perfect place to get my mother and I gift cards.  That, or there was a location in very close proximity to his workplace, or Penn Station, or both.  (Steve, if you are reading this, I kid.  You know I love your thoughtful gifts! Now, get thinking because you have exactly one month until my birthday!)

Therefore, since making a purchase was a necessity and not an option, my mom picked up a very cute gym bag, and I nabbed a workout tank (on sale for $29).  At the counter, I noticed some individually packaged thongs, which I can only assume have some sort of special power as they were priced at thirteen dollars a pair.  The girl at checkout snapped me out of my daydream when she asked if we needed a bag.  "No toots, we're just going to cut the tags off of this bad boy and throw everything in there!"  My actual response was a terse "Yes.  We would like a bag."  Sheesh!

I met a friend for lunch at El Merkury last week and, I have to admit, the experience was a bit confusing. There's a menu overhead but you place your order through a touchscreen system. Since it was our first time visiting, we asked several questions about the salads since we were both looking to keep our lunch on the light side. 

The menu overhead featured some sparkling waters, so I thought that's what I was ordering when I selected the lemon mint water from the touchscreen menu. We received drinks that looked more like lemonade, so I wanted to double check to see if there was any sugar. I was told that there was just a little bit, but I like to opt for unsweetened whenever possible. I traded my drink for a bottle of water. So my first piece of advice would be to put clearer descriptions on the touchscreen menu to avoid any confusion. 

The salads were pretty plain. Since we wanted to try each of the two dressings, we opted for dressing on the side. I personally thought both dressings looked and tasted very similar and couldn't detect much of a difference. The dressings were clearly very healthy - I don't even know if they had any oil in them. The result was a rather bland tasting salad, though the ingredients were all clearly very fresh. The chicken on top of my salad was tender and lightly seasoned. 

We also ordered a side of guacamole, which didn't come with chips (again, something that should be noted on the touchscreen) and was filled with a lot of diced cucumber (or similar veg). We dumped this on top of our salads but, again, I don't think it added a whole lot of taste. 

I get that El Merkury specializes in foods that are fried, so maybe it was a mistake to think that we could also get a delicious but healthy meal. Healthy, yes. Delicious, not really. If I go back, it would be for the other parts of the menu.

Downgrade!

I'd be misleading people if I kept my four star review at four stars; my recent experiences with Chow's have been anything but.  

For starters, they won't take credit cards for orders under $20.  Does take-out Chinese EVER cost more than ten dollars?  I think not.   

Next, the food.  Last Friday I defied Lenten mores and ordered the chicken with broccoli.  At $4.50, there is no denying that this is a total deal-- until you taste the chicken.  The uniformly flat pieces seemed suspect, and the taste was not good, no matter how much sauce was soaked through.  The chicken itself was also minimal; the dish would have been more appropriately named, broccoli with chicken.    

Even though I ask every time I call, there is still no option of brown rice; just boring old white or fried.  Surely I can't be the only person who wants brown?

The "amazing chicken" was still tasty the last time I ordered it, and I've always been pretty happy with their wonton soup.  When I'm craving one of these items on my lunch break, Chow's will suffice, but I'll be trekking to Han Dynasty for now on when I really want to get down with some good Chinese.

I ordered a buffalo chicken cheesesteak and a soda from Talk of the Town for lunch today via GrubHub. The delivery was quoted at about an hour, which was accurate. The sandwich was actually pretty good, if a bit small for more than eight bucks. It was the right amount of food for lunch, just on the expensive side. 

The soda arrived in a to-go cup with a lid. I thought that was kind of strange since I was expecting a can. Then I noticed that the cup itself reeked of cigarette smoke. As did the napkins and the bag that contained my sandwich. Gross. There are few things I find more offensive than a big whiff of cigarette smoke, and the last thing I want is for my lunch to be permeated with the stuff. Needless to say, I won't be ordering takeout from Talk of the Town again, though I wouldn't rule out a visit to the actual storefront.

My experience at Schlafly over the weekend was a little strange, to be honest. I sat down and ordered a club soda and some fish tacos. The tacos were brought over in less than five minutes which was a little suspect, but I was truly hungry and took my chances. They were actually edible and I was happy to have a somewhat healthy meal before flying home. 

I asked for the check and my server offered to give me a refill of my club soda in a to-go cup, which was very nice. My bill came to nineteen dollars and some change; I put thirty on the table. My server came by and picked up the check and cash, said she appreciated me, and was off. I started to realize after a few minutes that she wasn't coming back. I don't mean to sound cheap, but I wasn't about to leave a fifty percent tip, either! I basically had to hunt down said server by the kitchen to ask for some change. It was awkward! Next time, I'm eating before I get to the airport.

I feel kind of bad writing this review, since I belonged to this gym for a number of years, but a little constructive criticism is exactly what this place needs.  Before I get into any of that, I just want to state the positive~ I have always felt very comfortable going here, and for a small gym, there didn't seem to be anything missing with respect to cardio and resistance machines.  The price is right and fresh towels are provided, which is a great feature.  Also, I love the look of the gym~ tons of brick and wood with exposed ceilings.  They had the industrial look going before every other place had it too.

Over the past year or so, there have definitely been some regressions.  At least one or two treadmills are out of order at any given time, and of the ones that do work, some of the buttons do not--specifically, the one that slows the belt ("Jane, stop this crazy thing!")!  Also, about half the time, one of the treadmills is occupied by the person who is supposed to be working the desk, and not just when the gym is empty.  On numerous occasions, there were people waiting for a treadmill while one or two sat out of order and another was taken up by a gym employee.  Are you kidding me?  One of the resistance machines has a rope attachment that has been worn down to its last few threads for quite some time, one or two of the TVs have been broken for months, etc.    

These things could all be easily taken care of and should be.  It's understandable that not everything is going to be perfect all the time, but after a few of these things started adding up with seemingly no change, I reluctantly decided to move on.  In the past, I would have given this gym four stars, but now I can't see giving it more than two with all things considered.

I've experienced better is right. Of all Saladworks locations I've patronized, this was one of the worst. The workers were friendly but the restaurant wasn't a place I'd like to sit down and eat a meal. 

The salad I did get was totally fine, but the salads on display looked sad and gross. They aren't trying very hard, and it shows.

I don't know if I'm being stingy or if all this economy business has me paying more attention to financial matters, but lately I'm feeling like quality is declining and yet prices are crazy high!

Hang on.  Wait just a minute.  I think my micro and macro economics professors just got their wings!  Finally, five-plus years later, I get it!  

Joking aside, 2007's Best of Philly happy hour winner leaves A LOT to be desired.  They boast $5 wines by the glass-- but that's only for two selections, one red and one white.  The Cabernet they had on special was pretty beat, and since we didn't want to take a chance on the white, my friend and I ordered a bottle of chardonnay off the regular menu that was actually really good.

After a couple drinks, we ordered the tomato & mozzarella pizza and a wedge salad to share.  The pizza was good for sure but there was no substance.  A saltine is thicker than the crust used in this pizza, no joke.  As for the wedge salad?  I had to ask the bartender if he brought the right one-- it was a hunk of iceberg with some really random vegetables leaned up against it, and an unidentifiable gray substance on the side.  When the bartender confirmed that this was indeed the wedge salad, I asked where the Gorgonzola came in-- oh the gray stuff, of course!  The menu didn't mention that it would be presented in a baby poop-inspired way so that's probably why I didn't realize.  My bad!  

Rae is a cool-looking spot for sure, but I think they take advantage of the fact that they are the only real restaurant in the 30th Street Station/Cira Centre vicinity.  They miss the mark on "creative, complex and imaginative" because they try too hard to get overly fancy, which is just annoying and unnecessary (much like the 5 star reviews that are clearly written by Rae staff).  I can see why it's a popular spot, and the complimentary valet is definitely a bonus, but I don't think I'll be going out of my way to grab a drink or bite to eat there again.

I probably (definitely) made some mistakes with my first Buena Onda experience. For starters, I didn't actually check them out in-person; I ordered delivery from a service. Second, I didn't order tacos. What was I honestly thinking?! 

So while this review is strictly for my delivery experience, I'm confident that I'll stop in for the real deal experience soon.

That said, my meal was solid. I ordered tortilla soup and a chop salad with chicken. The soup serving was pretty small. But, with a thick broth that was chock full of chicken and avocado, it was actually pretty filling. The salad presented really well - the veggies were super fresh and there was a very nice sized serving of sliced, grilled, seasoned chicken. The chicken was a little bit dry, and I definitely was not crazy about the sweet taste of the cotija lime dressing. Also, the tortilla strips that topped both the soup and salad were quite hard/chewy - I had to be cautious because of my sensitive teeth. 

Clearly, Buena Onda is all about the taco experience, and I definitely went way off the grid with my order. Next time, I'm in it for the tacos and I'll surely update my review once that experience takes place.

Went to the Hut on Wednesday night with two of my girlfriends.  We sat on the outside deck which was nice, although a combination of the overhead lights and fan caused a blacklight effect that was giving me an intense headache.  Luckily, someone turned off the fan and the Jamaican rave experience ceased.

Other yelpers mentioned very slow service and I would say that they were partially right~ our server was very attentive (as were the other staff members who consistently refilled our chips and mango salsa basket) but the food took a long time to come out.  Not such a big deal for my group of friends that night because we talk for hours anyway, but I could see how it would be annoying if you were hungry and didn't want to be there for three hours.  

The coconut shrimp app was DELISH.  I wish we had ordered two since the plate had four shrimp and there were three of us.  Two of us got the jerk chicken breast platters and the other had the mango chicken platter.  The chicken was tender and very flavorful but perhaps a bit too spicy on the jerk plates.  The mango chicken was really good also but my friend kept coming across a lot of small bones throughout her dish-- I think it might have been harder to see them in the mango sauce versus the jerk sauce where you could see them more clearly.  

I'm glad we got to check it out but I don't see myself dining here often with so many other options that I prefer in the city.  Also, the $4 corking fee for EACH bottle of wine or six pack was pretty ridic.

As far as my care at this office goes, I feel pretty confident. But that's once I'm in the exam room. Everything before and after that point is why this facility gets an average rating. The receptionists are hit and miss... mostly miss. I've gotten attitude and short attention spans on almost every call I've placed to the office. God forbid you ask whether your insurance covers something and they have to open a file or place a call to find out. 

The doctors are solid. I used to see Dr. Hyder but after seeing Dr. Prasad once I ended up continuing with her. She's no longer in the Cinnaminson office but on my visit last week I saw Dr. Kessler and she was great, too.

Okay, Smiths.  To be fair, your establishment is pretty swank for a sports bar and my brain did start chanting "sau-sage par-ty, sau-sage par-ty!" upon entering.  However, $26 for two slightly-dirty Ketel One martinis?  For realz?!  Not to mention, the martini I specifically requested was listed on the board as having blue-cheese stuffed olives and yet the olives in my drink, while indeed plump and delicious, were hollow and... empty inside.  Sad.  

I'll be back to check out a game and some of those delicious-looking apps, but I definitely won't be hitting the hard stuff.

This was the go-to movie theatre during my teenage and college years. And apparently, it still is since Loews' parking lot is always full and the theatre remains relatively nice. The one thing I don't love about the place is that the crowds can be unruly depending on the movie and time of day (usually a night or weekend, which is becoming less and less likely a time that I'll go to the movies nowadays). That's probably not something most movie theatres have control over but it is a reason that I'll typically opt for the former Ritz in Voorhees or the Ritz locations in the city. That said, it's the perfect theatre for a weekday flick and very convenient to the area's shopping and restaurants.

I've been here twice now, the first time for a manicure and the second for a pedicure. For a manicure, it's a very nice place and you'll certainly get your money's worth. But for pedicure services, no one can match my regular guy Thom from the salon I frequent in NJ.

The pedicure chairs are not comfortable. Basically, you are sitting on a cushioned bench against a wall. From this angle, lifting your leg for certain parts of the service feels more like exercise. For the cost of a pedi at Rescue, I want to relax and zone out, not pull a muscle trying keep from sliding off the bench as I hold my leg in a 90 degree angle. 

I would certainly return to Rescue for another manicure or some of the services they are better known for, but for pedis I'll stick to my usual spot.

I definitely like this location of Foodery more than the other. Even though it's smaller and cramped, I feel like I can find what I'm looking for quickly. The prices are still astronomical. A mixed six pack and a bag of Doritos set us back somewhere around $26 on Saturday. And before you go thinking we picked a bunch of fancy stuff, consider the following. The beers in our sixer were: Dogfish Head 60 Minute, Harpoon IPA, Ballast Point Sculpin, Victory Weizen Bock, Cerberus something or other (looks slightly fancy with a foil topper) and Great Lakes Edmund Fitzgerald. Come on.

At around 12:45 a.m. on a recent night out, it was decided that one more drink was necessary, along with some bar food.  Since I was the driver that evening (cue shock and awe), our fate was in my hands.  I tried to think of a location that would have both ample street parking and a quick and easy route to the bridge.  Prohibition Taproom came to mind.

The bar and furnishings were dark and mostly made of wood.  A string of old-fashioned looking lights hung above the bar, and they would dim a little on occasion, which I loved.  A DJ played some serious jams that were heavy on the gangsta rap.  It had been a while since I'd heard Easy E, Dre and Ice Cube and I was digging it wholeheartedly.  Everything flowed perfectly with the old school, moody vibe.  

We sat down at the bar and asked if the kitchen was still open.  It was maybe five after 1 at this point, and the bartender took a look at the clock and told us that everything in the kitchen gets turned off at 1.  There were no ifs, ands or buts, and no offers to see if there was anything that could be done.  For a new bar trying to make it in a recession, I found this response to be pretty off-putting.  I got over it when I looked at the beer list, though.  One glance at the words Blanche de Bruxelles, and I knew that Prohibition Taproom would soon become one my spots.  Next time, I'm coming earlier so I don't miss the kitchen cut-off.

Being in the Market & Shops at Comcast Center reminds me all too much of my former life in the corporate world. Shudder.

That said, if I did work in the Comcast Center, I'd be pleased with the options for lunch that I'd be able to take advantage of without even leaving the building. Percy Street Barbecue and DiBruno Bros., most notably. 

The "Shops" would leave me wanting. There isn't much to get excited about. A lady who wants to flex some plastic on her lunch break is better off at Liberty Place or Walnut Street.

I recently noticed Giorgio on one of the apps I use regularly for delivery. My go-to pizza spots are Kermit's and Santucci's, but I was in the mood for something different and gave Giorgio Pizza a try. It's worth noting that the prices at Giorgio are a lot lower than these other spots.

We ordered a sausage pizza and some arancini. Delivery was fast and the food was just the right temp. While the sausage on the pizza was average, I found the pizza overall to be pretty solid. The arancini was cooked nicely but it was sitting in sauce so the parts facing the sauce became soggy. I'd recommend serving the sauce separately for take-out or delivery.

I would definitely consider Giorgio again for fast pizza delivery when I'm not looking for anything extra fancy.

Compared with other Starbucks locations, this one seemed fairly new. There were several comfy-looking chairs and the entire place was spotless. 

The staff seemed a bit amateur. I asked about the ingredients in a pumpkin latte and got a bewildered look from a staffer, like I had just asked a question about quantum physics. After I explained ("You know, is there sweetened syrup? Just spices? What exactly gives the latte it's pumpkin flavor?"), she relaxed and ran through the ingredients list, which seemed too sugary for what I wanted (and there's no sugar-free version of the pumpkin latte). I went with a regular latte and the boyfriend ordered a mocha. 

There were several staffers but the process wasn't as seamless as other locations. Still, this is one of the few coffee shops in the area that I could find on my Yelp app, so it did the trick.

Woe is me to give any government-run service more than three stars. Like Dan F, it was the third time that was the charm for me with PennDOT. 

After 14 months of living in Philly, I decided it was finally time to commit to being a Pennsylvanian. So on Monday I got all dolled up (license photo, of course!) and had my hand on the door when it occurred to me that I should double check the business hours. Closed. Slightly miffed, but not as much as I would have been had I made the trek, I went about my day. 

On attempt two I actually made it to the office. I had every document ready to go, but when the woman behind the counter took an extra long time studying my birth certificate, I knew something was wrong. Turns out, my birth registration certificate - the same one I've been using my entire life for all matters of importance - was no longer acceptable because it wasn't an actual birth certificate. Huh? Turns out, you need to apply for a birth certificate because your birth registration certificate isn't actually the real thing. (And yes, that's going to cost ya - $20 to the state!) Luckily, a passport can be used as a document in lieu of a birth certificate. Too bad I didn't have that with me. Imagine my crankiness.

Third visit, chip on shoulder, I returned. I had a full bladder just in case they added urine sample to the proof of identity requirements (kidding). This visit was quick, relatively painless, and I was out the door with my temporary license in less than an hour. Next up: registration and license plates.

My first trip to Mac's was solid. A server set us up at a table for six right away and he was on top of his serving game for our visit. When I wasn't sure what I wanted to drink, he brought over a few different samples for me to try. Still kicking myself for not ordering the high ABV coffee IPA that was available. 

A friend seemed to enjoy a hummus plate so I ordered one to snack on. I liked that there were a lot of vegetables and not just pita. For the most part the plate was okay, but the first red pepper strip I picked up was slimy, so I avoided those. The cucumber slices were good but they were layered with some sad looking tomato slices. The garlicky hummus had some random red onion slices sticking straight out of it. 

Don't go to Mac's for the hummus plate. Do go for the beer and friendly service. (And maybe some french fries - those looked really good!)

My friend and I spent much of Bastille Day at the bar at London Grill. The bartenders were friendly and in jovial moods. There were some liquor promo girls giving out free samples of product, which was cool. 

Once we decided we were hungry, I ordered a burger and my friend ordered parmesan truffle fries. The burger was curiously served on an English muffin-type roll, but it was pretty tasty. The fries that came with, along with my friend's fries, were room temp and not delish. She sent hers back but I had my burger so I was okay. A new batch came out approximately one minute later and they were definitely hotter but still just so-so. 

It's not often that I'm in Fairmount so I'm not sure I would go out of my way just to hit up London Grille. But if I found myself in the area, I wouldn't be opposed to stopping by, either.

Somehow I missed the fact that this place even existed. It's a bizarre part ice cream shop part café. I agree with Tom M that the decor is dated. It's what I'd expect a restaurant in Harrisburg to look like. To-go is the way to go at this place. For me anyway. 

The dessert case was interesting. I think I saw the biggest apple pie crust ever. How they get it to rise so high I have no idea. A peanut butter pie looked absolutely delicious. But last night, it was all about the ice cream.

I tried samples of two different flavors before making my decision. I eventually settled on a waffle cone with rocky road on the bottom and birthday cake ice cream on top. The birthday cake ice cream was so sweet and delicious. Probably a little too sweet for some people, but I was loving it. By the time I reached the rocky road, it tasted bland in comparison. Art finished off the second half of my cone, having already devoured his cone with mint chocolate chip and cookie dough. 

Both cones came to eight bucks, which seems like a really good price when compared to the likes of Franklin Fountain and Capogiro. It's not as good as either place, but it's still an option.

Public House: A Users Guide for the Ladies

Your experience at Public House will depend solely on when you go.  

If you don't mind hobnobbing with married men who pretend they are still single (think "oops, I forgot my wedding band" types), definitely hit up Friday nights.  You'll get a mix of suits who are still out from the happy hour that should have ended three hours ago, along with some younger gentlemen who look like they missed the stop for Mad River.  Expect the place to be jam packed, expect to run into at least one of the accidents you dated back in your naïve years and expect your dirty martini to be spilled all over your arm when you are bumped by one of the many drunks.  Good times.  

And now a look at the brighter side.  During the week, Public House can be a decent place to grab a drink and socialize.  It's far less crowded and the service is less spread thin.  Sometimes Bryen from Mr. Greengenes plays an acoustic set on Wednesday nights, and you know you love some Third Eye Blind throwbacks mid-week.  

Public House isn't a bad place, it just depends on the day you go and your tolerance level for others.

Solid standard Chinese. And they deliver. I ordered chicken and broccoli one weekend when I had the craving but didn't want to eat anything too heavy. Lots of tasty white meat (nothing scary), and lots of slightly crunchy broccoli (just the way I like it). The sauce wasn't too heavy and the rice was perfectly cooked. I also liked the wonton soup. Definitely interested in giving this place another shot sometime soon!

With so many other options in the general vicinity, Black Sheep just doesn't excite me. The beer selection isn't very vast, and the drafts seem overpriced, even for the location.  

The juke box is awful. It's an Internet juke, so while you do have the ability to select the songs you want to hear, it will cost double the credits, which adds up. The house selection includes top 40 stuff and some outdated albums from ten years ago.  

It has been years since I've eaten at Black Sheep, which saves this review from dipping to two stars. If I were reviewing on bar alone, I'd go there, but since I understand that the kitchen is an attraction, I'll stick with three. Based on the other reviews, I feel like maybe I'm missing something and should probably give this place a chance... but it won't be an easy sell getting me back in there.

After reading the negative reviews on this place I expected to spew nothing but vitriol, but I actually had a pretty fine experience. To be fair, I didn't have to wait in any lines, because when I walked into the theatre, a friend had already purchased our tickets ($9 for a Sunday matinee-- not cheap but not outrageous, either). 

I didn't hit up the concession stand but a friend who went down for a coffee said the lines were short but the workers themselves were extremely slow-moving. 

There was no assigned seating for our particular movie. The seats were comfortable and the theatre itself was relatively clean. No one in the crowd was annoying and cell phones were silent through the duration-- always a plus. 

I wouldn't go out of my way to see a movie here, but the location can't be beat for a dinner and movie night in University City.

I was running errands in Haddon Twp and pulled my car over when I spotted Westmont Party Supply. I'd seen the store before but never had a reason to pop in. But with a list of items to pick up for an upcoming bachelorette party, it was as good a time as any.

The store was a little more rundown looking than I expected. Some shelves were half empty. Kinda weird. But they had a decent selection of bachelorette party stuff (think G-rated - if you want anything phallic-shaped you'll need to hit up a Spencers or other novelty shop) and I was able to grab a couple things. They also randomly had a selection of sprinkles for cakes or cupcakes and I picked up a small cup of all pink for .99. 

Not bad if you're in the area, and it's always nice to shop local.

Tippling Place was the third cocktail bar I walked into on Saturday night around 8pm but it was the first with an available seat. I think this place flies just below the radar, which is great when all you want is a place to sit and enjoy a beverage. The bartenders are friendly and there isn't any attitude. Just a cool, comfy setting and great drinks. 

The cocktail menu is pretty extensive but I was disappointed that there weren't any hot beverages listed. So I went with a different seasonal delight, which was a pumpkin egg nog of sorts. It wasn't as heavy as a traditional spiked nog though it had all the right flavors. My second drink was made with rye and it was boozy. I loved the pretty cocktail glass it was served in - very vintage.

Drink prices are steep; right in line with other cocktail bars in this city.

C'est vrai: J'aime French Bakery! 

The third time was the charm for me with this adorable new bakery. On my first attempt, I tried to meet Alisha S on a Monday, only to find that the shop is closed on Mondays. Alisha had arrived before me and walked in through the open doors. Though she was informed that they are not open on Mondays, the employees sent her away with some complimentary pastries - so nice! 

My second attempt was for a savory breakfast. Alas, there was no quiche left by the time I arrived, and I needed something substantial before my long day. 

Finally, another meeting with Alisha was scheduled and the bakery was both open and stocked with several quiche options! I ordered the quiche lorraine which came with a small side salad. It was absolutely perfect - decadent and just the right size for lunch. I haven't tried the sweet pastries yet, but there will be many more visits in the future. 

I'd love to see an enhanced menu of savory items (perhaps some baguette sandwiches?). Also, I'd REALLY love some wifi (but understand if they don't want to be the type of place where people like me stick around too long). In any case, looking forward to my next visit! À la prochaine!

So far, so good. I had my first experience with ECO Cleaners a couple weeks ago. I dropped my clothes off on a Monday or Tuesday in hopes that I could have them by Friday, which was not a problem. My usual spot always takes at least a week. 

On Friday morning, I received a text message from the cleaners informing me that my clothes were ready for pick-up. I haven't done an Inspector Gadget-style study of my threads but they seemed appropriately cleaned and pressed. Also, this place was a lot less expensive than my usual dry cleaner. 

Today I dropped off a second batch, which will again be ready by Friday. If all continues to go well, ECO may become my go-to dry cleaner. Super happy to have this business so close and convenient to my home.

When a double date was scheduled with one of my favorite couples, I needed to select a restaurant with good food and a fairly laid-back atmosphere.  One in which we would not offend our neighboring diners, once the wine was flowing and our inappropriate "remember when" stories were unleashed for the billionth time.  

I had only been to West Side Gravy once before but I knew it would meet my requirements while being wallet-friendly to boot.  We arrived to find the restaurant mostly full and very loud.  The background music I had enjoyed during my quiet lunch was completely drowned out.  Fortunately, we were able to snag a table in the rear corner of the dining room, and many of the families with younger kids left soon after our arrival (coincidence?).

We ordered all the fat kid appetizers: crispy cheesesteak eggrolls with horseradish cream sauce and frizzled onions, cheddar and bacon-topped potato skins and West Side fries, topped with bacon and melted cheese, with wine gravy for dipping.  Everything was as delicious as it sounds and we tried to convince ourselves that it wasn't really that bad since we didn't each order an appetizer.  Ah, denial.

My dinner of (now I'm cringing) fried chicken left a little to be desired.  All of the pieces were dark meat, which was disappointing.  The potato salad served alongside was tasty, but the mayo-laden coleslaw was overkill.  My companions all seemed happy with their dishes.  The spicy bacon-wrapped meatloaf over mashed potatoes was devoured, as was the seared ahi tuna special.  

Health fanatics that we are, we passed on dessert and decided to finish up our wine and continue on with our night.  I wouldn't mind returning again soon, and I may even try something that doesn't get prepared in a fryer!

Kanella was the latest installment in my BYO girls' night-outs.  I had bailed on the ladies a few days prior due to a hectic schedule, but after having a pretty rough day, my friends convinced me to cross the bridge and join them.  Always better to sulk in the company of good friends than on one's own, no?  

The service was great--our server was full of character and didn't seem to mind explaining menu items we weren't familiar with.  He was on-point with refilling wine and water glasses alike.  

We started with a trio of dips and some pita bread.  There was easily enough garlic in said dips to take out all the vampires in Nintendo's Castlevania (I, II and III), so be warned.  The entrée selections were very heavy on meats and whole fish.  Since I'm not very adventurous when it comes to protein, and I wasn't very hungry to begin with, I opted for a Horia Tiki salad (basically a Greek salad) and the Garides Saganaki appetizer, which was a small serving of roasted shrimp in a feta-tomato sauce.  The salad was fantastic--the dressing was more acidic than oily, which I prefer.  The shrimp were good, but they came with their heads attached which is not my favorite presentation.  My friends dined on the octopus app, the pork entrée and the goat stew entrée.  Everyone seemed happy although I did not taste any of them for myself.  

Dinner was finished with an assortment of Cypriot pastries and a thick and buttery date tart that had a cinnamon-tasting ice cream.  I had French-press coffee for the first time, which was a presentation in itself and a nice end to the meal.

Xochitl is one of my favorite places to go for a drink in Philly. I hope that doesn't change anytime soon. The margaritas are the best and I do believe they are a bit larger than they used to be. But several staff changes (including the chef) over the past year lead me to this review update. 

I'm going to shoot straight: this new version of Xochitl is overpriced. Not for the drinks, which I feel are worth their tag, but for the food, which is sadly not as good as it was in the past. Wanting to share a few small plates for dinner on Saturday night, we ordered a red snapper ceviche for $14. The fish was more like sashimi with some red onion and orange pieces thrown in. There was absolutely no citrus taste to the fish itself, which is a staple in ceviche. It really lacked any kind of taste other than the snapper, which could have used a little salt as well. 

Two types of tacos were better in show. The steak tacos were juicy and very flavorful, and the chicken tacos with a nice, healthy slice of avocado were great... with the exception of a small bone in one of mine. The accompanying sides of black beans were slightly warmer than room temp and not so great. 

These three plates plus two margaritas each came close to $100, including a generous tip (we received a couple new drinks on the house in exchange for our thoughts on them so we wanted to make sure our server Michelle was covered). Happy hour will probably be the way to go for me in the future, because I cannot live without those amazing margs. Sadly, the late night happy hour I used to love on Thursday nights is no longer, but I'll happily pull up a seat from 5-7 on weekdays.

I ordered delivery from Poke Bowl recently and was pretty happy with my order. I got the Ahi on Fire bowl, regular size. I did ask for the sriracha aioli on the side, which was a solid decision. I'm a little picky about aioli so having the ability to control the amount was perfect. 

The bowl came with sticky rice, fresh tuna, jalapeños, scallions, spicy shoyu and a couple other ingredients. I have to agree with Megan Y that there was more heat than actual flavor. Next time, I think I'll create my own bowl and add some seaweed and cucumber to enhance. 

Overall, solid poke delivery and I'll be ordering again in the near future.

Excuse me, have you had the mac and cheese? It comes in a piping hot cup which keeps the cheese gooey until the last mouthful, and is topped with buttery breadcrumbs that provide a perfect little crunch. 

I shared one side of mac with two other ladies during dinner last night, but it just wasn't enough. So I went back for a midnight feeding and ordered another... which I ate all by myself. I'll spend the day in self-loathing mode but damn that mac was good.

After closing down a nearby restaurant, it was decided that Tria was the closest spot for a drink in a quiet atmosphere.  At around midnight, the bar was surprisingly quiet for a Saturday and there were only a few tables still occupied.  I loved the dark, sexy vibe, flickering candles and the music selection, which was loud enough to hear but not so much that we had to shout over it.  

Since I had already enjoyed several beverages throughout the late afternoon and evening, I asked the bartender for a light beer of his choice.  He suggested one of their newest beers, Avril, which turned out to be a refreshing Belgian Ale.

It was a lovely evening and I plan to return soon for another relaxing night, perhaps with wine and cheese next time.

I've been to this Sephora only twice, but both experiences were very positive. My first time was for a makeup application. I didn't make an appointment in advance because it was a weekday morning and I figured there wouldn't be a wait. Wrong! I quickly found out that the makeup counter is always slamming. Fortunately, there was a spot available and I was able to slide in - I don't know what I would have done if they hadn't been able to accommodate! 

There is a $50 minimum purchase for the makeup application, but you can buy whatever you want. It's a good excuse to stock up on the essentials. I picked up two of my old standbys which needed replacing, and I also bought the lip color that was used on me that day. My makeup artist was great, and fun to talk to, but I do wish I would have spoken up a bit more about what I wanted. 

Unfortunately, I returned a few days later after deciding that the lip color was way too bright for my day to day. It was returned with no questions asked, and the woman at the counter even gave my friend and I some free samples while she was at it. Meanwhile, after signing up for Sephora's insider card, I received an email that my birthday sample pack is waiting for pick-up. Happy bday to me!

While in NJ this week with some time to spare, I did a Yelp search for nail salons and Tara's was among the highest-rated in the vicinity. Several people mentioned calling first and that was solid advice - this is a small operation and only two people were working. I gave them a ring around 3 and they asked me to come in at 4, which worked for my schedule. 

There was a short wait time and then I was up for my pedicure. Unfortunately, the chair was wonky and I couldn't move the seat back or recline it at all. Not ideal since I'm fairly tall, but the massage function made up for that a bit. 

The woman who did my nails was friendly and, very importantly, gentle. I do not like for my cuticles to be cut on my hands at all and my request was honored. My services were very relaxing! 

I gave my nails a good twenty minutes to dry, but one of my nails smudged about ten minutes after I left. Two days later, I have also seen some chipping. I'm hoping the top coat I applied today can fend off any more. 

Overall, for the price, which was very reasonable, I'd consider booking there again if in the area. I'll just be prepared with my top coat!

For the organizational freak in me, The Container Store fulfills my every wish. I got so excited by the potential of the merchandise on my last visit that I had to force myself to focus and stick with the tasks at hand. Which were: airtight mason jars for my flour, sugar, etc., a vertical wrapping paper container and a box for Christmas decorations. 

So maybe I got a little sidetracked by all the after-holiday sales. At least I have mini cards to attach to next year's gifts!

Frugal shoppers beware, gettin' tidy comes at a price. Set limits and try not to get bamboozled by the aisles and aisles of promised structure to your chaotic life.

My first visit to Tbar was almost a year ago, while I was training with my then-manager Kevin L. It was our third and final day together before I would be unleashed to my own devices and we needed a place to settle in for some calls. Tbar fit the bill on that cold day, and aside from accidentally dripping some hot tea on my brand new Mac and nearly having panic attacks over it, it was a good experience. 

My second visit occurred yesterday with my now-manager Colleen C. The place was pretty quiet early in the afternoon, and we scored seats on the extremely comfy couches. I confessed to never having bubble tea before, and it was pretty much decided that I had to try it. I ordered an almond flavored tea with skim milk and just a touch of sugar. The tea was delicious, and I was curious about the wide straw and unsure of what was to come. Then, the bubbles started popping up through the straw and I'm pretty sure the look on my face was priceless. It was interesting. I liked it, for something different, although it's probably something I would go for only once in a while. 

While we were there, a pressed sandwich was made for another customer and it smelled absolutely heavenly. I'll probably head back and set up shop for a day sometime soon.

I've been back to Osteria twice for happy hour and both times have been solid. If you arrive early you can have your choice of seats at the bar; the crowds don't start rolling in until after 6. 

Glasses of prosecco, a red wine and a white wine are all $5. Pretty solid! There is also a beer and cocktail on the happy hour list as well. I'm a fan of the prosecco.

All pizzas are half off and there is a variety of small plates - I tried the trentino and parma pizzas and both were great. The wings were also very good. They are small and cooked perfectly and have a slightly sweet glaze and some seasonings. 

Pro-tip: you can get from Osteria to Distrito on the inside if you need to avoid the elements!

I am way overdue on an upgrade to Buena Onda. We order lunch or dinner from them pretty regularly, and it's rare that I receive an order that I'm not happy with, though it does occasionally happen. Thankfully, our orders are on point more often than not.

One thing Buena Onda does better than most of its competitors is packaging. Tacos arrive in grooved cardboard containers that keep the tacos from spilling all over. We enjoy the fish and shrimp tacos but have tried many of the others as well. 

Recently, buena bowls have been added to the menu, and they are great! So far, I've tried one with tofu chorizo and one with shrimp. Both were excellent and kept me full all day, which is what I want out of a healthy(ish) lunch. 

I have been pretty disappointed by the serving sizes of the guacamole and salsa, which come at standard restaurant prices but really small portions. Nonetheless, I love Buena Onda for quick and easy Mexican food, delivered to my front door.

I checked out Brodo on day two and while there are definitely some kinks that need to be worked out, I anticipate that this will be a solid spot for lunch in center city. I knew I wanted a salad but I also wanted a taste of one of the delicious-sounding soups. Fortunately, they have a combo option where you can do a half sandwich or salad and a cup of soup. I did the salad/soup and with a largish bottle of diet Snapple, the total setback was just over ten bucks. Not too shabby!

My lunch partner and I had arrived just after noon, right before the rush. As we collected our utensils and parked ourselves at a table, it was clear that there was going to be some major back up with regards to the amount of customers and the time it was taking to get orders out. We didn't have to wait too long but there was a large crowd of people waiting for the rest of our lunch. As we waited, I noticed the Boylan's soda fountain. Nice!   

The half and half combo is the perfect size for lunch. The Maryland crab soup was average but did the trick (admittedly, I chose it specifically for the "LF" insignia, meaning low fat, but there are plenty of richer options), and the cobb salad had crisp romaine lettuce and just the right amount of toppings and dressing - not too much but not lacking. 

It seemed like table wipe-downs were being overlooked in the rush, but other than that and the small wait for our lunch, my experience was solid. Hopefully in a few weeks, Brodo will be running like a well-oiled machine.

One of my girlfriends and I decided to get together to gab over pedis instead of our usual cocktails, and Rescue was one of the few nicer salons with evening hours. Unfortunately, my friend was unable to make it at the last minute, but that wasn't going to change my plans. I called Rescue and ended up moving my appointment up by an hour, which was more convenient for me. 

My last visit to Rescue was about a year and a half ago, and at the time I felt they could not match my favorite salon. Unfortunately for me, that salon closed, and since then I've been a nail care wanderer, checking out all types of salons around the city. I've found a few places I like, but I'm not fully committed to any of them. It had been a while since my last Rescue experience, so it was time for another try. 

My pedi with Anna Marie last night was pretty wonderful. I'm still not a huge fan of the bench seating, but it was more comfortable than I remembered. Maybe those yoga classes are paying off. Even though the pedi was only a half hour, it still felt really thorough and my nails and skin were properly filed, buffed, scrubbed and polished. Like an idiot, I wore socks and pointy boots to the appointment (it was cold and rainy!) so I stuck around for a good 35 minutes after to let the polish dry. No one made me feel like I was wearing out my welcome as I waited, either. I was offered tea or coffee and told to relax as long as I wanted, which was so nice. My toes were then slathered in oil and wrapped with plastic wrap to protect the pedi from my boots. There was still a very slight smudge by the time I got home but it's practically miniscule and certainly not the fault of Rescue. Stupid pointy boots.

I also noticed there is now a check-in offer for a $100 massage and manicure package. It's so tempting. I may return sooner than later.

Wild child notwithstanding,* I do like having La Va as a local coffee option. Last night, I went to meet a friend for a cup and catch-up. My sweet tooth was kicking, and I had every intention of trying one of the chocolate desserts I had ogled in the case during visits past. I asked the barista about them, and he told me there were three different varieties and his favorite was the chocolate mousse. I paid for my large latte and took my chocolate mousse bomb to a table.

Holy chocolate heaven, Batman. I'm surprised I was able to put the spoon down after a single bite and save the rest for when my friend arrived. I could have easily scarfed and destroyed the evidence, but I'm glad I shared, because sharing is nice, and all girls love chocolate. I will definitely consider a sweet treat from La Va again (just not if I've already indulged in one of their oozy fresh mozzarella, tomato and olive tapenade panini - that would be going overboard).  


*The moment I walked in, I noticed a toddler running rampant. The parents clearly did not care that there were meetings taking place, people doing work, etc. Their kid was just booking around the store, running into people's stuff, touching things, etc. 

If it was annoying for me within the first 30 seconds of my arrival, surely it must have been annoying for the other customers. I wish I could review the parents, but this sidebar will have to do.

I got Prime Rib'd, y'all.

I was warned that the happy hour at Prime Rib was so magnificent, so unbelievably dealtastic, that it had actually overpowered some of the most seasoned drinkers I know. I had heard about the battles fought, the stories that have become legends, and yet I went in blind, became instantly mesmerized by the old money and botox, and ordered my half-priced Kettle martini with blue cheese stuffed olives, up. And then I ordered another. And then I ordered a cosmo (that tasted more like a gimlet). And it was only after my third drink that I thought it wise to order some food for my empty-besides-the-vodka stomach. 

I think you know where this story is going.

After a few tasty clams casino and some potato skin crisps, some renegade in our group insisted we order yet another drink. I got a glass of sauvignon blanc. What I needed was a large water and two advil, plus a full night's sleep. 

Onward into the night we went. I can only hope the other people we encountered throughout the evening were as intoxicated as our crew/me. It may be a while before I'm able to face a martini again. And that is really saying something.

Starbucks in my home town! The future is now! 

Like Yelper Steve P, I too was very skeptical when I saw the Starbucks sign outside of the building that once was a mom and pop pancake house way back in the day. But I was pleasantly surprised by the large, inviting space when I walked through the doors. This would be a great spot to get some work done or have a casual meeting. 

I ordered an Americano and asked if they had the egg white breakfast sandwich, since I didn't see it on display. The employee at the register looked through the refrigerator but, unfortunately, they didn't have my go-to. I opted instead for the bacon, gouda and egg sandwich which was tasty if not as light as the egg white option. My Americano was HOT - I couldn't drink it for a good twenty minutes. 

Overall, glad to see this new location so close to home. No more driving to Delran for my Starbucks fix!

Way back in 2009 when I attended my friend Jessica M's wedding, I was so blown away by the DJ she hired that I sang their praises to anyone who would listen. A year or so later, at my girl Karen B's wedding, we tore up the dance floor all night. Once again, No Macarena was responsible. I knew - KNEW - that they would one day DJ my wedding, and they were one of the first vendors I booked once my man and I set a date. 

Kim, the owner, hooked us up with Jonas, who was amazing to work with. We had some venue changes a couple months out and he worked with our venue contact on logistics. I sent over the music request sheet a couple weeks out and we spoke on the phone to go over everything, including how to pronounce the names of everyone in our wedding party. I thought this was great and so thoughtful. 

We were stuck on a final song and I told Jonas the song we wanted, but thought would be awkward because of a talking interlude. He sent me a version without the talking part, which is what we ended up going with - it was the perfect choice (Home, by Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros, in case anyone is curious)! Also, I asked Jonas to play my grandparents' song, and he checked with me first to make sure they were ready and available for their dance. He really thought of everything.   

My only advice would be to provide all of your song requests up front. Including songs that aren't part of the reception but that you still want to hear on the dance floor. This will save you many trips to the DJ booth and will probably make the night easier for your DJ (sorry, Jonas, but thank you for being so great about all of my last minute requests!).

It took some time, but I finally made it in to FedNuts today. And while I didn't partake in the donuts or chicken (both of which were tempting and delicious-looking), I did have a large cup of smooth coffee while enjoying conversation with the revolving door of industry peeps and neighborhood loyalists.

Felicia and Blake make the ordering process look seamless, even as the small space filled with eager chicken-lovin' hopefuls right before noon. Arrive well before that to enjoy counter seating and some of the non-fancy donuts, which are only available early in the day. Next time, that chicken is mine.

I've been taking Platoon's free classes at the Comcast Center for the past four weeks and I absolutely love them. The trainers, Michelle and Malik, are awesome and inspirational. 

I'll admit, I begrudgingly went to the second class dreading the various cycles we had gone through the week before. I assumed that because the classes were free, they would be exactly the same. Wrong! Every single class has been different. Each has been painful in its own special way, but for me, not knowing what's next makes it easier to push through. This has kept me going back for more week after week. 

Although I already have a gym membership and pay for another boot camp in NJ, I am seriously considering looking into Platoon's programs.

Super solid delivery experience from Southgate last weekend! Though my husband and I have been to the restaurant plenty of times, it was our first time trying delivery. The restaurant did an incredible job wrapping everything securely, and the time between placing our order and receiving it was really quick! 

We started with the KFC (spicy) and the pork dumplings. My husband loves dumplings and I was lucky to snag one. Southgate's were very tasty and I really liked the dipping sauce. The KFC was delicious, as always. 

I stayed consistent with my main and got the Seoul hot chicken sandwich, with fries. It was delicious and definitely spicy. My husband had the pork ssam - I didn't try it but it looked great. Can't wait until we can enjoy a meal at the restaurant again but, in the meantime, I'm happy to know we can enjoy the same delicious food at home.

I wasn't sure what to expect with Suraya but I absolutely loved everything about it! I'm a fan of the order at the counter, get your number and find your own seat style of dining. Maybe not for every meal, but for lunch or brunch, I'm totally down. 

Suraya was incredibly beautiful, as expected. I love Root and Cafe La Maude so was not surprised that these two wonderful businesses combined to make for one lovely offspring. 

In our haste to try a medley of items, I completely dropped the ball and forgot to order a side of fries. Who even am I? Next time, for sure. Things we did try: crispy chickpea hummous (perfection), cheese/tomato/onion/long hot/parsley man'oush (very good but I'd recommend sharing along with other items so you have a wider variety of flavors), and the kafta kabab (my partner hogged it and I only got a small bite but it was awesome!). 

My man loved his clementine ginger soda and my orange blossom iced tea was nice as well. 

The only thing that bums me out is that Suraya is all the way across town from where I live. How come Fishtown gets all the nice things?! I am looking forward to making the trek again when dinner is added to the mix. Suraya is worth the trip.

I was out for a long walk yesterday when I came up to Hale & True, and immediately noticed the signage outside. They are currently offering cider to-go through their window. How could I resist? The employee was friendly and informative about the different types of cider. They had two different bottled ciders, another in cans, and everything on tap was available for growler fills. 

The employee put on gloves for the transaction and it was quick and easy. I went with the Lil' Sunshine, which is made with honey and orange peel. I'm saving my cider for the weekend and can't wait to pop it open for a little taste of sunshine!

I met up with a friend for lunch outside on a gorgeous afternoon a few weeks ago. There were plenty of outdoor tables which were covered by a tent that was open along one side. Because it was so sunny, it actually felt quite warm but I bet the tent would be great at blocking some wind on a chillier day. 

I was happy to see some booze free options on the beverage list, and ordered a Don't Call Me Shirley, which was a simple club soda with housemade grenadine - fantastic! 

We shared the arugula salad, margherita and mushroom pizzas. I specifically requested the salad first but everything was brought out at the same time. Nonetheless, every single item was delicious! So delicious, that my husband and I ordered dinner from the Pizzeria Vetri in Rittenhouse that same night.

I feel like Philadelphia has gone from pizza desert to pizza wonderland in a pretty short time. I don't always think of Vetri when I think of pizza, but it's a consistently solid spot that shouldn't be overlooked.

I've been on the receiving end of André's emails for several months now. The salon always seems to have great specials, but I don't typically require any services outside of my usual cut and color every eight weeks. I'm very loyal to my regular stylist and don't feel the need to experiment outside of our monogamous relationship.

However, the day came when I had a fancy event to host (helloooo Yelpy Awards!) and I wanted to step up my game with some sexified hair. Since my regular salon is located in Vineland, NJ and is not open on Mondays, I had to improvise. Enter André Richard Salon. 

The blow out bar was something that I'd heard about through emails and on Twitter, and when I found out that all services on Mondays are 20% off, I was sold. I made a quick and easy appointment online with LB, and the salon called to confirm. 

LB was super sweet and definitely seemed to know her way around hair. She expertly blew out my tresses and managed to work some serious body into my locks. I felt like a straight up diva walking out of my appointment, and my hair is still holding onto some volume a day later. Next time I have a fancy event and I can't get out of the city, I know where I'm going.

Thanks to the care instructions I received at Pure, my white orchid has been thriving. So well, in fact, that it grew so top-heavy with blooms that the simple base it came in could no longer anchor the plant down - even with a weight thrown in! After watching my lovely take a flying leap from the windowsill one day, I finally got the hint and off to Pure we went. 

One of the florists helped me pick out an appropriate base, and then she transported the plant and added some taller stems to keep the branch upright. I am so pleased with the results and how much prettier the orchid looks in a proper flower pot. 

I do not believe the orchid will attempt any more dives.

I really wish I hadn't waited to write this review as the details aren't as fresh in my memory. But, I'd be remiss if I didn't still pop up to give my five star seal of approval! 

My husband and I had reservations for an early dinner on a Saturday in October. We tried a lot from the menu: date truffles, garlic yogurt, baked cheese, croquettes, chili chicken kebab, and whole roasted fish. Honestly, I think there was more but, like I said, it's a little hazy over a month later. All I know for sure is that our table was covered with gorgeous food! 

Every dish packed a ton of flavor but there was a lot of variety between each plate. Extra props for the fish, which was sea bass on our visit. If you know anything about Jen Carroll, it's that she knows her way around a fish-you'd be kind of silly not to order one at her restaurant! The sea bass was absolutely perfect.  

I was partaking in a sober October, and was thrilled to try the N/A Groni, which I had read about prior to our dinner. Basically, it's a booze-free take on a negroni. I absolutely love bitter cocktails and this version was delicious and made me feel really excited to sip on something interesting. 

Unfortunately, we had to rush through our desserts as we were running behind for another commitment. Our own fault as we really took our time during dinner. I won't make that mistake again; next time, Spice Finch is the main event! Looking forward to trying the breakfast and brunch menus as well.

I may be having a little too much fun at Juniper Commons. What? There's no such thing? Okay then. We'll just settle on lots of fun being had during my two visits so far. Not to mention, great food and drinks. 

There's a lot about the 80s that should probably be left in the past, but the folks at Sbraga Dining managed to pull out all the best parts and incorporate them into their new restaurant. The music selection is on point. I'm talking dance in your chair, sing all the words magical. 

The decor is most definitely 80s-esque without being cheesy. I am in love with the lounge area, with its great furniture and throwback culinary magazines. The shirtless Tom Selleck photo on the wall in the ladies room is the cherry on top. 

The food that I've tried has been great. I enjoy salads more than the average person and the tableside Caesar and wedge are both awesome. I've had the crab cake on both visits and it was even better on night two. The baked potato is perfection. I've also had bites of the clam chowder, manicotti, eggplant parmesan, fettuccine alfredo, and creamed spinach. All great choices. 

The cocktails are mostly gin-based with a couple other fun options like house-made wine coolers. The Flying Caucasian, a gin and coffee concoction, went down really, really easy. My next reservation has already been made and I am looking forward to many more visits!

After almost giving up on finding really good sushi near my apartment, I conducted a little yelp research and came across Oh Yoko.  Not only did they have great reviews, but a few yelpers noted that the owners are huge fans of the Beatles and play only Beatles music in the restaurant.  I quickly realized this place had the potential to both satisfy my sushi craving and provide a solution for what to get my step-dad for Christmas (he's into sushi and also happens to be John Lennon's number one fan!). 

I went to check the place out myself for lunch on Saturday.  In Mi, one of the owners, kept me company as I was dining solo and they were not too busy at the time.  I learned that Oh Yoko has been open for three years and all of the fish comes from Hawaii.  The menu was large and had plenty of delicious-sounding options.  There was a huge list of special rolls that made choosing only one very difficult.  I opted for a volcano roll, which came with spicy tuna, mango, avocado, masago and crunch.  True to its name, the dish arrived in the shape of a volcano, with wedges of mango and avocado in the center.  It was phenomenal.
