So good, that I decided to order another roll~ this time with shrimp tempura and spicy tuna on top.  Meanwhile, In Mi brought me a bowl of their clear soup, which was a perfect complement to the sushi.  

I left feeling very full but with a new favorite sushi spot and a gift card for my parents.  Success!

This review is of the private spaces at Hotel Monaco. I have not actually stayed there or seen any of their guest rooms, but I did swing by recently for a site visit and I was completely blown away by the gorgeous decor and fabulous layout. The lobby area is filled with unique chairs, tables and decorative pieces, all of which are bright, colorful and patterned, all of which still manage to exist in harmony despite the craziness. 

The large event space fits up to 350 with the adjoining area across the hall, and the space manages a personality that is both classy and modern. It's a refreshing change from your standard hotel ballrooms. For smaller meetings, there are several board rooms on the lower level, plus a gorgeous private dining room that would be perfect for a swanky bachelor or bachelorette party. Or a fancy business lunch, I suppose. 

The rooftop lounge, Stratus, is also incredible. There is great indoor and outdoor space, separated by funky glass garage doors. Plus, there are two private rooms on each side of the outdoor area that are just really cool. I am really looking forward to checking out this space when the weather gets warmer. 

In summary, I'd like to plan every private party at the Hotel Monaco.

There isn't too much to say that hasn't already been said.  This particular location is clean, nice-looking and always packed with fun-loving people.  Once in a while, you will run into people from the local sports scene, which is always fun.  

My most recent visit was on Friday night, after the Flyers' disappointing overtime loss to the Montreal Canadiens.  When my friends and I arrived shortly after the game, Riley Cote and Arron Asham were already seated and drinking beers with a group of people.  How these guys showered and got over there so quickly remains a mystery.  Is there an underground tunnel that leads from the Flyers' locker room to Chickie's main bar?

In addition to the lively crowd and local sports figures, there were also Amstel Light girls giving out free beer.  Score!

At the eleventh hour while getting ready for Feastival last night, I decided it would be fun to have an updo for the event. Since I definitely didn't want to pay $50-75 like the last two I had (bridesmaid problems), I yelped "cheap updo" and Jean Madeline popped up in the results. I scoped out the reviews and their website, and within an hour I was at the salon reading the latest issue of Glamour. 

My stylist was Gia and she was only three weeks away from graduation, so I knew I was in good hands. I don't know how the students get anything done with their instructors pacing the floors, but props to all of them! 

I requested a modernized bun. Not one of those goofy things women are wearing on the tops of their heads these days, but something a bit classic just with some volume. Gia the miracle worker got down to teasing and pinning. The end result was a fabulous 'do - possibly my favorite updo in my hair's history, even! 

Of course, I tipped on the price of a normal updo and the entire thing cost me $35. Still a total steal, considering. I will absolutely think of Jean Madeline for my next special occasion!

Kermit's is overdue for an update from me. I'm there about once a week but could easily be there more because of my addiction to carbs. Fortunately, they do carry other, less carb-forward items! Soups and salads, for one. Their soups vary but I'm a fan of the potato leek. The salads are always delicious!  

Obviously, my favorite items are the pizza, bagels and a few of the sweets. I'm not crazy about the icing used for the cakes (it's got that whipped cream taste - I prefer sugary frostings) but I love their brownies and cheesecake bars. They also have great hot and iced coffee and there are rumors of soft serve for the summer. That's a rumor I can get behind.

I was pleasantly surprised by my dinner at Olly on Tuesday night! I'd heard some good things, and was expecting a nice meal, but dinner absolutely exceeded my expectations. The space is really cozy and inviting; there aren't too many tables so be sure to make a reservation if you want to eat in the dining room!

My friend and I shared a bottle of sparking water which was fine, but I would love to see some inventive non-alcoholic options on the menu (currently they have iced tea and soda). 

The food was awesome, and our server was fantastic. We started with buffalo cauliflower which was much lighter than what I was expecting. Here, you could actually taste the cauliflower, and the sprinkling of blue cheese was a nice addition. Next, we had the mushroom carpaccio, which was delicious! It was spread over the plate with some mixed greens and had a hearty sprinkling of parmesan. 

My friend chose the gnudi for her main (really nice!) while I went with the special of the day, a cod and clam chowder. This dish was hearty and loaded with delicious veggies and tons of flavor. Such a perfect cold weather meal! 

We couldn't resist dessert and had the chocolate tart and apple crisp. The tart was definitely my favorite; it was super rich and came with the most fantastic whipped cream and a caramel sauce that was phenoms. Loved it! 

Scrolling through my insta last night, I saw a photo of some really bomb-looking margherita pizza. Turns out, also from the folks behind Olly! They just opened a concept called Gigi Pizza, which you can access through Olly or a separate door on Bainbridge. Planning my visit!

My first experience at Heads & Tails was on Friday, and it will not be my last. The boutique salon was recommended from a business owner friend who always looks amazing. I booked my blow out with Dana and hoped for the best. 

I was a bundle of nerves when I arrived to my appointment - that night I would be hosting a large event and I wanted everything to go smoothly while simultaneously looking cute, calm and collected. Dana hooked it up with a glass of red while she got to work on my tresses. We chatted easily and my nerves started to calm. 

My hair is that weird length between short and long so I wasn't sure how a blow out would look, but Dana knew exactly what she was doing. In the end, I had a great style that I felt comfortable with and that even boosted my confidence. To my utter amazement, my hair still looked great after a heavy night's sleep and I was able to rock the look for an extra day. Already looking forward to my next visit!

If you haven't had brunch at Xochitl yet, get thee a reservation. It won't be long before Sunday's little secret gets out. 

I've now been for breakfast on two separate occasions, and on both visits, everything has gone beyond my expectations. Full disclosure: My second visit was comped because my boyfriend and I were invited to come in and sample the menu. But our first visit was on us, and we arrived on the very first Sunday they started offering the brunch menu.

Starting with the drinks, the coffee has an ever so slight cinnamon taste that really goes well with the bold flavors of the food. Mimosas are served cold and taste fresh-squeezed. Bloody Marias are a bold take on traditional BMs, served with tequila and a chili-salt rim. Waters are filled regularly without having to make requests. 

Xochitl's ceviche remains one of my favorite preparations in the city. So light, so flavorful, no matter what variation they are serving it is always delicious. Skip the usual guacamole and share this light starter instead.

On both visits the boy and I ordered the same exact thing. For him, huevos con chorizo: Two sunny-side eggs baked in a dish with kale, potatoes and loads of chorizo. Just as good as it sounds. For me, huevos revueltos: Eggs scrambled with thick-cut, almost pancetta-like bacon pieces and spicy peppers, topped with queso fresco and spicy salsa and served with corn tortillas. Every bit as good with egg whites substituted for whole eggs, which I requested on my second visit. 

We also tried the cornmeal and black bean pancakes, topped with fresh whipped cream, seasonal berries and the most delicious syrup I've ever had the pleasure of eating. These pancakes were nothing like any I've ever known before and yet they ranked among the very best. Highly recommended. 

The sun-lit room with happy music made me actually feel like I was on a mini-vacation. This is how brunch is supposed to be.

Shout out to Ed and crew! 

After scratching up my car pretty solidly in a tight driveway earlier this year, plus more love taps than any car should endure, my vehicle was looking pretty beat up. 

I pass Philadelphia Auto Body regularly and noticed their signs to check them out on Yelp. I was impressed by the reviews and before/after photos, so brought my car in for an estimate. Admittedly, it was a little more than I wanted to spend, but Ed walked through every step and I realized I had underestimated the amount of work needed. At the end of the day, I feel like the price was well worth the result. 

My car looks beautiful! There is zero evidence of the driveway incident, and my bumper was also touched up quite a bit (anything more would have required a new bumper so I am thrilled with the results of the touch up). Additionally, Ed recommended a bumper license plate protector for the front of my car - a genius suggestion that looks great and will hopefully help keep the front from getting too banged up in the future. Last but not least, the team identified some shoddy repair work from a previous incident that was handled by another shop in the city. They fixed these mistakes as part of my service, which I greatly appreciate. 

But wait, there's more! My car was returned with a full detail. Goodbye, Jersey shore sand and grime. 

I feel like my car is new again. I'm so happy! Highly recommend these guys and wouldn't hesitate to bring my car there again.
